items.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Biomarker Discovery for Precision Psychiatry.
items.abstract: Poor phenotype quality and small cohorts remain major constraints in psychiatric biomarker research, and recent methodological advances increasingly address them. Language models turn clinical text into analysable variables at a scale manual chart review cannot reach. Self-supervised models learn from the unlabelled signals psychiatry already collects. Variant-effect prediction makes molecular interpretation computable, and research agents have generated and experimentally confirmed candidates outside psychiatry. These capabilities act early, on what is measured, what can be learned from it and which candidates are proposed. None of the artificial intelligence capabilities reviewed here yet reaches the stages at which a candidate becomes a clinical test. Producing candidates is becoming cheap while qualifying them is not. This review is organised around that asymmetry rather than by disorder or marker catalogue. It separates the measured characteristic, the prediction model and the intended clinical use, and treats method family as distinct from evidential stage. Across the selected evidence, discrimination is supported more strongly in development data than in independent evaluation, and prospective evidence that model-guided use improves care is scarce. Many reported metrics also address a simpler task than the intended decision: diagnosis instead of differential diagnosis, general prognosis instead of differential treatment benefit. The review proposes a six-stage framework linking intended use, measurement validity, model evaluation, comparative utility and monitored deployment, and places each capability on it, clarifying where methodological progress can accelerate discovery and where conventional clinical validation remains indispensable.

items.title: Narrative group intervention for wellbeing and violence reduction among incarcerated women: a Sicilian qualitative study.
items.abstract: Purpose This study describes an action research intervention conducted in the female ward of a Sicilian penitentiary, aimed at promoting emotional awareness, enhancing relational competencies, and fostering solidarity, with the consequent goals of reducing interpersonal violence and improving psychological wellbeing. Design/methodology/approach The intervention involved 20 women over one month, employing female Greek myths as narrative tools to facilitate the elaboration of traumatic experiences and the reconstruction of personal identity. Two groups of ten participants engaged in one two-hour session per week for each group over four consecutive weeks (totaling 4 sessions / 8 h per participant). Needs assessment was conducted through individual clinical interviews. Findings The intervention produced heightened awareness of experienced violence, improved emotional regulation, and strengthened metacognitive capacities. Participants spontaneously assumed the role of peer educators, disseminating content throughout the broader ward community. A marked improvement in the relational climate was observed, alongside emerging solidarity dynamics. Artistic artefacts served as instruments of public representation and institutional communication. Research limitations/implications The absence of a control group, ethically precluded in custodial settings, restricts causal inference. Outcome assessment relied primarily on qualitative observation rather than standardised psychometric instruments. Penitentiary contingencies prevented follow-up evaluation of the stability of observed changes. Findings pertain to a single Sicilian institution and may not be generalisable across diverse custodial contexts. Future research should incorporate pre- and post-intervention standardised measures, longitudinal follow-up, and comparative analysis of different narrative typologies to strengthen evidence and enhance replicability of the intervention model. Practical implications The intervention demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of myth-based narrative group work in women's custodial settings, providing practitioners with a structured, gender-sensitive and culturally accessible psychoeducational model. The protocol - characterised by brief duration, low resource requirements, and adaptability to varied educational levels - is transferable across different institutional contexts. The spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics further suggests that structured group interventions can amplify their impact beyond formal participants. Penitentiary professionals, psychologists and educators may adopt and adapt this approach to promote emotional regulation and violence reduction. Social implications This study contributes to advancing gender-responsive and rehabilitative approaches within the penitentiary system, addressing the specific vulnerabilities of women in prison. By targeting interpersonal violence and promoting prosocial dynamics, the intervention supports safer detention environments and broader social reintegration. The emphasis on solidarity, emotional competence and identity reconstruction speaks to wider societal commitments to gender equality, restorative justice and the reduction of social inequalities. The cascading effects observed through peer education indicate potential for sustainable, community-level change within custodial institutions, with implications for public health and post-release social inclusion. Originality/value This study makes an original contribution by introducing female Greek myths as narrative mediators in a women's prison psychoeducational intervention, demonstrating their effectiveness across diverse educational levels without requiring direct trauma exposure. A further distinctive element is the spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics, indicating the capacity of structured group work to generate systemic change beyond formal boundaries. The interdisciplinary integration of anthropological and psychological perspectives, combined with an ecologically situated action research design, provides a novel and transferable framework for evidence-informed practice in custodial settings. items.title: Deals for delivery: Exploring consumer perceptions of price promotions and nutrition information on meal delivery apps.
items.abstract: Objective Meal delivery apps (MDAs) increase access to unhealthy foods and employ promotional strategies to encourage purchase. MDAs are often not captured by nutrition-related policies applied in other settings (e.g. energy labelling required on menus in physical fast food stores). This study aimed to understand Australian consumers' (i) use of and perceptions of promotions on MDAs, (ii) perceptions of healthiness of foods available on MDAs, and (iii) preferences for the inclusion of nutrition information on MDAs. Methods Twelve online focus groups were conducted with 112 Australian adults. Data were analysed thematically. Results Three themes emerged: (1) expectations that MDAs were for convenience and treats, not healthiness; (2) promotional offers were considered integral to using MDAs and often influenced food choice; and (3) limited interest in nutrition information on MDAs - most participants perceived that it would not be useful given health was not a priority. Conclusions This study offers insights into how consumers perceive price promotions and the complex interplay of factors influencing food choice on MDAs. Implications for public health Policy interventions that restrict promotion of unhealthy foods and increase promotions for healthy foods (e.g. price promotions) may assist in improving the nutritional quality of purchases on MDAs.

items.title: PENGARUH PROGRAM MOTOR COGNITIVE COORDINATION TERHADAP PENINGKATAN KONSENTRASI: studi eksperimen pada siswa SD berbasis gelombang otak)
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji efektivitas penerapan Motor Cognitive Coordination (MCC) dalam meningkatkan konsentrasi siswa sekolah dasar, dengan menganalisis kontribusi gelombang otak beta. Latar belakangnya didasari oleh pentingnya integrasi fungsi motorik dan kognitif dalam pembelajaran. Metode yang digunakan adalah desain eksperimen pretest-posttest control group design dengan subjek siswa SD kelas 4-6, yang dibagi menjadi kelompok eksperimen (menerima program MCC) dan kelompok kontrol. Hasil analisis statistik menunjukkan adanya peningkatan signifikan pada tingkat konsentrasi siswa di kelompok eksperimen setelah perlakuan (p < 0,05), yang juga sejalan dengan kenaikan aktivitas gelombang otak beta pada kelompok yang sama. Uji korelasi menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat antara peningkatan gelombang otak beta dan peningkatan konsentrasi. Temuan ini menyimpulkan bahwa program MCC efektif dalam meningkatkan konsentrasi, yang terbukti dari kontribusi gelombang otak beta yang meningkat. Implikasi dari penelitian ini adalah MCC dapat menjadi pendekatan inovatif yang diintegrasikan ke dalam strategi pembelajaran untuk meningkatkan kemampuan kognitif, khususnya konsentrasi, pada siswa sekolah dasar. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of Motor Cognitive Coordination (MCC) implementation in improving the concentration of elementary school students, by analyzing the contribution of beta brain waves. The background is based on the importance of integrating motor and cognitive functions in learning. The method used is a pretest-posttest control group design with elementary school students in grades 4-6, who were divided into an experimental group (receiving the MCC program) and a control group. The results of the statistical analysis showed a significant increase in the level of concentration of students in the experimental group after treatment (p < 0.05), which is also in line with the increase in beta brain wave activity in the same group. The correlation test showed a strong positive relationship between the increase in beta brain waves and increased concentration. These findings conclude that the MCC program is effective in improving concentration, as evidenced by the increased contribution of beta brain waves. The implication of this study is that MCC can be an innovative approach integrated into learning strategies to improve cognitive abilities, especially concentration, in elementary school students.

items.title: Towards sustainable construction: A Roadmap for Aligning BES6001 with the UN SDGs
items.abstract: The architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector has grown significantly over recent decades, sparking ongoing debate about its environmental impact. While advancing sustainability is essential, the sector’s role in meeting housing needs, upgrading infrastructure, and restoring biodiversity remains critical to delivering safe and resilient communities. Responsible sourcing and green supply chains are increasingly recognised as key mechanisms for delivering sustainable construction. BES6001 is a certification standard for responsible sourcing, offering a structured and transparent framework for AEC organisations producing materials. However, its potential contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently explored. This study examines the alignment between BES6001 and the SDGs, through the development of a conceptual roadmap. The roadmap was subject to expert review and identified strongest contributions to SDG-8 and SDG-12, although findings are based on preliminary validation (n=7). By analysing BES6001’s scoring criteria and principles, the roadmap illustrates how UK organisations may support the operationalisation of SDG commitments through BES6001 certification. Recommendations include revising BES6001 to strengthen SDG alignment and holistic review of SDG targets for developed regions where current goals may lack relevance. items.title: Diagnostic drivers of psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland 2013-2023: implications for service planning.
items.abstract: Objectives Psychiatric inpatient care is a high-resource component of mental health systems. Understanding the diagnoses driving inpatient care is essential for evidence-based service planning. This study describes psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland from 2013 to 2023 by diagnosis, sex, and age group. Methods National descriptive analyses using aggregated data from the National Psychiatric Inpatient Reporting System, covering acute inpatient admissions in Ireland. The outcome was total number of inpatient bed days, categorised by ICD-10 diagnostic group. Primary analyses focused on public services, with private services reported separately. We additionally report on child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS), adult services, and sex-stratified results. Results Between 2013 and 2023, there were k=3,993,628 public and k=1,879,877 private inpatient bed days. In public services, schizophrenia spectrum disorders accounted for 41.9% of bed days (k=1,673,529), more than twice as many as the next most prevalent diagnosis. Men accounted for 51.2% of acute public bed days. In private adult services, depressive disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (28.5%, k=513,166). In public and private CAMHS, eating disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (25.6%, k=46,850 and 24.4%, k=18,775), respectively. Conclusion This national analysis demonstrates that schizophrenia spectrum disorders represent, by far, the largest diagnostic group, accounting for 42% of public acute psychiatric inpatient beds days, highlighting the sustained, intensive service demands associated with these disorders. These data provide a clear empirical basis for future service planning, highlighting where targeted enhancements to community-based care could most effectively reduce the need for hospitalisation.

items.title: Involuntary Treatment in First-Episode Psychosis and Mania: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: The study aimed to examine how involuntary status at first presentation affects 5-year trajectories of first-episode psychosis or first-episode mania (FEP/FEM). The authors conducted a population-based cohort study on FEP/FEM. Legal status at first episode was classified as involuntary or voluntary. Participants were followed up to 5 years to examine relapse, emergency department use, vocational status, and Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS) scores. Relapse was compared by using log-rank tests; repeated-measures outcomes used mixed-effects models that adjusted for age and sex, with linear, logistic, or negative binomial regression as appropriate. The cohort included 200 individuals (voluntary, N=139; involuntary, N=61). The involuntary group was older than the voluntary group (p<0.001) and had greater illness severity (Clinical Global Impressions-Severity mean=5.5 vs. 5.1, p=0.002) at FEP/FEM. Time to relapse did not differ, nor did emergency department visits or psychiatric hospitalizations. Functioning improved at a similar rate in both groups; however, the involuntary group remained lower in functioning (SOFAS mean difference=-5.9, p=0.007) and had higher odds of being vocationally disengaged throughout follow-up (odds ratio=3.82, p=0.009). The authors found that involuntary treatment at FEP/FEM is common and is characterized by greater baseline illness severity. Involuntary status can serve as an entry point into care without excess long-term service utilization, and both groups showed similar rates of functional improvement. Persistently lower functioning and higher odds of vocational disengagement in the involuntary group support the need for targeted vocational interventions.

items.title: Life in the fast lane: early-successional species show four different strategies.
items.abstract: Background and aims Global land-use change and climate change are transforming tropical forests into regrowing secondary forests, where early-successional species play a crucial role by colonizing abandoned lands and paving the way for later-successional species. While often considered a homogeneous group with uniformly fast strategies, this study evaluates the diversity of early-successional strategies from Ghanaian tropical dry and wet forests. Methods We selected 30 early-successional species from Ghanaian dry and wet forests differing in leaf habit (deciduous vs. evergreen), and measured wood density and 12 morphological and physiological leaf traits related to drought adaptation and resource acquisition. Traits were compared between forest types and leaf habits using two-way ANOVA, and multivariate analyses identified trait associations and trade-offs. Key results Dry forest species were more drought-tolerant and had slower gas exchange rates than wet forest species, reflecting reduced water use under limited water availability. Multivariate trait analysis showed that early-successional species span a two-dimensional trait space with two main trade-offs: (1) drought tolerance (i.e. high absolute leaf turgor loss point and wood density) versus gas exchange, and (2) investment in leaf structural carbon versus nutrients. The two axes defined four strategies: species that (1) tolerate drought and have tough leaves ("tolerant-and-tough"), (2) tolerate drought and have nutrient-rich leaves ("tolerant-and-rich"), (3) grow rapidly and have tough leaves ("fast-and-tough"), and (4) grow rapidly and have nutrient-rich leaves ("fast-and-rich"). Conclusions Early-successional species followed four diverse strategies rather than converging on a single, fast-growing, acquisitive strategy. Their strategies also extended beyond the commonly described fast-slow gradient, with unexpected trait combinations reflecting the contrasting demands of rapid carbon gain and water conservation during early succession. Such variation may steer successional trajectories because different environmental conditions select for different early-successional strategies.

items.title: Prospective, Randomized Comparison of Electromyographic Neuromuscular Responses from the Adductor Pollicis and Abductor Digiti Minimi Muscles during Rocuronium-induced Neuromuscular Block.
items.abstract: Background Many clinicians monitor the abductor digiti minimi (ADM) muscle during surgery using electromyography (EMG) for ease and consistency of electrode placement, while practice guidelines recommend monitoring of responses at the adductor pollicis (AP) muscle. This study compared the onset time of rocuronium neuromuscular block and the sugammadex-induced recovery time recorded simultaneously from the AP and ADM muscles. Methods In 44 consenting patients undergoing general anesthesia, simultaneous EMG recording of ADM and AP muscles was performed. Right- and left-hand selection of monitored muscle (AP vs . ADM) was randomized, and patients' handedness was recorded. The primary outcomes were the onset time of neuromuscular block (administration of rocuronium until train-of-four [TOF] count equal to 0), recovery time (time from sugammadex administration until TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9), and time to maximal recovery (sugammadex administration until TOF ratio equal to 1.0). Results There were no significant differences between ADM and AP measurements in onset time, recovery to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9, or time to maximal recovery (TOF ratio equal to 1.0) between EMG responses recorded simultaneously from ADM and AP muscles. However, a difference in recovery times between ADM and AP existed, depending on which hand was monitored. When ADM was monitored on the right hand, the readings showed earlier recovery than AP, and the mean difference was 93 s (25% faster) and 105 s (20% faster) for time to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9 and time to TOF ratio equal to 1.0, respectively. There was no difference between the AP and ADM muscles when monitoring was performed on the left hand. Conclusions The current study underscores the equivalency between ADM and AP muscles for routine neuromuscular monitoring during surgery. When monitoring the nondominant arm, the ADM and AP muscles have similar recoveries. In the dominant arm, the ADM muscle recovery is significantly faster than that of the AP muscle.

items.title: Understanding the Experiences and Needs of Parents With Children With Epidermolysis Bullosa. A Qualitative Study to Inform the Development of a Self-help Toolkit.
items.abstract: Background Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) is a rare genetic condition characterised by skin fragility and blistering. There is no cure for EB and management includes wound care, dressing changes, and medications for pain relief and chronic itch. Parents of children with EB have a significant additional caregiving role, including provision of physical care, and this alongside other aspects of the condition can put parents at risk of psychological stress and distress. Objectives The primary aim of this study was to understand the support needs of parent caregivers of children with EB. A secondary aim was to consider how these needs might be addressed with the development of a self-help toolkit. Methods Thematic analysis using semi-structured interviews conducted with both parents of children with EB and expert healthcare professionals (HCPs). Results Parents described experiencing a range of complex emotions, including sadness, worry and uncertainty about the future, and guilt. The interviews with HCPs supported the parental accounts and highlighted the need for a tailored psychosocial self-help intervention. The findings suggest that a self-help intervention would need to acknowledge the wider family impact alongside recognition that considerable psychosocial impact is associated with the provision of continuing care. Conclusions Future psychosocial interventions must be designed around the needs of families, with a systemic approach to include siblings and the wider family unit. Approaches drawing on acceptance and commitment therapy might also be particularly relevant to this population but only if adapted to consider systemic issues.

items.title: Mental health literacy among Arab-Palestinians in Israel and its association with socioeconomic characteristics and healthcare utilization.
items.abstract: Background Research on Mental Health Literacy (MHL) has expanded across cultural minority groups, yet little is known about the relationships between socioeconomic status (SES), MHL, and mental health (MH) service utilization. This study investigates the relationship between MHL, SES, and MH service utilization among Palestinian citizens of Israel (PCIs). Methods A cross-sectional survey (n = 372, M age 36.88 ± 13.52 years, 68% female), based on the Australian National Survey of Mental Health Literacy and Stigma, examined associations between SES indicators (education and income), MHL components, and MH service utilization. Compared to the PCI population, the sample included more women, older people, and more people with higher education. Results Higher SES, as assessed by both indicators, was significantly associated with greater mental health literacy (MHL) at the bivariate level, particularly in terms of accurate disorder identification, knowledge of appropriate interventions, and lower levels of stigma. Hierarchical logistic regression revealed that education and income were significantly associated with MH service use (OR = 3.62, 95% CI: 1.38-9.45; OR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.13-0.99, respectively), and first-aid MHL knowledge also contributed to explaining variance (OR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.75-0.99). Other MHL indices, such as stigma and knowledge of potential helpers, were not significantly associated with service utilization. Conclusions The findings underscore the interplay between structural inequalities and cultural beliefs in shaping MH knowledge and behavior, and highlight the need for culturally sensitive, socioeconomically accessible interventions to improve MH outcomes in minority populations. The authors advocate for integrating MHL education into secondary educational settings and implementing policy reforms that address both material disparities and cultural barriers to care. These insights contribute to the global discourse on MH disparities in indigenous and marginalized communities.

items.title: Effects of Combined Sound and Working Memory Therapy on Medial Olivocochlear System and Auditory Sensory Gating in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Preliminary Investigation Using Contralateral Suppression of Transient Evoked Otoacoustic Emission.
items.abstract: Background and objectives : This preliminary investigation evaluated the effectiveness of sound therapy and working memory training in improving auditory sensory gating in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), as measured by contralateral suppression of otoacoustic emissions. Subjects and methods : Twenty-one children diagnosed with ASD participated in the study. Participants were randomly assigned to either a control group or an experimental group. The experimental group received a combined intervention consisting of sound and working memory training (SWMT). Within this group, participants were subdivided to receive one of three sound stimuli-white noise, waterfall sound, or Quranic recitation-along with working memory training. Contralateral transient evoked otoacoustic emissions (TEOAEs) were recorded before and after the intervention. Measurements included the absolute amplitude of overall suppression and frequency-specific suppression amplitudes. Statistical analyses were conducted to evaluate changes in TEOAE suppression from before to after the intervention, as well as to compare differences between groups. Results : Based on TEOAE absolute amplitude, all experimental groups demonstrated increased contralateral TEOAE suppression following SWMT, with the greatest improvement observed in the white noise group. In addition, white noise WMT produced enhanced suppression across all octave frequencies, whereas the effects of waterfall sound and Quranic recitation WMT were restricted to frequencies of 1 kHz and 4 kHz, respectively. These findings are consistent with the gain score analysis, in which white noise yielded the highest suppression across all frequencies except 1 kHz. Conclusions : SWMT appears to be a promising approach for enhancing auditory sensory gating in children with ASD, as evidenced by improvements in contralateral TEOAE suppression. Among the sound modalities tested, white noise combined with working memory training produced the greatest enhancement in TEOAE suppression.

items.title: Prognostic value of histomorphological and immunohistochemical parameters in gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) exhibit heterogeneous biological behavior, ranging from indolent lesions to aggressive malignancies, making accurate prognostic assessment essential. Prognosis is commonly determined using tumor size, mitotic count, and anatomical location; however, additional histopathological parameters may provide further prognostic insight. In this retrospective study, 40 GIST cases were evaluated to investigate the prognostic significance of histomorphological and immunohistochemical features. Tumors were classified into prognostic risk groups according to the Miettinen classification and categorized as low/very low risk or intermediate/high risk. Histomorphological parameters, including growth pattern, presence of necrosis, cellular atypia, and cell morphology, were assessed, along with immunohistochemical expression of Ki-67, CD34, smooth muscle actin, desmin, and S-100. Intermediate- and high-risk tumors were significantly associated with infiltrative growth pattern, tumor necrosis, and moderate-to-severe cellular atypia compared with low-risk tumors (p<0.05). The Ki-67 proliferation index was also significantly higher in the intermediate/high-risk group (p<0.001). No statistically significant associations were observed between prognostic risk groups and CD34, smooth muscle actin, desmin, or S-100 expression. These findings indicate that histomorphological features, such as necrosis, growth pattern, and cellular atypia, together with the Ki-67 proliferation index, may serve as valuable adjunctive prognostic markers in GISTs, complementing conventional risk stratification systems.

items.title: Development of Context-Tailored Trauma Team Activation Criteria for Injured Patients in Cameroon.
items.abstract: Background Due to high service demand, there is a critical need to rapidly identify injured patients in the greatest need of emergency trauma care resources in the Cameroon health system. We evaluated context-specific indicators of mortality to develop a triage tool for trauma team activation (TTA) in Cameroon. Methods Data were extracted from the 10-site Cameroon Trauma Registry between July 2022 and December 2023. Injury and care patterns were evaluated as potential predictors of hospital mortality using logistic regression. Variables associated with mortality were included in the novel Cameroon triage criteria (CTC). Receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curves compared discrimination of mortality for CTC, estimated Injury Severity Score (eISS), and a United States level 1 trauma center team activation criteria. Results Of 6912 patients, there were 313 (5%) in-hospital deaths. Factors independently associated with in-hospital death included burn injury (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.62), falls in patients greater than age 60 (aOR = 2.76), moderate-to-severe head injury (aOR = 12.5), and primary survey abnormalities (aOR = 11.8). The CTC (ROC AUC = 0.76, 95% CI = 0.73-0.79) was found to have superior discrimination to the US criteria (ROC AUC = 0.70, 95% CI = 0.67-0.72) and similar discrimination to eISS (ROC AUC = 0.78, 95% CI = 0.75-0.80). Conclusion The CTC demonstrates mortality prediction using injury mechanism and primary survey data that can be obtained within minutes of arrival to identify highest risk patients in need of resources. We can prospectively validate these criteria in our 10-hospital registry network to evaluate the impact of CTC activation on trauma survival.

items.title: Proposal for an Australian Model of Care providing accessible treatments for people living with borderline personality disorder.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo define a comprehensive model of care that improves accessibility of treatments across primary, private and public mental health care sectors for people with borderline personality disorder (BPD) in Australia.MethodsThis Model describes a staged/tiered approach utilising brief, short- and long-term psychological treatments in individual or group therapy settings. These treatments utilise generalist (common factors) and specialist approaches, enhancing the capacity of healthcare providers to offer care, thereby improving access to appropriate evidence-based psychological treatments.FindingsPeople experiencing milder symptoms of BPD may benefit from brief treatments employing a generalist psychotherapy approach. People with moderate to severe BPD may benefit from generalist/specialist approaches within the private and public sectors. People experiencing complex and high-risk BPD may require longer-term specialist psychotherapy and multidisciplinary care. Treatment type and duration should be tailored to the person's presentation and needs, with clear pathways for escalation of care when required.ConclusionsThis model of care proposes that psychological treatment be delivered at a level and within a timeframe appropriate to each person's needs and proximal to where they live. A Core Competency Framework, based on evidence-based common factors psychological treatment, can facilitate delivery of these services in a holistic, equitable, and streamlined manner.

items.title: Exploring the impact of Mexican front-of-package nutrition warning labels on sugar-sweetened beverage purchases and consumption among Mexican Americans in the USA, 2022-2023.
items.abstract: To examine awareness and self-reported influence of Mexican front-of-package warning labels (FoPWL) on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) among Mexican American adults in the USA. Data were analysed from Mexican Americans in the 2022 and 2023 annual cross-sectional International Food Policy Study surveys. FoPWL awareness (≥sometimes) and reported reductions in buying cola (2022-2023), soda (2022 only) and sweetened fruit drinks (2022 only) due to FoPWL were assessed. Weighted, adjusted negative binomial models tested associations between reported reductions in SSB purchases and past 7-d SSB consumption (2022 only). Online survey. Mexican Americans in US aged 18-100 years (2022, n 3329; 2023, n 2972). Overall, 43 % of participants reported being aware of FoPWL on beverages ≥ 'sometimes,' with higher awareness among participants with limited health literacy (v. adequate) (AOR = 1·5, p < 0·001), high (v. low) education (AOR = 1·50, p < 0·001) and more frequent Spanish language use (AOR = 1·59 p < 0·001). Self-reported purchasing less cola due to the FOPWL was also more likely among those with limited literacy (AOR = 1·28, p < 0·05) and high (v. low) education (AOR = 1·21, p < 0·05), while more frequent Spanish use was associated with reported purchasing less of all three drink categories (p < 0·001). In 2022, reported buying less of all three SSB due to the front-of-package nutrient warning labels was associated with lower SSB consumption (p < 0·001). Mexican American adults - particularly those with lower health literacy, higher education and more frequent Spanish use - reported greater awareness of Mexico's FoPWL on beverages and purchasing less SSB due to the labels, suggesting FoPWL could be considered for the USA.

items.title: Community-based nutrition interventions across the continuum of care in humanitarian settings: a systematic review and evidence map.
items.abstract: Objective To systematically review and map the evidence on community-based nutrition interventions implemented in humanitarian and emergency settings in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC), focusing on intervention types, outcomes, evidence gaps and implications for humanitarian nutrition systems. Design Systematic review and evidence mapping conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eight electronic databases and twenty-six organisational websites were searched for studies published between 2010 and 2024. Studies are mapped by intervention and outcome categories. Findings are synthesised narratively. Setting Humanitarian and emergency settings in LMIC affected by conflict, fragility, displacement or natural disasters. Participants Women, infants, children, adolescents, caregivers and households receiving community-based nutrition interventions delivered through community health workers (CHW), volunteers, peer counsellors, care groups or other community platforms. Results Fifty-three documents met inclusion criteria, including thirty-nine primary study documents representing thirty-three interventions across twenty countries and fourteen systematic reviews. Most evidence originates from Africa and focuses on community groups, nutrition counselling and community-based management of acute malnutrition. Preventive interventions generally improved infant and young child feeding practices and caregiver behaviours but showed inconsistent effects on anthropometric outcomes. Treatment interventions delivered through CHW and community volunteers improved recovery, programme coverage and treatment performance. However, evidence on dietary intake, food security, caregiver capacity, relapse prevention and longer-term outcomes remains limited. Conclusions Community-based nutrition interventions are central to extending nutrition service delivery in humanitarian settings and show strong potential to improve feeding practices and treatment outcomes. More integrated and context-sensitive evaluation frameworks are needed to strengthen evidence for resilient humanitarian nutrition programming.

items.title: "We'll Just Warm Ourselves up with Drugs": Polysubstance Use among Sexual and Gender Minority Persons (SGMP) Who Inject Drugs in Los Angeles, California.
items.abstract: Background In the United States, sexual and gender minority people (SGMP), including lesbian-, gay-, bisexual-, and transgender-identifying individuals, report disproportionately higher rates of illicit single substance use and polysubstance use compared to their heterosexual and cisgender counterparts. We conducted a qualitative analysis to better understand the disparate polysubstance use-related outcomes among SGMP reported in the extant literature. Our research question was: How and why do SGM people who inject drugs engage in polysubstance use? Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with SGMP assigned male at birth ( n = 15). Eligibility criteria included sex with men and injection drug use and/or opioid use in the last two years. Data were collected at a community site associated with a syringe services program in Los Angeles, CA between May 2022 and November 2022. Results All participants reported lifetime polysubstance use and discussed use of: (1) methamphetamines to meet increased energy demands of living in materially insecure risk environments followed by opioids for energy management and to prevent "overamping;" (2) methamphetamine to enhance sexual drive and experiences followed by opioids, cannabis, or gamma-hydroxybutyrate use to balance stimulant effects; and (3) multiple substances (such as opioids, methamphetamine, cocaine, alcohol) for mood management, emotional regulation, and managing past traumatic experiences. Conclusions Our findings describe and contextualize drivers of polysubstance use patterns among SGMP experiencing significant intersectional stressors exacerbated by material needs insecurity. Interventions must comprehensively integrate basic needs, mental health, substance use, and sexual health services to address inequitable polysubstance use-related health outcomes among SGMP.

items.title: Analysing marketing strategies for alcoholic beverages on Brazilian television, 2018-2020: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Objective To analyse the frequency and distribution of alcoholic beverage advertisements and to identify patterns of co-occurring marketing strategies on the three highest-rated broadcast television channels in Brazil between 2018 and 2020. Design Cross-sectional study based on 1296 h of television programming recorded between 2018 and 2020. Alcoholic beverage advertisements were analysed to assess their frequency and distribution according to day of the week and programme audience ranking, while empirical patterns of co-occurring marketing strategies were identified using principal component analysis (PCA). Setting The three highest-rated free-to-air television channels in Brazil. Participants All alcoholic beverage advertisements. Results Of the advertisements identified ( n 2369), 11·2 % promoted alcoholic beverages ( n 269). Overall, alcoholic beverage advertisements were more frequently aired on weekends than on weekdays and were predominantly aired outside programmes included in the monthly top 10 audience rankings. Four empirical patterns of co-occurring marketing strategies were identified: 'Brand Characteristics,' 'Sports and Well-being,' 'Relationships' and 'Celebrity and Pleasure.' Each pattern showed a distinct temporal distribution across the study period, with 'Celebrity and Pleasure' being more prominent in 2018 than in 2019, 'Relationships' showing the highest representation in 2019, 'Sports and Well-being' in 2018 and 2020 and 'Brand Characteristics' standing out in 2020. Conclusion Alcoholic beverage marketing was widely present on Brazil's major broadcast television channels and showed distinct patterns of co-occurring marketing strategies over time. The limitations of current regulations reinforce the need for stricter policies to reduce exposure to alcohol marketing and its potential impact on alcohol consumption.

items.title: Obesity Medications in Older Adults: A Geriatrics 5Ms Framework for Safe and Patient-Centered Prescribing.
items.abstract: Obesity medications that act through gut-derived hormonal pathways include glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1), dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1/GIP), and emerging triple glucagon-like peptide-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon receptor agonists. These therapies are increasingly prescribed for weight management and glycemic control, as well as for their cardiometabolic and renal benefits. While these medications offer substantial benefits to patients across multiple health conditions, their use in older adults warrants heightened scrutiny. Older adults face increased risks of sarcopenia and frailty, and evidence from major clinical trials suggests that a substantial proportion of medication-associated weight loss agents may result in loss of lean mass, potentially posing risks for this population. Other adverse effects that may be more consequential in older adults include dehydration, malnutrition, perioperative aspiration, and fat-predominant weight regain after discontinuation. This paper provides a clinically oriented framework to guide prescribing decisions for older adults. Drawing on patient scenarios from common geriatric contexts, including frailty, cognitive impairment, glucocorticoid use, and surgical planning, we propose prescribing approaches that optimize therapeutic benefits while mitigating potential harms. We integrate these recommendations within the Geriatrics 5Ms Framework (Mind, Mobility, Medications, Multicomplexity, and Matters Most) to contextualize treatment within geriatrics practice. Lifestyle co-interventions, particularly resistance training, adequate protein intake, and ongoing functional monitoring, emerge as essential components for older adults receiving these therapies. We also discuss identifying priority areas for future research, including age-stratified clinical trials and the routine inclusion of body composition and physical function outcomes.

items.title: Establishing Welfare Evacuation Shelters for Children With Medical Complexity: A Prefecture-Wide Policy Shift Driven by Simulation in Tottori, Japan.
items.abstract: Objective Children with medical complexity (CMC) are highly vulnerable during disasters, yet few Japanese welfare evacuation shelters accept them, leading to hospital-dependent planning. We aimed to assess the key issues hindering the establishment of welfare evacuation shelters for CMC. Methods In Tottori Prefecture (2020-2024), the government, municipalities, a university hospital, and device partners used facility assessments, staff education, and tabletop/field simulations (weekday earthquake with power outage and ventilator-dependent 5-year-old model) to identify gaps and iteratively revise manuals. Results Key issues included space underestimation, difficult mobility, power insecurity, unreliable verbal information, unclear deterioration pathways, and undefined public health nurse (PHN) roles. Revisions established PHN-led reception/triage, standardized information collection, specified power sourcing, and set escalation/transport flows. A section on "Persons Requiring Medical Care" was added to prefectural policies, and the disaster medical guidance was updated, shifting preparedness from hospital-centered to shelter-based welfare. Conclusion This simulation-driven intersectoral model appears scalable; however, it was performed in a single prefecture with limited follow-up, impairing generalizability.

items.title: Consumer and provider preferences for digital health technologies to improve access to comprehensive primary health care in very remote Aboriginal communities in the Northern Territory of Australia.
items.abstract: Introduction Access to comprehensive primary health care in very remote Aboriginal communities in the Northern Territory (NT) of Australia is limited by local primary healthcare workforce shortages. Digital health technologies (DHTs) have the potential to improve access, but user co-design of the technology is a critical success factor for uptake, effectiveness, and sustainability. This study aimed to elicit the relative preferences of a very remote Aboriginal community and their primary healthcare providers (clinicians and health service managers) for DHT attributes on a common scale. Methods Twenty-four attributes of DHTs were identified through qualitative research with a very remote, almost exclusively Aboriginal, community to improve access to comprehensive primary health care. A D-efficient incomplete block design was used to arrange the attributes in a best-worst scaling survey for preference elicitation. The survey was administered in-person from January to June 2024 by Aboriginal community-based researchers to a target sample of 20% of the community's Aboriginal population, stratified by age and gender. Primary healthcare providers working in the NT were invited through professional networks from November 2024 to September 2025 to complete the same survey online. Results were analysed using multinomial logit models by stakeholder group: Aboriginal community members and primary healthcare providers. Results Representative samples comprising 46 Aboriginal community members (24% of the community's adult population) and 50 NT primary healthcare providers (80% clinicians and 20% health service managers) completed the survey. Results showed a substantial divergence between Aboriginal community members' and healthcare providers' preference scores for DHT attributes; 12/24 (50%) attributes differed significantly between the groups. However, both groups had high preference scores for 'a support person available to interpret so patients can understand, communicate, and participate in discussions with [the] health professional', 'respect[ing] the patient's culture and community', and 'minimis[ing] travel away from community'. The Aboriginal community members' preferences for DHTs to reduce wait times for a specialist appointment, reduce wait times on the day of any healthcare appointment, and functionality to involve a family member/carer in discussions with health professionals when needed, were considered less important by healthcare providers. Instead, primary healthcare providers preferred that DHTs be used to provide information to help patients clearly understand and manage their own and their family's health. Conclusion When designing comprehensive primary healthcare models that use DHTs to optimise service delivery in remote NT Aboriginal communities, it is of utmost importance for Aboriginal community members and healthcare providers that the service delivery models provide support persons to help patients understand, communicate and participate fully in healthcare discussions, demonstrate respect for the patients' culture and community, and minimise travel away from community. Investment in DHTs for remote NT Aboriginal communities should prioritise solutions that reduce the time to obtain a specialist appointment and wait times on the day of any healthcare appointment. Given the notable differences between the preferences of Aboriginal community members and primary healthcare providers, it is important that all stakeholders are involved in design through implementation, monitoring and evaluation to ensure effective and sustainable digital health initiatives.

items.title: [Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism and the evolution of its clinical characteristics in China].
items.abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common clinical endocrine and metabolic disorder. Its clinical phenotype spectrum is undergoing a profound shift, evolving from the classic, severe presentations characterized by bone and kidney involvement towards more occult and subclinical forms. With the increasing adoption of routine biochemical screening and advancements in diagnostic technologies, there has been a notable rise in subclinical phenotypes of PHPT in China, particularly asymptomatic PHPT and normocalcemic PHPT. This trend not only reflects the progress of Chinese public health system but also imposes higher demands for precision in clinical diagnosis and treatment. Meanwhile, preoperative localization techniques have evolved from traditional ultrasound and radionuclide scanning to the era of four-dimensional CT and choline positron emission tomography, laying a solid foundation for the widespread adoption of minimally invasive parathyroidectomy. However, the clinical management of PHPT in China still faces significant challenges, including insufficient awareness among primary care physicians, imbalanced accessibility to advanced imaging equipment, and the complexity of managing multi-gland disease. This review systematically examines relevant literature published both domestically and internationally in recent years. It aims to outline the theoretical evolution, technological advancements, and disease characteristics specific to the Chinese population, with the goal of providing a reference for the standardized diagnosis and treatment of PHPT in China.

items.title: 2,611 Liver Transplants: Indications and Survival Rates of a High-Volume Latin American Center.
items.abstract: Introduction and objectives The liver transplantation program at the Centro de Transplante de Fígado do Ceará (CTFC), one of the largest centers in Northern and Northeastern Brazil, was evaluated over a 23-year period to describe indications, recipient characteristics, and survival outcomes. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort included 2611 liver transplants performed in 2491 patients between 2002 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and laboratory data were collected from medical records and managed using REDCap. Survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results Most recipients were middle-aged men, predominantly from outside the state, and nearly all procedures were funded by the public health system. The main indications for transplantation were decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and alcohol-related liver disease, reflecting global epidemiological shifts. Overall survival rates were 88% at one month, 79% at one year, and 71% at 5 years, with progressive improvement over time. Donor characteristics and ischemia times were consistent with international standards. Conclusions These results show that a high-volume public transplant center can achieve outcomes comparable to major international programs while serving a socioeconomically diverse population.

items.title: Epicardial adipose tissue volumes improve prediction of myocardial infarction in women on top of SCORE2, CACS and plaque burden: Long-term follow-up of 25,000 individuals.
items.abstract: Increased epicardial adipose tissue volume (EATV) is a risk marker for future myocardial infarction (MI), but its value beyond SCORE2 (Systemic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2), the coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and the coronary artery segment involvement score (SIS) remains poorly studied. To determine the incremental value of EATV normalized to heart volume (EATVh) on top of SCORE2, CACS and SIS in predicting future MI. We studied associations between EATVh, SCORE2, CACS, SIS and the risk of MI in a general population cohort of 25,155 participants (age 50-64, 50.7% women). Sex-stratified multivariable Cox-regression estimated hazard ratios (HR) and ROC-analysis with variables dichotomized at their 75th percentile assessed incremental predictive value. A total of 304 MI (71 in women) occurred during follow-up (median: 7.8 years). In adjusted analysis, EATVh and SCORE2 were independently associated with MI in women, but only SIS and SCORE2 in men. The highest HR per EATVh IQR was found in women <55 years (1.89). ROC-analysis showed that adding EATVh to SCORE2, CACS and SIS improved MI prediction in women but not men (AUC: 0.681 vs. 0.667; p < 0.05 for both). EATVh provides independent, modest incremental information on the risk of future MI in women on top of CACS and SIS, but not in men. Further studies in more diverse population segments including younger and symptomatic individuals are warranted.

items.title: [Development of an ICT utilization checklist for community-workplace collaboration promotion programs in local government: Consensus through a two-round Delphi study].
items.abstract: Objective To develop a checklist for utilizing information and communication technology (ICT) in community-workplace collaboration programs implemented by local government, based on a consensus among municipal personnel responsible for these programs in organizations utilizing multiple ICT tools.Methods Using data from a questionnaire and interview surveys conducted in 2022-2023, a checklist comprising seven domains was drafted: online meetings (eight items), e-mail newsletters (seven items), websites (eight items), live online seminars (eight items), on-demand online seminars (eight items), health-related applications (nine items), and common foundational items across ICT utilization (eight items). The expert panel was selected from a nationwide survey conducted in June 2024 among prefectures and public health centers with community-workplace collaboration councils. Personnel responsible for community-workplace collaboration programs were invited from 54 organizations in which five or more ICT tools were utilized. A two-round Delphi study was conducted using an initial checklist based on the findings of the questionnaire and interview surveys. Participants rated the importance of items on a five-point scale, reported their implementation status, and provided open-ended comments. Consensus was defined as an agreement rate ≥70%, a median importance score ≥4, and an interquartile range ＜1.5.Results Responses were obtained from 39 of 54 organizations (72.2%) in the first round, and 35 of 39 (89.7%) in the second round. The items were revised after the first round. In the second round, 55 items had an agreement rate ≥70%, and 53 items had an agreement rate ≥80%. The final checklist comprised 55 items across the seven domains: online meetings (eight items), e-mail newsletters (seven items), websites (eight items), live online seminars (eight items), on-demand online seminars (seven items), health-related applications (nine items), and common foundational items across ICT utilization (eight items).Conclusion Using the Delphi method, a checklist was developed that encompasses the preparation, organizational and operational systems, implementation strategies, and evaluation components necessary for ICT utilization in community-workplace collaboration programs. Organizations can assess their Internet infrastructure and organizational readiness using the common foundational items before selectively applying the domain-specific checklists based on the ICT tools being implemented. The checklist may also assist organizations that are already using ICT, to periodically evaluate its effectiveness. Despite achieving consensus for all checklist items, several items related to budget, operational systems and evaluation had low implementation rates, indicating a necessity for strategies to enhance effective ICT utilization.

items.title: [A survey on the required roles of dietitians in providing nutritional and dietary support during natural disasters].
items.abstract: Objectives When large-scale natural disasters occur, the Japan Dietetic Association-Disaster Assistance Team (JDA-DAT) dispatches dietitians to disaster-affected areas, where they collaborate with the affected local governments to provide nutrition and dietary support. Recognizing local government needs may result in more effective support. Therefore, this study aimed to identify the types of tasks that local government officials expect from JDA-DAT as aid providers. The findings of this study will contribute to the development of a more comprehensive disaster support system.Methods A nationwide survey was conducted targeting officials in the nutrition-related and disaster management departments of local governments nationwide. The survey investigated the priority of tasks expected of the JDA-DAT in disaster-affected areas and the types of tasks the recipients would like the JDA-DAT to undertake outside the disaster area (backup support). The priorities of tasks expected of the JDA-DAT in disaster-affected areas were classified as follows: ratings of 4 and 5 were considered high priority, 3 as medium priority, and 1 and 2 as low priority.Results The tasks in disaster-affected areas expected of the JDA-DAT, ranked in order of highest priority, were as follows: "tailored nutritional counseling for individuals necessitating special consideration who require nutrition and dietary support", "identification of residents requiring nutrition and dietary support (nutritional assessment) at evacuation shelters", "assessment of meal conditions at evacuation shelters and proposals for provided meals based on nutrient adequacy or deficiency (e.g., menu planning)", "management of stockpiled food and relief supplies (special dietary products): sorting special dietary products from general food items", and "support for coordination of provided meals (soup kitchens and boxed meal distribution): hygiene guidance". The items with high priority were similar in prefectural government offices and ordinance-designated cities/special wards, whereas some items were assigned high priority in municipalities (cities, towns, and villages).Conclusions The local government officials anticipate a wide range of support activities from the JDA-DAT. In particular, identifying individuals requiring special consideration and providing individualized support have received high priority. Furthermore, our findings suggest that the priority of requested support varies according to the type of municipality, underscoring the significance of supporters in understanding the roles of different local governments when engaging in disaster support activities.

items.title: [Development of the effort scale for academic advancement (ESAA): Examining its association with well-being].
items.abstract: Objective Effort is defined as engagement in goal-directed activities and may contribute to well-being (WB). However, only a few studies have directly examined this association. This study aimed to develop the effort scale for academic advancement (ESAA), a multidimensional scale for assessing effort in studying for university entrance examinations, and to examine its reliability and validity (Study 1). Moreover, we examined the association between effort related to academic advancement and WB (Study 2).Method In Study 1, we developed the initial ESAA items based on a three-dimensional effort framework comprising intensity, persistence, and direction. We conducted a web-based survey of individuals aged 18-34 years who had undergone university entrance examinations and assessed their efforts. We used an exploratory factor analysis to examine the factor structure of the ESAA, and we assessed its internal consistency using Cronbach's alpha coefficient. Furthermore, we examined criterion-related validity by testing the correlations between each subscale score and the external criteria. Moreover, we examined the associations between the ESAA scores and background variables, including age, sex, and first-choice admission status. In Study 2, we conducted a follow-up survey of participants from Study 1. We assessed factorial validity using confirmatory factor analysis and examined test-retest reliability using correlations between corresponding subscale scores across the two surveys. We finally examined the associations between effort and life satisfaction, an indicator of WB, using multiple regression analyses while controlling for covariates.Results In Study 1, we included 534 participants, and exploratory factor analysis yielded a three-factor structure. Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranged from 0.92 to 0.93, supporting internal consistency. Each subscale score significantly correlated with the external criteria, and associations with background variables differed across the subscales. We included 295 participants in Study 2. Confirmatory factor analysis showed an acceptable model fit. Correlations between the corresponding subscale scores ranged from 0.77 to 0.81, indicating sufficient test-retest reliability. In multiple regression analyses, each subscale score was positively associated with life satisfaction when entered individually. However, only intensity remained positively associated when all the subscale scores were entered simultaneously.Conclusion These findings indicate that the ESAA has acceptable reliability and validity for assessing efforts related to academic advancement. Moreover, effort intensity was associated with WB even after controlling for goal attainment, that is, whether participants were admitted to their first-choice university. Future studies should extend these findings to other contexts.

items.title: [Comparing long-term care risks and health care expenditures for older adults in Kashiwanoha campus and other areas of Kashiwa City].
items.abstract: Objectives Japan's "Healthy Japan 21 (Third Phase)" highlights the need for environments that naturally support health, yet, few studies have assessed health outcomes in community-dwelling older adults based on the area of residence. This study compared long-term care (LTC) risk scores and projected medical and LTC costs for older adults who lived in the Kashiwanoha Campus area, a district developed under the concept of a healthy, secure, and publicly-privately-academically managed community, and older adults who lived in other parts of Kashiwa City.Methods We analyzed data of the 2022 Health and Lifestyle Survey in Kashiwa City, part of the Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study, including 5,895 community-dwelling adults aged ≥65 years who were certified to not need support or LTC. Differences in LTC risk scores between Kashiwanoha and other areas were assessed using multivariable linear regression accounting for school district clusters. Based on prior studies, we estimated three-year cumulative medical and LTC costs and six-year cumulative LTC costs. Sensitivity analyses included income-stratified analyses, propensity score matching, a nine-year longitudinal analysis of changes in LTC risk scores, and item-level analyses using risk ratios for each of the 10 LTC risk score components.Results Living in the Kashiwanoha area was associated with 0.32 points lower LTC risk scores than in other areas (95% CI: －0.45 to －0.19). Sensitivity analyses showed differences of 0.25 to 0.81 points across income strata, consistently lower point estimates in propensity score matching, and a 0.58-point difference in the nine-year longitudinal analysis, although the latter two were not statistically significant. Among the 10 LTC risk items, "walking continuously for 15 minutes" was more common among Kashiwanoha residents. Based on the main analysis and the nine-year longitudinal analysis, the three-year cumulative medical and LTC costs in the Kashiwanoha area were estimated to be ¥18,208 to ¥33,002 lower per person, and the six-year cumulative LTC costs were estimated to be ¥10,112 to ¥18,328 lower per person.Conclusions In the main and some sensitivity analyses, older adults in Kashiwanoha had significantly lower LTC risk than those in other areas. The projected three-year reduction in medical and LTC costs was ¥18.208 to ¥33.002 million per 1,000 persons. Multifaceted urban development in Kashiwanoha may have contributed to residents health promotion. Further studies are warranted to clarify the environmental factors that contribute to the health and functioning of residents.

items.title: [A descriptive study on concerns, stress, and help-seeking among fathers of preschool-age children: Analysis of the 2022 Comprehensive Survey of Living Condition data].
items.abstract: Objectives We sought to identify the reasons for concerns and stress, and help-seeking behaviors among fathers of preschool-aged children, and to provide data for developing support systems targeting fathers.Methods This cross-sectional study used health and household survey data from the 2022 Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions. Participants were divided into two groups (those with and without concerns or stress), and their background characteristics, including fathers' age and educational attainment, were compared. Residual analyses were performed for statistically significant variables. Subsequently, we presented the distribution of causes of these concerns or stress. Finally, binary logistic regression analysis was performed between the outcome of help-seeking behavior and background characteristics, and we calculated odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (Cis), with "not seeking help" coded as 1 and "seeking help" coded as 0.Results Forty-seven percent of fathers reported concerns or stress; 26% of them did not seek counseling, and 16% scored ≥10 points on the K6 scale. Main reasons for concerns and stress among fathers were: "own work" (52%), "income, family finances, debts, etc." (18%), and "childcare" (6%). Regarding help-seeking behaviors, older fathers, fathers having mood or anxiety disorders (OR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.24-1.75), and fathers working ≥11 hours per day were more likely not to seek help than those working 8 hours per day (OR 1.24, 95% CI: 1.02-1.51). Conclusion Approximately half of fathers reported concern or stress due to "own work," "income, household finances, debt, etc.," and "childcare." Supporting fathers extends beyond childcare support, but requires a support system to improve their workplace environments, consciously encouraging supporters to create an atmosphere conducive to consultation, and checking fathers' concerns and stress levels, including the necessity of mental health screening. Further studies on concrete approaches to support fathers should be conducted, and support providers should be trained accordingly.

items.title: Attitude and acceptability of IVF add-ons to improve reproductive outcomes: a focus group qualitative study.
items.abstract: Study question What factors are important for patients when evaluating the efficacy, safety, cost, and acceptability of IVF add-ons? Summary answer Although efficacy is the most important factor for patients, interim markers of success can also be important. What is known already IVF add-ons are increasingly offered alongside assisted conception despite limited evidence of their efficacy, safety, or value for money. Capturing patient perspectives on their acceptability and outcome priorities is essential to guide ethical clinical practice and inform future research. Study design, size, duration Three online focus groups were conducted with 12 people who had used assisted reproductive technologies and were not currently in treatment. The focus groups were conducted in small groups of three to five people with each focus group lasting ∼2 h. Participants/materials, setting, methods Participants were recruited through fertility charities and patient advocacy groups. All 12 participants were women and lived in the UK. All were currently in a relationship, and most had prior experience of using IVF add-ons. Online focus groups were conducted to discuss views on the efficacy, safety, and acceptability of IVF add-ons, and to identify preferred outcomes. Main results and the role of chance Nearly all participants defined the most important outcome of using an add-on to be achieving a live birth. However, they recognized that a live birth could feel a distant endpoint within the IVF treatment and therefore valued interim milestones as indicators of success. The main theme found in relation to understanding the risks involved was the need for patients to balance risk with desperation to have a baby. In terms of cost, two themes emerged, the need to balance cost with needing money for future treatments and the differing views on what is an acceptable cost. When receiving information about add-ons, participants reflected on the importance of finding reputable sources while also having to navigate conflicting information. Overall, the effectiveness of an add-on was valued over cost and safety, although cost and the risk of regret remained important considerations in decision-making. Most participants would not regret using add-ons, although some said they may regret not having used them. Limitations, reasons for caution All participants were women, and most were White. Findings may not be applicable to other populations. Wider implications of the findings Capturing participants' views on efficacy, safety, cost, and acceptability is essential not only to guide future research priorities but also to inform ethical clinical practice and policy. By incorporating patient perspectives, future trials can ensure that outcomes reflect what matters most to those undergoing treatment, thereby improving the relevance and impact of research in reproductive medicine. Funding AFFINITY is funded by a public research grant from the National Institute for Health and Care Research's (NIHR) Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation (EME) programme-Award ID NIHR168789. Disclosures The authors have no conflict of interest to declare. Trial registration number N/A.

items.title: Observed Service Utilization Differences and Audiometric Profiles Among Adults With Hearing Loss in Eastern Coastal Provinces in China.
items.abstract: Background and objectives : Hearing loss is a major public health concern that hampers communication, social participation, and quality of life. To date, large-scale demographic and audiometric characteristic data for adults seeking hearing care services in China are limited. We aimed to assemble demographic and audiometric profiles for adults requesting hearing care services for the first time in selected eastern coastal provinces of China, with a focus on service- and region-specific patterns in observed service utilization. Subjects and methods : This multicenter retrospective study included 2,413 adult first-time patients who initially sought hearing care services between January and June 2025, including 2,242 patients who visited public hospitals and 171 patients who visited private hearing aid clinics. Demographic and audiometric data were extracted from institutional databases. Hearing loss severity was assessed using better-ear four-frequency average hearing loss scores. Differences between groups were analyzed using analysis of variance and chi-square tests. Multiple linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with hearing loss severity. Results : Mean patient age was 55.65 years (51.1% were male). Patients attending private hearing aid clinics were significantly older than those visiting public hospitals and had more severe hearing loss. Sensorineural hearing loss was the most common (56.8%), followed by normal hearing (29.1%), mixed hearing loss (12.4%), and conductive hearing loss (1.7%). Regional differences in sex distribution and hearing loss profiles were observed. Conclusions : This multicenter retrospective study describes observed service utilization and service-specific audiometric profile differences among adults presenting at selected hearing care institutions in Chinese eastern coastal provinces. Patients attending participating private hearing aid clinics operated by one provider were generally older and had more severe hearing loss, whereas public hospitals received a broader and more heterogeneous patient population. These findings should be interpreted descriptively and may help encourage earlier hearing screening, referral coordination, and integration of diagnostic and rehabilitation-oriented hearing care services.

items.title: Population Genetic Screening of Hemoglobinopathy Carrier Prevalence Compared to Medical Records.
items.abstract: Objective To better understand the gap between hemoglobinopathy (HBP) prevalence and that which is documented in electronic medical records (EMRs) to quantify genetic HBP carrier prevalence compared to case counts documented in the EMR. Patients and methods We used genetic data from the Tapestry study to quantify the prevalence of HBPs and carrier traits, targeting sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia. Genetic findings were compared with International Classification of Diseases, 10 th Revision (ICD-10) codes for hemoglobinopathies (D56 for β-thalassemia and D57 for SCD). Results A total of 50,008 participants were included in the genetic analysis. Twelve participants with diagnosis codes for α-thalassemia and sickle cell disease were previously confirmed with genetic results leaving 49,996 individuals. Of those, 116 participants' (0.23%) genetic testing demonstrated heterozygosity for sickle cell trait, and a majority self-reported Black ancestry (75%). Most (n=97 of 116) did not carry a sickle cell ICD-10 diagnosis code. There were 98 (0.20%) participant carriers for β-thalassemia with White ancestry most common (80.6%), followed by Asian ancestry (15.3%). Only 47 (48.0%) had a β-thalassemia ICD-10 diagnosis code. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that sickle cell and β-thalassemia carrier traits are prevalent at clinically significant levels and are substantially under-represented in EMRs. This gap raises important public health concerns, as under-identification may lead to missed opportunities for early diagnosis, reproductive counseling, and preventive care. These results highlight the need for enhanced public health efforts and primary care engagement to improve detection and equitable management of hemoglobinopathies.

items.title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film
items.abstract: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. These small, detailed edits are slow and tedious to make in standard editing tools because users have to map high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame adjustments. At the same time, these fine-scale adjustments, which we call micro-edits, can be nuanced and expressive, with different choices serving different creative goals. In this work, we start by conducting a formative study with professional editors to understand the structure of micro-edits and how they are used. We then derive a mathematical formalization for this structure to develop tools that leverage AI and optimization to make exploring micro-edits simpler and more efficient for users. Finally, we validate our tools in multiple user studies and a wide range of video examples.

items.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
items.abstract: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. Perturbing a single decoder block already recovers much of the improvement, while keeping the model entirely frozen and adding a random bias to its output logits matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on most reasoning tasks. This suggests an alternative explanation based on output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting. We formalize this view as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), a general procedure that generates perturbed predictors, selects high-performing members on a small validation set, and aggregates their predictions. This interpretation connects Neural Thickets to established inference-time methods, including sampling, self-consistency, and verifier-guided selection. A first-order analysis further shows that small weight perturbations act primarily through their induced logit shifts. We extend this analysis to vision, where logit PSV substantially improves performance under domain shift, including on Earth observation, while full-weight perturbations provide little additional benefit. Together, these results suggest that the gains attributed to nearby weight-space experts can instead be obtained through output diversity, selection, and voting. Logit PSV realizes these benefits with a fully frozen model, providing a simple, training-free alternative to full-weight perturbation ensembles across language and vision.

items.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
items.abstract: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. We observe that finer detail does not necessarily require more global communication: low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange, while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally. Based on this insight, we introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples output detail from the length of the global attention sequence. SpecSlot expands each spatial anchor into multiple slots, each assigned a disjoint band of DCT coefficients; this separates anchor density from spectral subdivision. Only the lowest-frequency slot from each anchor participates in global attention, while all slots interact locally. This allows the model to increase spectral detail without enlarging the global sequence. A spatial head further adds a local correction to the spectral prediction, while the generative state, target, and loss remain in pixel space. On ImageNet-256, SpecSlot achieves a comparable final FID to a FLOPs-matched JiT control while converging faster. On ImageNet-512, it improves FID by 2.84 over the control with 3.9% fewer FLOPs, and comes within only 0.69 FID of JiT-B/16 at 38.2% lower cost. On text-to-image generation, SpecSlot surpasses JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench by 1.06 at 40.6% lower forward cost.
