items.title: Seven Years of TESS Precovery Observations of the Dwarf-planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
items.abstract: The trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED$_{138}$ was announced in 2026 October as the first dwarf-planet candidate in our solar system discovered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observed it in five month-long sectors between 2019 and 2026, four of them before its discovery. We subtract every Gaia DR3 star from these crowded full-frame images with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve (TGLC) package, then remove static residuals with a running median. Stacking the images along its predicted path detects 2026 ED$_{138}$ in all five sectors at 5-21$σ$, and at 34$σ$ combined. The TESS positions alone confirm the JPL orbit, and its brightness is consistent with the 0.08 mag fading expected from its increasing distance and changing phase angle.

items.title: The coupled spread of information and potential-driven motion in evacuating agent populations
items.abstract: Whether a population evacuates safely depends on two coupled processes: how a warning spreads through it, and how that information moves people. We model this coupling with an agent-based framework, in which each agent's information state--susceptible, exposed, informed or reverted--gates its motion. Only informed agents respond to a global background potential encoding hazards and safe zones, while all agents interact locally through a Lennard-Jones potential. The total potential experienced by an agent drives an Ito stochastic differential equation. Tests show that landscapes with potential minima leave far fewer agents never exposed than in a flat, uniform potential control landscape, as informed agents driven toward the minima sweep past susceptible neighbors. In our tests, conduit routes raise the fraction of agents in the safe-zone minima, but leave greater numbers of agents never exposed, when compared to an unguided evacuation. This is attributed to conduits shortening trips at the cost of informed agents having fewer encounters with susceptible neighbors who could receive their information. Independently, the effective information transmission rate estimated from these encounters falls roughly sixty-fold below its well-mixed value within the first time unit, because state transitions create spatial mechanisms of net transmission suppression that mean-field closure does not capture.

items.title: Structural Change in the Multilayer World Trade Web: An Economic Dominance Theory Approach
items.abstract: Most studies of the World Trade Web (WTW) describe its topology: degrees, strengths, centralities, communities, or the similarity between product networks and years. This paper presents Economic Dominance Theory (EDT), initiated by Lantner (1974), and positions it as an alternative theory of structural dependence in directed flow networks rather than an additional toolbox. EDT normalizes bilateral flows into a Ghosh matrix of directed propagation and measures circular interdependence through its determinant, which aggregates the feedback circuits by which influence returns to its origin. Through the log-determinant and its trace expansion, a single quantity decomposes exactly by feedback length, arc and node deletion, product layer, network partition and, in the dynamic extension developed here, time. Structural change can therefore be measured without defining a distance between graphs, and layers and regions become exact components of one object rather than separate descriptions. EDT differs from centrality and community detection, which describe positions and densities rather than feedback closure; from economic complexity, which addresses capabilities rather than dependence; and from input-output and value-chain analysis, whose algebra it shares but which locate positions along chains where EDT measures their closure. An application to CEPII BACI data (1995-2023, 96 HS2 layers) shows what this adds. Circular interdependence did not deepen with trade: the diffusion determinant, which rises when feedback weakens, goes from 0.12 in 1995 to 0.21 in 2006, falls to 0.16 in 2013 and reaches 0.19 in 2023. This net weakening comes from cross-product feedback, which carries more than 90% of order-two and about 99% of order-three feedback. Geography depends on feedback length: short reciprocal loops remain regional, while long feedback is overwhelmingly transregional.

items.title: From Airspace Degradation to Deconfliction: Predicting Safety-Critical Traffic States through the Evolution of Multiscale Complexity Metrics
items.abstract: Growing air traffic demand is pushing airspace management towards the limits of its operational capacity, with steadily increasing workload for air traffic control officers, with direct consequences for safety. Understanding which traffic conditions give rise to safety-critical situations is therefore an essential open problem. Here we compare a large number of deconfliction events with equivalent conflict-free scenarios, extracted from thirteen weeks of air traffic control data over the Swedish Flight Information Region. We describe the traffic structure before each event through thirty sector-complexity metrics computed at multiple spatial and temporal scales, and use them as inputs of Machine Learning models. We find that the need of deconflictions can be predicted with an accuracy reaching $70\%$, but only when the traffic is described at the sector spatial scale. Predictability increases monotonically in the minutes preceding the clearance, showing that situations requiring deconflicting actions are not sudden occurrences, but rather the endpoint of a progressive degradation process. Additionally, the information needed for such prediction mainly resides in specific characteristics of the overall traffic structure, and not only in the conflicting pair. These results numerically demonstrate that safety-critical airspace states can be anticipated from the collective behaviour of the traffic, paving the way for early-warning systems that flag degraded, safety-relevant conditions before an intervention is required.

items.title: Optical clock network tracks tidal variations of the gravity potential
items.abstract: Gravity affects the passage of time, as described by General Relativity. On Earth, the rate of a clock as seen by a fixed observer changes by about one part in $10^{16}$ per metre in height. Chronometric levelling exploits this effect to directly measure differences in gravity potential by comparing distant clocks. It has been proposed as a complementary approach to established geodetic techniques for linking height reference systems and monitoring the terrestrial gravity potential. Experimental demonstrations have to date focused primarily on static potential differences. Yet, the potentials of the Moon, the Sun and other celestial bodies as well as the Earth's response to their tidal forcing change clock rates by several $10^{-17}$, providing a predictable test signal to demonstrate optical clock networks resolving small variations in relativistic time dilation. Here, we report chronometric observations of time-varying gravity potential differences using a network of optical clocks and phase-stabilized fibre links in Europe. Two distinct geographical configurations, with baselines of about 800 km each, result in different combinations of diurnal and semidiurnal tidal components. One comparison uses a transportable optical clock as a remote sensor. The measured rate shifts track the tidal variations, resolving the predicted signal within 1 d of measurement and agreeing with model predictions. These results extend experimental chronometric levelling from static to dynamic potential differences and highlight the need to account for the time dependence of relativistic time dilation in frequency metrology. They also open the prospect for quantum clock networks with improved stability and availability to move beyond known tides and monitor other gravity potential variations, such as those arising from surface deformation and mass redistribution in geologically or volcanically active regions.

items.title: Early-Buyer Groups and Fast-Wallet Teams on a Bonding-Curve Launchpad: A Prospective Measurement Study of pump.fun on Solana
items.abstract: We study coordinated groups of wallets on a bonding-curve launchpad (pump.fun on Solana), using a complete record of 200\,443 token launches, 15\,854\,121 curve trades and 51\,025\,958 SOL transfers over 88.3 hours. A prospective, multi-channel discovery procedure (co-buying, shared funding, joint signing, transfers, consolidation) yields 23\,710 wallet groups. Without ground-truth labels we validate them by out-of-sample link prediction, independent non-trading links and a comparison with naive co-buy clustering at equal numbers of flagged tokens: raw clustering collapses into one giant component, yet it ranks tokens at least as well as the groups, so the value of the structure is descriptive. Group activity is highly concentrated and splits into serial creators and long-lived rings of early buyers. Known members buy earlier than other buyers of the same token and extract more cash than an activity-matched placebo set, while late buyers' net cash flow is negative; tokens with members show a pump-like price path, but the contrast vanishes when controls are restricted to comparable tokens, so we report it as an association. A follower entering at the earliest group signal loses money out of sample in all 32 configurations and does no better than random entry. A few pools of tens to over a hundred fast wallets are associated with a two- to four-fold higher chance of reaching 20 SOL, also within creators, with a smaller excess at 60 SOL and none for graduation; on a final hold-out the team rules keep a precision of about one half to three quarters, yet many signals arrive when the curve already holds 20 SOL, one team supplies most of them, and they add no information beyond early curve state. We also document evaluation errors that turn the same data into apparent profit.

items.title: Magma Buoyancy Couples Lunar Mantle Convection and Magmatism: Long-Lasting Mare Volcanism and Radius Change in a 3-D Regional Model
items.abstract: To understand the mantle evolution that has caused the observed histories of mare volcanism and radius change of the Moon, we developed a 3-D regional spherical shell mantle convection model with magmatism. Magma generated by decompression melting segregates from the convecting matrix and percolates upward through it. In our model, internal heating forms a basal partially molten layer during the first several hundred million years. Finger-like magma ascents then grow from the top of this layer and evolve into buoyant, partially molten plumes. The plumes ascend by the buoyancy of magma, while decompression melting in the ascending plumes generates more magma that further drives the ascent. Magma supply to the top of the mantle peaks between 4 and 3.5 Gyr ago, coincident with a maximum in radial expansion driven by volume change of the mantle associated with melting, and both decline as the mantle cools and solidifies. Magma supply, however, persists for billions of years because earlier plumes leave thermally softened conduits, through which later plumes repeatedly rise at fixed locations. These stable conduits are a consequence of the 3-D geometry. Recycling of magmatic products formed in the uppermost mantle also triggers renewed magma ascent through the conduits. Our results provide a mechanism for the observed long-lasting localized volcanism that peaked at 4-3.5 Gyr ago and quantitatively account for early expansion followed by contraction. The conditions required for consistency with the observed history imply an initially hot but mostly solid mantle with a dense basal layer.

items.title: Update on the Orbital Motion of Encke's Periodic Comet: Nongravitational Deceleration Gradually Gaining
items.abstract: The end of an era in cometary astronomy --- as the transition from a nongravitational acceleration to a deceleration in the motion of Encke's comet was advertised in a paper of mine five years ago --- has now turned into a new era, as recent computations of the comet's nongravitational orbits performed independently by S. Nakano (CBAT) and by D. Farnocchia (JPL) appear to suggest. The new values of parameter A_2, compatible both with each other and with the earlier values in my previous paper, show that the magnitude of the deceleration has continued to grow. Critically assessed are the controversial computations at the Minor Planet Center, which contradict the above results and imply that Encke's comet was reverting to the acceleration. A plot of the number of observations used in the orbital solutions as a function of time shows an exponential rise following the introduction of CCD arrays, but not after use of photography became common five or six decades earlier. Dips in observer activity appear during the two World Wars. Because the comet has recently been observed along the entire orbit, the effective times that computed values of the nongravitational parameters apply to had to be redefined.

items.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
items.abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and Rényi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.

items.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
items.abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

items.title: Beyond individual features: Identifying computational principles in perceiving visual beauty
items.abstract: Prior research in empirical aesthetics has related beauty to visual features like curvature, color, or shape. Although these feature-based accounts have identified reliable visual correlates of beauty, the literature on feature preferences is highly fragmented, with individual features studied for individual stimulus domains. Here, we argue that making further progress hinges on complementing feature-based approaches with approaches aimed at distilling computational principles that underlie the perception of beauty. Recent advances in computational neuroscience can drive this new line of research by linking visual beauty to the coding of visual information in artificial neural networks and the biological brain. We highlight two examples of how this approach has identified overarching computational principles. First, metabolic processing costs, both in artificial and biological vision, are inversely related to perceived beauty, suggesting that beauty may reflect energy-efficient, fluent visual coding. Second, integrative processing in artificial and biological vision captures the efficient spatial representation of image elements across space and predicts beauty ratings. Synthesizing these findings, we derive a neuro-computational framework for assessing computational principles in the perception of beauty, which uses artificial neural networks for exploration at scale and then validates candidate principles using human behavior and brain data. We discuss candidate principles that could be explored using this approach, like spatiotemporal predictability, and delineate how the new insights could be reconciled with feature-based approaches. In conclusion, complementing feature-based studies with studies targeting computational principles promises a comprehensive and mechanistic understanding of why certain visual stimuli are perceived as beautiful, and others are not.

items.title: Tactile alert placement in driving contexts based on neurocognitive evidence and eight consensus based design guidelines
items.abstract: Abstract Tactile alerts can communicate spatial and temporal information in automo-tive human–machine interfaces while reducing reliance on visual and auditory channels. Evidence on appropriate body locations for such alerts remains dis-tributed across automotive human-machine interface (HMI), haptic-interface, and somatosensory research. This study examines how body location may influ-ence the perception and processing of tactile alerts in driving contexts. It adopts a sequential evidence-to-consensus design comprising a scoping review of automo-tive HMI studies, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR; an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on tactile perception and processing; and a modified Delphi study with six specialists from automotive industry, design, and neuroscience. The scoping review identified fifteen eligible studies, while the umbrella review synthesized evidence from six eligible reviews. The integrated evidence indicates that body regions differ in tactile acuity and sensitivity and that spatial congruence between stimulation location and event direction may support alert interpretation and response. Ten preliminary design guidelines were formulated and subsequently evaluated and refined through expert consensus, resulting in eight consensus-supported guidelines.

items.title: Anti-Neuronal Antibodies in Patients with Sjögren's Syndrome and Acute Cerebellar Ataxia: Two Case Reports.
items.abstract: We herein report two patients presenting with acute cerebellar ataxia shortly after the diagnosis of Sjögren's syndrome (SS). Two women (43- and 55-year-old) patients showed normal MRI, inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, and moderate response to immunotherapy in long-term follow-up. A broad panel of antibodies was negative for the 43-year-old patient. However, indirect immunohistochemistry showed serum/CSF antibodies with a distinctive reactivity pattern on rat brain sections. The 55-year-old patient showed anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase in serum and CSF. Five control SS patients without neurological symptoms did not have anti-neuronal antibodies. Anti-neuronal antibody investigation may contribute to the differential diagnosis of neurological involvement in SS.

items.title: A common marking method influences fish-parasite interactions
items.abstract: Being able to identify the same individual organism through time is essential to robustly address many outstanding questions in ecology and evolution. For organisms that can move, and that have no reliable identifying features, researchers must often use some form of artificial marking system. In fish, a commonly used system is Visible Implant Elastomer (VIE) marking. Previous studies indicate that this marking system does not alter the survival, growth, or behaviour of marked fish. Here, using 26 VIE-marked and 46 control guppies, Poecilia reticulata, I found that VIE marking indeed did not impact fish growth. However, one month after marking, VIE-marked fish experienced an estimated ~3.7-fold higher Gyrodactylus turnbulli parasite burden during experimental infections. Two months post-marking, G. turnbulli individuals transmitted faster to VIE-marked than unmarked fish, although at this timepoint their subsequent growth was not different on fish from different treatment groups. Despite its lack of impact on common metrics of fish health, therefore, VIE marking appears to have important, long-lasting impacts on fish-parasite interactions. These findings suggest caution with assuming that marking animals is biologically neutral: that assumption may fail when the response variable involves host-parasite interactions.

items.title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of sexually selected infanticide facilitate species coexistence
items.abstract: Understanding how biodiversity is maintained is a central question in community ecology. Modern coexistence theory predicts that stable coexistence occurs when stabilizing mechanisms are strong enough to overcome competitive ability differences. Recent studies suggest that adaptations to conspecific interactions may provide such a stabilizing mechanism when their demographic costs increase with conspecific density. We examined whether sexually selected male infanticide can promote species coexistence by generating density-dependent demographic costs. We developed a stage-structured eco-evolutionary model of two species competing for a shared resource, with infanticidal and non-infanticidal male strategies, and confirmed that the infanticidal strategy was maintained depending on the parameters related to intraspecific competition: the infanticide rate and its fecundity cost. In a competitively superior species, the infanticidal strategy, which imposed demographic costs that increase with conspecific density, was maintained at a sufficiently high frequency, thereby strengthening self-limitation and reducing the species' equilibrium density. This reduction increased the invasion growth rate of the inferior competitor and expanded the parameter region permitting stable coexistence. These results show that sexually selected infanticide favored at the individual level can generate population-level self-regulation and alter community-level coexistence.

items.title: Weeds are plants of human-modified environments, not plants out of place
items.abstract: The question “What makes a plant a weed?” has persisted in both the agricultural sciences and plant ecology and evolution for well over a hundred years. Various authors—agriculturists focused on crop yield, ecologists examining community assembly, and plant biologists interested in adaptation—have each defined the term weed. However, these definitions, developed from unique vantage points, have led to siloed studies and thus constraints on our understanding of weedy plant evolution. Here we briefly review how weeds have been defined historically and argue that weeds are best defined by the environment they occupy: plants that are found, uncultivated and reproducing, in human-modified environments. We then ask whether weeds are human commensals, populations that depend on human-provided resources and have diverged from non-commensal ancestors, treating human dependence as a gradient to be measured. We highlight critical gaps in our understanding of weedy plant occurrence across agricultural, suburban, and urban environments, and propose a database approach leading to testable hypotheses for studying weed presence and persistence. Important outcomes of our reframing include a bridge between agricultural and (sub)urban research disciplines and a shared, data-driven basis for comparing species across the human-modified environments they occupy, illuminating the forces that underlie the weedy lifestyle.

items.title: From living heritage to healing place: synergistic healing mechanisms of the water villages in Lingnan, China
items.abstract: Abstract Lingnan water villages in the Pearl River Delta, China, represent a unique form of living cultural and ecological heritage. Although their heritage and landscape values are widely recognized, less is known about how these everyday rural environments contribute to visitors' restorative experience and rural well-being. This study investigates the perceived restorative potential of Lingnan water village landscapes using the Perceived Restorativeness Scale (PRS), Attention Restoration Theory (ART), and structural equation modeling (SEM). Survey data were collected from 415 visitors across six representative villages. Results indicate that natural landscapes and traditional street-alley spaces form a dual foundation for restoration, while folk culture is particularly associated with psychological “Being Away” and fascination. The healing potential is not dominated by a single element but emerges from the synergy of ecology, spatial structure, and cultural practices. This study contributes to rural studies by reframing therapeutic landscapes as a mechanism of rural well-being, place-making, and differentiated revitalization in peri-urban heritage villages. It also offers practical implications for integrating ecological conservation, cultural continuity, and experience-oriented rural tourism.

items.title: Experimental evidence that dietary antioxidants induce an antiviral transcriptomic signature in a wild seabird.
items.abstract: Infectious disease emergence in natural systems is driven by complex host-pathogen-environment interactions. Nutritional factors, particularly dietary antioxidants, can modulate physiological states by enhancing immune function and mitigating oxidative damage, but the underlying molecular mechanisms in wildlife remain poorly understood. To bridge this gap, we conducted a transcriptomic analysis of blood samples from both healthy and clinically affected magnificent frigatebirds Fregata magnificens chicks treated with either resveratrol (a plant-derived polyphenol with known antiviral and antioxidant properties) or a placebo. Resveratrol supplementation induced significant gene expression changes, particularly in diseased individuals, where we identified the upregulation of ten key genes in treated sick chicks, including the interferon-stimulated genes (IFI6, OASL2) and immune regulators (SOCS1, PLAC8); two additional transcripts were unannotated. Furthermore, resveratrol treatment was associated with increased expression of DDX60, a potent antiviral factor, and CYGB1, which supports cytoprotection. In contrast, healthy chicks showed fewer differentially expressed genes, primarily associated with metabolism and cellular organization. Collectively, our results reveal a transcriptional signature consistent with dietary antioxidants such as resveratrol acting as active molecular modulators of host defense, rather than simple passive antioxidants, although direct evidence of enhanced antiviral protection (e.g. reduced viral load) remains to be established. This study highlights the utility of transcriptomic approaches to link nutritional ecology with disease dynamics, offering a framework for understanding how dietary quality shapes host defense strategies and population resilience under increasing pathogen pressure.

items.title: Mechanical and Psychological Domains of Thought are Analogically Asymmetrical
items.abstract: Psychology and physics are two core domains of human cognition. Little is known about their epistemic relation. Does our understanding of common physical-mechanical systems better inform our understanding of psychology, or vice versa? To answer this question, we compared analogies that explain one domain in terms of the other. In Study 1, we found the best analogies with a mechanical base explaining a psychological target were preferred to the best analogies in the opposite direction. In Study 2, we generated analogies from random pairings of mechanical and psychological systems and again found a preference for analogies with a mechanical base. In Study 3, participants overwhelmingly generated analogies with a mechanical (instead of psychological) base. And Study 4 showed that analogies with a mechanical base were also preferred to those with bases from other domains. These results suggest that the physical-mechanical domain may serve as a privileged launchpad for explanation.

items.title: Bayes Factors for Structural Equation Models with Blavaan and Bridge Sampling
items.abstract: Bayes factors offer a graded measure of statistical evidence that is increasingly popular in experimental psychology. In the field of structural equation modeling (SEM), however, computational and conceptual challenges have frustrated the broader adoption of Bayes factors. We present a practical Bayes factor workflow that uses bridge sampling to estimate marginal likelihoods for models specified in standard SEM syntax. The workflow starts from a unit-information (UI) prior derived from maximum-likelihood fits, providing a Bayesian analogue of the BIC. We then show how targeted prior variants for focal structural relations may alter and often sharpen the evidence, particularly when directional information is taken into account. A simulation study demonstrates that bridge-sampled UI Bayes factors closely track the BIC approximation and that correct directional prior information substantially increases support for the data-generating model. An empirical dataset is used to showcase two specific extensions, namely (a) robust mixture priors, and (b) Bayesian model averaging. The model averaging integrates across structurally different models and across different prior distributions for the model parameters. The proposed Bayes factor workflow is intended to make Bayesian model comparison in SEM feasible, transparent, and extensible.

items.title: Preliminary Psychometric Analysis of an Online Diagnostic Assessment of Statistical Reasoning for Psychology Students: A Cognitive Psychology Perspective
items.abstract: Digital tools make diagnostic tests easy to build, but convenience does not guarantee that scores reflect the intended thinking processes. This study examined item quality and reliability of Draft 1 of the Statistical Reasoning Diagnostic Assessment for Psychology Students (SRDA-PSY), an online two-tier diagnostic test covering six domains of statistical reasoning, interpreting the results through cognitive psychology principles. Forty-one psychology students took the test via Google Forms. Classical test theory analyses (difficulty, discrimination, distractor effectiveness, two-tier response patterns, and KR-20) were triangulated with a single expert review. The mean score was 83%, and 26 of 41 items were very easy. All 15 items of moderate or easy difficulty discriminated well, but only 21% of distractors were functional. The key was the longest option in 57 of 63 option sets, and the six items without this cue were much harder (mean p = .53 vs. .89), suggesting that many items could be answered with an option-form heuristic rather than analytic reasoning. On two-tier items, students often endorsed a correct general principle but failed to apply it to the case, consistent with the view that intuitive and scientific conceptions can coexist. KR-20 was .90 but dropped to .78 when the two lowest-scoring respondents were removed, and expert review and empirical data detected different weaknesses. The content of SRDA-PSY is promising, but option form must be revised so that scores reflect statistical reasoning. Digital assessment development, including AI-assisted item writing, should combine expert review, empirical tryouts, and automated audits of option-form cues.

items.title: A Structured Framework for Cumulative Research Reporting in Psychology: Integrating Replication, Effect Sizes, and Meta-Analytic Evidence
items.abstract: The accumulation of scientific knowledge in psychology is often impeded by the predominance of isolated empirical studies that rarely integrate their findings quantitatively with prior evidence. This limitation contributes to fragmented knowledge bases, inconsistent effect size estimates, and reduced cumulative scientific progress. The present article proposes and formalizes a Cumulative Integrated Reporting (CIR) framework, a structured methodology for empirical reporting designed to improve the systematic integration of new findings within the existing body of literature. The CIR framework consists of four interconnected components: (a) mandatory reporting of effect sizes with appropriate uncertainty estimates, (b) formal comparison with effect sizes from prior studies and relevant meta-analyses, (c) Bayesian-compatible updating of cumulative evidence distributions, and (d) transparent documentation of methodological moderators that could account for cross-study heterogeneity. We illustrate the framework with an applied example using the association between emotional regulation and perceived stress, demonstrating how a single observed effect (r = -.34) can be meaningfully situated within a prior distribution of cumulative evidence. We discuss implications for journal reporting standards, graduate training, and the reformulation of replication as a continuous epistemic practice rather than a discrete binary event. The CIR framework represents a methodologically tractable and practically implementable step toward transforming psychology's reporting culture from one oriented toward confirmatory hypothesis testing to one oriented toward cumulative quantitative synthesis.

items.title: Methodological Flexibility in the Iowa Gambling Task Undermines Interpretability: A Meta-method Review
items.abstract: Methodological flexibility–researcher degrees of freedom in procedure and scoring–can contribute to poor measurement and low replicability of findings. To quantify methodological flexibility in the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), a widely used measure of decision-making in clinical psychology, we conducted a meta-method review of a random sample of 100 studies. We found prevalent under-reporting and wide-spread modifications of procedural details. We identified 244 distinct scores used to quantify IGT outcomes, 177 of which appeared only once in our sample. To quantify the potential impact of this flexibility, we performed a multiverse analysis using 205 scores on an open IGT dataset. Correlations among these ranged from rs = -0.942 to 0.998 with a median r = 0.022, suggesting that different scoring strategies can produce extremely different study outcomes. Given these findings, without substantive information about which specific procedural and scoring choices were employed, results from the IGT are rendered uninterpretable. Supplementary Materials, Data, and Code are available at github.com/anniria/igt-methodological-flexibility.

items.title: Transparency for Whom? Participants' Informed Consent in the Era of Open Data
items.abstract: Open data can extend the use of participants’ information far beyond the study for which it was collected, making informed consent for data sharing an important part of research transparency. We examined whether psychology journals that promote open data address this issue in their guidelines and whether articles sharing data report relevant information about consent. We reviewed the websites of 83 journals identified through the TOP Factor list and examined 196 empirical articles sharing data, published in 2024–2025. No journal provided explicit guidance on obtaining consent specifically for sharing participants’ data on open platforms; four required authors to report consent for secondary data use when applicable. Only seven articles (3.57%) provided information connecting informed consent to data sharing, and in six cases this information was identifiable only in repository materials. These findings reveal a transparency gap: consent for data sharing is rarely made explicit in journal guidance or research reports, even when data are openly shared. We recommend clearer communication with participants about data sharing, more detailed reporting and sharing of consent materials, and stronger guidance from journals and institutions.

items.title: Toward Standards for Responsible AI in Health Communication: A Dual Method Pre-Deployment Risk Evaluation Framework and Case Study
items.abstract: Context: Generative AI tools are increasingly being considered for use in public health research and practice, yet standardized frameworks for pre-deployment evaluation of the risks AI tools pose - across dimensions of platform safety, audience appropriateness, and user readiness - have not been established for health communication contexts. Program or Policy: We developed and implemented a dual-method pre-deployment evaluation framework that combines adversarial red-teaming and structured user testing to assess the readiness of a health communication AI tool. The framework was applied to the Trusted Health Information Assistant (THIA), a retrieval-augmented generation chatbot designed by NORC at the University of Chicago for use in public health communication research. Implementation: The framework was implemented sequentially, beginning with red-teaming to identify safety, audience appropriateness, and reliability concerns before engaging end users. Five independent testers completed 28 structured red-team prompts, after which identified issues were remediated and verified. User testing was subsequently conducted with six participants (e.g., caregivers of older adults) and included direct interaction with THIA, pre- and post-survey assessments, semi-structured interviews, and a review of backend analytics. Evaluation: The sequential, dual-method design successfully identified distinct categories of risk. Red-teaming identified platform integrity issues, including personally identifiable information (PII) handling and citation reliability. User testing subsequently assessed platform readiness under real-world conditions, surfacing trust dynamics and usability patterns. The convergence of findings across both methods validated the complementary design: each method identified distinct dimensions, together producing a more thorough and actionable assessment. Discussion: As generative AI tools increasingly enter public health research and practice, ensuring that potential risks are systematically identified and addressed before they reach end users is paramount. Yet the field lacks shared standards for pre-deployment evaluation. AI developers rarely publish evaluation findings, leaving public health organizations with few replicable models to guide their own assessments. This report addresses that gap by documenting a structured, sequential framework including methods, instruments, scoring rubrics, and reporting structures for evaluating health communication AI tools prior to deployment.

items.title: QUARTZ: Cross-Dataset Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Retinal Vasculometry
items.abstract: Examination of retinal images provides a non-invasive means to assess the body's microvascular system, with vessel morphology linked to ocular and systemic diseases. QUARTZ (QUantitative Analysis of Retinal vessel Topology and siZe) is an automated, artificial intelligence-enabled retinal vasculometry system designed for processing large-scale retinal image datasets, including over 4 million images from within the National Health Service, to facilitate epidemiological studies. The system is uniquely capable of extracting useful information from lower quality images, including those which are partially illuminated, enabling analysis of a greater proportion of images. To enhance cross-dataset generalisation of the system from an earlier dataset-tailored approach, this work leverages 26 annotated retinal image datasets spanning diverse demographics, diseases, camera types, and imaging protocols. Evaluation on the external EPIC-Norfolk dataset demonstrates robust performance with F1 scores of 0.8305, 0.8477, 0.8741, 0.9532, and 0.8677 for arteriole, venule, vessel, optic disc, and optic cup segmentation, respectively, and 0.9197 for image quality classification. The cross-dataset generalisation approach demonstrated increased performance for arteriole/venule segmentation and optic disc segmentation. However, improvements in performance were not observed for optic cup segmentation, or for image quality classification. An online tool is provided to support wider adoption and reproducible biomarker research across diverse populations and imaging settings. In addition, the new public CHASE-AV database is introduced for arteriole and venule segmentation.

items.title: A Synthetic Virology Platform for Rapid Prototyping of Influenza A Virus mutants
items.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

items.title: The toll of an early bell? School start time and adolescent sleep quality in Flanders, Belgium
items.abstract: Study objectives: Adolescent sleep deprivation is a major public health concern, with insufficient and poor-quality sleep associated with adverse physical, mental and cognitive outcomes. Early school start times may contribute to sleep restriction by conflicting with the biologically delayed sleep patterns that emerge during puberty. This study examined the effect of school start times on sleep duration and sleep quality among secondary school students. Methods: Data were obtained from the 2022 Flemish Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) study, including 12,329 adolescents from grade 1 to 6 in 94 secondary schools in Flanders. School start times were obtained from participating schools and sleep duration and sleep quality were assessed using self-report measures. Data were analyzed using traditional statistical methods (i.e., linear regression) and debiased machine learning methods (i.e., assumption lean regression, dose response curves and modified treatment policies). Results: No clinically meaningful effects of school start times on sleep outcomes were observed. In machine learning models, a 10-minute delay in start time was associated with non-significant changes in sleep quality (0.01 points on a 1-5 scale; 95% CI, -0.05 to 0.06) and school-day sleep duration (3.5 minutes; 95% CI, -1.0 to 8.0). Conclusions: Within the narrow range of school start times observed in Flemish secondary schools, confidence intervals excluded clinically meaningful effects of later start times on adolescent sleep duration and sleep quality. Whether larger delays would improve sleep remains to be determined.

items.title: An Agentic AI Pipeline for an Evidence-Grounded Environmental Health Public Information System: Development and Evaluation
items.abstract: Background: Existing environmental and health information systems typically provide isolated data streams, requiring users to interpret heterogeneous information sources without personalized guidance. Residents and health providers of urban regions with complex environmental conditions, such as the Salt Lake Valley, frequently seek timely, location-specific information about weather, air quality, and their associated health impacts, but may find it difficult to integrate this information in their decision-making, precluding the effective translation of valuable environmental health information into action. Objective: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that delivers evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses to health-related environmental questions raised lay persons by dynamically orchestrating authoritative weather, neighborhood-scale environmental observations, air quality, and health-evidence resources. Methods: We developed an agentic AI pipeline using LangGraph and OpenAI large language models to interpret natural language queries, select and invoke relevant external tools, retrieve real-time environmental data and evidence-based health guidance, and synthesize responses. The pipeline integrates multiple authoritative resources, including weather forecasts, air-quality observations, geospatial services, and a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module built from asthma-related clinical guidance. The system incorporates fallback mechanisms to improve robustness when external services are unavailable. We evaluated the pipeline using a curated benchmark of representative user questions, assessing tool-needed recognition, correct tool selection, avoidance of irrelevant tools, parameter mapping, analytic pathway selection, and incorporation of tool outputs into the final response. Results: The developed system successfully integrated heterogeneous environmental and health information sources into a unified conversational interface that produces evidence-grounded, neighborhood-scale responses for the Salt Lake Valley. Evaluation demonstrated generally strong tool recognition, parameter mapping, and incorporation of retrieved information across diverse question types, supporting the pipeline's ability to retrieve and integrate authoritative environmental and health information consumable by lay persons and providing an important step for the T3 and T4 phases of the translational pipeline of exposure health informatics. Conclusions: By combining existing environmental health knowledge with local sensor observations and neighborhood-scale environmental measurements, and authoritative state and national weather and air quality resources, the system delivers more localized and context-aware guidance than approaches that rely on authoritative regional or state-level information. Rather than depending on the internal knowledge of a large language model, the pipeline dynamically retrieves, synthesizes, and attributes evidence from authoritative sources. The modular architecture enables seamless integration of additional environmental data streams, health knowledge sources, and geographic regions, providing a scalable foundation for future translational pipelines, completing the T3 to T4 path for environmental health.

items.title: Modeling Mosquito Dynamics and West Nile Virus Risk in Canada: A Systematic Mapping Review of Approaches and Research Gaps
items.abstract: Mosquito population dynamics are strongly shaped by environmental conditions and are central to mosquito-borne disease risk. In Canada, West Nile virus (WNV) remains the dominant mosquito-borne viral disease of public health concern, while climate change may alter mosquito distributions, seasonal activity, and the risk of WNV and other emerging mosquito-borne diseases. This systematic mapping review synthesizes Canadian studies on mosquito population dynamics, vector distribution, surveillance, WNV risk, and emerging mosquito-borne disease risk, with attention to modeling approaches, environmental drivers, biological-process representation, data sources, model support, and geographic coverage. A total of 50 studies met the eligibility criteria. Statistical and data-driven models formed the largest modeling category, while mechanistic mosquito population models provided the clearest representation of life-history processes. Temperature was the most consistently represented environmental driver, whereas precipitation was commonly included but represented in varying ways. Model support and transparency varied, with calibration reported more often than independent validation, uncertainty analysis, sensitivity analysis, out-of-sample prediction, or code and data availability. Studies were concentrated in Ontario and national-scale analyses; Atlantic and northern Canada were represented by a small number of empirical or surveillance studies but lacked eligible quantitative modeling studies. The main gap is the lack of integrated models linking climate-sensitive mosquito population dynamics, surveillance data, and WNV transmission. Future work should prioritize integrated, climate-informed frameworks to support mosquito and WNV risk assessment in Canada.

items.title: The Culture of Dissemblance Among Black American Women: A Mixed Methods Assessment
items.abstract: Disparities in the treatment of mood and stress disorders like posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) may partially reflect a limited culturally informed understanding of emotional processing. The culture of dissemblance (COD) describes how American Black women learned to mask their emotional expression as a protective mechanism within a society that places them at greater risk of psychosocial stressors while invalidating their emotional experience. This mixed methods study examined COD among forty-nine Black women (ages 40–55), who completed a semi-structured interview assessing emotional engagement alongside self-report measures of emotion regulation, trauma exposure, PTSD symptoms, racial discrimination, and Black identity. Thematic analysis indicated that participants experienced negative judgments of their emotional expression and learned to monitor emotional responses for self-protection. 83.7% of women reported less emotional expression in public with 40.8% of women identified the workplace as the primary site for emotional masking. Interview-based COD endorsement associated with belief in negative public perception of Black people but not with the other variables of interests. Treatment approaches should center Black women's cultural knowledge to address mental health disparities.

items.title: A real-world indoor dynamic skeleton dataset of elderly abnormal gait including crutch-assisted walking
items.abstract: Abstract Falls and gait imbalance are a major health threat to older adults, yet public skeleton datasets that targetelderly adults in real indoor care environments, particularly for clinically critical unbalanced gaits such ascrutch-assisted walking, remain scarce. Here we present ElderlyPipe, a dynamic skeleton dataset of elderlyabnormal gait recorded in real indoor care environments. The release comprises 63,855 quality-assured skele-ton frames grouped into 287 continuous segments and 28,735 standardized 24-frame windows, covering fourbehaviours: standing, walking, crutch-assisted walking (using_crutch), and sitting. The skeletons are com-pleted by hierarchical occlusion compensation and refined by visibility-aware adaptive Kalman smoothing.Benchmarks on the release show that the temporal association of skeleton sequences underpins imbalanceanalysis: a spatiotemporal graph model outperforms its single-frame counterpart in overall F1 (0.656 vs.0.605) and better separates crutch-assisted walking, the representative unbalanced state, from everyday be-haviours. The anonymized skeleton sequences, metadata, cross-validation splits, documentation, the completeprocessing pipeline, and the baseline code are openly released under a persistent identifier.

items.title: Managing Surgical Waiting Lists in Public Health Systems: A Soft Systems Methodology Study in Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Prolonged surgical waiting lists are a persistentchallenge in publicly funded health systems. In Brazil's Unified Health System(SUS), managing elective surgical demand involves complex organizationalpressures and competing stakeholder priorities. Soft Systems Methodology (SSM)offers a framework for addressing such situations, yet its application inresource-constrained public health systems in low- and middle-income countriesremains limited. This study used SSM to examine the organizational complexitiesof elective surgical waiting list management at a federal orthopedic hospitalin Brazil and to identify systemically desirable and culturally feasibleimprovements. Methods: A qualitative case study based on SSM was conducted at theNational Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics (INTO). Data were collectedbetween March and October 2024 through 22 semi-structured interviews, documentanalysis, and field observations. The six-stage SSM process was used to explorethe problem situation, develop conceptual models, and identify feasibleimprovements. Results: Three dominant worldviews shaped waiting list management:INTO as a Surgical Executor, focused on productivity and waiting-timereduction; as a SUS Network Actor, concerned with equity and federativecoordination; and as a Center of Excellence, committed to research, teaching,and high-complexity care. The interaction of these institutional logicsgenerated tensions in prioritization, governance, and care pathways. Anintegrated conceptual model comprising eleven interdependent activities wasdeveloped to reconcile these perspectives by linking demand management,prioritization, network coordination, operational performance, and academicobjectives. Conclusions: Surgical waiting list management in large public orthopedic hospitals is a complex organizational problem shaped by competinginstitutional logics and federative governance constraints, rather thanoperational bottlenecks alone. SSM made these tensions explicit and supportedstrategic decision-making by identifying systemically desirable and culturallyfeasible improvements. The integrated model provides a foundation for futuredecision-support tools and quantitative modeling, highlighting the value ofqualitative systems approaches in resource-constrained health systems.

items.title: Explainable Protein Language Model Embeddings for Rapid Antibiotic Resistance Gene Classification
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major public-health threat because resistant infections narrow therapeutic options, delay effective treatment, and increase the clinical and economic burden of bacterial disease. Conventional phenotypic susceptibility testing remains essential but requires 24–48 hours after isolate growth, while sequence-based interpretation requires curated databases and bioinformatics expertise. This paper presents ResiScan, an explainable machine-learning framework for rapid classification of antibiotic resistance genes from protein sequences. The proposed system uses the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) protein homolog model data and extracts contextual protein representations with the pre-trained ESM2 model. Each protein sequence is tokenized, truncated to 512 residues for computational consistency, passed through ESM2, and represented by a 320-dimensional mean-pooled embedding. A logistic regression classifier is trained on these embeddings, with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) applied only to the training partition to address severe class imbalance across five target resistance classes: beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, macrolide, tetracycline, and vancomycin. The framework further integrates SHAP-based feature attribution to expose which embedding dimensions contribute most strongly to each prediction, and provides an interactive Gradio web interface for non-specialist use. The prototype achieves 99.25% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 0.9507 on a held-out test set of 400 protein sequences, demonstrating a practical balance among speed, interpretability, and deployability.

items.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Rubella Infection Among Female Students in Secondary Schools in Aden, Yemen: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Rubella is a highly contagious viral infection that poses a significant public health threat, particularly to pregnant women and their fetuses, potentially leading to congenital rubella syndrome (CRS). Understanding the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding rubella among adolescent girls is crucial for designing effective prevention strategies. This study aimed to assess the KAP regarding rubella infection among female secondary school students in Aden, Yemen. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 441 female secondary school students in Aden, Yemen, from May 2026 to October 2026. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge about rubella, attitudes toward prevention, and vaccination practices. The questionnaire was validated with a content validity index of 0.89 and a Cronbach's alpha of 0.78. Knowledge was assessed using six core items (range 0–6), attitudes using five statements (range 0–5), and practices using three preventive behaviors (range 0–3). Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression analysis were performed using R statistical software version 4.3.1. Results: The mean age of participants was 17.5 ± 1.03 years. The majority were single (94.1%), resided in urban areas (99.1%), and attended public schools (69.6%). Overall, 34.7% demonstrated good knowledge, and positive attitudes toward rubella prevention were observed in 44.2% of participants. Regarding practices, 46.9% of female students had good preventive practices regarding rubella infection, and only 28.1% reported having received rubella vaccination. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that students from middle-income families were significantly more likely to have good knowledge compared to low-income families (aOR = 2.83, 95% CI: 1.11–7.36, p = 0.029). In subgroup analysis, maternal education (p = 0.018), paternal education (p = 0.001), and family income (p = 0.002) were significantly associated with good knowledge among private school students. Conclusion: This study revealed moderate knowledge and attitudes toward rubella among female secondary school students in Aden; however, vaccination coverage remains alarmingly low. Targeted health education programs and improved vaccination strategies are urgently needed to prevent potential rubella outbreaks and CRS cases in this vulnerable population.

items.title: A Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate with Predicted Broad Genotype Coverage Against Toxoplasma gondii Designed by Reverse Vaccinology and Immunoinformatics Strategies
items.abstract: Abstract Background Toxoplasma gondii ( T. gondii ) is a globally prevalent zoonotic pathogen with major veterinary importance, causing significant livestock reproductive losses and facilitating zoonotic transmission to humans. Despite extensive efforts, there is no available efficient vaccine except for Toxovax, which is only approved for sheep and suffers from some limitations. The parasite’s complex multistage life cycle and strain diversity present major obstacles for vaccine development. Traditional vaccine strategies, including killed, attenuated, and subunit vaccines, provide only limited protection, in addition to posing potential translational drawbacks. Multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) approaches have emerged as a promising alternative that combines conserved immunodominant epitopes, enabling a robust immune response. Our study aimed to computationally design and evaluate a novel MEV candidate capable of eliciting predicted broad genotypic coverage against T. gondii. It thus, serves as a One Health candidate intended for veterinary disease control, which consequently serves the public health by reducing foodborne zoonotic transmission risk and translational potential for cross-species experimental validation. Methods Eighteen T. gondii proteins expressed in different life stages of multiple genotypes were screened for antigenicity, allergenicity, and epitope conservancy. Selected proteins were analyzed to predict MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes using stringent thresholds. Followed by evaluating the candidate epitopes for their cytokine induction potential and theoretical population coverage. Selected epitopes were then assembled into constructs and assessed for physicochemical properties, secondary and tertiary structure stability, immune response simulation, and molecular docking to TLR2 and TLR4. The candidate construct was subjected to complex stability analysis through molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. Codon optimization and in silico cloning were then performed for potential E. Coli expression. Results Forty-three conserved and non-allergenic epitopes were selected and constituted different constructs. Out of which, MEV-2A demonstrated high predicted antigenicity, 100 % hypothetical worldwide population coverage, Th1-skewed cytokine induction, high stability, and computational binding affinity towards TLR2 and TLR4, suggesting that MEV-2A is a promising candidate for further validation. Conclusion MEV-2A is a computationally designed and optimized multi-epitope vaccine targeting multi-stages and multi-genotypes of T. gondii, aimed to serve as a One Health candidate for livestock disease control and human zoonotic risk reduction , which warrants further experimental in vitro and in vivo validations. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Ethiopia, yet the utilization of confirmatory and supportive diagnostic tests is not adequately characterized. Methods A quantitative cross‑sectional study was conducted from December 2023 to August 2024. items.abstract: Abstract Background Digital health technologies are increasingly deployed to strengthen healthcare delivery in low- and middle-income countries, yet unequal access to the material resources, skills and opportunities required for meaningful use may reproduce existing inequalities. Evidence on provider-level digital inequality between rural and urban healthcare settings in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. This study examined rural-urban differences in multidimensional digital health access among healthcare workers in Ghana's public district hospitals. items.title: Post-exposure prophylaxis and possible breakthrough infections among human rabies case in China, 2019–2024: a nationwide retrospective surveillance study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Rabies remains a uniformly fatal yet preventable zoonotic disease that continues to pose a public health threat in China, especially in rural populations. Although post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is highly effective when delivered promptly and correctly, deaths still occur, including rare infections that develop despite prophylaxis. This study characterized exposure patterns, PEP use, and possible breakthrough infections among human rabies deaths in China from 2019 to 2024. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of data from China's national rabies surveillance system. Clinically diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed human rabies cases reported between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024 were included. We analyzed demographic characteristics, exposure information, animal sources, wound sites, PEP measures, and incubation periods. Multivariable unconditional logistic regression identified factors associated with PEP receipt, while Cox proportional hazards models, Mann–Whitney U tests, and Kruskal–Wallis H tests were used to examine factors associated with the incubation period. Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests compared standard and non-standard PEP cases. Results Among 930 human rabies deaths, most patients were male, rural farmers, and middle-aged or older adults. Dogs caused 86.88% of exposures, yet only 1.83% of owned biting animals had documented rabies vaccination. PEP uptake was very low: 852 cases (91.62%) received no prophylaxis whatsoever, and only 51 cases (5.48%) received rabies vaccine. Non-category III exposure, wounds at lower-risk sites, injury by household animals, and single-victim incidents were associated with lower likelihood of receiving wound care, vaccination, or rabies immunoglobulin. Among 697 cases with a documented incubation period, the median was 70 days (IQR: 38–134.5). Head, face, or neck exposure and multiple-victim incidents were independently associated with shorter incubation periods. Seventy-eight patients developed rabies despite receiving at least one prophylaxis measure; 60 (76.92%) had clearly non-standard PEP, whereas 18 (23.08%) had no identifiable procedural failure. These possible breakthrough infections accounted for 1.94% of all cases and were characterized by category III exposure, head, face, or neck injuries, stray-dog bites, and a short median incubation period of 16 days. Conclusion Most human rabies deaths in China resulted from a failure to initiate or complete PEP, reflecting preventable gaps in risk perception, access, affordability, and follow-up. Possible breakthrough infections were rare but were concentrated in extremely high-risk exposures. Targeted health education, improved prophylaxis adherence, integrated bite case management, and strengthened dog vaccination under a One Health framework are essential to eliminate dog-mediated human rabies deaths.

items.title: Graviceptive Neglect treatment in acute stroke using transcranial Electrical stimulation clinical trial (GravNegElect): rationale, objectives, and design
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability globally and is often related to poor functional recovery and a high risk of falling. These outcomes correlate closely with an impaired perception of visual verticality (VV), a frequent condition referred to as visual graviceptive neglect (V-GN). Our prior findings indicate that post-stroke VV is most frequently rotated away from the lesioned hemisphere in the roll plane. Furthermore, we demonstrated that a focal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) montage (known as high-definition tDCS; HD-tDCS) can induce a remarkable and sustained rotation away from the stimulated hemisphere when positioned over the temporo-parietal junction (TPJ), a key integrative cortical hub for VV. Therefore, we hypothesize that stimulating the contralesional TPJ in sub-acute stroke individuals will correct their V-GN. Methods: This phase IIa, randomised, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial aims to determine whether HD-tDCS can safely correct V-GN in individuals who have experienced a stroke affecting either hemisphere. Ancillary aims are to investigate whether HD-tDCS influences ocular torsion; explore neuroanatomical characteristics related to V-GN; investigate the relationship between EEG functional connectivity and V-GN; and determine the cerebrovascular reactivity effects of HD-tDCS. A total of 28 individuals diagnosed with acute or early sub-acute unihemispheric ischemic stroke (50% with right hemisphere lesions) will be randomized to receive six 20-minute sessions (conducted within 2 days) of either 2mA cathode-centre HD-tDCS or sham stimulation over the contralesional TPJ. VV will be assessed using the bucket method. The primary outcome is the change in VV from baseline to immediately after the intervention protocol, while the secondary outcome is VV assessed at 1 month post-intervention. Fundus photography (ocular torsion), vascular reactivity using transcranial Doppler, and resting state EEG (functional connectivity) will be assessed at the same time-points as VV. Structural and resting state functional MRI will be performed 2-15 days after stroke onset. Fractional anisotropy within the V-GN network regions-of-interest (ROIs) and transcallosal TPJ tract will be correlated with baseline VV and V-GN response to intervention. Discussion: This trial has the potential for a significant public health impact by providing foundational clinical and physiological evidence to develop future clinical interventions for V-GN. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06747676. Registered on 12 December 2024. Version 2.

items.title: The relationship between time attitudes and health behaviours among Chinese university students: A network analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background Health behaviours are closely associated with global disease prevention and public health burden. The relationship between time attitudes and health behaviours has received increasing attention; however, their association structure and possible potential directional relationships remain unclear. Methods A total of 2395 university students from Gansu Province were recruited using convenience sampling. Time attitudes were measured using the Adolescent Time Attitude Scale (ATAS), and health behaviours were assessed using the Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile-II Revised (HPLP-IIR) and the Adolescent Health Related Risky Behaviour Inventory (AHRBI). Undirected network analysis, community detection, and Bayesian network analysis were employed to examine the association structure and potential directional dependencies between time attitudes, health-promoting behaviours, and health-risk behaviours. Results The network comprised 17 nodes. Aggression violence (AV) had the highest expected influence (EI = 1.471), and future positive (FuP) showed the highest bridge expected influence (BEI = 0.240). Community detection revealed a relatively clear modular structure with three communities (Q = 0.456). Bayesian network analysis indicated directional paths from past negative to suicide/self-harm (direction probability = 0.628) and from present negative to rule-breaking (direction probability = 0.696) between time attitudes and health-risk behaviours. Between time attitudes and health-promoting behaviours, paths from past negative to health responsibility (direction probability = 0.620) and from spiritual growth to future positive (direction probability = 0.601) were observed. Conclusions This study provides preliminary empirical evidence for the internal association between time attitudes and health behaviours among university students. Past negative and present negative may be potential key nodes linking time attitudes to health-risk behaviours, while future positive may be a potential bridge node linking time attitudes to health-promoting behaviours. Given the cross-sectional design, the DAG directions should be regarded as candidate relationships rather than causal mechanisms. Trial Registration Not applicable.

items.title: Attention and Discourse on Myocarditis Across 6 Chinese Social Media Platforms: An Infodemiology Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Myocarditis carries substantial morbidity, and the COVID-19 pandemic amplified public and media attention to the condition. In China, where mass vaccination overlapped with successive respiratory seasons, myocarditis settled into a durable high-attention state, yet how that attention spreads across the country's fragmented, multimodal social-media landscape remains poorly understood. We characterized the temporal dynamics, sentiment, cognitive dimensions, and thematic structure of myocarditis-related discourse across six major Chinese platforms over 36 months to derive actionable targets for infodemic management and public-health communication. Methods We conducted an infodemiology study spanning 1 July 2023 to 31 July 2026 across Weibo, Bilibili, Zhihu, Xiaohongshu, Douyin and Kuaishou, applying a frozen 68-term keyword lexicon. Acquisition used the official advanced-search API (Weibo), a signed REST API (Bilibili), and Playwright-driven real-browser automation (remaining platforms). Of 114,999 retrieved records, 112,243 (97.60%) were retained after de-identification, deduplication, relevance filtering and entertainment-noise suppression. Processing comprised jieba segmentation, SnowNLP sentiment scoring (random subsample n = 60,000), TF-IDF plus K-means topic modelling (k = 8) on 29,352 high/medium-relevance records, a nine-class rule-based cognitive-dimension classifier, and alignment to seven influenza-season-aligned phases. Ethics approval: TJ-IRB202404084. Results Public attention followed a stable winter-spring surge and summer-autumn plateau pattern, growing nearly threefold from phase 1 (7,973 records) to phase 6 (23,516). Provenance was highly concentrated: Weibo accounted for 77.9% (87,412 records), followed by Bilibili (7.0%), Xiaohongshu (5.2%), Douyin (5.0%), Zhihu (3.3%) and Kuaishou (1.5%). Sentiment was net positive (mean 0.712; 71.7% positive, 23.2% negative, 5.1% neutral), though most anxious during peak-volume months. Discourse migrated from categorical disease naming toward experiential symptom, diagnosis and recovery narratives. The largest topic cluster was a first-person pediatric care narrative (42.6%); 'myocarditis mistaken for a cold or COVID-19' accounted for 8.4%. High-frequency terms, 'cold' (42,758), 'symptoms' (36,360), 'cough' and 'influenza', revealed persistent respiratory-cardiac semantic conflation. Conclusions The myocarditis infodemic on Chinese social media is large, seasonal, experiential and shaped by recurrent respiratory-cardiac semantic overlap in lay discourse. These findings support influenza-calendar-timed, family-centered, clinician-led communication and argue for embedding myocarditis infoveillance within China's event-based media-surveillance architecture, treating public confusion as both an exploratory signal and a health-literacy resource.

items.title: Cross-Country Transportability of Machine Learning Models for Childhood Malaria Infection Prediction: Reciprocal Validation and Recalibration in Nigeria and Mali
items.abstract: Background: The cross-country transportability of childhood malaria prediction models remains unclear across populations with different prevalence and environmental conditions. Nigeria and Mali share correlates of malaria infection. We evaluated correlates of malaria rapid diagnostic test (RDT) positivity and the transportability of four machine learning algorithms using nationally representative 2021 Mali and Nigeria Malaria Indicator Surveys Methods: We included children aged 6–59 months with valid RDT results (Mali, n = 8,730; Nigeria, n = 10,717). Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified correlates. We assessed regularised logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and an artificial neural network using five-fold cluster-aware cross-validation, reciprocal zero-shot external validation, and cross-fitted local recalibration. Results: Weighted RDT positivity was 19.4% in Mali and 39.6% in Nigeria. Increasing age, lower wealth and maternal education, larger household size, and unprotected or surface water were shared correlates. Internal discrimination was moderate (ROC-AUC 0.690–0.719), with complex models consistently and moderately outperforming regularised logistic regression. External discrimination was lower (ROC-AUC 0.668–0.689). Mali-trained models underpredicted Nigerian RDT positivity by 18.9–26.5 percentage points, whereas Nigeria-trained models overpredicted Malian positivity by 24.5–27.1 percentage points. Recalibration reduced mean prediction gaps to approximately zero with slightly improved discrimination Conclusions: Cross-country prediction requires external validation and representative local recalibration before wider public health use and should not replace confirmatory testing.

items.title: Barriers and Enablers to the Development and Translation of Tuberculosis Biomarkers and Tests: a Scoping Review Protocol
items.abstract: Introduction: Tuberculosis remains a major global health challenge, causing over a million deaths annually and affecting an estimated 10 million people worldwide each year. Diagnostic delays and the lack of accurate, deployable tests across TB disease states continue to hamper public health control efforts. Despite sustained investment in TB biomarker research, translation into clinical use has been limited, often because traditional approaches focus on technology development in isolation and overlook the scientific, regulatory, social, and market interdependencies that shape whether a test reaches the people who need it. This protocol describes a scoping review that will identify and map barriers and enablers for the development, validation, regulatory approval, commercialisation, and implementation of TB biomarkers and tests. Methods This scoping review follows Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches will be conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and EBSCOHOST (including CINAHL and Global Health), supplemented by grey literature from WHO, FIND, and regulatory bodies. Qualitative and mixed-methods studies published in English within the last 20 years will be the primary source type; opinion pieces, editorials, commentaries, and narrative reviews will be included conditionally if evidence is insufficient. Two independent reviewers will screen titles, abstracts, and full texts, and extract data using a standardised form capturing barriers and enablers across each stage of the development and translation pathway. Results Findings will be synthesised using descriptive content analysis and thematic synthesis, with data charted across the TB patient care pathway and the technology translation pathway, and evidence gaps identified and reported. Conclusions By systematically mapping barriers and enablers across the biomarker and test translation pathway, this review will provide researchers, funders, regulators, and implementers with a synthesised evidence base to support more effective investment and policy decisions, helping accelerate translation of TB biomarkers and tests into practice.

items.title: The Asynchronous Frame: Patient Portal Messaging Between Psychiatric Visits.
items.abstract: Asynchronous patient portal messaging has become a routine part of psychiatric practice, yet its impact on the therapeutic frame remains poorly defined. Unlike telephone calls or e-mail, portal-based communication is embedded into the electronic health record, extending care beyond scheduled visits. Although patient portals may improve access, transparency, and satisfaction, concerns have been raised about their effects on therapeutic boundaries, the therapeutic alliance, and clinician workload. The authors introduce the concept of the asynchronous frame to describe the explicit and implicit expectations governing between-session communication. Defining this frame collaboratively may preserve therapeutic integrity, support clinicians, and promote safe, patient-centered psychiatric care.
