items.title: Geometric inference of cross-species transcriptome correspondence.
items.abstract: Sequence homology reveals evolutionary gene correspondences, but identifying functionally corresponding genes within specific cell types or during cell fate specification remains non-trivial. Here, frameworks that translate insights from model organisms into other species would accelerate wet-lab studies, so we develop Species-OT, a cross-species transcriptome analysis framework using Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport, which quantitatively compares the geometry of transcriptome distributions. Given a pair of bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, Species-OT returns a gene-to-gene correspondence capturing probabilistic alignments of regulatory roles and a transcriptomic distance quantifying overall divergence. Applied pairwise, Species-OT yields a transcriptomic discrepancy array and a hierarchical clustering tree analogous to a phylogenetic tree. We validate Species-OT using bulk RNA-seq data for cell fate specification from pluripotent stem cells in mice, monkeys, and humans and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data from pluripotent stem cells of six mammalian species. Species-OT identifies gene correspondences within cell fate specification, while transcriptomic discrepancies recapitulate expected species relationships.

items.title: Organoids and organs-on-a-chip as new approach methodologies at the convergence of cell biology and bioengineering.
items.abstract: The rapid growth of new approach methodologies (NAMs), including organoids and organs-on-a-chip (OOCs), has revealed a need for interdisciplinary dialogue between cell biologists and bioengineers to develop human models that can best complement therapeutic development. Stem cell-derived and bioengineered human tissue models are redefining how we understand human physiology and pathophysiology, offering control that traditional preclinical models cannot provide. By recapitulating complex tissue microenvironments, multi-organ interactions, and patient-specific biology, these systems are bridging long-standing gaps in the drug development and clinical application pipelines. Here, we synthesize advances in organoids, OOCs, and other bioengineered technologies for translational medicine to identify remaining gaps, including challenges in reproducibility, validation, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging opportunities at the intersection of synthetic biology, multi-omics, machine learning, and genetic engineering are positioning NAMs not merely as improved experimental tools but as foundational platforms for accelerating therapeutic discovery and enabling personalized medicine at scale.

items.title: Somatic DNA-repeat expansions initiate distinct yet analogous changes in Huntington's disease cortical and striatal neurons.
items.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) affects the neocortex and striatum with different timing, severity, and gene-expression changes. These pathologies have long been proposed to involve different pathogenic mechanisms, with one brain area's degeneration leading to the other's. Striatal neurons degenerate in HD as their huntingtin (HTT) CAG-repeat tracts expand somatically beyond 150 CAGs. Here, we find that cortical pyramidal neurons in HD undergo biological changes analogous to those in striatal neurons-the same sequence of pathological phases, with toxicity also commencing at ∼150 CAGs but then changing their gene expression in distinct ways. Pyramidal neurons' precise molecular identities, rather than their areal or laminar locations, appeared to determine the extent of this somatic DNA-repeat expansion, which varied up to 20-fold among pyramidal neuron subtypes. Cortical and striatal neurons also shared a key pathological feature: nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein in those nuclei with expansions well beyond 150 CAGs.

items.title: Sex-specific associations between Mediterranean Diet Score and long-term risk of mortality, dementia and other chronic diseases. 20-year evidence from a Swedish population study of 70-year old individuals.
items.abstract: Objectives To investigate the association between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS) and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer, and dementia morbidity over 10- and 20-year follow-up periods in a population-based cohort of older adults. Design A prospective population-based cohort study. Setting Gothenburg, Sweden. Participants A total of 1298 participants (56.2% women) aged 70years at baseline from the general population and recruited from the Gothenburg H70 and Population Study of Women in Gothenburg (PSWG) birth cohorts. Measurements Dietary intake was assessed via face-to-face, semi-structured diet history interviews. The MDS was calculated based on eight food groups (excluding alcohol). Outcomes were identified through linkage with national health and death registers. Cox proportional hazard models were used, adjusting for BMI, smoking, marital status, physical activity, and education. Results A higher MDS was associated with a lower risk of 20-year dementia morbidity in men (multivariable-adjusted HR=0.83; 95% CI: 0.71-0.96), but not in women. This association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing, and the sex-by-MDS interaction (p=0.048) was nominally significant, but not robust to multiple testing. No statistically significant associations were found for CVD or cancer morbidity in either sex over the available follow-up (i.e., 10 and 20years, and up to 18years for cancer; 20-year CVD follow-up in men: HR=0.98; 95% CI: 0.88-1.08). For all-cause mortality, an initial association in men at 10years (HR=0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.99) was no longer significant after full adjustment (HR=0.92; 95% CI: 0.84-1.01). Conclusions Higher MDS levels were associated with lower dementia risk in men, but this finding was not robust to multiple testing correction and requires confirmation in larger studies. No association was found with all-cause mortality, CVD and cancer morbidity. A limitation of these findings is that dietary assessment was conducted at a single time point (age 70), and that dementia ascertainment relied on registers which are estimated to miss > 50% of cases, particularly among home-dwellers.

items.title: Cognitive training combined with aerobic exercise improves negative symptoms in recent-onset schizophrenia: Results from a 12-month randomized trial.
items.abstract: Negative symptoms are often considered as a core feature of schizophrenia. High initial severity levels are predictive of poor clinical outcomes, and negative symptoms are often considered notoriously difficult to treat. However, some research indicates that combining cognitive training with aerobic exercise yields notable improvements in negative symptoms for individuals with multi-episode schizophrenia. Our Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) compared the impact of 12 months of Cognitive Training combined with Aerobic Exercise (CT&E) compared to Cognitive Training (CT) alone in 65 first episode schizophrenia patients (73% male; age = 22.5 years; education = 12.8 years). All participants were provided with cognitive training and the CT&E group also participated in an aerobic exercise program. Negative Symptoms were assessed with the SANS at baseline and subsequently every 2-weeks. Negative symptoms were secondary outcomes from our original RCT (Nuechterlein et al. 2023) and considered of high clinical relevance because of their relationship to functional outcome. Piecewise Linear Mixed Effects Models showed an overall differential effect of treatment over 12 months in which the intervention groups improved at similar rates over the first 6 months, while the CT&E group continued to improve on SANS Total Score (p < 0.001). Similar patterns were observed on SANS Expressive and Experiential domains. These findings indicate that aerobic exercise, when combined with cognitive training, can improve both expressive and experiential negative symptoms in individuals living with schizophrenia. The results extend the potential for exercise-based interventions to promote negative symptom reduction during a critical "early phase" that may impact long-term outcomes.

items.title: Can you see it? Visual outcomes in surgically treated tuberculum sellae meningiomas: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction Meningiomas located on the tuberculum sellae often exhibit a strong association with the optic apparatus. Hence, ophthalmologic dysfunction often serves as the most common manifestation of tuberculum sellae meningiomas. Objective To assess visual outcomes following transcranial microsurgical resection of tuberculum sellae meningiomas. Material and methods A systematic review and meta-analysis adhering to Cochrane Standards and PRISMA framework were conducted. PubMed, Embase, and Web Of Science databases were searched until May 2024. A subgroup analysis was performed based on the optic nerve decompression. Studies were categorized into two groups: Group 1 included papers in which less than 50 % of patients underwent optic nerve decompression, while Group 2 comprised studies where more than 50 % of patients received some form of optic nerve decompression. The study has been registered on PROSPERO, with the registration number CRD42024530649. Results Thirty-two studies (N = 1.941) met the inclusion criteria. Visual function improvement rate was found to be 61 % (95 % CI: 55-66 %), while for the unchanged it was 26 % (95 % CI: 20-32 %) and worsened by 11 % (95 % CI: 8-13 %). The overall gross total removal rate across the studies was 85 % (95 % CI: 82-88 %) and recurrence was 4 % (95 % CI: 3-6 %). Among the studies that did not perform optic canal unroofing in the majority of cases (Group 1), the visual improvement rate was 60 % (95 % CI: 51-70 %), gross total remove rate was 87 % (95 % CI: 82-92 %) and recurrence was 3 % (95 % CI: 1-6 %). Group 2 showed rates of 69 % (95 % CI: 60-78 %), 89 % (95 % CI: 84-94 %), and 1 % (95 % CI: 0-3 %), respectively. Conclusions In conclusion, the study findings suggest that transcranial microsurgical resection of for tuberculum sellae meningiomas yields positive outcomes in terms of improving visual function, gross total resection rates, and recurrence, especially those that did the optic nerve decompression in the majority of the cases.

items.title: The effects of cannabis legalization on psychological and physical impairment in individuals who use cannabis frequently.
items.abstract: We investigated the relationship between the use of cannabis available after legalization and adverse effects in individuals diagnosed with Cannabis Use Disorder (CUD). We utilized an existing longitudinal study of high-risk individuals (364 high-risk participants in treatment for substance use disorder (SUD) in adolescence and 407 of their siblings) that were assessed twice before January 2014 (when recreational cannabis dispensaries first opened in Colorado) and once after 2014. We hypothesized that participants who met DSM criteria for CUD after 2014, when high THC concentration cannabis products became more readily available, would demonstrate more adverse physical and psychological symptoms and endorse more DSM criteria compared to those meeting DSM criteria for CUD before 2014. In general, we did not find evidence for significant mean differences in impairment after 2014. Contrary to expectation, we found that high-risk participants with CUD endorsed significantly more DSM criteria before 2014 than after 2014. Exploratory trajectory analyses identified a small subgroup of high-risk participants (21.5%) and siblings (20.1%) exhibiting an increase in the number of CUD criteria endorsed who experienced significantly more psychological and physical symptoms after 2014. It is possible that increased THC potency products have had less effect on individuals in this high-risk sample, many of whom have been daily users for many years and have substantial tolerance for THC. Similar studies of individuals who use cannabis recreationally and less frequently are necessary.

items.title: Sex hormone regulation of neutrophil function is dependent on activation state.
items.abstract: Cellular physiology is critically modulated by hormones. Our understanding of their effect on neutrophil, most abundant leukocytes, function is limited. The goal of this study was to characterize the molecular mechanisms that underline hormones' modulation of neutrophil effector functions and the effect of activation state on this modulation. Neutrophils were isolated from young adult (2.5-6months of age) male and female mice with or without lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection (primed state). Isolated neutrophils (primed and non-primed (healthy)) were incubated with estradiol (E2) or dihydrotestosterone (DHT), and cellular changes were assessed using mass spectrometry and functional assays. Our results showed that the effect of hormones on neutrophil function is sex specific. For neutrophils isolated from female mice, both E2 and DHT decreased degranulation, increased phagocytosis, with no effect on NETosis regardless of activation state. E2 increased the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) and migration of neutrophils in an activation-dependent manner. DHT increased glycolysis and PPP regardless of activation. In neutrophils isolated from male mice, DHT and E2 decreased degranulation in primed cells only. DHT increased phagocytosis and glycolysis in primed cells while E2 decreased glycolysis and PPP in healthy cells. E2 also increased phagocytosis in healthy cells while decreasing it in primed. DHT increased migration of healthy cells with no effect on primed. These results showed that hormone modulation of female neutrophil function is independent of activation state, while its effect on male derived neutrophils is activation dependent. We propose that these differences contribute to the sex differences observed in inflammatory responses.

items.title: Modeling reaction-diffusion processes in simplified to complex astroglial branchlet geometries using different simulation tools.
items.abstract: Computational modeling of spatial biochemical processes in neuroscience is increasingly important as advances in experimental and imaging techniques provide detailed insights into cellular organization. Reaction-diffusion models are commonly used to study the diffusion and interactions of ions and molecules within neuronal cells, and multiple open-access simulation platforms have been developed to support such analysis. However, a comprehensive analysis of commonly used simulation tools, including MCell, STEPS, NeuroRD, and NEURON, remains lacking, particularly for realistic glial cell geometries, as these tools were originally developed for neurons. Here, we present a systematic analysis of these four simulation environments by implementing equivalent calcium diffusion and calcium-calmodulin reaction-diffusion models across a range of spatial domains. These include simplified geometries (cylinders and rectangular cuboids) as well as biologically realistic astroglial morphologies derived from electron microscopy data, including mouse Bergmann glia and mouse and human cortical astrocytes. Using matched kinetic parameters and diffusion constants, we examine simulation outputs and morphological variations across platforms under comparable conditions. We find that all tools produce overall consistent results for the systems considered, indicating that each can reliably capture diffusion and reaction-diffusion dynamics in simplified and complex geometries. At the same time, we show that the structural heterogeneity of branchlets from human astrocytes and mouse Bergmann glia gives rise to distinct calcium signaling, demonstrating that fine-scale morphology critically shapes astroglial dynamics and must be accurately captured by simulation frameworks. In addition, notable differences emerge in geometry representation, implementation strategies, computational aspects, and usability of the tools. By highlighting key trade-offs between geometric fidelity, flexibility, and computational cost in modeling intracellular biochemical processes, these findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate simulation tools. More broadly, our results support the use of reaction-diffusion modeling in morphologically realistic astrocytic environments and contribute to enabling mechanistic studies of localized signaling events at synaptic and perisynaptic sites.

items.title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release.
items.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

items.title: Trans-synaptic interaction of orphan GPCR GPR88 and adhesion GPCR BAI3 through C1ql1 maintains synapse integrity.
items.abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)-localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

items.title: Nanomaterial-genetics enables near-infrared-driven genetically targeted neuromodulation.
items.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

items.title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease.
items.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

items.title: Ultrasound neuromodulation hypotheses on the directionality of effects and community resource.
items.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a promising non-invasive technique for brain stimulation and focal neuromodulation. Research with humans and animal models has raised the possibility that TUS can be biased towards enhancing or suppressing neural function. Here, we first collate a set of hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects and conduct an initial meta-analysis on available healthy human participant TUS studies reporting stimulation parameters and outcomes (n = 47 studies, 52 experiments). In initial exploratory analyses with univariate tests, we find that parameters, such as the intensity and continuity of stimulation (duty cycle, DC) show statistical trends towards likely TUS neural enhancement or suppression of function. Machine-learning analyses were limited by the currently small sample size. Given that human TUS sample sizes are expected to increase, predictability on the directionality of TUS effects could improve if a database is available. Therefore, we establish an inTUS database and resource for the systematic reporting of TUS parameters and outcomes to assist in greater precision in TUS use for brain stimulation and neuromodulation. The paper concludes with a selective review of human clinical TUS studies illustrating how hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects could be developed for empirical testing in the intended clinical application, not limited to the examples provided.

items.title: Facing far forward: Mental health in large-scale combat operations.
items.abstract: Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCO) present unprecedented challenges to the provision of medical and mental health care on the battlefield. Characterized by restricted mobility, contested logistics, disrupted communication, drone attacks, subterranean environments and the necessity for prolonged field care, the LSCO environment will severely disrupt traditional models of combat and operational stress control (COSC) that rely on far-forward specialty providers and fixed facilities. This article introduces a special issue of Military Psychology dedicated to reviewing mental health in LSCO. By outlining the anticipated psychological demands of future near-peer conflicts, the goal of this special issue is to facilitate a shared and comprehensive understanding of possible threats and lay the groundwork for a way ahead to manage mental health in LSCO. Specifically, to maintain warfighter readiness and operational effectiveness, foundational COSC principles - Proximity, Immediacy, Expectancy, and Simplicity - must be reimagined. We highlight possible shifts in conceptualizing mental health care, including relying on leader-led interventions, peer-to-peer support and the training of non-specialty medical personnel (e.g. medics and corpsmen) to manage acute combat stress reactions using evidence-informed, rapid-intervention protocols. Ultimately, the goal is to synthesize current research, lessons learned from global operations, and conceptual frameworks to establish priorities for mental health training, intervention development, and policy in preparation for managing mental health in LSCO environments.

items.title: Brace for impact: A roadmap for the future of mental health in large-scale combat operations.
items.abstract: Large-scale combat operations (LSCO) are expected to present critical challenges to military units in terms of austere conditions, the potential for misinformation, specific LSCO-related threats, and the limitations of access to traditional medical care. As part of a special issue of Military Psychology dedicated to the topic of mental health in LSCO, 25 articles address these challenges. Articles cover key threats such as mass casualty events, drone warfare, and threats to the community. Articles also identify how traditional military mental health support may need to be adapted to take prolonged field care into account, with a focus on mental health support becoming the responsibility of individuals, informal peers, trained peers, and leaders. Furthermore, the articles address special topics such as the impact of LSCO on medical personnel burnout, attitudes toward novel solutions such as mindfulness, and training models for integrating mental skills into simulations and field-based exercises. Collectively, these articles inform the development of a schematic model of LSCO Mental Health. In addition, future research topics provide direction for assessing, preventing, and intervening with mental health health and cognitive strain in the LSCO context. By bringing this array of articles together, the field can prepare more effectively to meet the psychological demands of the LSCO battlespace.

items.title: Orexin and pupillary modulation for hunger control.
items.abstract: Fasting-based interventions improve metabolic health and are also explored as adjuncts in other clinical settings, but hunger remains a barrier to adherence. Fasting activates AgRP/NPY neurons (ANs), a hunger-promoting population whose inhibition reduces eating in hungry animals. Here we identify hypocretin/orexin neurons (HONs), classically associated with arousal, as rapid suppressors of AN activity. HON ablation increased AN population activity, whereas HON optostimulation rapidly suppressed it. Combined recordings of AN activity and pupil size-a direct arousal metric not previously linked to AN dynamics-revealed that HONs contributed to pupil dilation-associated AN suppression. In fasted mice, sensory stimulation rapidly recruited this pupil-HON pathway, and suppressed AN activity and eating. These findings reveal an arousal-hunger pathway through which self-initiated pupil dilations, or dilations driven by salient environmental events, interrupt fasting-induced hunger signals. They also suggest a framework for noninvasive, sensory-, and pupillometry-guided approaches to hunger control during fasting.

items.title: Forniceal deep brain stimulation improves memory in Rett syndrome mice by promoting the maturation of newborn hippocampal neurons.
items.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is associated with an increase in hippocampal neurogenesis and memory benefits, but the causal mechanism is unclear. Here, we use a mouse model of Rett syndrome, a severe learning disability syndrome caused by MECP2 loss of function, to find that DBS promotes the maturation and integration of newborn dentate granule cells (DGCs) into the neural circuit. Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.

items.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
items.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions. Through genetic manipulations, we show that reducing hippocampal Kcr levels impairs memory, while increasing Kcr levels by means of crotonate administration enhances long-term memory. Single-nuclei transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses reveal that crotonate facilitates activation of genes regulating glutamate signaling. Cell-cell communication analysis further suggests a strengthening of glutamatergic signaling within hippocampal excitatory neurons following crotonate administration. Real-time fluorescence imaging with genetically encoded sensors functionally validates our multiomics and computational findings-demonstrating the role of Kcr in regulating presynaptic glutamate release and neuronal activity. In summary, our findings elucidate a key mechanism underlying long-term memory consolidation and excitatory neurotransmission, linking epigenetic events to synaptic function and behavior.

items.title: Dlx1&2 directly promote expression of Cxcl14 to control synapse development and interneuron survival.
items.abstract: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Here we used scRNA-Seq to identify genes that are dysregulated in Dlx1/2 conditional mutants in mouse immature CGE- and MGE-derived cortical and olfactory bulb GABAergic interneurons. Dlx1/2 -regulated genes included Cxcl14 and Nr2f2 that are important for cortical interneuron (CIN) survival. We also identified DLX2-bound putative regulatory elements (pREs) of these Dlx -regulated genes. Within the Dlx -expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14 , is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.

items.title: Colours of the mind: A qualitative study exploring the relationship between neurodivergence and creativity.
items.abstract: The neurodiversity movement advocates for a societal framework that recognises neurodivergence as a difference, rather than a disorder. Despite the advocacy efforts, neurodivergent people still face issues with their physical and mental health at higher rates than the general population. Some scholars argue that these disproportionate rates originate from stress resulting from discrimination and societal stigma faced by neurodivergent people. This study aims to challenge these societal views through exploring one of the reported strengths of being neurodivergent: creativity. This study aims to explore why neurodivergent populations may be creative. To research this complex relationship between being neurodivergence and creativity a qualitative study was conducted. Ten neurodivergent adults who had studied or were currently studying a creative degree were interviewed on Zoom, exploring their beliefs about this relationship. An inductive thematic analysis was then carried out. The analysis gave rise to three themes: (1) The Construct of Creativity, (2) Resilience, & (3) Empowerment. These themes provided hypotheses for understanding the connection between neurodivergence and creativity. The results provided two hypotheses. The 'innate trait hypothesis' posits that traits thought to be intrinsic to neurodivergence may be beneficial in fostering creativity. The innate traits that arose were divergent thinking, monotropism and communication differences. The 'social isolation hypothesis' posits that the discrimination that neurodivergent people face leads to profound isolation and in some cases mental health challenges. Neurodivergent people may then use creativity as a method for regulating their emotions, providing solace from distress. Moreover, the isolation they experience provides an opportunity for introspection, which fuels creativity. Our results highlight that some neurodivergent traits, when placed within a creative context, can become strengths. This highlights the possibility that the pathologisation of neurodivergent traits is not just damaging but also invalid, with the reality being much more nuanced.

items.title: Sleep-dependent DNA methylation remodeling in basolateral amygdala fear engrams.
items.abstract: How sleep consolidates fear memories at the molecular level within individual engram neurons is unknown. Using activity-dependent tagging and sequencing, we profiled the DNA methylome and transcriptome of engram and non-engram nuclei from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) after contextual fear conditioning with and without post-learning sleep deprivation. Fear learning induces coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engram neurons, with each showing unique temporal dynamics, revealing CpH methylation as a separate component of the engram's epigenetic signature. Interestingly, sleep deprivation partially reverses learning-induced methylation changes and impairs memory recall, indicating that sleep supports engram-specific epigenetic consolidation. Integrating the engram methylome with single-cell transcriptome profiling, we construct a multi-omic molecular atlas of the BLA fear engram and identify Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target. BLA-wide and engram-specific Mid1 knockdown establishes its functional requirement for fear memory consolidation, providing an approach to identify behaviorally relevant epigenetic targets.

items.title: Perceptions of homogeneity reproduction in health sciences academia.
items.abstract: Academic institutions privilege norms of continuous productivity and uninterrupted availability, creating conformity pressures that systematically disadvantage those who deviate from an implicit template of the 'ideal academic'. This study explores how doctoral students and faculty in the health sciences perceive the reproduction of social homogeneity. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine participants at a German university hospital. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis with extended idiographic engagement. Participants perceived homogeneity as reproduced through external exclusion, enacted by others through networks, normative expectations, or institutional arrangements, and self-exclusion, whereby individuals withdrew, reduced visibility, or reshaped identity in anticipation of exclusion ('anticipatory compliance'). Across both processes, the tacit norm of the ideal academic organised access and belonging. Supportive supervision and visible role models were perceived as partial buffers but did not structurally alter underlying norms. Interpreted through the social identity threat framework, these accounts support an exploratory interpretation of a possible self-reinforcing cycle: structural homogeneity may generate identity-threatening environments that activate concealment and withdrawal, potentially concentrating homogeneity further. These findings suggest that achieving substantive inclusion requires challenging the structural conditions that naturalise presence, mobility, and availability as measures of academic success.

items.title: When Fakes Feel Real: Behavioral and Neural Mechanisms of Deepfake Hyperrealism in Younger and Older Adults.
items.abstract: Deepfakes are designed to mimic real people and constitute an emerging exploitation threat. They are potent methods of fraud as humans detect deepfake images at near or below chance levels, and deepfakes are frequently perceived as more real even than real images (deepfake hyperrealism). Anterior insula (aINS) function is implicated in processing salient, untrustworthy cues suggesting that low aINS recruitment during deepfake perception may underlie experiences of deepfake hyperrealism. Further, aging may confer increased experiences of deepfake hyperrealism, given increased susceptibility to deception and reduced aINS sensitivity to deceptive stimuli with age. Here, 156 participants (62 younger: 18-37 years, 94 older: 60-89 years) evaluated the realness of real and deepfake face images while undergoing fMRI. Behavioral results revealed deepfake hyperrealism in both age groups, with these effects more pronounced in older adults. Our imaging results indicated lower aINS activation was associated with higher realness ratings and aINS activity was also lower for deepfake than real images in both younger and older adults. These findings provide additional support for deepfake hyperrealism in perception, underscoring the threat of deepfakes as a method of exploitation across adulthood. Results also support that muted aINS response to deepfakes constitutes a neuromechanism in deception vulnerability.

items.title: Disrupted Top-Down Modulation as a Mechanism of Impaired Multisensory Processing in Autistic Children.
items.abstract: Atypical sensory processing is commonly observed in autism, particularly when integration across sensory modalities is required. The neural mechanisms underlying multisensory differences remain unclear. We recorded EEG while autistic children aged 8-13 (AU;n = 40), siblings of autistic children (SIB;n = 26), and non-autistic controls (NA;n = 36) performed a simple reaction-time task to auditory (A), visual (V), and audiovisual (AV) stimuli. Analyses targeted event-related potentials (ERPs), alpha-band event-related desynchronization (α-ERD), and long-range theta-band functional connectivity. Groups did not differ across unisensory measures, indicating comparable unisensory processing. By contrast, multisensory integration (MSI;AV-(A+V)) differed across groups: NA children showed significant ERP MSI over parieto-central sites that was absent in AU and SIB; and α-ERD MSI was significantly reduced in AU, with SIB showing an intermediate profile. Connectivity analyses revealed reduced AV fronto-parieto-occipital coupling in autistic children relative to non-autistic children, suggesting weaker large-scale coordination during multisensory processing. These results point to a multisensory-specific deficit spanning early sensory encoding, posterior α-ERD, and fronto-posterior coupling and support disrupted multisensory influences on sensory processing due to reduced multisensory attentional orienting. SIB profiles suggest inherited liability for these neural phenotypes. These results help explain well-documented behavioral MSI differences in autism by linking impaired early enhancement with attenuated top-down control of sensory cortex.

items.title: Prefrontal Cortical Changes With Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement in Opioid Use Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: Despite decades of clinical implementation of medications for opioid use disorder (OUD), overdose mortality rates remain high, underscoring a critical need for interventions that target the brain mechanisms underlying addiction. To assess the neural mechanisms of Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) and their associations with clinical outcomes, including craving and abstinence duration. This randomized clinical trial was conducted from November 2020 to September 2024 among individuals with OUD recruited from an inpatient rehabilitation facility in New York and randomized to MORE or psychoeducational supportive therapy (PST). Data were analyzed from October 2024 to August 2026. Treatment with MORE (comprising training in mindfulness, drug cue reappraisal, and savoring positive experiences) or PST (active control condition) across 8 weekly 2-hour group sessions. Outcomes included treatment-related changes in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) blood oxygen level-dependent signal (primary), abstinence length (secondary), and cue-induced craving (secondary). Drug cue reactivity task analyses included 59 participants (MORE, n = 24; 5 women [20.8%]; mean [SD] age, 43.6 [11.3] years; PST, n = 35; 8 women [22.9%]; mean [SD] age, 42.8 [10.0] years). Movie-watching and follow-up analyses were conducted in subsets of 37 (MORE, n = 18; PST, n = 19) and 38 participants (MORE, n = 13; PST, n = 25), respectively. Compared with PST, MORE reduced drug-biased activity in the middle frontal gyrus and other brain areas, including the precuneus, during downregulation of responses to drug cues relative to upregulation of responses to natural reward cues (even when controlling for passive cue viewing; z > 3.1; P 3.1; P < .05). Relative to PST, MORE also reduced medial PFC synchronization to naturalistic drug-related movie scenes (q = 0.019) and significantly extended abstinence duration at follow-up (approximately 4 months posttreatment; χ2 = 6.7; P = .04; Cohen w = 0.19). This neuroimaging randomized clinical trial demonstrates that MORE may restructure function in PFC nodes of the reward, salience, and control networks, positioning it as a biologically grounded adjunct to pharmacotherapy for OUD. items.title: Susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors in relation to visual working memory in children with and without attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
items.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder associated with increased distractibility. Previous research has reported that susceptibility to task-irrelevant visual distraction is linked with visual working memory (WM) capacity in adults. Here, we examined how neural susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors related to visual WM capacity in children with and without ADHD. Across two experiments, electroencephalography (EEG) signals were recorded from 146 Chinese children aged 7-15 (63 with ADHD, 23% girls; collected in 2022-2024), during which they performed visual tasks of varying difficulty with auditory distractors. The mismatch negativity (MMN) amplitude was measured as neural susceptibility to auditory distractors, and a K-score was calculated to assess visual WM capacity. In typically developing (TD) children, those with higher visual WM capacity showed less susceptibility to auditory distractors under high audiovisual competition (r = 0.494), whereas this relation reversed under low competition (r = -0.319). Conversely, in children with ADHD, lower visual WM capacity predicted higher susceptibility under both high (r = 0.442) and low competition (r = 0.326). These findings indicate that susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distraction is related to visual WM capacity in children, but the patterns differ between typical and atypical neurodevelopment and are modulated by audiovisual competition.

items.title: Naturalistic Movie Viewing Reveals a Distributed Network Supporting Audiovisual Speech Processing
items.abstract: Traditional paradigms in cognitive neuroscience often fail to capture the richness of real-world experiences. To bridge this gap, researchers increasingly use naturalistic stimuli such as movies, which provide complex, multisensory input. Speech perception is a prime example of such complexity: it is inherently multisensory, involving the integration of auditory cues, lip movements, and facial expressions. Prior studies suggest that the left posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS) and superior temporal gyrus (STG) play a critical role in this integration. However, most studies of audiovisual speech have relied on simplified or artificial stimuli, limiting ecological validity. To address these gaps, we analyzed fMRI data from human participants watching two full-length films (500 Days of Summer, Citizenfour) to assess the consistency of multisensory speech processes across distinct genres and narratives. We manually annotated word onset times and modality (audiovisual vs. auditory-only). Across two movies and 38 participants we observed consistent speech-related activation in the pSTS and STG across speech types. Compared to auditory-only speech, audiovisual speech recruited a broad left-lateralized network including the angular gyrus, posterior temporal cortex, temporal pole, and inferior frontal gyrus, along with the right cerebellum. These findings were also consistently present in single-subject data. Importantly, most of the regions observed in our analyses have been implicated in multisensory function in the nonhuman primate literature despite receiving relatively little focus in human neuroimaging. Together our results demonstrate that speech processing during naturalistic viewing recruits a distributed network extending substantially beyond regions traditionally emphasized in audiovisual speech research.

items.title: Towards a scalable effective connectivity estimation in fMRI
items.abstract: Characterizing directed connections between brain regions is fundamental for understanding the brain’s network organization and how it supports cognitive processes. However, a reliable methodology allowing assessment of effective connectivity (EC) at the whole-brain level and across high-resolution parcellations has remained elusive. This limitation reflects a trade-off between model detail and scalability. Mechanistic approaches such as Dynamic Causal Modeling (DCM) provide a principled description of directed interactions but become impractical for large parcellations, whereas scalable methods based on linear-system inversion often fail to reliably recover key features of the underlying effective connectivity. Here, using data from the Human Connectome Project S1200 release, we show that the multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (mOU) approach for EC estimation can be adapted to yield EC estimates that are in broad agreement with those of an advanced DCM, at least when the spatial variability of the hemodynamic response falls within the physiological range characteristic of the healthy adult brain. Furthermore, thanks to its low computational cost, mOU can be easily scaled up to large neuroimaging cohorts and high-resolution parcellations. High-resolution, mOU-based EC outperforms functional connectivity for single-subject connectome fingerprinting. In addition, it enables a high-resolution characterization of the brain’s hierarchical organization and modular architecture by identifying directed interactions within and between communities and revealing driver and receiver regions. Overall, our methodology provides a reliable and scalable EC estimation pipeline of wide applicability to cognitive and network neuroscience.

items.title: Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Dementia: From Network Degeneration to Compassionate and Skilled Care
items.abstract: Dementia is a progressive syndrome characterized by neurodegeneration across distributed brain networks that results in cognitive, behavioral, and functional declines. Conventional psychoeducation provides disease facts and resources but often lacks the mechanistic grounding needed to translate knowledge into durable caregiver skills. Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) extends traditional approaches by offering brain-based explanations of symptoms and caregiving challenges, paired with learning principles optimized for stressed learners. This chapter proposes a dementia-specific NIPE framework grounded in network-level neuroscience and cognitive reserve, specifying core content domains across the disease course, delivery structures, and mechanism of efficacy. The chapter synthesizes evidence for effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, cultural adaptation, clinician training, and outcome measurement, presenting NIPE as a pragmatic approach to strengthening person-centered dementia care.

items.title: Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in the Era of Environmental Sustainability: Can We Achieve Excellence?
items.abstract: Background The healthcare sector is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, prompting an urgent need for environmentally sustainable practices. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management presents unique challenges in this context due to the frequent use of metered-dose inhalers containing high global warming potential propellants and the resource-intensive nature of acute exacerbations. Methods This expert consensus paper explores how COPD care can be optimized to reduce environmental impact, while maintaining high standards of clinical effectiveness. We examine the patient journey, adherence patterns, and therapeutic strategies, including the role of single-inhaler triple therapy in preventing exacerbation, as determinants of healthcare-related emissions. Results The potential of dry powder inhalers, accurate diagnosis, patient engagement, and sustained disease stability are highlighted as levers for environmentally sustainable care. We advocate for the integration of environmental impact as a formal outcome in randomized controlled trials, supported by standardized Life Cycle Assessment methodologies. Conclusions Our findings suggest that environmentally conscious COPD management is not only possible but may enhance clinical outcomes and system sustainability.

items.title: Widening educational inequalities for young people attending child and adolescent mental health services: a longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Background A 'mortality gap' is well-documented in individuals with severe mental illness but an 'education gap' emerges much earlier in life, with major long-term consequences. While educational attainment has improved in most high-income countries in recent decades, it is unknown whether these improvements have narrowed the education gap for young people who attend child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). Methods This nationwide, longitudinal cohort study used linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) databank for a large cohort of individuals in Wales born between 1992 and 2003 and followed to 2019. We compared performance on the General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) exams, taken at age 16, between young people with and without prior CAMHS contact. We divided the population into two sequential birth cohorts (1992-1997 vs 1998-2003) and tested whether the association between CAMHS contact and failure to achieve key GCSE thresholds changed over time. Results In the total population, the proportion of young people failing to achieve the basic GCSE level one threshold fell from 6.9% in the older (1992-1997) cohort to 3.7% in the younger (1998-2003) cohort. Young people who attended CAMHS, however, were significantly more likely to fail to achieve level one GCSEs in both cohorts (aOR = 4.28, 95% CI = 4.08, 4.48). Critically, this gap widened over time for GCSE Level-1 attainment, both for CAMHS outpatients (interaction aOR = 1.30, 95% CI = 1.20, 1.40) and CAMHS inpatients (interaction aOR = 1.80, 95% CI = 1.47, 2.19). Conclusions Despite overall improvements in educational attainment in the general population, there is a growing gap in educational attainment between young people accessing CAMHS and their peers. The failure to attain basic qualifications may lead to lifelong socioeconomic disadvantage. Research on how to effectively address the educational needs of young people attending CAMHS is an urgent economic and public health issue.

Data were analysed using an inductive thematic analysis based on a hybrid approach combining artificial intelligence-powered coding through ChatGPT-4 with manual triangulation.ResultsThree main themes were identified: (1) experiences and perceptions of pain, including the nature and characterization of pain and its relationship with Parkinson's disease; (2) the impact of pain on daily life; and (3) feelings associated with pain, including emotional changes related to pain and its broader psychological impact.ConclusionsPain in people with Parkinson's disease is an interconnected and context-dependent experience extending beyond its physical manifestations. items.title: The impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty in old age: A systematic literature review and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM).
items.abstract: BackgroundFrailty is common in older adults and associated with inadequate nutrition, reduced physical function, and increased vulnerability. While physical exercise benefits frailty outcomes, evidence on combined nutrition and exercise interventions remains unclear.AimTo systematically review evidence on the impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty status among community-dwelling frail older adults (≥65 years).MethodsThe review followed the Cochrane Handbook, Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidelines. Searches were conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus. Randomised controlled trials explicitly defining frailty were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and assessed methodology using RoB 2.0. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis without meta-analysis was performed.SummaryOf 2447 records identified, 10 publications met the inclusion criteria. Two trials directly assessed frailty reversal and reported improvements favouring structured exercise, with one showing additional benefit when combined with a nutritional supplement. Odds of frailty reversal ranged from two- to fivefold. Additional studies reported modest improvements in mobility disability risk, lean body mass, and functional performance. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high, limited by small samples and heterogeneity.Although some studies reported favourable effects of combined nutrition and exercise interventions, the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether nutrition adds benefits beyond exercise alone. Structured exercise consistently benefited frailty-related outcomes. However, due to few studies and substantial heterogeneity, firm conclusions cannot be drawn. Further standardised trials are needed to clarify the role of nutritional components within combined nutrition-exercise interventions in frailty management.

items.title: Content Adaptations and Usability Improvements in a Brazilian Digital Mental Health Platform: Lessons Learned from Iterative User-Centered Research.
items.abstract: Introduction: Digital mental health interventions are especially relevant in low- and middle-income countries, where access to face-to-face care is limited. However, many platforms insufficiently incorporate user experience, reducing engagement and effectiveness, particularly among vulnerable populations. Methods: This study adopted an exploratory mixed-methods approach conducted across four sequential phases to improve a Brazilian digital mental health platform focused on anxiety and stress management. Data were collected from four sources: focus groups with 36 community leaders from a low-income urban area; surveys with 36 highly educated users; think-aloud usability interviews with 10 participants; and an online survey with 102 young adults. Qualitative and quantitative data were integrated to identify design and content gaps. Results: Participants consistently reported the need for culturally resonant language, shorter and more dynamic videos, greater diversity among presenters, and improved visual design and accessibility. These findings guided platform adaptations, including revised audiovisual formats, updated language and imagery, and enhanced accessibility features. The results reinforce the importance of user-centered and culturally sensitive design in digital mental health tools, particularly in socially diverse contexts. Conclusion: Findings suggest that user-centered adaptation processes can help improve the usability and cultural relevance of digital mental health interventions.

items.title: Extent, Clinical Consequences, and Temporal Changes of Traumatic Dental Injuries Among 12-Year-Old Brazilian Adolescents: A Repeated Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Background/aim Population studies of traumatic dental injuries often focus on prevalence, providing limited information on severity and clinical relevance. This study characterized traumatic dental injuries by extent, distribution, and clinical consequences among Brazilian 12-year-olds, examined associated factors, and assessed temporal changes between 2010 and 2023. Material and methods Data from the 2023 Brazilian National Oral Health Survey included 6680 participants with valid injury data and were compared with 2010 data from 7241 participants with valid injury data. Injuries were assessed in the eight permanent incisors. Outcomes included overall and tooth-specific prevalence, extent (number of affected teeth), and clinically consequential injuries, defined as enamel-dentin fracture, pulpal involvement, or tooth loss. Associations and temporal comparisons used survey-weighted Poisson regression. Results In 2023, traumatic dental injury prevalence was 13.66%, and 31.15% of affected adolescents had two or more injured teeth. No sociodemographic or clinical characteristic was associated with overall injury occurrence or multiple-tooth involvement after adjustment. Among affected adolescents, clinically consequential injuries were more prevalent in females than males (adjusted prevalence ratio, 3.16; 95% confidence interval, 1.32-7.55). From 2010 to 2023, overall prevalence decreased from 21.47% to 13.66%. Adjusted prevalence ratios for 2023 versus 2010 were 0.61 for overall injury and 0.62 for clinically consequential injury, with no evidence of change in multiple-tooth involvement. The largest tooth-specific reductions occurred in the maxillary central incisors, while four of eight incisors showed no evidence of change. Conclusions In 2023, traumatic dental injuries affected approximately one in seven Brazilian 12-year-olds. No adjusted associations were evident for overall occurrence or multiple-tooth involvement, although clinically consequential injuries were more prevalent among females. Overall traumatic dental injury occurrence declined between 2010 and 2023. Among affected adolescents, adjusted analysis suggested a lower prevalence of clinically consequential injuries in 2023, although this estimate was less precise.

items.title: Resource waves across snowpacks and alpine vegetation extend seasonal resource availability in alpine ecosystems.
items.abstract: Alpine ecosystems are energy-limited and highly seasonal. Consumers in the alpine zone must track rapidly shifting windows of prey availability during the short growing season. Prolonged snowmelt creates a mosaic of persistent snowfields, scrubs and alpine tundra. In addition to vegetation-dwelling arthropods, wind-transported arthropods deposited on snowpacks, known as arthropod fallout, provide an allochthonous subsidy from lower elevations to alpine environments. Asynchronous arthropod phenology across alpine vegetation and snowpack may create resource waves and prolong food availability for alpine consumers. However, no multi-mountain studies have jointly quantified the phenology of vegetation-dwelling arthropods and arthropod fallout. We examined whether phenological asynchrony between arthropod fallout on snowpacks and vegetation-dwelling arthropods creates sequential resource peaks that extend food availability for alpine consumers. Across three mountains in the Japanese Alps (Tateyama, Norikura and Kisokoma) along broad climatic gradients, we sampled arthropods over 2 years at half-monthly intervals from late May to early August on alpine snowpacks and in alpine vegetation, including Japanese stone pine scrub and alpine tundra. Seasonal changes in arthropod biomass were estimated using taxon-specific length-mass regressions. Community structures of arthropods were analysed using non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS). Seasonal changes in abundance and biomass of arthropods on vegetation and snowpacks were examined using generalised linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs). Aphids dominated on snowpacks, whereas Diptera were most abundant in vegetation. Arthropod abundance peaked sequentially across habitats, occurring early on snowpacks, mid-season in Japanese stone pine scrub and late in alpine tundra. Biomass was high early on snowpacks but increased later in vegetation, with the increase occurring earlier in scrub than in alpine tundra. Our findings suggest that arthropod fallout and vegetation-dwelling arthropods provide food resources for alpine consumers during different periods of the growing season. These sequential peaks in arthropod abundance and biomass create resource waves that extend seasonal food availability for consumers. Warming and earlier snowmelt may disrupt these resource waves through taxon-specific responses to changing temperature and snow conditions. Conserving the snow-scrub-tundra mosaic and its temporal complementarity should therefore be a priority for sustaining alpine biodiversity under rapid climate change.

items.title: Crosstalk along the gut-liver axis in liver disease: Clinical and mechanistic aspects.
items.abstract: The gut and liver are anatomically and physiologically interconnected, forming a dynamic axis that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of many liver diseases. Gut-derived factors can influence hepatic injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, acting both as disease modifiers and, in some cases, as primary drivers of aetiology. Conversely, liver-derived factors including bile acids shape microbial ecology, epithelial barrier function, and intestinal immune homeostasis. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical and mechanistic aspects of the gut-liver axis in hepatology. Using autoimmune, metabolic, and toxic hepatobiliary disorders as model conditions, we highlight recent advances in understanding how intestinal permeability, microbiota composition, and immune signalling contribute to disease initiation and progression. Emphasis is placed on the bidirectional nature of gut-liver interactions and their implications for disease stratification, prevention, and therapy. Finally, we identify key knowledge gaps and outline priorities for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

items.title: Functional divergence of biochar and nano-Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> in microbial chain elongation: Adsorptive regulation as an overlooked equilibrium driver.
items.abstract: Microbial chain elongation (CE) offers a promising route for producing medium-chain carboxylic acids (MCFAs), but its performance is often limited by product accumulation and associated inhibition. Here, biochar was shown to enhance CE not only by improving initial performance but, more importantly, by sustaining MCFA production through adsorption-mediated regulation, in contrast to nano-Fe 3 O 4 . Notably, secondary biochar addition to steady-state fermentation broth reinitiated substrate consumption and led to additional butyrate production. Nano-Fe 3 O 4 , while achieving a higher initial caproate concentration (14.35 ± 0.86 g COD/L, 1.82-fold of the control) through enhanced electron transfer, did not further stimulate CE once steady state was reached. Adsorption analysis showed that biochar retained 2146.7 mg COD/L of caproate and 756.9 mg COD/L of butyrate, substantially lowering dissolved product concentrations. Thermodynamic evaluation revealed that this in situ adsorption reduced product activity and increased the driving force for chain elongation, thereby increasing the apparent thermodynamic driving force and sustaining MCFA formation under near-steady-state conditions. These findings highlight adsorption-mediated equilibrium regulation as a previously overlooked mechanism by which biochar prolongs CE performance.

items.title: Zero-valent iron powder- and sponge iron-biochar composites drive enhanced nitrate conversion in autotrophic nitrate reduction by distinct electron delivery strategies.
items.abstract: Iron-mediated autotrophic denitrification is promising for low-carbon wastewater treatment because it requires little external carbon and avoids secondary pollution. Current studies show that enhanced electron transfer between iron and carbon may improve its nitrogen removal efficiency, while the intermediate processes and mechanisms of electron-transfer mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. Therefore, in this study iron powder (IP) and sponge iron (SI) were combined with conductive biochar to construct iron-carbon autotrophic denitrification systems. And we compared the system's denitrification performance, iron corrosion characteristics, and microbial responses. Results revealed that both iron sources enhanced nitrate reduction. However, IP was associated with more pronounced accumulation of NH 4 + and NO 2 - , whereas SI produced fewer intermediate metabolites. Corrosion of the iron substrates produced conductive Fe 3 O 4 , which bonded with organic matter coating the biochar surface, creating an "iron oxide-biochar-biofilm" conductive network thereby enhancing the potential for extracellular electron transfer within the system. The two systems showed different microbial responses. The IP system developed a community dominated by Thiobacillus, and genes associated with the dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) were significantly enriched, indicating a strong tendency toward DNRA in the system. In contrast, the SI system supports diverse and synergistic microbial networks; the simultaneous enrichment of denitrification genes and electron transport genes promotes the relatively complete conversion of nitrogen into gaseous nitrogen for removal. This study provides a mechanistic basis for the design and operational optimization of iron-based autotrophic denitrification materials for low C/N wastewater.

items.title: Biochar-immobilised phosphate-solubilising bacteria enhance soil available phosphorus by affecting phosphorus fraction transformation and phosphorus-acquiring microbiota.
items.abstract: Phosphate-solubilising bacteria (PSB) play an important role in phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P uptake. However, their effectiveness is often limited by environmental instability and soil poor survival. Biochar has been proposed as a suitable carrier for microbial immobilisation; however, the effects of biochar-immobilised PSB on soil P fractions and the microbial mechanisms underlying P transformation remain unclear. In this study, we developed a biochar-immobilised PSB using Klebsiella sp. N107 and assessed its effects on soil P availability, P fraction transformation, and microbial processes regulating P cycling. A pot experiment was conducted: no fertilisation, conventional fertilisation (NPK), NPK + pristine biochar (NPKB), NPK + PSB (NPKP), and NPK + biochar-immobilised PSB (NPKBP). Soil properties, P fractions, organic acids, enzyme activities, and metagenomic characteristics were analysed. Compared with NPKB and NPKP, NPKBP enhanced plant P uptake and soil available P. It also increased labile P fractions, organic acid concentrations, and the activities of P acquiring enzymes. Genes associated with P transport (pit, ugpB, ugpQ, and ugpE), polyphosphate degradation (ppk1 and ppk2), organic P mineralisation (phoA and phoD), and inorganic P solubilisation (gcd, ppa, and ppx) were upregulated. P acquiring taxa, including Sphingomonas, Gaiella, and Bradyrhizobium, were enriched and contributed functionally to P cycling. Overall, biochar-immobilised PSB improved soil P availability by promoting P fraction transformation and restructuring microbial communities involved in P cycling. Soil pH, organic acids, and available nitrogen were identified as key drivers of these processes, highlighting the potential of biochar-immobilised PSB to improve soil P utilisation and management.

items.title: Shotgun Metagenomic Profiling of Phlebotomus papatasi (Diptera: Psychodidae, Phlebotomine) in Zoonotic Cutaneous Leishmaniasis Endemic Foci of Iraq: Microbiota, Resistome, and Virulome.
items.abstract: This study aims to develop a regional baseline for future individual-level and comparative studies of microbial ecology and symbiont-based vector control. Phlebotomus papatasi is a major vector of Leishmania major and an important component of the transmission cycle of zoonotic cutaneous leishmaniasis (ZCL) in Iraq, although the internal microbial communities of this vector are poorly characterised in the region. In this study, shotgun metagenomic sequencing was employed to investigate the microbial communities of a pooled sample of 129 blood-fed female Ph. papatasi collected from ZCL-endemic foci in Nineveh Governorate, Iraq, from 2024 to 2025. Approximately 32.9 million raw reads were obtained from sequencing, with the quality-filtered, host-removed, and low-diversity-filtered reads analysed for taxonomic and functional profiles. The data revealed a complex microbial community inside blood-fed Ph. papatasi dominated by bacteria. Moreover, several species of Proteobacteria in blood-fed Ph. papatasi were detected, which accounted for 98.32% of the classified reads, with Enterobacter cloacae as the most common species (74.34% of classified reads). Strains associated with Wolbachia were also detected (approximately 8.96% of classified reads). The microbial data further revealed the presence of genes associated with antimicrobial resistance including oqxA/oqxB-associated efflux and AmpC-type β-lactamase families, and virulence factors associated with motility, iron acquisition, and secretion systems. Nevertheless, the data represented the distribution of sequencing reads within the pooled sample (single sample), rather than the prevalence or average abundance among individual sand flies.

items.title: Tissue-specific transcriptional reprogramming in the fat body is associated with long-term immune protection in Galleria mellonella after immune priming with Bacillus species.
items.abstract: Background Immune priming in insects is well-documented, but its persistence across larval development and the tissue-specific mechanisms remain poorly understood. Whether closely related bacteria differ in inducing durable memory and whether protection correlates with transcriptional reprogramming in specific organs is unclear. Methods First-instar Galleria mellonella larvae were orally primed with inactivated Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. galleriae (Bt), B. cereus (Bc), or B. subtilis (Bs) and challenged at fourth-instar with virulent Bt subsp. galleriae. Survival was recorded for 7 days, and phenoloxidase activity was measured in hemolymph 24 h post-challenge. In parallel, fourth-instar larvae received the same cells; at 12 h, transcription of 10 immune genes was analyzed in hemocytes, fat body, and midgut, and lysozyme-like activity was measured in the midgut at 24 h. Results Immune priming was species-specific: Bt conferred strong homologous protection against Bt subps. Galleriae (82% survival), Bc moderate cross-protection (60%), Bs none (27%). Protection correlated specifically with Toll pathway activation and AMP induction in the fat body, whereas Bs triggered strong hemocyte responses yet failed to activate the fat body or restore PO activity. Conclusion Oral priming in G. mellonella is species-specific and organ-compartmentalized. Effective long-term protection requires transcriptional reprogramming in the fat body, whereas hemocyte-restricted activation is insufficient - revealing that immune memory is organized at the organ level rather than systemically. These findings link tissue-specific responses to protective efficacy.

items.title: PBDE-to-OPE Substitution in Urban Greenspace Soils: OPE-Dominated Burdens and Endpoint-Specific Risk Priorities.
items.abstract: The phaseout of polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) and expanded use of organophosphate esters (OPEs) have reshaped flame-retardant contamination, yet how legacy PBDEs and emerging OPEs coexist in urban soils, and how this coexistence reshapes risk priorities, remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 230 surface soil samples from 49 greenspace sites in Shenzhen, China, for 12 PBDEs and 14 OPEs and evaluated their occurrence, sources and risks. Median ΣOPEs (233 ng/g dry weight, dw) was 22-fold higher than median ΣPBDEs (10.6 ng/g dw), indicating strong OPE dominance in present-day soil burdens. OPE distributions were positively correlated with human activity indicators, whereas PBDEs were more closely associated with soil properties, particularly organic matter. Despite the concentration dominance of OPEs, risk priorities differed by endpoint. OPEs dominated ecological risk and contributed 99.8% of total carcinogenic risk, whereas residual PBDEs contributed 66.9% of total noncarcinogenic hazard despite accounting for only 4.2% of total concentration. Source-resolved analysis further showed that the mass-dominant Alkyl-OPE-rich source was not the dominant contributor to health risk: noncarcinogenic hazard was driven mainly by a legacy PBDE source, whereas carcinogenic risk was dominated by a TDCIPP-rich foam-related factor. Although estimated human health risks remained within commonly used risk threshold, these results show that PBDE-to-OPE substitution can produce endpoint-specific risk priorities, highlighting the need for source-resolved and toxicity-weighted assessment to prioritize contaminants and sources when managing legacy and emerging contaminants in urban soils.

items.title: Plastic Film Mulching Affects Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons Contamination in Farmland Soils across Mainland China: Nationwide Comparison.
items.abstract: The application of plastic mulch films is widespread in contemporary agriculture, and China alone consumes more than any other country. However, the contamination and sources of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), which exhibit carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic toxicity, remain unclear in farmlands with and without mulching nationwide in mainland China, as does the influence of plastic mulch films on PAH accumulation. Topsoil samples were simultaneously obtained in this study from mulched and non-mulched farmlands across mainland China to systematically compare the contamination characteristics of PAHs and to analyze the influence of plastic mulching. The results demonstrate that mulched farmland had significantly lower PAH levels than non-mulched farmland (p 0.05). PAHs in mulched farmland were predominantly derived from field-scale agricultural sources and nearby traffic emissions, whereas those in non-mulched farmland were characterized by regional-scale atmospheric mixed inputs. North China exhibited the highest proportions (exceeding 70%) of both mulched and non-mulched farmlands posing potential cancer risks to humans, whereas Northwest China showed the lowest proportions (below 20%). Influenced by plastic mulching, the abundances of film-microplastics and fiber-microplastics were significantly positively correlated with PAH concentrations in mulched farmland (p < 0.05) and could serve as indicators of PAH contamination in mulched farmland, but showed no significant correlation in non-mulched farmland. This study provides evidence for differentiated pollution prevention and control strategies in mulched versus non-mulched farmland systems.

items.title: Lead-Aggravated Duodenal Barrier Injury Accompanied by Fecal Microbiota Alterations in 5xFAD Mice.
items.abstract: Lead (Pb) is a persistent environmental toxicant, yet its effects on intestinal homeostasis in the 5xFAD background remain poorly characterized. Six-month-old 5xFAD mice were exposed to 200 μg/L Pb in drinking water for 8 weeks, with age-matched wild-type and unexposed 5xFAD mice serving as reference groups. We integrated duodenal metal profiling, mucosal architecture assessment, proteomic analysis, and fecal 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the Pb-associated intestinal responses. Pb exposure increased duodenal Pb burden and reduced Ca, Cu, and Mg concentrations relative to unexposed 5xFAD mice. These elemental changes were accompanied by more pronounced villus shortening, crypt deepening, a lower villus height-to-crypt depth ratio, and loss of AB-PAS-positive goblet cells, suggesting impaired mucosal architecture and mucus-associated protection. Duodenal proteomic screening identified Pb-associated patterns involving epithelial junction organization, cell adhesion, calcium signaling, mineral absorption, complement activation, and mucosal immune pathways. In parallel, Pb-exposed 5xFAD mice showed lower fecal microbial richness and diversity than the unexposed 5xFAD mice, together with reduced abundances of Lachnospiraceae-related commensals and compositional shifts involving taxa associated with inflammatory or barrier-stress responses. Chronic Pb exposure in 5xFAD mice was associated with concurrent changes in duodenal metal homeostasis, mucosal structure, pathway-level proteomic profiles, and distal fecal microbial ecology. The duodenal findings highlight the proximal small intestine as a relevant peripheral site of Pb toxicity.
