items.title: Probabilistic Stellar Mass and Radius Estimation with Bayesian Hierarchical Stacking
items.abstract: Accurate stellar parameters are essential for the characterisation of exoplanets, yet most host stars lack direct measurements of mass and radius. We aim to predict stellar masses and radii from commonly available observables and to quantify uncertainties and systematic effects in a way that is consistent with stellar observations. By not relying on a single model, we aim to obtain more robust predictive distributions and reduce sensitivity to model misspecification and outliers. We develop a Bayesian machine-learning framework that combines three probabilistic models through Bayesian hierarchical stacking (BHS): a Bayesian additive regression tree model, a two-process heteroscedastic sparse Gaussian process, and a hierarchical Bayesian neural network. The method propagates measurement uncertainties, accounts for correlations among inputs, and aggregates model variance into final predictive distributions. On a held-out test set the method attains a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 3.5% for mass and 2.1% for radius, improving on empirical-relation-based methods and standard machine-learning baselines. For 44 Kepler LEGACY stars, the BHS masses differ from estimates obtained with the BAyesian STellar Algorithm (BASTA) by a MARD of 4.8%, compared with 8.5% between the empirical relations and BASTA. Applied to about 2400 exoplanet host stars, the predictions differ from literature values by a MARD of 2.7% in both mass and radius. Residual analysis reveals mild underestimation for cool dwarfs, consistent with sparse training coverage, and positive offsets near the main-sequence turn-off that may reflect priors in isochrone-based catalogues. Internal consistency with g = GM/R^2 is greater for the BHS predictions, with a scatter in Delta log g lower by a factor of three than that of the literature values.

items.title: Counterfactual assessment of social media interventions by separating exposure from engagement
items.abstract: Social media interventions are usually evaluated in individual-level experiments, which are costly to scale and often miss collective effects. We propose the Exposure--Engagement model, whose parameters separately control what social media users are exposed to (recommendation) and how they engage (behaviour). After fitting it to the Italian Twitter debate (2018--2022), we validate it at individual and collective levels. We simulate behavioural interventions (prebunking and accuracy prompts), calibrated on effect sizes, and a recommender-system intervention (chronological feed), comparing effects on engagement, attention diversity, and segregation. All three reduce engagement. Behavioural interventions slightly reduce diversity, leaving segregation unchanged, whereas the chronological feed increases diversity and reduces segregation. For these interventions, changing recommendation does more for the debate's structure than changing behaviour. We design a recommender-system intervention that increases engagement and diversity while reducing segregation, although with about a tenth of the chronological feed's gains, showing the framework's potential for pro-social intervention design.

items.title: Searching for Circumplanetary Dust in the Cavity of the AB Aurigae Disk with ALMA
items.abstract: The young intermediate-mass star AB Aurigae is surrounded by a transition disk whose cavity contains several proposed protoplanets, including the debated source "AB Aur b" at a projected separation of $\approx 0.6$ arcsec ($\approx 93$ au). To search for circumplanetary material associated with these candidates, we have obtained the most sensitive ($\sim 20$ $μ$Jy/beam rms) and highest angular resolution ($\sim 30$ mas) ALMA Band 7 (0.88 mm) observations of AB Aur to date. We recover the asymmetric dust ring in the continuum emission peaking at $\sim 0.9$ arcsec ($\sim 140$ au) and compact emission at the stellar position, but detect no point source at the location of AB Aur b or any of the other proposed protoplanet candidates down to a $3σ$ limit of $60$ $μ$Jy. For optically thin emission, this corresponds to a dust mass of $\lesssim 0.0059 M_\oplus$ (for a dust temperature of 40 K), comparable to the circumplanetary disk around PDS 70 c. The $^{12}$CO emission fills the continuum cavity, revealing inner spiral structure and a clear rotation pattern. The gas at the position of AB Aur b is smoothly connected to the ambient disk with no localized excess or obvious kinematic deviation. If any proposed candidates are accreting, their circumplanetary material must have a low dust mass, a small physical size, dust that is optically thick, or a dearth of large mm-emitting grains.

items.title: Revisiting Sub-Neptune Population Synthesis: The Role of Core Luminosity in Boil-off, Photoevaporation, and the Radius Distribution
items.abstract: The observed bimodal radius distribution of close-in small planets provides important constraints on their formation and evolution. Two atmospheric escape mechanisms, photoevaporation and core-powered mass loss, have been widely invoked to explain this distribution. In this work, we revisit the physical assumptions underlying these models and investigate the role of core luminosity in driving outflows and shaping the radius distribution. We develop a population synthesis framework based on the SEAMIST evolution model, which self-consistently couples the two mass-loss mechanisms while accounting for envelope metallicity. We find that envelope metallicity strongly affects the resulting radius distribution, with 50-100$\times$ solar metallicity providing a good match to the observed population. Boil-off generally dominates atmospheric mass loss, while photoevaporation typically removes at most 3 wt\% of the envelope mass. We find that core luminosity contributes only $\sim$10-20\% of the thermal energy available for envelope re-equilibration during boil-off, producing an absolute mass-loss enhancement of only $\sim$0.4wt\%. Its effect is larger during photoevaporation, where the longer mass-loss timescale allows core heating to accumulate. Nevertheless, core luminosity has little impact on the long-term planetary radius distribution. These results suggest that core-powered mass loss is better understood as a modification to atmospheric escape through its lower-boundary conditions rather than as a distinct mass-loss mechanism. In our best-fit model, the radiative atmosphere contributes a significant $\sim$20\% of the total optical radius. Consequently, we highlight the need for improved radiative-atmosphere modeling in sub-Neptune evolution models to better understand the observed population distribution.

items.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
items.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their hosts stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants as well as chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca ii triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profile characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85-145019.95, a new gas disc system which exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 Rsun to 0.34 Rsun and from 0.54 Rsun to 1.93 Rsun. We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few km to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

items.title: Temporal Ecology of the Grapevine Microbiome: A Framework for Assembly, Persistence and Disease in Perennial Crops
items.abstract: Plant microbiome studies increasingly resolve community composition, but evidence derived largely from annual-plant models and cross-sectional surveys remains poorly suited to reconstruct ecological history in woody crops. We propose grapevine as an information-rich reference system for temporal microbiome ecology because clonal propagation, grafting, nursery-to-vineyard transfer, organs with contrasting lifespans, recurrent management and chronic disease align assembly processes across nested timescales. We synthesise current evidence into a four-clock framework spanning microbial arrival and establishment over days to weeks, seasonal organ renewal, multi-year field transitions and decades of host ageing and disease development. Grapevine compartments can be treated as a candidate connected metacommunity in which source pools, dispersal, abiotic and host filtering, and priority effects shape residence. Disturbance may elicit resistant, resilient or history-dependent responses. This framework separates pathogen detection from microbial activity, tissue damage and symptom expression, and views chronic disease as a trajectory in host-microbiome function. We identify the limits of current amplicon-based and cross-sectional evidence and propose designs combining individual-level longitudinal sampling, quantitative load, spatial and functional multi-omics, cultivation, synthetic communities and multisite validation. The framework generates testable hypotheses for separating temporal association from persistence, legacy, memory and disease causation across perennial crop systems.

items.title: A Bayesian functional model with multilevel partition priors for group studies in neuroscience.
items.abstract: The statistical analysis of group studies in neuroscience is particularly challenging due to the complex spatio-temporal nature of the data, its multiple levels and the inter-individual variability in brain responses. Traditional ANOVA-based studies and linear mixed effects models typically provide only a limited exploration of the dynamics of group brain activity and of the variability in individual responses, potentially leading to overly simplistic conclusions and/or missing more intricate patterns. In this study we propose a novel Bayesian model-based clustering approach for functional data that simultaneously assesses group effects and individual deviations across the main temporal features in the data. To this end, we develop a multilevel partition prior to model the functional scores arising from a functional Principal Components decomposition of neuroscientific recordings. The proposed approach enables a thorough exploration of group differences and individual deviations without compromising on the spatio-temporal nature of the data. Through a simulation study we demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves correct classification in different clustering scenarios under low and high noise levels in the data. Finally, we consider an Electroencephalogram case study involving an object recognition task, where the proposed approach provides new insights into the underlying brain mechanisms generating the data and their variability.

items.title: Reciprocal blockade of the opioid and D2-like dopamine receptors in the nucleus accumbens modulates the pain-related behaviors in an animal model of inflammatory pain.
items.abstract: Studies showed that dopamine and opioid systems in the brain have essential role in the modulation of pain perception. The evidence indicated that in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), both dopamine type 2 (D2) receptors and opioid receptors are highly expressed. However, the interaction of these systems in NAc was not investigated in the modulation of inflammatory pain. One hundred twenty-six adult male Wistar rats received unilateral microinjections of different doses of morphine (2.5, 5, 10, and 25 mmol/0.5 μl) and quinpirole (8, 16, and 32 mmol/0.5 μl) to assess their effects as opioid and D2-like receptor agonists in the NAc. In the next step, the rats were administered varying doses of sulpiride (3, 6, 12, and 24 mmol/0.5 μl), a D2-like receptor antagonist, before an effective dose of quinpirole (32 mmol/0.5 μl). They also received naloxone (1.5, 5, and 15 mmol/0.5 μl) before the same effective dose of quinpirole (32 mmol/0.5 μl). The formalin test was employed to evaluate their inflammatory pain thresholds. Results indicated that intra-accumbal administration of morphine- and quinpirole-induced antinociceptive responses. However, sulpiride significantly diminished these responses. Naloxone also reduced the quinpirole's antinociceptive effects. Interestingly, sulpiride was less effective in reversing the analgesic effects of morphine (η2 = 0.17 in the first phase and η2 = 0.37 in the late phase) than naloxone in reversing the quinpirole's analgesic effects (η2 = 0.4 in the first phase and η2 = 0.53 in the late phase). These findings suggest an interaction between the opioidergic and dopaminergic systems in pain relief.

items.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for assessing fetal head descent during labor.
items.abstract: Objectives Ultrasound assessment of fetal head station is more accurate than digital examination, but its use is limited by the lack of equipment dedicated to the labor ward. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may overcome this barrier. We assessed the agreement between a handheld POCUS device and a conventional high-end system in measuring fetal head descent. Methods Seventy singleton pregnancies were examined in the second stage of labor. Two experienced operators, blinded to each other's results, performed translabial scans in randomized sequence, one with a handheld wireless device and one with a conventional system. Angle of progression (AoP) and head-perineum distance (HPD) were compared by intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Intraobserver repeatability was assessed in a subgroup by repeating both measurements de novo with each device. A blinded observer scored image quality (IQS) and measurement quality (MQS) from 0 to 3. Results Mean AoP was 121.8 (12.0)° with the conventional system and 121.9 (12.3)° with POCUS (p=0.71); mean HPD was 31.5 (7.8) and 31.4 (8.1) mm (p=0.69). The ICC was 0.96 (95 % CI 0.94-0.98) for AoP and 0.97 (0.95-0.98) for HPD, with a bias of 0.16° (limits of agreement -6.6 to 6.9) and -0.10 mm (-4.2 to 4.0). IQS and MQS did not differ between devices. Intraobserver ICC ranged from 0.93 to 0.98, with a within-subject coefficient of variation of 2.4-4.2 %. Conclusions Handheld POCUS measurements of fetal head descent agree closely with those obtained with conventional equipment, with comparable repeatability and image quality, and may facilitate wider use of intrapartum ultrasound.

items.title: Metal-Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores.
items.abstract: Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2-96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4-99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

items.title: Clinical detection and attribution of common disease in exposed populations.
items.abstract: Introduction Routine clinical assessment may misdiagnose or underdiagnose diseases such as chronic kidney disease (CKD), asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis when it fails to account for work and environmental exposure risks. Existing research addresses these diagnostic failures separately, and no published review organizes the diagnostic challenge by stages. In this study, we reviewed the evidence on exposure-informed assessment and developed a clinical framework that illustrates the stages of diagnostic loss. Content Building on the principles of the HIV care cascade, we conducted a framework synthesis. We searched Europe PMC, web-based sources, grey literature, and major burden-estimation reports for literature published from January 2000 onward. All the identified studies were categorized into six stages, namely clinical detection; disease classification; etiological attribution; reporting or compensation; death registration; cause-of-death coding. These studies were also further subdivided based upon the type of evidence provided; whether they showed changes in individual patient diagnoses or were solely derived from population trends or associated clinical findings. Summary Sixty-one sources contributed 64 findings. One study documented a change in individual diagnoses after systematic exposure assessment. At the population level, two studies found associations between exposure and increased prevalence of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Other studies described exposure-disease relationships including instances of gaps in screening and reporting, and limitations of gathering mortality records and accurately estimating disease burden. At the patient level, the evidence was sparse. Outlook This synthesis is hypothesis-generating. Routine clinical assessment may miss or misattribute common diseases when exposure history is treated as peripheral, instead of as a major part of the initial risk model. The clinical framework developed in this study demonstrates instances in which exposure-informed care could alter detection, classification, attribution, and management. Further studies are needed to establish and fully integrate it into clinical care.

items.title: More than a style: the association between managerial behaviors and nurse job satisfaction in Trinidad.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the association between specific nurse manager leadership behaviors and the job satisfaction levels of registered nurses in Trinidad. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, descriptive correlational design was employed. A convenience sample of 100 registered nurses from two major public hospitals completed an online survey incorporating the Leader Behavior Description Questionnaire (LBDQ-XII) and a researcher-developed Job Satisfaction Scale (Cronbach's a = 0.835). Data were analyzed using Spearman's rho correlations and Chi-square tests. Findings Behaviors reflecting Consideration (relationship-orientation) were significantly and positively correlated with satisfaction (r = 0.341, p Practical implications Healthcare organizations may consider viewing leadership not as an isolated solution, but as an organizational resource embedded within broader work environment strategies. While competency-based training in relational behaviors (such as active listening and constructive feedback) and balanced promotion criteria may support nurse managers, sustainable improvements in job satisfaction and retention likely require multi-pronged initiatives that concurrently address staffing adequacy, operational workloads and the escalating complexity of clinical care. Originality/value First empirical evidence linking specific managerial behaviors to nurse satisfaction in Trinidad and Tobago. Moving beyond broad leadership styles, it utilizes the LBDQ-XII to identify a specific behavioral imbalance, high task-orientation versus low relational support, as a primary factor associated with workforce dissatisfaction in the Caribbean context.

items.title: Ecology and conservation of subterranean biodiversity of Greater Lisbon, Portugal
items.abstract: Abstract Subterranean ecosystems harbour fauna moulded by extreme and stable conditions such as absence of light, narrow temperature ranges, high humidity and low availability of organic matter. The adaptations of cave fauna, coupled with the isolation of populations, often lead to a higher incidence of endemics and greater vulnerability to environmental changes. These ecosystems face severe threats caused by pollution and overexploitation, habitat loss and climate change, particularly evident in areas of increased human pressure as capitals of countries. In Portugal, more than 100 endemic cave‐adapted species have been identified, and close to its capital, highly urbanized and industrialized, the Greater Lisbon area hosts several unique endemic subterranean species that lack protection measures. We assessed the invertebrate faunal biodiversity and the conservation status of caves in the Greater Lisbon area. Our results show that arthropods dominate, in abundance and richness, the caves of the Greater Lisbon area, followed by molluscs. Ten endemic subterranean species were found, and of the 20 troglobionts recorded, 11 were found in only one cave, 5 in two caves and 4 in three or more. The overall most diverse was Poço Velho Cave, and the most troglobiont‐diverse was Alvide Cave, both in Cascais. Based on our results, we propose a preliminary conservation priority hierarchy for the studied caves. Our findings reveal that Greater Lisbon harbours irreplaceable subterranean habitats, that support diverse and exclusive invertebrate fauna, which face tremendous threats to their survival, underscoring the need for targeted conservation planning and biodiversity monitoring.

items.title: Two clinical trajectories in general adult psychiatry: divergent service use and mortality.
items.abstract: Background Psychiatric in-patient populations are heterogeneous. Severe and enduring psychiatric illness (SEPI) and trauma, stressor-related and substance use (TSRS) presentations differ clinically, but their service demands and mortality within one system are poorly characterised. Aims To characterise in-patient service use and mortality across clinical trajectories in one National Health Service general adult psychiatry (GAP) service. Method Longitudinal cohort study of 5204 in-patient episodes (2016-2024) aggregated to 2665 patients classified as SEPI (schizophrenia spectrum, bipolar disorder, severe unipolar depression) or TSRS, the latter subdivided into borderline personality disorder (BPD) and non-psychotic mood, stress-related and substance-use presentations. Analyses used person-years, standardised mortality ratios (SMRs), survival analysis and years of life lost. Results SEPI comprised 28.9% of patients but 69.3% of bed utilisation, with longer, recurrent admissions. TSRS presentations were brief and crisis-driven; BPD had the highest admission frequency with short stays. Cumulative mortality was 53% higher in SEPI than TSRS (13.5 v . 8.8%), but after adjustment for age and illness duration mortality was similar across groups (SMR 4.87). TSRS deaths occurred at younger ages, particularly in BPD, whereas SEPI deaths reflected common physical illnesses occurring far earlier than in the general population. Most deaths (98.5%) occurred outside in-patient settings. Conclusions GAP services accommodate two trajectories with contrasting demands but similarly high mortality (SMR 4.87): enduring, medically managed illness with high cumulative resource use, and episodic brief crisis presentations. Recognising this is essential for service design, since current models combine structurally distinct demands within a single system.

items.title: Healthcare use by people with dementia from diagnosis to the end of life: latent class and longitudinal analysis of linked healthcare data.
items.abstract: Background The first year after diagnosis and the last year of life are critical periods for people with dementia. Aims To (a) identify subgroups within a large sample of people with dementia, characterised by healthcare use in the year after diagnosis and the last year of life; (b) describe the biopsychosocial characteristics associated with these subgroups; and (c) explore moves between subgroups over time. Method A retrospective cohort of people diagnosed with dementia in London, UK, was assembled using linked clinical and administrative data-sets. We used latent class analysis to identify subgroups based on hospital and specialist mental healthcare service use in the year following diagnosis and the year before death. We used multinomial logistic regression to describe biopsychosocial characteristics and class membership, and latent transition analysis to explore moves between subgroups. Results Among 8623 people with dementia, we identified 3 subgroups of healthcare use in the year after diagnosis: 'low use' (49%), 'hospital use' (34%) and 'mental healthcare use' (17%). In the last year of life, four subgroups were identified: 'low use' (32%), 'moderate hospital use' (43%), 'high hospital use' (9%) and 'community healthcare use' (17%). Biopsychosocial factors, including age, ethnicity, and cognitive and physical problems, associated with subgroups differed for the time periods. Male gender, mixed dementia and vascular dementia diagnoses were associated with a higher risk of unplanned hospital use. Transition probabilities indicated unstable patterns of healthcare use after diagnosis and before death. Conclusions Distinct subgroups and healthcare patterns in two care periods can facilitate proactive, needs-based service provision while potentially reducing emergency hospital use.

items.title: Patient and caregiver characteristics and outcomes following compulsory admission for anorexia nervosa treatment.
items.abstract: Background A proportion of patients with anorexia nervosa require compulsory admission due to treatment refusal in the context of high medical or psychiatric risk. Aims The clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes of patients with anorexia nervosa compulsorily admitted for in-patient care (current and previous) were compared with those of patients admitted voluntarily. The characteristics of their caregivers were also evaluated. Method This is a secondary analysis of the Transition Care in Anorexia Nervosa Through Guidance Online from Peer and Carer Expertise trial. We included 274 patient-caregiver dyads: 62 on compulsory admission ('current compulsory'), 48 on voluntary admission with a history of compulsory treatment ('previous compulsory') and 164 on voluntary admission without a history of compulsory treatment ('voluntary'). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, and longitudinal clinical outcomes at 3-6 and 9-12 months, were compared across groups. Results Patients in the current compulsory group had an earlier age of onset, a higher proportion of obsessive-compulsive disorder comorbidity and less motivation and confidence to change compared with the voluntary group. The previous compulsory group showed a longer illness duration, older age and lower body mass index (BMI) compared with the other groups. All groups showed improvement, with similar outcomes at the end of the study except for depression symptoms and BMI. Caregivers had varying levels of distress and caregiving skills at baseline, which had improved by the end of the study. Conclusions People receiving current or previous compulsory treatment presented with diverse clinical presentations. Further studies are needed to determine whether more individualised approaches improve outcomes in these subgroups. items.title: Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation.
items.abstract: Psychiatric diagnosis depends on the clinician's ability to infer mental states from complex and dynamically evolving interpersonal signals. During the psychiatric interview, clinicians do not only collect explicit symptoms; they continuously sample a rich array of non-verbal and paralinguistic cues including gaze, prosody, affective reciprocity, and interactional timing. These signals are central to psychiatric assessment, yet their contribution to diagnostic reasoning remains poorly formalized. In this Review, we propose a computational account of clinical impressions in psychiatry. We integrate evidence from phenomenological psychopathology, social cognition, and computational neuroscience. We argue that such impressions may arise when the clinician's generative model of social interaction is persistently disconfirmed by subtle deviations in interpersonal behaviour, generating high-level social prediction errors experienced as a sense of incongruity or failed attunement. We formalize this process as VIBE: Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation. VIBE denotes a pre-reflective epistemic signal generated when observed interpersonal cues deviate from the clinician's expected model of social reciprocity. It is not a diagnostic criterion but orients hypothesis generation by drawing attention to disturbances in interpersonal predictability. We hypothesize that VIBE may constitute a transdiagnostic mechanism: different disorders, from schizophrenia to autism spectrum disorder and mood disorders, may disrupt distinct dimensions of interpersonal prediction. The Praecox Feeling, first described by Rümke in 1942, can be read as the earliest clinical formalization of this process and as its schizophrenia-spectrum instance, in which the profile of interpersonal violations is consistent enough to be clinically recognizable. This framework recasts the diagnostic impression as an embodied inferential process rather than an opaque subjective faculty. Teaching clinicians to articulate, examine, and recalibrate these impressions could strengthen diagnostic reasoning, reduce bias, and improve therapeutic attunement. VIBE provides a bridge between phenomenological psychopathology and computational neuroscience, and offers a tractable, empirically testable model for studying the neurocomputational basis of psychiatric clinical judgement.

items.title: Which morphological skills predict development in vocabulary? Contrasting morphological awareness with morphological analysis.
items.abstract: Morphemes are the smallest units of meaning in language. This study examined which of two related morphological skills support vocabulary growth: morphological awareness (recognizing and manipulating morphemes) and morphological analysis (using morphemes to infer meanings). We studied 336 English-speaking children (F = 154, M = 182; Mage = 6 years and 8 months; 55% European, with <10% each Acadian, Asian, African, Aboriginal, and Middle Eastern). In Grade 1, children completed morphological awareness and analysis tasks, and controls of reading comprehension, word identification, phonological awareness, nonverbal ability, and working memory. Vocabulary was measured at Grades 1 and 4. Structural equation modeling revealed that only morphological analysis uniquely predicted gains in vocabulary.

items.title: Developing a microsimulation model of Alzheimer's disease for the evaluation of disease modifying therapies.
items.abstract: Clinical trials of amyloid-targeting therapies (ATTs) for Alzheimer's Disease (AD) showed slowing of decline in continuous cognitive and functional outcomes over eighteen months of follow-up. Existing simulation models used to extrapolate these results do not account for the distinct but correlated trajectories of cognitive and functional decline, limiting their accuracy in evaluating ATT effects on both domains. We developed an AD microsimulation model using an amyloid-positive memory clinic population that can translate slowed cognitive decline into effects on clinical functional independence stages. The model contained stages of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), community dementia, institutionalisation, and death. The transitions from MCI to dementia and from dementia to institutionalisation or death were related to Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) measurements through statistical joint models. Model validation showed that observed and predicted cumulative incidence curves overlapped for all stage transitions, indicating an accurate description of time in each stage. An untreated cohort starting with MCI had a mean duration of MCI, mild, moderate and severe community dementia, and institutionalisation of 3.3, 2.3, 1.6, 1.1, and 1.7 years, respectively, totalling 10.0 years. When ATTs slowed MMSE decline by 30% during MCI and mild dementia (community dementia with an MMSE above 20), the duration of MCI and mild dementia was prolonged by 0.4 and 1.0 years, respectively, and institutionalisation was delayed by 1.1 year. The time institutionalised remained similar. Our AD microsimulation model can translate ATT effects on cognition into effects on functional independence and can be used to assess the cost-effectiveness of new therapies.

items.title: Spatiotemporally resolved single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals cellular and regional vulnerability in the midbrain in Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is clinically and biologically heterogeneous, and ethnic differences may influence its pathogenesis. However, single-nucleus transcriptomic data from East Asian populations remain limited. Here, we present a spatially resolved single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the human substantia nigra (SN) across the PD continuum, control, incidental Lewy body disease (iLBD), and advanced PD, in pathologically confirmed Korean individuals. Our integrative analysis revealed early α-synuclein aggregation in the ventrolateral SN, subtype-selective vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons, and relative preservation of the dorsomedial SN and ventral tegmental area. Trajectory and gene regulatory network analyses of astrocytes and microglia revealed spatiotemporally distinct, disease-associated glial responses, each driven by divergent molecular programs. We also identified two transcriptionally distinct vascular spatial clusters that exhibited differential vulnerability and remodeling. Spatial ligand-receptor analysis of α-synuclein-positive regions revealed intercellular signaling events associated with early pathology, including extracellular matrix remodeling and synaptic adhesion, which were prominent in the iLBD but largely diminished in advanced PD. Integration with PD genome-wide association studies using MAGMA demonstrated differential coupling between genetic risk, spatially resolved cell-state programs, and pseudotime-inferred microglial dynamics across ancestries. This study provides the first high-resolution, spatially mapped single-nucleus transcriptomic resource from an East Asian PD cohort, illuminating early perturbations in the midbrain intercellular and microenvironment that may underlie selective dopaminergic vulnerability and guide the development of ancestry-informed therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Selective Social Conformity in Adolescents With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury: Differential Patterns Across Social Influence Sources and Judgment Contexts.
items.abstract: Introduction Social conformity among adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) may vary depending on the characteristics of social information and the context in which social judgments are made. This study examined social conformity patterns in adolescents with NSSI across different social influence sources and judgment contexts. Methods Two independent behavioral experiments were conducted. Study 1 included 39 adolescents with NSSI and 50 healthy controls (HCs) and employed a risk perception task to examine conformity responses following social feedback from adolescents versus adults. Study 2 included an independent sample of 53 adolescents with NSSI and 40 HCs and used a facial attractiveness social evaluation task to examine conformity responses under the same two social influence source conditions. A cross-study joint analysis was conducted to compare source-related conformity patterns between the studies. Results In Study 1, adolescents with NSSI showed greater conformity effects following adolescent feedback than adult feedback, whereas HCs did not show a significant difference between feedback sources. In Study 2, adolescents with NSSI exhibited significantly lower conformity effects than HCs under both adolescent and adult feedback conditions. HCs showed stronger conformity effects following adolescent feedback than adult feedback, whereas adolescents with NSSI did not show a significant source-related difference. The cross-study joint analysis revealed a significant Rating Discrepancy × Participant Group × Social Influence Source × Study interaction, indicating that source-related conformity patterns differed significantly between the two studies. Conclusions Social conformity among adolescents with NSSI was not uniformly enhanced across the two judgment contexts. Instead, conformity patterns differed in relation to social influence sources and between the two judgment paradigms. These findings extend research on peer-related influences in NSSI and provide experimental behavioral evidence for understanding how adolescents with NSSI adjust their social judgments following feedback from others.

items.title: Distinct Cross-Lagged Relations of Cognitive Reappraisal and Expressive Suppression With Perceived Social Support Among Chinese Adolescents.
items.abstract: Introduction Converging evidence suggests a close relationship between emotion regulation (ER) and perceived social support (PSS) among adolescents. Yet, little is currently known about their longitudinal cross-lagged associations within the Chinese cultural context, as well as the differential effects of different ER strategies. To address these gaps, the present study aimed to examine the cross-lagged associations between PSS and two specific ER strategies-cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression-in Chinese adolescents. Methods A total of 316 adolescents from Zhoukou, China (45.9% female; M age = 16.42, SD = 0.61, aged 14-18 years) participated in a three-wave longitudinal study, with data collected at 6-month intervals during senior high school. To examine hypothesized cross-lagged associations, we employed cross-lagged panel models, a well-established method for analyzing temporal associations (Kenny 1975). Results Cross-lagged panel model revealed that PSS at Time 1 was positively associated with cognitive reappraisal at Time 2, which in turn was positively related to PSS at Time 3. PSS at Time 2 also showed a positive correlation with cognitive reappraisal at Time 3. In contrast, no significant cross-lagged effects were observed between PSS and expressive suppression over time. Conclusions These findings contribute to a more nuanced understanding of the longitudinal cross-lagged associations between PSS and ER in adolescence, highlighting the association between supportive social environments and adolescents' ER strategies.

items.title: Growing Through It: A Longitudinal Examination of Body Dissatisfaction, Mental Health, and Resilience During Adolescence.
items.abstract: Introduction Research indicates adolescence, specifically puberty, is a critical period of psychological and physiological development. It is well known that body image is a key aspect of developmental psychology impacting mental health. Yet little is known about the buffering effects of resilience to moderate the relationship between body image and mental health over time. The present study investigated the effects of body mass index (BMI), higher age, and early pubertal status as risk factors predicting subsequent changes in body dissatisfaction and body esteem longitudinally. The study also sought to explore body dissatisfaction, body esteem, and resilience as independent variables in the prediction of future changes in depressive symptomology. Methods Following a retrospective longitudinal observational research design stemming from a larger research project, 228 adolescents aged 10-16 completed physiological and psychosocial measures across 2 years (baseline (Year 0) and follow-up (Year 2)). Measures used in this study included the Tanner Stages of Development (pubertal development); Harpenden stadiometer, Michelli GSE 460 scale, Center for Disease Control (CDC) BMI equation, and CDC 2022 extended growth charts (BMI and BMI percentile); Body Image Assessment Procedure for Pre-Adolescents (BIA-P; body dissatisfaction); Body Esteem Scale for Adolescents and Adults (BESSA; body esteem); Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire (SMFQ; depressive symptomology); and Connor Davidson Resilience Scale, 10-Item Short-Form (CD-RISC 10; resilience). Results Multivariate regression analyses indicated that early puberty status predicted significant increases in body dissatisfaction over time, while BMI and age were not significant predictors. Additionally, BMI, age, and puberty status did not demonstrate any significant predictive associations with body esteem at follow-up. Baseline body dissatisfaction and body esteem were then examined as independent predictors of changes in depressive symptomology, and analyses evaluated whether resilience moderated these associations. Among adolescents reporting no change or decreases in resilience, higher levels of body dissatisfaction at baseline predicted greater increases in depressive symptomology at follow-up; however, this association was not observed among adolescents with increases in resilience, indicating a significant moderating effect of resilience on this relationship (p = 0.0080). Body esteem at baseline did not significantly predict depressive symptomology at follow-up, nor was this relationship moderated by changes in resilience (p = 0.3972). Conclusions Findings provide a deeper understanding of risk and protective factors associated with depressive symptomology in adolescents, highlighting resilience as an important independent variable that may buffer the impact of body dissatisfaction on mood outcomes. These results may help researchers and clinicians better conceptualize how resilience functions in adolescents navigating puberty and body image and support its consideration in interventions aimed at mitigating mood disturbances.

items.title: The Association Between Cognitive Flexibility and Eating Behaviors in Autistic Women With Eating Disorders.
items.abstract: Objective Reduced cognitive flexibility is a trait associated with autism and has also been implicated in eating disorders (EDs). However, most studies have not distinguished between autistic and non-autistic individuals in ED samples, potentially obscuring group-specific patterns. This study investigated self-reported cognitive flexibility and its association with eating behaviors (traditional ED pathology and ARFID symptomatology) across four groups: autistic women with EDs (ASD + ED), non-autistic women with EDs (ED), autistic women without EDs (ASD), and non-autistic controls. Method Participants included 30 ASD + ED, 30 ED, 29 ASD, and 60 control women (N = 149). All completed the Detail and Flexibility Questionnaire (DFlex), the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q), and the Nine Item ARFID Screen (NIAS). Group comparisons were conducted on self-reported cognitive flexibility (cognitive rigidity, attention to detail), ED pathology, and ARFID symptoms. Associations between cognitive flexibility and eating behaviors were examined across and within groups. Results ASD + ED and ASD groups showed significantly greater difficulties in self-reported cognitive flexibility than ED and control groups, which did not differ from each other. Associations between self-reported cognitive flexibility and eating behaviors varied across groups, with attention to detail showing the clearest pattern. Attention to detail was associated with ED pathology in the ASD + ED group and with ARFID symptomatology in the ASD + ED, ASD, and control groups, but not in the ED group. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest that self-reported cognitive inflexibility may be more strongly associated with autism than with EDs alone and highlight the importance of considering co-occurring autism when examining cognitive characteristics in ED populations. Public significance statement This study explored how cognitive traits - like attention to detail - relate to eating behaviors in autistic and non-autistic women with and without eating disorders. Findings suggest that certain thinking patterns may be more closely linked to autism than to eating disorders alone, underscoring the need for greater clinical awareness of autism-specific features when assessing and supporting individuals with disordered eating.

items.title: Algorithmic Grief Invisibility & Fragmented Narratives: A Theory-Building Framework for Algorithmically Mediated Grief.
items.abstract: Grief increasingly unfolds within digitally mediated environments in which automated systems shape visibility, continuity, and social acknowledgment. This article advances a theoretical contribution to thanatology by introducing algorithmic grief invisibility (AGI), a framework for understanding how algorithmically mediated environments can function as contemporary sites of disenfranchised grief without attributing agency or intent to technology. Drawing on Doka's disenfranchised grief, Neimeyer's meaning reconstruction, and continuing bonds scholarship, it theorizes that disruptions in visibility, moderation, sequencing, and social feedback may fragment three narrative threads central to bereavement adaptation: the event story of the loss, the relational back story through which continuing bonds are sustained, and identity reconstruction. As a pre-empirical contribution, AGI is offered to support scholarly dialogue, clinical reflection, and future research questions, rather than to test hypotheses or document prevalence. Clinical and educational implications are discussed as reflective extensions of established grief theory.

items.title: From naturals to strivers: How stereotypes in social and moral dimensions change with age to drive children's preference development.
items.abstract: Children observe some people succeed through natural talent (naturals), whereas others succeed through sustained effort (strivers). Children's preference for naturals or strivers may influence the people they admire and choose as role models and may have implications for their social judgment and achievement development. However, little is known about how children's preferences for naturals versus strivers develop and the factors that explain these preferences. We examined the development of preferences for naturals versus strivers among 221 Han Chinese children (5.06-11.99 years, 114 girls), as well as associations with external perceptions of naturals and strivers (warmth, competence, and morality) and internal self-cognitions (self-concept and mindset). Results revealed an age-related pattern in children's preferences, with younger children tending to prefer naturals and a preference for strivers observed from ages 7-8 onward. These preferences can be explained by the sociomoral value of effort (viewing strivers as warmer and less likely to free-ride). These results extend previous research on the instrumental value of effort and underscore the distinct roles of external stereotypes and internal self--cognitions in shaping social preferences. This study can inform educators how to understand children's preferences for naturals versus strivers and the sociomoral significance of effort in daily interactions.

items.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic regulation of young children's frustration: A person-specific, dynamic approach.
items.abstract: Young children may draw on both intrinsic physiological systems and extrinsic caregiver support to manage frustration. While regulation is often conceptualized as feedback-control processes, there has been limited empirical evidence on how they unfold in real time. Taking a person-specific, dynamic network approach, we examined whether parasympathetic changes and maternal responsiveness serve as active regulators that effectively dampen children's regulatory demands (reflected in sympathetic arousal and challenging behaviors) on a moment-to-moment basis during a frustration challenge. Data from 139 mother-child dyads (30-60 months; 48% female; 94% White; data collected June 2017-December 2019 in central Pennsylvania, U.S.) revealed that parasympathetic responses can function as real-time regulators through both dynamic increases and decreases across children; physiological regulation was related to better effortful control (standardized coefficient β = .22). Parental regulation primarily modulated challenging behaviors and was less evident among children with greater negative affectivity and externalizing risks (βs = -.19 and -.22). Findings demonstrate how children's self-regulation emerges from heterogeneous, dynamic systems where intrinsic and extrinsic processes operate to maintain homeostasis. By linking micro-level regulation dynamics with children's emotional and behavioral characteristics, the findings further highlight the value of capturing active, unfolding regulation patterns for understanding early functioning strengths and risks.

items.title: Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ): Development and Initial Validation.
items.abstract: Nociplastic pain is implicated in many chronic pain conditions, yet it has been defined primarily by the absence of structural causes-a diagnosis by exclusion. No validated nociplastic pain questionnaire exists. This study examined hypothesized pain-specific features of nociplastic pain and developed a brief self-report instrument, the Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ). We generated items based on literature review and input from experts and individuals with lived experience. We administered the items and measures of other pain-related constructs (pain intensity/interference, catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, and perceived stress) to 888 participants with diverse chronic pain conditions. Factor analyses supported four dimensions captured by internally consistent 4-item subscales (αs ≥0.74): 1) location variability, 2) exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, 3) widespreadness, and 4) allodynia. The NociQ total score adequately discriminated presumed nociplastic and non-nociplastic conditions (AUCs 0.73-0.75). Participants who had widespread pain or reported more presumed nociplastic conditions scored higher on all scales (ps <.001, ds=0.35-1.37). NociQ scales demonstrated small-to-moderate correlations with measures of theoretically distinct constructs (rs=0.10-0.44), supporting discriminant validity, and explained additional variance in pain intensity beyond those measures (ΔR²s=.02-.07; ps <.05), supporting incremental validity. Results indicate four nociplastic pain characteristics, including two, location variability and exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, psychometrically validated here for the first time. The 16-item NociQ demonstrates promising reliability and validity as a brief questionnaire of nociplastic pain. Future research should examine its clinical utility, such as in matching patients to pain mechanism-targeted treatments.

items.title: The Algorithmically Positioned Self: Rethinking Dialogicality in Human-AI Interaction.
items.abstract: AI platforms are creating new conditions for meeting the voices with which people come to understand themselves. One easy way out of this problem is to conclude that the use of AI constitutes a new type of Other, or a new I-position, in dialogical self theory (DST). This paper takes issue with such a conclusion and proposes that AI produces a unique semiotic context for communication - utterances that are responsive and appear to be other-generated, but that are not generated by an embodiment or historically positioned subject such as human dialogue assumes in DST. Dialogicality thus does not lie in the AI; it arises from the interplay between the individual person, the AI-produced utterance, and the person's repertoire of culturally mediated positions. Based on DST, semiotic-cultural psychology, and work on algorithmic curation and AI companions, the paper offers a human-system configuration approach to AI interaction wherein technological factors (ranking systems, interfaces, goals, and generated language) are taken up into meaning transformation by human beings. It makes the distinction between human agency and system effect, highlights the difference between high agency and low agency using three analytical examples, incorporates the culture into the theory, and explains how it contributes to understanding of the algorithmic, datafied, and distributed self. It ends with limited, testable hypotheses and a revised discussion of the clinical and educational significance of the theory. Its ultimate objective is to understand what the emergence of AI teaches us about I-position, Other, and dialogue according to DST.

items.title: Ventilation inhomogeneity in Duchenne muscular dystrophy before the initiation of ventilatory support: Insights from electrical impedance tomography.
items.abstract: Prior to the onset of overt ventilatory failure, patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) can display non-uniform respiratory mechanics, resulting from atelectasis in small lung regions secondary to rapid, shallow breathing and/or peripheral airway obstruction, thereby predisposing to the development of ventilation inhomogeneity. To investigate ventilation distribution in DMD patients before the initiation of long-term assisted ventilation by using electrical impedance tomography (EIT). Patients and interventions: Eighteen DMD patients underwent EIT between 1 January and 31 December 2025. Primary study endpoint: Global Inhomogeneity Index (GI). EIT data were compared with those obtained from a group of 11 healthy, similarly aged male medical residents. GI was significantly higher in the DMD patients with respect to healthy males [0.44 ± 0.13 (0.36-0.77) vs 0.37 ± 0.03 (0.32-0.43); p < 0.001]. A GI of 0.5 maximised the distinction between DMD patients with a ventilation distribution pattern similar to or different from the healthy subjects. Before initiation of assisted ventilation, a subset of DMD patients may develop lung ventilation inhomogeneity, which can be readily assessed by means of EIT. Whether such inhomogeneity is predictive of major clinical events therefore constitutes a critical question to be addressed.

items.title: Germicidal ultraviolet to reduce transmission of respiratory infections indoors: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Respiratory infections that transmit through air contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality. Although preclinical data on germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) for air treatment are promising, its real-world effectiveness remains incompletely understood. Review effectiveness and safety of GUV for preventing respiratory infection transmission. Medline, Embase, Global Health, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Engineering Village, Epistemonikos, Scopus, and Environmental Science Collection from inception through December 2025. Studies of GUV with a comparator, measuring human outcomes including respiratory infections, absenteeism, or adverse events. At least two investigators extracted data. We identified 57 reports describing 40 studies published between 1940 and 2025: 30 non-randomized controlled trials, 4 randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 4 case series, 1 cohort study, and 1 cross-sectional study. Non-randomized studies indicated GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air (measles and chickenpox), although results were mixed for undifferentiated respiratory illnesses and absenteeism. Two RCTs were inconclusive or showed only modest effects. Safety monitoring in 16 studies identified no increased eye or skin irritation from properly installed GUV. All studies had at least one threat to validity; 89% were non-randomized, and 83% lacked statistical power calculations. Heterogeneous study designs, interventions, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. Several older clinical studies indicated that GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air, but its broader effectiveness against respiratory infection remains uncertain. Inconclusive results may reflect methodological and epidemiological limitations rather than true ineffectiveness. Adequately powered RCTs with robust clinical endpoints are needed. https://osf.io/fg6qx.

items.title: An investigation into post-pandemic ethnic group and deprivation inequalities in influenza and COVID-19 hospitalizations.
items.abstract: Health system decision-makers need evidence on how modifiable factors contribute to inequalities to inform effective interventions. We examined ethnic group and deprivation inequalities in influenza and COVID-19 hospitalizations in England (2023-2024) among vaccine-eligible individuals, using causal mediation analysis to assess the roles of deprivation, vaccination uptake and comorbidities. For influenza, hospitalization odds were highest among Pakistani and Bangladeshi groups, compared with White British individuals. Deprivation mediated 26% of the total ethnic group effect for the Pakistani group and 41% for the Bangladeshi group, whilst comorbidities contributed little. Ethnic group differences in COVID-19 hospitalizations were minimal in this post-pandemic period. For both infections, the most deprived group had disproportionately high hospitalization compared to the least deprived. For influenza, vaccination uptake mediated 17%-26% of deprivation effects, whilst for COVID-19, there were no meaningful residual deprivation inequalities after including vaccination uptake and comorbidities. Vaccination uptake and deprivation mediate a substantial proportion of inequalities in hospitalization for influenza and COVID-19 in the vaccine-eligible cohort. Improving vaccination coverage in under-vaccinated groups should remain a public health priority.

items.title: Prediction of Unfavorable Functional Status at Hospital Discharge in Older Adults with Traumatic Brain Injury : Model Development and Internal Evaluation.
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) in older adults is an increasing public health burden. An early risk assessment of poor functional outcome can help guide prognosis and communication. The objective of the present study was to develop and internally validate a prediction model for poor functional status at discharge from the hospital for older adults with TBI. A retrospective cohort study included 3,193 patients aged ≥65 years with TBI. The Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) was used to evaluate the functional status of the patient at hospital discharge and was dichotomized as favorable (GOS 4-5) or unfavorable (GOS 1-3). Logistic regression was used to analyze candidate predictors; then, backward selection with the Akaike Information Criterion was used for multivariable analysis. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was used to measure discrimination, and the calibration intercept, calibration slope, and Brier score were used to measure calibration. Optimism-corrected performance was estimated using 1,000 bootstrapped resamples in the internal validation. Bootstrap inclusion frequencies were used to evaluate the predictor-selection stability. Among 3,193 patients, 224 (7.0%) had poor functional outcomes. Warfarin use, motor weakness, hypotension, category of GCS, pupillary response, basilar skull fracture, acute subdural hematoma, contusion/intracerebral hematoma, intraventricular hemorrhage, and basal cistern obliteration were predictor variables retained in the final model. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.964 (95% CI, 0.948-0.979). After 1,000 bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.962 with a calibration intercept of -0.001 and the calibration slope of 0.959. The model demonstrated strong discrimination with limited optimism after bootstrap internal validation. External validation in independent populations is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Joint Association of Longitudinal Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator Patterns and Hypertension Status with Incident Stroke Among Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages 0-3: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: The prognostic value of longitudinal single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) patterns for stroke, particularly when considered in combination with hypertension (HTN), remains unclear among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3. This study aimed to examine the association of combined longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status with incident stroke among adults with CKM syndrome stages 0-3. A nationwide prospective cohort study. We included adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKM stages 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. SPISE was calculated at Waves 1 and 3, and incident stroke was ascertained through Wave 5. K-means clustering was used to identify longitudinal SPISE patterns, which were dichotomized as persistently low or non-persistently low. Participants were then cross-classified according to longitudinal SPISE pattern and baseline HTN status. Cumulative SPISE exposure was calculated from repeated SPISE measurements. Cox models were used to examine associations with incident stroke. Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-performance analyses were also performed. Among 4,443 participants, 348 incident strokes occurred. A persistently low longitudinal SPISE pattern was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke than a persistently high pattern [hazard ratio (HR), 2.29; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.59-3.29]. Compared with the group with no HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern, stroke risk was higher in the group with no HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.12-1.95), the group with HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.10-2.23), and the group with HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.84-3.26). Higher cumulative SPISE exposure was inversely associated with incident stroke (HR per 1-unit increment, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93-0.97), with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. Incorporating the combined longitudinal SPISE pattern and HTN status increased the apparent C-index from 0.612 to 0.646. However, optimism-corrected discrimination was comparable between the combined model and the HTN-only model. The combination of longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status identified a subgroup at the highest risk of incident stroke in this CKM population.

items.title: Demographic Data Concordance: A Prospective Observational Study of Adolescents, Caregivers, and the Electronic Health Record.
items.abstract: (1) To measure the concordance of patient demographic data in the electronic health record (EHR); and (2) to determine the level of agreement for patient demographic data between patient report-EHR and patients-caregivers. We conducted a prospective observational survey of 295 patients (age 12 to 17 years) and caregiver dyads presenting to a pediatric emergency department. The primary outcome was concordance, reporting kappa statistics with 95% CI, of caregiver-reported patient race, ethnicity, and sex and the EHR. Secondary outcomes were concordance between: (1) patient report and EHR and (2) patient and caregiver report, including gender identity and preferred language. We surveyed dyads on the perceived impact of demographic characteristics on emergency care and caregivers on preferences for reporting data. For caregiver and EHR report of race, there was substantial agreement for Asian (κ=0.65, 95% CI: 0.44-0.86), Black/African American/African (κ=0.76, 95% CI: 0.66-0.86), and White (κ=0.66, 95% CI: 0.58-0.75) race and moderate agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=0.53, 95% CI: 0.44-0.61). Patient report and the EHR had similar concordance for race and poor agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=-0.17, 95% CI: -0.22 to -0.12). For patients and caregivers, there was strong concordance for race, ethnicity, language, and gender identity. Caregivers were more likely than pediatric patients to report that demographic factors affected emergency care. Most caregivers did not have preferences about demographic data reporting methods. Concordance of patient race and ethnicity data in the EHR was variable and should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Concept Mapping Analysis of Sustainability Factors and Strategies for Childhood Obesity Prevention Programs.
items.abstract: This study aimed to identify and prioritize sustainability factors and strategies and to explore their relationships based on expert-informed concept mapping analysis. Three rounds of consultation were conducted sequentially among a total sample of 44 experienced experts in childhood obesity intervention. Experts first rated the importance and feasibility of factors and strategies related to program sustainability and then completed a card sorting task to group factors and strategies according to whether the same strategies could address them. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using the Average Deviation index. A go-zone plot was generated to visualize strategy priorities by importance and feasibility. Multidimensional scaling and hierarchical cluster analysis were used to identify clusters of sustainability factors and strategies. The results showed that "matching stakeholders' perceived needs" was rated as the most important factor, and 12 strategies were rated as both highly important and feasible in the go-zone plot. Six clusters of sustainability factors and strategies emerged: (1) alignment and collaboration, (2) workforce engagement, (3) capacity building, (4) resource security, (5) sustainability-focused enhancement, and (6) streamlining and optimization. This assessment and categorization of factors and strategies can help practitioners prioritize practices based on their specific needs and contextual conditions to sustain childhood obesity prevention programs.

items.title: HDL-C as a mediator of PPCP-related kidney function decline in community-dwelling elderly: a mixture analysis approach.
items.abstract: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) are widespread environmental contaminants, but their associations with kidney function and lipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. This study included 2758 adults aged ≥ 60 years in Anhui Province, China, during 2022-2023 and used a cross sectional design. Urinary concentrations of 48 PPCPs and two metabolites were measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation. Individual associations were assessed using logistic and linear regression, and mixture associations using weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression. Restricted cubic splines examined nonlinear associations, and exploratory mediation analyses assessed the statistical contribution of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Among nine PPCPs with detection frequencies > 50%, doxycycline, enrofloxacin, acetaminophen, metformin, and cotinine were associated with lower eGFR after full adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Coefficients ranged from - 3.00 to - 0.93 mL/min/1.73 m2 per tenfold increase in urinary concentration. Tylosin and caffeine were positively associated with eGFR. The WQS index was inversely associated with eGFR, with metformin receiving the largest weight. HDL-C showed a positive nonlinear association with eGFR. Under the mediation model assumptions, HDL-C statistically accounted for 12.21-29.30% of the associations involving enrofloxacin, metformin, and acetaminophen, and 13.78% of the mixture association. The indirect association for cotinine was nonsignificant. These findings remain exploratory. Prospective studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and address possible reverse causation.

items.title: The Legacy Impact of the CATIE Study on Healthcare Policy and Psychiatric Resident Education: A Cross-Sectional Mixed-Methods Survey of U.S. Psychiatry Residency and State Medical Directors.
items.abstract: The Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness (CATIE) study has had a lasting impact on the treatment of schizophrenia, yet its current role in psychiatric education and treatment policy remains unclear. This study aimed to assess how the CATIE trial is taught in U.S. psychiatry residency programs and whether its findings influence state-level treatment protocols. A cross-sectional mixed-methods survey was distributed to U.S. psychiatry residency program directors and members of the National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors (NASMHPD) Medical Directors Council. The survey included closed-ended and open-ended questions assessing the educational and policy relevance of the CATIE study. Quantitative data were summarized descriptively, and qualitative responses were analyzed thematically and categorized by sentiment. Participation was voluntary and anonymous, and institutional review board exemption was obtained. A total of 75 responses were analyzed, including 60 from psychiatry residency program directors and 15 from NASMHPD medical directors. Among residency directors, 56% reported teaching the CATIE study for its clinical significance, 32% for its historical relevance, and 12% did not routinely include it in training. In contrast, 80% of state medical directors reported that CATIE findings no longer inform treatment protocols or formulary decisions. Qualitative responses highlighted CATIE's continued educational value for teaching study design, clinical decision-making, and the evolution of antipsychotic therapy, while also noting concerns regarding generalizability. These findings underscore a widening gap between academic instruction and policy application of psychiatric evidence. The CATIE study continues to serve as a valuable educational tool in psychiatric training, yet its influence on state-level clinical policy appears limited. These findings highlight a divergence between academic and institutional priorities and suggest a need for updated research that reflects contemporary clinical realities and pharmacologic advancements.

items.title: Meeting report of the fifth symposium organized by the coalition to strengthen the HPV immunization community (CHIC): Nairobi, Kenya - advancing sustainable HPV vaccination programs in Africa.
items.abstract: HPV vaccination coverage across Africa has improved substantially in recent years but remains below elimination thresholds, with persistent gaps in reaching hard-to-reach populations and growing uncertainty around future financing. This report summarizes proceedings from the fifth regional symposium of the Coalition to Strengthen the HPV Immunization Community (CHIC), held in Nairobi, Kenya, in October 2025 in collaboration with Kenya's Ministry of Health. The three-day symposium convened over 100 participants from 22 African countries, including national immunisation program managers, ministry officials, researchers, civil society representatives, and global partners (WHO, UNICEF, Gavi, PATH, the Gates Foundation). The agenda, developed through stakeholder interviews and prior scientific and advisory input, centered on six subthemes related to program sustainability. Plenary sessions addressed epidemiological trends, national policy updates including Kenya's transition to a single-dose schedule, and implications of Gavi's upcoming consolidated funding model (Gavi 6.0). Country snapshot presentations and service-delivery case studies facilitated cross-country peer learning. On day three, though an electronic poll of helped to prioritize 12 candidate implementation themes, which structured subsequent round table working groups. Countries then developed individual action plans identifying priority challenges, responsible stakeholders, and implementation timelines. Sustainable service delivery, financing, and data systems emerged as the highest-priority implementation themes. Country action plans most frequently targeted data systems strengthening, communication and community engagement, sustainable service delivery, and financing mechanisms, with additional attention to service integration, hard-to-reach populations, and target population expansion. Cross-cutting synthesis identified recurring concerns regarding HPV vaccination for people living with HIV, fragmented data systems, the role of program integration, financing sustainability under evolving donor models, and underrecognized risks from misinformation, including emerging AI-generated content. The symposium reinforced CHIC's role as a platform for peer-to-peer learning across countries at varying stages of HPV vaccine introduction, surfacing shared structural barriers to sustainability alongside country-specific action plans. Findings underscore the need for sustained political commitment, financing transition planning, digital system strengthening, and multisectoral integration to support the WHO goal of cervical cancer elimination by 2030.

items.title: Early Custody Mortality: Operational Safeguards for Nursing Practice.
items.abstract: Individuals entering U.S. jail face elevated mortaility risk, particularly during the earliest stages of detention. To examine national mortality patterns to identify timing- and mechanism-specific risk concentrations and their implications for forensic nursing practice and early-custody care. We conducted a descriptive analysis of Bureau of Justice Statistics mortality data to identify stable patterns in timing (≤24 hr, ≤7 days, ≤30 days), mechanisms of death, and distribution across the early-custody period. Findings were translated into operational domains relevant to intake and early-custody management from a nursing perspective. Mortality risk was highly concentrated in early custody. Approximately 40% of deaths occurred within 1 week of admission, more than half of suicides occurred within 30 days, and about 12% occurred within 24 hours. Suicide was the leading cause of death, with ~90% involving hanging or suffocation. Drug and alcohol intoxication deaths clustered on the first day of detention. Early custody represents a predictable and concentrated nursing and public health risk window. The convergence of suicide risk, substance-related mortality, and uneven implementation of nursing-sensitive practices suggests that booking and early detention should be treated as structured clinical events. Screening, observation, withdrawal management, and medication continuity may serve as important operational safeguards to strengthen early-custody mortality prevention.

items.title: Prevalence of food insecurity in households with children under 5 years of age in Ecuador: analysis of the national child malnutrition surveys.
items.abstract: To estimate the national prevalence and distribution of food insecurity (FI) among households with children younger than 5 years in Ecuador and to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) using two consecutive nationally representative surveys. This cross-sectional study employed descriptive statistics and Tobit regression models using STATA v17. We used secondary data from the National Survey on Child Malnutrition in Ecuador, including food security (FS) information for 2022-2023 and 2023-2024, to construct the prevalence time series. We analysed data from 19 187 households (22 260 children) surveyed in the first round and 20 186 households (23 187 children) surveyed in the second round. FIES showed adequate reliability in both rounds (Rasch reliability 0·80 and 0·79). Seven of eight FIES items showed significant reductions between rounds. The prevalence of moderate-or-severe FI remained high, decreasing from 40·79 % in 2022-2023 to 39·18 % in 2023-2024 (p = 0·239). Severe FI declined significantly from 4·83 % to 3·52 % (p = 0·002). In both rounds, FI was more prevalent in rural areas, the Amazon region, priority territories, Indigenous and Afro-descendant populations and households experiencing poverty or unmet basic needs. In 2023-2024, FI was associated with priority area residence, Indigenous ethnicity, poverty due to unmet basic needs, older child age groups and stunting. Despite reductions in severe FI, nearly four in ten households with young children in Ecuador continue to experience moderate-or-severe FI, with persistent territorial, ethnic and socio-economic inequalities. Integrated policies linking FS, child nutrition and poverty reduction are needed.
