items.title: Parental coping and child psychosocial adaptation in pediatric Wilson disease.
items.abstract: Objectives Pediatric data on psychosocial adaptation in Wilson disease remain limited. In particular, the relationship between parental psychosocial functioning and child quality of life and adaptation is still insufficiently understood. Methods This cross-sectional study included 50 children with Wilson disease and one parent of each child. Children completed the Revised Children's Quality of Life Questionnaire (KINDL-R) and the JSR coping questionnaire. Parents completed the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28), Brief Coping Orientation to Problems Experienced (Brief COPE), Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS), and the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). Canonical correlation analysis was used to examine multivariate associations between child and parent variable sets. Results The full canonical model was statistically significant, and five canonical functions were extracted; however, only the first function reached statistical significance (Rc = 0.802, Wilks' λ = 0.202, p = 0.001). This function linked parental problem-focused, emotion-focused, and avoidance coping, together with general psychological distress, with child dispositional active, social, and emotion-focused coping, total quality of life, and, to a lesser extent, internalizing problems. Redundancy indices supported the practical interpretability of the identified parent-child psychosocial pattern. Conclusions Psychosocial adaptation in children with Wilson disease appears to be meaningfully related to parental psychosocial functioning, particularly parental coping patterns and general psychological distress. These findings support a family-oriented approach to psychosocial assessment and care in pediatric Wilson disease.

items.title: Addressing Mind-Wandering in Health Misinformation Interventions: Fact-Checking Across Immediate and Long-Term Effects.
items.abstract: In the era of social media information, previous fact-checking studies have overlooked individual cognitive states such as mind-wandering, thereby limiting the generalizability of fact-checking findings in real-life scenarios. This study aims to examine the immediate and short-term effects of mind-wandering and fact-checking on interventions against health misinformation. Grounded in the dual processing model for online credibility assessments, this study used the within-subject experimental design ( N = 156) to manipulate the frequency of fact-checking exposures, assessed mind-wandering using thought probes during the task, and collected information accuracy scores immediately after the intervention and 1 week later as indicators of intervention effectiveness. The results showed that, in the immediate post-test, fact-checking exposure frequency had the significant positive effect on intervention effectiveness, and mind-wandering was negatively associated with intervention effectiveness. Nine exposures to fact-checking reduced the negative association between mind-wandering and intervention effectiveness. However, in the 1-week post-test, the effect of fact-checking exposure frequency was not significant, whereas mind-wandering remained negatively associated with intervention effectiveness. Nevertheless, nine exposures to fact-checking still reduced this short-term negative association. This study suggests that effective fact-checking interventions depend not only on repeated exposure to fact-checking information but also on individuals' mind-wandering.

items.title: Adolescents' in vivo emotional responses to digital and in-person peer experiences: Differences by context and links to daily life depressive symptoms.
items.abstract: The rise of digital media has raised questions about potential links to adolescent depression, especially among girls. This study investigated whether affective responses to daily peer interactions, and depressive symptoms, varied by context - digital media or in-person. A sample of 110 adolescents assigned female at birth, aged 12-17 ( M = 15.30, SD = 1.51; 83.6% White and 96.7% non-Hispanic) and enriched for risk for depression and suicidality, participated in 30 days of ecological momentary assessments over 3 months. Participants reported their most recent "worst" and "best" peer interactions, the context of these interactions (digital media or in-person), their affective responses to these interactions, and depressive symptoms. Multilevel models revealed that greater negative affect during negative interactions was associated with higher depressive symptoms, regardless of context ( B = 0.02, p B = -2.01, p = .02), which, in turn, was associated with lower depressive symptoms ( B = 0.08, p = .01). Findings highlight the protective role of positive in-person experiences in adolescent emotional well-being, and challenge assumptions that negative digital experiences are the primary causes of depressive symptoms.

items.title: Social Discrimination and Psychological Distress Across Gender: The Effects of Social Support and Resilience.
items.abstract: Aims Despite social changes that have contributed to greater gender equality, there is still a long way to go, as differences in living conditions between women and men can affect their mental health. The main goal of this study is to examine the relationships among psychological distress, social discrimination, perceived social support, and resilience by gender. Methods This is a cross-sectional study with 752 participants aged 18 to 84 years (M = 39.34; SD = 13.77). The tools used included the Brief Symptom Inventory, the Portuguese Everyday Discrimination Scale, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Results We identified a strong correlation between psychological distress and social discrimination (r = .642, p Discussion These findings suggest that, despite differences in living conditions, men and women use distinct coping mechanisms for adversity, and these mechanisms do not follow a linear pattern. The results emphasize the value of a gender-sensitive approach when analyzing mental health, one that considers how multiple social identities may shape distress. items.title: Helpful and in Danger: Attributes and Correlates of Perceived Occupational Heroism.
items.abstract: Some occupations such as firefighters are described as heroic, while others, such as healthcare workers, are applauded as "heroes" in crises. In two preregistered correlational studies conducted on representative U.K. samples, we evaluated theory-based attributes of occupational heroism, and its relationship to specific policy-relevant attitudes toward occupations. In Study 1 ( N = 430), we confirmed that occupational heroism relates to the perceived helpfulness and risk exposure of workers. In Study 2 ( N = 840), we further showed that occupational heroism is associated with a moral shield: workers' hero status correlates with decreased acceptability of criticism toward them, and increased support for deregulating them and protecting them from punishment for rule-breaking. Unlike previous findings suggesting a willingness to exploit heroized workers, heroism correlated with increased gratitude toward workers, support for their demands, and perception that they are vulnerable. Societal consequences and relevance for policy-making are discussed.

items.title: Carbapenem Resistance Among Gram-Negative Bacteria in Bioaerosols at Biomedical Waste Disposal Site in Ahmedabad, India
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health concern, with Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant bacteria (CRG) classified by WHO as critical priority pathogens. Biomedical waste disposal sites (BMWs) may act as reservoirs for resistant organisms, posing occupational and community risks. This study investigated the phenotypic and genotypic characterization of Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant bacteria in bioaerosols collected from BMW facilities in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. Bioaerosols were sampled using active Six-stage Andersen Impactors and passive settled plates. Isolates were identified by MALDI-TOF, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST). Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed for 26 representative isolates, and resistance gene profiling was conducted using CARD and ResFinder databases. Representative isolates belonged to Moraxellaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Pseudomonadaceae families. All species showed resistance to linezolid, and approximately 60% were multidrug resistant to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. Genotypic analysis confirmed the prevalence of carbapenemase genes, with blaNDM-1 most frequent, followed by blaNDM-7, blaVIM-2, blaVIM-11, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-235. This is the first report documenting Acinetobacter baumannii, A. schindleri, A. towneri, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas juntendi in bioaerosols from BMW sites. Biomedical waste environments serve as critical reservoirs of AMR. These findings emphasize the need for surveillance, protective measures, and integration of environmental AMR monitoring into public health policy.

items.title: Enterovirus D68 in Europe, 2025: continent-wide predominance of subclade A2/D and shift from pediatric to adult cases
items.abstract: Background: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) has predominantly caused infections in children, and detected cases have mainly been infected by subclade B3. In 2025, however, a substantial number of infections in adults was noted. Aim To detail the molecular epidemiology of the 2025 season in Europe. Methods Case and sequencing data was collected from members in the European Non-Polio Enterovirus Network (ENPEN). The participating sites included both clinical and public health laboratories. Results Data was collected from 13 countries at 23 sites. There were 187 clinical cases infected with EV-D68 and 127 detections in wastewater. Age data were available for 76\% (143/187), among which 90 cases were adults. VP1-based genotyping showed subclade A2/D to predominate in all age groups and across all participating countries, as well as in the sewage sampling performed at one site. Two interclade recombinant sequences were detected among 22 whole genome sequences. Conclusion The observed shift towards adult cases and subclade A2/D predominance warrants continued monitoring to determine whether this represents a sustained epidemiological change. The detection of interclade recombinant variants highlights a need to supplement regular VP1-based genotyping with whole-genome sequencing.

items.title: Evaluating the Acceptability of Lyme Disease Prevention Strategies in Ottawa, Canada: A Mixed-Methods Study
items.abstract: Introduction: In recent years, the province of Ontario has reported one of the highest Lyme disease incidence rates in Canada due to the abundance of habitat that favours the survival and reproduction of ticks and wildlife species that carry the LD pathogen (Borrelia burgdorferi). The aim of this study was to understand the acceptability and feasibility of various methods for LD prevention in the context of peri-urban settings in Ottawa, where LD is an emerging problem. Methods: This research used an exploratory sequential mixed methods design. We conducted 12 semi-structured key informant interviews with public health practitioners, land management officials, and community members to identify the most locally acceptable and feasible LD interventions. We used themes that emerged during the interviews to develop and refine a previously validated questionnaire and implement a population-representative cross-sectional survey to evaluate public acceptability and feasibility, which applied a 9-point acceptability scale to this context. The survey also collected information on frequency of tick bites, uptake of LD prevention behaviours, and explanatory variables including demographic information, property type and characteristics, and engagement with occupational or recreational outdoor activities. We distributed the survey to the Ottawa public via a web panel in 2024. Results: A total of 1015 participants responded to the survey. Findings from both key informant interviews and the population survey indicated higher acceptability of personal protection strategies and landscape management strategies. Twenty-nine (29) percent of survey respondents reported knowing someone with an LD diagnosis and 3% reported having received a diagnosis of LD at some point, while 22% and 16% of respondents reported having at least one tick encounter or tick bite in the last year, respectively. Only 10% reported consistently using some methods of protection against ticks while outdoors. Acceptability of interventions was more consistently associated with respondents’ sociodemographic characteristics than with their risk and exposure indices, which varied greatly in their contribution to acceptability across intervention types. Conclusions: In our study, participants generally found host-targeted and chemical strategies to be the least acceptable type of intervention to prevent LD, while personal prevention strategies, land management, and natural alternatives to chemicals were found to be the most acceptable in the Ottawa context. The factors associated with higher acceptability varied by intervention type. This information will be helpful in producing high quality, targeted messaging to promote the uptake of different LD interventions. Overall, these findings will help to better inform policy on feasible and acceptable LD prevention practices that respond to local population preferences and context.

items.title: Pragmatic Evaluation of Effectiveness and Acceptability of the Bristol Medication Review Toolkit (BRISMED) Protocol for a multicentre cluster randomised trial
items.abstract: Introduction: Medicines are a key healthcare intervention. Medicines optimisation aims to ensure safe and effective use of medicines, with medication reviews a critical component. However, evidence around how reviews should be structured and delivered is limited. The Bristol Medication Review Toolkit comprises a review model and practical supporting materials to facilitate comprehensive, patient-centred, structured medication reviews. The BRISMED trial aims to evaluate the clinical effectiveness and acceptability of the Toolkit compared with standard general practice care. Methods BRISMED is a multicentre, open-label, cluster-randomised controlled trial, with two parallel groups. General practices within the Oxford RCGP Research Surveillance Centre (RSC) network will be selected to participate, representing 500 primary care networks (PCNs) in England. Randomisation will occur at PCN level. The intervention will take place at the practice level, with no patient-level recruitment. Practices will either undertake usual care (control group, 250 PCNs) or receive the BRISMED Toolkit (intervention group, 250 PCNs) over the same 12-month intervention delivery period. The primary outcome will be potentially inappropriate prescribing (PIP), defined as the proportion of patients with ≥1 STOPP/START indicator at 12 months (binary outcome per patient). Secondary outcomes will include additional prescribing metrics and healthcare utilisation. Outcomes will be determined using routinely collected electronic health data. The primary analysis will use mixed-effects logistic regression, on an intention-to-treat basis. A parallel mixed-methods process evaluation in a subset of practices will examine intervention implementation and provide context for interpretation of the trial findings, alongside a cost consequence analysis. Findings will be disseminated through publications, conferences and stakeholder engagement. Patients and the public will contribute throughout the study, supporting research delivery and dissemination. Ethics and registration The study has received approval from the West of Scotland NHS Research Ethics Committee 1 (reference 24/WS/0031). The trial is prospectively registered with ISRCTN (reference 12979016, registration date 3/6/2024).

items.title: Study on Digital Dependence in Later Life through Psychosocial Drivers of Screen Addiction among Urban Elderly People through Logistic Regression Approach
items.abstract: Abstract The increasing use of digital technologies among elderly individuals has led to emerging concerns regarding screen addiction, particularly in urban settings characterized by social isolation. This study examines the determinants of screen addiction using a multiple logistic regression framework. The binary response variable captures the presence of screen dependency, while covariates include socio-demographic, psychological, and lifestyle factors such as loneliness, living status, physical activity, social interaction, sleep quality, and digital literacy. A synthetic dataset is generated to reflect realistic behavioral patterns, and model parameters are estimated via maximum likelihood. The analysis identifies loneliness and living alone as significant risk factors, whereas social interaction and physical activity exhibit protective effects. The findings provide quantitative insights into an emerging public health issue and support the design of targeted intervention strategies.\cite{pew2019tech}

items.title: Personal experiences in the health-disease process of Spinocerebellar Ataxia 7: a phenomenological study
items.abstract: Abstract Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7 (SCA7) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder characterized by gait disturbances, dysarthria, and vision loss. In Mexico, a high incidence has been documented in the state of Veracruz, with many families having one or more affected members. This has negative repercussions on the economy, social, work, and family relationships, making it a public health problem. This study employs qualitative and interpretive methodologies derived from phenomenology based on people's everyday lives to understand their experiences. A person with the disease, a primary caregiver, and a person at risk describe the meaning and impact of the disease on their family and community. From a holistic perspective, the objective is to enable social work and the multidisciplinary team to understand how daily life is altered by the changes to which people must adapt due to the disease, their daily experiences in relation to their knowledge, how they feel upon receiving the diagnosis, the prognosis, the explanation, and the meaning they attribute to SCA7. This will enable the design of individualized, group, and community intervention strategies to mitigate the social effects of the disease and address the factors that disrupt their family and community relationships.

items.title: Post-Earthquake Dust Contamination: Elemental Composition, Asbestos, and Inorganic Fibers in a GIS-Based Environmental Health Assessment of Hatay, Türkiye
items.abstract: Abstract The twin earthquakes that struck Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye on February 6, 2023, caused widespread destruction and loss of life. This study offers a unique perspective on multi-pollutant assessment in post-earthquake urban areas by detecting heavy metals, asbestos, and inorganic fibers in dust samples taken from collapsed building foundations in the Hatay city center, and identifying potentially sensitive areas in terms of environmental and public health using GIS. Dust samples collected from 61 locations were sieved into three size fractions, and elemental analyzed via XRF. Qualitative pollution was assessed using the enrichment factor and ecological risk index, and spatial distribution maps generated for heavy metal concentration. SEM-EDS identified 1,370 fibrous objects across 23 sites, including 10 potentially asbestos fibers. Despite the extremely small absolute number of confirmed asbestos fibers, asbestos was detected primarily at sites consisting of older informal housing, suggesting legacy contamination. Spatial analysis showed elemental concentrations positively correlated with demolished building age and proximity to traffic arteries, revealing distinct anthropogenic contamination hotspots. The ecological risk index of 168.6 indicated moderate ecological risk for the overall study area. High concentrations of major elements such as Ca, Si, Mg, Fe, and Al are consistent with composition of construction and demolition wastes, particularly those related to cement and raw materials, and were analyzed using PCA in this study. These findings highlight the need for protective measures against dust inhalation in post-earthquake areas and underscore the importance of further research on airborne exposure for environmental and public health.

items.title: Land Use and Land Cover Influence on the Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Pesticides in a Drinking Water Source Watershed in Northeastern Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Pesticide contamination of surface waters has become a major environmental concern in tropical watersheds because changes in land use intensify diffuse contaminant transport and threaten aquatic ecosystems and human health. This study investigated the spatial and temporal distribution of pesticides in relation to land use and land cover in the Mangues river watershed, a source of public drinking water in northeastern Brazil. Land-use mapping was integrated with the monitoring of 36 pesticides during three seasonal campaigns conducted between 2022 and 2023. The watershed showed strong anthropogenic pressure, with pasture representing 45.05% of the total land area and up to 76% in upstream segments. Fifteen pesticides were detected, thirteen of which are currently banned or unauthorized in Brazil, with organochlorines predominating. Significant temporal differences were observed among monitoring campaigns. Persistent organochlorines predominated throughout the monitoring period, whereas more recently used pesticides became more evident during the rainy season, reflecting the combined influence of historical contamination, land use, and seasonal hydrological processes. Endrin showed the highest concentration among organochlorines (12.71 µg L⁻¹) in October 2022, whereas methyl parathion reached the highest concentration overall (22.29 µg L⁻¹) in February 2023. These findings highlight the need for continuous environmental monitoring, riparian vegetation restoration, and integrated watershed management to protect water quality and aquatic ecosystems.

items.title: An implementation case study for Cascaded Case-Management Training and surge staffing intervention during Malawi’s 2022-2023 Outbreak
items.abstract: Abstract Background : Between 2022 and 2024 Malawi experienced the largest and deadliest cholera outbreak in its history, with more than 59,000 cases and an overall case fatality rate (CFR) of 3%. The outbreak was compounded by successive tropical cyclones and coincided with active COVID-19 and polio responses, exposing a two-decade capacity gap in cholera case management. In December 2022 the outbreak was declared a national public health emergency. Methods: We conducted an implementation case study of a three-component intervention delivered in February 2023: rapid cascaded case-management training, deployment of repurposed clinical surge staff, and facility-based mentorship at cholera treatment centres/units (CTCs/CTUs). Ten master trainers, trained a 46-member training-of-trainers (ToT), who then cascaded training to 600 clinicians across five parallel sites (Mzuzu, Lilongwe, Mponela, Blantyre and Liwonde) over 17 days. Knowledge was assessed with paired pre- and post-training tests (25 items). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated changes in test scores by cadre, time and training site. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex and district, estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for mortality across pre-intervention (January 2022 – January 2023), active-intervention (February 2023) and post-intervention (March – December 2023) phases, using the national cholera line list. Results: We trained and deployed 572 healthcare workers. Paired knowledge data were available for 475 cascaded-training participants (17% attrition). items.title: Toxic Leadership and Nurses’ Turnover Intention in a Bangladeshi Healthcare Context: Does Job Satisfaction Play a Role?
items.abstract: Abstract Background Retaining nurses is a critical health workforce concern, particularly in resource-constrained health systems. Toxic leadership has been linked to adverse workforce outcomes among nurses, but the mechanisms linking toxic leadership behavior to turnover intention may vary across healthcare contexts. This study examined the relationship between toxic leadership behavior and nurses’ turnover intention and investigated whether job satisfaction mediated this relationship in a tertiary public hospital in Bangladesh. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 203 registered nurses selected through simple random sampling. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results Toxic leadership behavior was positively related to turnover intention ( β = 0.551, 95% CI [0.425, 0.677], p β = −0.270, 95% CI [−0.416, −0.158], p β = −0.072, 95% CI [−0.212, 0.064], p = .304). The indirect effect through job satisfaction was also not significant ( β = 0.020, 95% CI [−0.019, 0.068], p = .357). Conclusions Toxic leadership behavior positively predicted turnover intention and negatively predicted job satisfaction. Job satisfaction did not mediate the relationship between toxic leadership behavior and turnover intention. Alternative mechanisms linking toxic leadership to withdrawal intentions require further investigation.

items.title: Meteorological and HYSPLIT-Derived Transport Influences on PM₂.₅ Exposure in a Khulna City, Bangladesh
items.abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is a major public health concern in South Asian cities, yet its meteorological drivers and transport dynamics remain poorly characterized in coastal Bangladesh. This study examined the temporal variability of PM₂.₅ in Khulna City using continuous hourly measurements from the CAMS-8 station (2024), combined with NASA POWER meteorological data and NOAA-HYSPLIT backward trajectories, through multiple linear regression, Random Forest, Seasonal-Trend Decomposition (STL), and K-means clustering. PM₂.₅ showed strong seasonality, peaking in winter (~121 µg m⁻³, nearly eight times the WHO 24-hour guideline) and falling to ~15 µg m⁻³ during the monsoon. Temperature and surface pressure were the dominant Random Forest predictors (58.7% and 50.2% of variance; OOB R² = 0.64), while temperature and relative humidity consistently suppressed PM₂.₅ in all MLR models. HYSPLIT analysis revealed a bimodal transport pattern: short-range northwesterly continental trajectories in winter versus long-range southerly maritime inflows during the monsoon. K-means clustering identified four pollution-meteorology regimes (~19 to ~121 µg m⁻³), and STL residuals detected pre-monsoon pollution spikes (~138 µg m⁻³) linked to long-range continental transport. These findings show that PM₂.₅ in Khulna is jointly governed by thermodynamic and transport processes, underscoring the need for season-specific air quality management.

items.title: Place and Post-Crisis Subjective Well-Being: A Year-Long Spatial Analysis of Built Environment and Public Sentiment in Tokyo
items.abstract: Abstract How did subjective well-being evolve after a public health crisis, and did this evolution vary across neighborhoods? Using a year of geotagged Twitter data from Tokyo (May 2021 to June 2022) across 2,040 grids, we examine the built environment's role in shaping well-being recovery. We use public sentiment expressed in social media as a proxy for the affective dimension of subjective well-being. To isolate economic confounding from the built environment–well-being relationship, we employ a Mixed Geographically Weighted Instrumental Variables Regression (MGWIVR) model that jointly addresses spatial heterogeneity and economic endogeneity. We find that recovery is neither temporally monotonic nor spatially uniform. Lifting emergency orders produced only a fleeting boost; the annual trend was a slight decline, punctuated by weekend and event-driven fluctuations. More striking, the same built environment attributes can have opposite effects in different districts: park density and educational facilities are positively associated with sentiment in some areas but negatively in others, while restaurant accessibility shows similar spatial reversal. This spatial contingency suggests that well-being recovery is not determined by the presence of facilities per se, but by how they interact with local socioeconomic and spatial conditions. These findings challenge the assumption that built environment improvements uniformly enhance subjective well-being, and demonstrate that well-being recovery is spatially contingent, challenging universalist assumptions in well-being research.

items.title: Fecal indicator bacteria in Alalay Lagoon, Cochabamba, Bolivia: sanitary assessment and implications for opportunistic pathogen monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Alalay Lagoon, located in Cochabamba, Bolivia, is affected by chronic fecal and chemical contamination, raising environmental and public health concerns. This study assessed the use of fecal indicator bacteria (FIB): total coliforms (TC), fecal coliforms (FC), and Escherichia coli , as sanitary indicators and supporting signals for microbiological risk in an urban eutrophic lagoon. Water samples from three lagoon sites were collected monthly from April 2019 to January 2020, with additional samples collected from inflow channels in January 2020, and were analyzed by culture-based methods. FIB levels exceeded Bolivian regulatory limits (fecal coliforms > 1,000 CFU/100 mL), supporting the influence of wastewater inputs. Spearman correlation analysis showed strong associations among classical fecal indicators, particularly TC and FC (ρ = 0.74, p Streptococcus faecalis showed a significant negative correlation with FC and a positive association with Clostridium spp., suggesting selective persistence patterns under lagoon conditions. The results indicate that FIB are useful for sanitary assessment of fecal contamination, but they should not be interpreted as definitive predictors of opportunistic pathogens. Complementary molecular-based and physicochemical monitoring is recommended to improve the risk assessment of impacted urban water bodies such as the Alalay Lagoon.

items.title: Reframing Leishmania 360° in the MISEV2023 Era: A Translational Framework for Extracellular Vesicle Biomarkers and One Health Implementation
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication between Leishmania parasites and their hosts through the transfer of proteins, lipids and nucleic acids that influence immune responses, parasite persistence and disease progression. Despite more than a decade of investigation, translation of EV-associated discoveries into clinical, veterinary and public-health applications remains limited. Methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting practices and insufficient validation continue to impede the development of clinically actionable biomarkers. Concurrently, the evolution from MISEV2018 to MISEV2023 reflects the broader maturation of extracellular-vesicle science, shifting the field from descriptive characterisation towards greater emphasis on reproducibility, functional validation and translational relevance. Here, we revisit the Leishmania 360° concept through the complementary lenses of MISEV2023, translational medicine and One Health. We argue that the principal challenge is no longer the identification of vesicular cargo, but the establishment of evidence-based frameworks capable of determining whether EV-associated signals are sufficiently validated to support clinical, veterinary or public-health decision-making. A central conceptual advance is the Dual-Compartment Liquid Biopsy Paradigm, whereby parasite-derived and host-response EVs are interpreted as complementary indicators of pathogen biology and host pathophysiology, providing a multidimensional framework for diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring and surveillance. Building upon this concept, we introduce LEV-MISEV, a claim-to-evidence framework that extends MISEV2023 principles beyond methodological reporting by linking biological, clinical and public-health claims to proportional evidentiary requirements. We further propose a staged translational framework comprising the Translational Readiness Level for Extracellular Vesicles (TRL-EV) and the Leishmania 360° Translational Evidence Matrix. Whereas TRL-EV evaluates biomarker maturity along the pathway from discovery to implementation, the Translational Evidence Matrix assesses the overall strength of evidence across biological, analytical, clinical, operational and One Health domains. Together, these complementary frameworks identify translational bottlenecks, prioritise validation efforts and support evidence-based implementation planning. Finally, we position EV signatures as a molecular intelligence layer within climate-informed One Health surveillance systems integrating human, canine, vector and environmental data. Application of these frameworks indicates that no EV-based application in leishmaniasis has yet progressed beyond the stage of clinically associated biomarker candidates. We therefore propose a translational roadmap that integrates biological plausibility, analytical validity, clinical validity, implementation readiness and One Health utility. Collectively, these concepts reposition EVs not merely as sources of candidate biomarkers, but as components of a translational platform capable of supporting precision diagnostics, therapeutic monitoring, risk assessment and integrated surveillance. More broadly, the proposed framework may provide a transferable model for evidence-based biomarker development across infectious, parasitic and vector-borne diseases beyond leishmaniasis.

items.title: Elimination of tumors and their metastasis by a thermally responsive silica nanoparticle decorated with an anti-PD-L1 antibody fragment.
items.abstract: Metastasis and recurrence remain the leading causes of cancer-related mortality; however, existing therapies offer limited protection against systemic tumor spread following primary treatment. Here, we report a dual-function nanoplatform, anti-programmed cell death protein-ligand 1 PD-L1 antigen-binding fragment (Fab)-conjugated thermally responsive silica (α-TRS) nanoparticles, rationally designed to achieve complete ablation of primary tumors through photothermal therapy (PTT) while simultaneously priming systemic antitumor immunity to suppress distant metastasis. Indocyanine green (ICG) was encapsulated within mesoporous silica nanoparticles with high efficiency (91.2%), and the Fab of an anti-PD-L1 antibody was site-specifically conjugated to the nanoparticle surface via NTA-Ni 2+ /His-tag chemistry. With 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation, α-TRS generated sufficient heat (∼50 °C) to induce ablative tumor cell death in vitro and achieved complete remission of 4T1 breast tumors and CT-26 colon tumors in vivo following intratumoral injection. Critically, mice cured of primary tumors by α-TRS-mediated PTT were fully protected against subsequent intravenous rechallenge with lung-metastatic 4T1 and CT-26 cells, whereas mice treated with PTT alone (TRS without Fab) showed only partial protection. This abscopal-like protection was mechanistically linked to the robust activation of tumor antigen-specific CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, including enhanced production of interferon (IFN)-γ, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, perforin, and granzyme B in response to tumor antigens. These findings suggest that ablative PTT combined with local PD-L1 checkpoint blockade can convert a localized thermal intervention into durable systemic immunity, offering a promising proof-of-concept strategy for simultaneously treating primary tumors and preventing metastatic recurrence.

items.title: The Association Between Self-Perceived Auditory Disability and Psychosocial Health in a Longitudinal Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Objectives Hearing loss affects millions of people worldwide and is linked to psychosocial consequences such as loneliness, depression, and anxiety. Self-reported hearing problems may offer unique insights into emotional and social functioning beyond what audiometric tests reveal. Evidence on the association between self-perceived auditory functioning and psychosocial health in adults remains scarce. This study seeks to explore this relationship. Design This study used baseline and follow-up data from the Netherlands Longitudinal Study on Hearing, a prospective cohort study with adults aged 18 to 70 years at enrollment. Self-perceived auditory disability was assessed using the Amsterdam Inventory for Auditory Disability and Handicap (AIADH), while psychosocial outcomes were measured using validated questionnaires assessing loneliness, distress, depression, anxiety, and somatization. The associations between self-perceived auditory disability and psychosocial outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations, accounting for repeated measurements, potential effect modifiers, and confounders. Results A total of 2897 participants (63% female; mean age at baseline 48.1 years) contributed data across up to four measurement rounds. Higher self-perceived auditory disability (AIADH) was consistently associated with worse psychosocial outcomes across all domains, showing graded associations. Compared with participants reporting little or no auditory disability (AIADH 0 to 6), those in the highest AIADH quartile (38 to 84) reported significantly higher loneliness scores (scale 0 to 11; B = 1.30; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.98 to 1.61), including both social loneliness (scale 0 to 5; B = 0.69; 95% CI: 0.52 to 0.87) and emotional loneliness (scale 0 to 6; B = 0.61; 95% CI: 0.41 to 0.82). Psychological distress (scale 0 to 32) increased progressively with higher AIADH scores, with participants in the highest quartile reporting on average 3.96 points higher distress levels than those in the lowest quartile (95% CI: 3.34 to 4.58). Higher AIADH scores were also associated with higher mean levels of depressive symptoms (scale 0 to 12; ratio of means [RoM] up to 4.50; 95% CI: 3.02 to 6.67), anxiety symptoms (scale 0 to 24; RoM up to 3.13; 95% CI: 2.36 to 4.15), and somatization symptoms (scale 0 to 32; RoM = 1.58; 95% CI: 1.46 to 1.71). Effect modification was observed in specific analyses by age, hearing device use, tinnitus, and age of onset of hearing loss. All associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for objective speech-in-noise performance. Conclusions These findings highlight the broad psychosocial impact of self-reported hearing difficulties, emphasizing that hearing loss affects not only communication but also mental well-being. Incorporating self-reported hearing assessments into audiological evaluations and providing psychosocial support when indicated alongside hearing interventions may improve overall well-being.

items.title: Domestic Measles Importations in Washington State, January 2026.
items.abstract: AbstractMeasles outbreaks are increasing in frequency and size in the United States. Within 2 weeks, there were five distinct out-of-state measles importations into Washington State epidemiologically connected to an outbreak in South Carolina, resulting in a total of 26 measles cases during January-February 2026. Genomic analyses supported epidemiologic conclusions regarding exposure sources of imported cases and independence among importations. Adherence to isolation and quarantine likely limited onward transmission in undervaccinated communities. Combining timely genomic data analysis with epidemiologic information can strengthen understanding of measles outbreaks as public health jurisdictions prepare to respond to increases in imported measles cases.

items.title: Longitudinal Serum Biomarker Profiles of Inflammation and Cartilage Matrix Metabolism During the First Year After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
items.abstract: Background Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury initiates biological processes linked to joint tissue degeneration. The longitudinal time course of serum biomarkers reflecting inflammation and cartilage metabolism after ACL reconstruction (ACLR), particularly in comparison with uninjured controls, has not been characterized across the first postoperative year. Hypothesis Inflammatory (monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 [MCP-1]) and degradative (matrix metalloproteinase-3 [MMP-3]) biomarker concentrations would be elevated pre-ACLR and decrease over time, whereas cartilage turnover biomarker concentrations (cartilage oligomeric matrix protein [COMP] and type II collagen degradation-to-synthesis ratio [C2C:CPII]) would increase postoperatively. Also, pre-ACLR biomarker concentrations would be associated with concentrations at 6 and 12 months post-ACLR. Study design Cohort study; Level of evidence, 2. Methods A total of 33 individuals with ACL injuries (52% female; mean age, 20.8 ± 2.4 years) were evaluated pre-ACLR and at 6 and 12 months post-ACLR. A total of 33 matched uninjured controls were included. Serum concentrations of MCP-1, MMP-3, COMP, and C2C:CPII were assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Linear mixed-effects models with model-based contrasts were used to evaluate differences across groups and time points. ACLR-only linear mixed-effects regression models were used to assess associations between pre-ACLR and follow-up biomarker concentrations. Exploratory post hoc models evaluated differences by concomitant injury status. Results MCP-1 was elevated in individuals with ACL injuries compared with controls at all ACLR time points (all P adj P adj P adj ≤ .021), with no changes across ACLR time points. C2C:CPII was greater at 12 months post-ACLR than at pre-ACLR and 6 months post-ACLR (both P adj P adj = .001). Pre-ACLR MCP-1, MMP-3, and COMP concentrations were associated with concentrations at both 6 and 12 months post-ACLR (all P ≤ .006), whereas C2C:CPII was associated only with 12-month concentrations ( P = .018). Conclusion Inflammatory and cartilage-related biomarkers remain altered throughout the first year after ACLR, suggesting that the biological response is not fully resolved by reconstruction and standard rehabilitation but extends beyond the early postoperative period.

items.title: Population-based trends and distributional changes in physical fitness among university students aged 19-22 years in China over three decades.
items.abstract: This paper aims to assess population-based trends and distributional changes in physical fitness among university students aged 19-22 years from 1985 to 2019. Height, weight, body mass index (BMI) and physical fitness data for Han Chinese university students aged 19-22 years were obtained from eight successive cross-sectional Chinese National Surveillance on Students' Constitution and Health surveys from 1985 to 2019. Population-based trends were estimated by sample-weighted linear regression with a post-stratification population-weighted procedure. There was a moderate decrease in 50-m dash performance, a small decrease in standing long jump performance, large decreases in endurance run performance, and a negligible improvement in stand/sit-and-reach performance. Males experienced a large decrease in body pull-up performance, whereas females experienced a small improvement in sit-up 60s performance. There were moderate increases in mean height and weight from 1985 to 2019 and BMI from 2000 to 2019. The variability increased in most test-sex-age groups. Performance in 50-m dashes, endurance runs, standing long jumps, and stand/sit-and-reaches among the low-fitness population and performance in pull-ups and sit-ups 60s among the middle-fitness population decreased more or improved less. The government should implement differentiated health promotion programs, especially for those with greater health risks.

items.title: Quality of Life and Factors Associated With Quality of Life Among Older Adults Living in Nursing Homes Worldwide: An Integrative Review.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate and synthesize existing research on factors influencing the quality of life (QoL) of older adults living in nursing homes worldwide. Method The current review followed Whittemore and Knafl's integrative review technique, using the Social Ecological Model (SEM) to organize and identify key components. Results Thirty articles met inclusion criteria, collectively addressing 10 subthemes organized into five principal themes based on the SEM. These themes, derived from individual study findings, included intrapersonal, interpersonal, institutional, community, and public policy factors. The identified subthemes encompassed sociodemographic factors, well-being and self-interest, physical health conditions, mental health conditions, social support, family relationships, staff-resident relationships, evaluation, community support, and policy factors. Conclusion Findings highlight that factors across all five SEM levels contribute to QoL of older adults in nursing homes, emphasizing the need for comprehensive, multi-level care to ensure holistic support for this population.

items.title: Describing the patient trajectory for unplanned care in a region of Flanders, Belgium: A prospective observational study.
items.abstract: Background Demand for unplanned care in Belgium is high, placing pressure on both out-of-hours primary care facilities (OOHPCF) and emergency departments (ED). Understanding patient trajectories may help optimise care pathways and resource planning for planned and unplanned care. Objective To describe patient presentations and trajectories at OOHPCF and EDs in a region of Flanders, Belgium. Methods Data were collected in six EDs and three OOHPCF in the greater {redacted} region. All consultations were recorded during three randomly selected days in EDs and one full week in OOHPCF in 2024. Results A total of 1,469 ED and 857 OOHPCF consultations were analysed. In EDs, trauma was the most common presentation (32%), followed by ear, nose and throat (ENT) and dermatology conditions (22%). In OOHPCF, trauma and orthopaedic problems accounted for 20% of consultations, followed by ENT (17%) and dermatology (14%). Most ED patients (71%) were discharged home. Self-referral accounted for 65% of ED visits; these patients were generally younger and presented with lower-acuity conditions. One in five patients had consulted another healthcare provider within the previous week. Pain and worry were the main drivers for attendance. Attending clinicians in both settings considered up to one-third of consultations manageable in planned care. Conclusion Rather than restricting access or apportioning blame to patients, our findings indicate the need to reassess measures throughout planned and unplanned care pathways for timely access to the most appropriate care setting while maintaining patient safety and equitable access to services.

items.title: Artificial Stone Silicosis: New Face of an Old Disease.
items.abstract: Artificial stone (AS) silicosis has emerged as a major global occupational health concern, challenging the perception of silicosis as a disease of the past. Driven by the fabrication of AS products containing high concentrations of crystalline silica (>90%), this rapidly progressive form disproportionately affects younger workers and develops after a much shorter exposure duration (median 7-19 years) than in classic silicosis. As cases continue to emerge worldwide, clinicians and occupational health practitioners are increasingly likely to encounter affected workers in clinical practice. This review provides a clinically focused synthesis of the current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and management of AS silicosis. Compared with traditional silicosis, the unique physicochemical properties of AS dust may amplify lung toxicity and promote a self-perpetuating inflammatory response. This frequently results in rapid development of progressive massive fibrosis, with disease progression often continuing after exposure cessation. Diagnosis is often delayed because of overlapping clinical features and the limited sensitivity of conventional screening tools, highlighting the importance of early clinical recognition, detailed occupational history-taking, and the use of high-resolution computed tomography where appropriate. Lung transplantation remains the only definitive treatment for advanced disease, underscoring the importance of prevention. Effective prevention requires strong workplace controls, systematic medical surveillance, and appropriate regulatory measures. Clinicians play a key role in early detection, patient education, and mandatory disease reporting. Coordinated action across clinical, occupational, and policy domains is essential to improve recognition, strengthen preventive measures, and avert further cases of this highly preventable occupational disease.

items.title: Microsporidiosis After Solid Organ Transplantation: A Multi-Species Case Series.
items.abstract: Background Microsporidiosis is an uncommon opportunistic infection in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Case-level data on multi-species disease and management remain limited. Methods We retrospectively reviewed SOT recipients with microsporidiosis at Mayo Clinic from January 2000 through February 2026. Cases were identified by text search and institutional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) records. Clinical, microbiologic, treatment, immunosuppression, and outcome data were abstracted. Results Ten recipients were identified: six kidney, two kidney-pancreas, and two heart recipients. Eight had enteritis and two had disseminated disease. Enterocytozoon bieneusi caused seven infections; the remaining cases were Encephalitozoon sp. enteritis, disseminated E. cuniculi, and disseminated Anncaliia algerae. All enteritis cases experienced diarrhea; seven experienced weight loss, five developed acute kidney injury, and five required hospitalization. The most common treatment administered was nitazoxanide (n = 6). Among these three achieved clinical remission, one improved without documented remission, and two had transient or partial improvement followed by recurrent diarrhea. Among four patients whose antimetabolite was held, reduced, or replaced at or before treatment, all improved clinically. In the two initially treated without antimetabolite modification, responses were transient or incomplete. Both Encephalitozoon infections achieved clinical remission with albendazole. Disseminated A. algerae was fatal. Conclusions Microsporidiosis after SOT demonstrated a species-associated clinical spectrum: E. bieneusi was confined to enteritis, whereas non-E. bieneusi species caused both enteric and disseminated disease. In E. bieneusi enteritis, nitazoxanide improved symptoms, but responses were incomplete when antimetabolite therapy was continued. Encephalitozoon infections responded to albendazole, whereas disseminated A. algerae was refractory and fatal.

items.title: Music-based interventions for people with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis.
items.abstract: Rationale People receiving haemodialysis for kidney failure experience substantial symptom burden, including anxiety, depression, and pain, which adversely affect physical function and quality of life. Music-based interventions are increasingly used as non-pharmacological strategies to address these symptoms; however, their effectiveness and the certainty of the evidence remain unclear. An updated systematic review of recent randomised controlled trials (RCTs) is therefore warranted. Objectives To assess the effects of music-based interventions on fatigue, blood pressure, depression, pain, anxiety, stress, quality of life, and sleep quality in people with kidney failure receiving haemodialysis. Search methods We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus and two trials registers up to 16 May 2025. Eligibility criteria We included RCTs involving participants with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis, comparing music-based interventions with controls where music-based interventions were not provided (e.g. standard care, headphones without music intervention, or video). We excluded studies involving temporary haemodialysis for acute kidney injury or other conditions. Outcomes We examined the impact of music-based interventions on fatigue, blood pressure, depression, and pain over the short term (up to four weeks), medium term (four weeks to six months), and long term (more than six months). These outcomes were prespecified as critical outcomes for GRADE assessment and included in the summary of findings table. Other important outcomes included anxiety, sleep quality, stress and quality of life. Risk of bias We used the Cochrane risk of bias 2 tool (RoB 2) to assess bias in the RCTs. Synthesis methods We synthesised results for each outcome using meta-analysis, where possible, applying a restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects model. We measured outcomes as mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs when all included studies used the same outcome scale, or standardised mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs when different outcome scales were used. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of evidence for critical outcomes. Included studies We included a total of 27 studies involving 1584 participants, of which 24 studies (1467 participants) contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Comparator interventions included usual care, no intervention, headphones without music or white noise, and video interventions. The studies took place in 13 countries and territories across Asia, Europe, North America, and South America. Synthesis of results Critical outcomes Fatigue Music-based interventions may reduce short-term fatigue (measured on the 10-point Piper Fatigue Scale) compared with usual care or other comparator interventions (MD -3.14, 95% CI -3.83 to -2.45; 1 study, 62 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on medium-term fatigue (SMD -1.99, 95% CI -3.92 to -0.06; I² = 91%; 2 studies, 86 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated fatigue in the long term. Blood pressure The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on short-term blood pressure (mmHg) (MD -5.95, 95% CI -10.56 to -1.34; I² = 70%; 8 studies, 674 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on medium-term blood pressure (MD -2.00, 95% CI -14.21 to 10.21; 1 study, 16 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated blood pressure in the long term. Depression The included studies evaluated depression using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Beck Depression Inventory and Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Music-based interventions may reduce depressive symptoms compared with usual care or other comparator interventions over the short term (SMD -0.88, 95% CI -1.51 to -0.25; I² = 84%; 6 studies, 489 participants; low-certainty evidence) and medium term (SMD -0.81, 95% CI -1.42 to -0.19; I² = 43%; 5 studies, 203 participants; low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated depression in the long term. Pain The included studies measured pain using the VAS, Kidney Disease Quality of Life Short Form, and McGill Pain Questionnaire. Music-based interventions may reduce short-term pain compared with usual care or other comparator interventions (SMD -0.89, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.15; I² = 92%; 8 studies, 675 participants; low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated pain in the medium or long term. Authors' conclusions Music-based interventions may reduce fatigue, depressive symptoms, and pain in people undergoing haemodialysis in the short term compared with usual care or other comparator interventions. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on blood pressure in the short term. In the medium term, music-based interventions may reduce depressive symptoms, but the evidence is very uncertain about their effects on fatigue and blood pressure. No studies reported long-term outcomes for these critical outcomes. Further large, well-designed RCTs with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the effects of music-based interventions for this population. items.title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in chickens: prevalence and genetic diversity: a systematic review and meta-analaysis.
items.abstract: 1. Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-EC) is an important antimicrobial-resistant pathogen in poultry that threatens animal health, food safety and public health. This study reviewed the global prevalence and genetic diversity of ESBL-EC in chickens and compared prevalence across continents and chicken production systems.2. A meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Forty-five studies published between 2014 and 2023, comprising 13 761 E. coli isolates from broiler, layer and mixed-breed chickens, were included. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled prevalence, while subgroup and meta-regression analyses explored heterogeneity. Any ESBL-associated genes were summarised.3. The pooled prevalence of ESBL-EC in chickens was 31.44% (95% CI: 23.81-39.07). Prevalence was highest in Asia (36.22%) and Africa (26.66%) and lowest in North America (5.20%). Broiler chickens showed substantially higher prevalence (33.13%) than layer chickens (8.79%).4. Genetic analysis demonstrated that CTX-M-type β-lactamases predominated, with blaCTX-M as the most frequently detected ESBL gene, followed by blaTEM and blaSHV . The higher prevalence in broiler chickens reflected intensive production systems, shorter production life spans and greater antimicrobial exposure. The lower prevalence in layer chickens reflects longer production life spans and comparatively lower antimicrobial usage.5. The resistant E. coli ESBL strain is widely distributed in poultry, particularly in production systems and in Asia and Africa. Strengthened antimicrobial stewardship, improved farm biosecurity and integrated 'One Health' surveillance are required to reduce the dissemination of ESBL-producing E. coli and mitigate associated public health risks.

items.title: Family Resilience and Coping in Disasters, Pandemics, and Large-Scale Crises: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Background Disasters, large-scale crises, and prolonged adversities such as pandemics can place sustained psychosocial pressure on families and disrupt everyday family functioning. Although family resilience is increasingly used to explain why some families adapt better than others, the evidence base is dispersed across conceptual, empirical, and intervention-focused work. Methods We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science and included peer-reviewed studies that examined family resilience or family coping in disaster, pandemic, or sustained adversity contexts. Study selection followed PRISMA 2020 principles. Data were extracted using a standardized form and synthesized using narrative and thematic approaches. Results Forty-two studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Across contexts, family resilience was most often described as a dynamic, system-level process that involves shared meaning-making, organizational flexibility, and effective communication. Parenting practices repeatedly emerged as a key pathway linking family resilience to child adjustment. Resilience-oriented family interventions reported overall beneficial effects across disaster, pandemic, and serious illness contexts, with no evidence of harm. Conclusions Family resilience is a critical contributor to psychosocial adaptation during disasters and large-scale crises. Interventions that strengthen family-level processes-especially communication, coping skills, and supportive parenting-may offer a scalable approach to improve preparedness, response, and longer-term recovery.

items.title: The Raine Study: a multigenerational Western Australian birth and life-course cohort advancing research on the developmental origins of health and disease.
items.abstract: The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework has transformed understanding of how early-life exposures shape health across the life course, yet populations from Oceania remain underrepresented in this research. The Raine Study is a globally unique, multigenerational longitudinal pregnancy cohort established in Western Australia, one of the world's most geographically isolated regions. The study recruited 2900 pregnant women (Generation1) in 1989, which resulted in 2868 live births forming Generation 2, and is now currently recruiting Generation 3 (the children of Generation 2). This paper describes the evolution of the Raine Study from its origins as a pregnancy cohort grounded in DOHaD to a comprehensive life-course and multigenerational research resource. This resource has led to key research findings that have informed international clinical guidelines and national and state health policies across areas including prenatal development and care safety, neurodevelopment, cardiometabolic health, obesity, liver disease, physical activity, mental health, sedentary behaviour, sleep, and assisted reproductive technologies. Central to the Raine Study's success is a longstanding commitment to participant partnership and engagement, resulting in exceptional retention and strong consumer involvement in governance and research prioritisation. The Raine Study demonstrates the critical value of well-characterised, place-based cohorts for advancing DOHaD and life-course science and provides a globally significant resource to inform prevention strategies, precision medicine, and public health policy across generations.

items.title: Post-Disaster Recovery, Cancer Care, and Family Well-Being in Japan: A Structural Equation Modeling Study.
items.abstract: Objective This study examined how subjective disaster recovery and cancer-care satisfaction jointly shape family well-being in Japan, and when better cancer care accompanies higher well-being. Methods A quota-stratified web survey of 2,179 adults aged 20-69 was conducted across Japan (September 2019), with quotas by Fukushima residency and family cancer experience. Subjective recovery from any major disaster within 10 years (unexposed; recovered or in prospect; no prospect), household cancer experience, and Short FAMCARE satisfaction were modeled against latent well-being by structural equation modeling. Results Among non-cancer households (n = 1,324), unrecovered damage was associated with lower well-being (β = -0.08, 95% CI -0.13 to -0.03, P = 0.001), with no association in cancer-affected households (β = 0.00, P = 0.98). Among cancer-affected families (n = 855), high satisfaction was associated with higher well-being (β = 0.17, P P = 0.014). Resting on small subgroups, this interaction is exploratory. Conclusions Better cancer care did not offset incomplete disaster recovery; its association with higher well-being was confined to households with recovery achieved or in prospect. These cross-sectional findings are consistent with delivering reconstruction and cancer care together.

items.title: Suicidal Behavior Before and After Hurricanes Irma and Maria in Puerto Rico: A Descriptive Analysis of Crisis Hotline (Línea PAS) Calls, 2015-2021.
items.abstract: Objective Natural disasters can increase the risk of suicidal behavior, particularly in resource-limited settings. We characterized suicidal ideation and attempts before and after Hurricanes Irma and Maria (September 2017) in Puerto Rico using crisis-hotline surveillance data. Methods We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of suicide-related calls to Línea PAS , Puerto Rico's 24/7 government crisis hotline, from January 2015 through December 2021 (84 months). Monthly counts of suicidal-ideation and suicide-attempt calls were aggregated, stratified by sex and age group, and displayed as a time series with September 2017 as the index event, with exact Poisson and Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Results Total suicide-related calls rose sharply about 2 months after landfall, peaking from November 2017 through January 2018 (maximum 4,548 calls in January 2018) before returning toward baseline by February 2018. Working-age adults (21-59 years) and women accounted for most calls. The surge coincided with prolonged power and telecommunications outages and with an independent rise in recorded suicide deaths. Conclusions These descriptive, ecological findings are consistent with a substantial mental-health burden following catastrophic hurricanes and coincided temporally with prolonged infrastructure disruption; the design cannot establish causation. They support integrating crisis-hotline-based behavioral-health surveillance and rapid utility restoration into disaster preparedness for climate-vulnerable regions.

items.title: Breakout Session 9: Physical Environment.
items.abstract: The physical environment of an alternate care facility (ACF) spans safety, security, infection prevention, emergency management, hazardous materials, and fire and life safety, and it proved inseparable from patient safety, staff wellbeing, and operational continuity. Symposium participants summarized operational lessons from establishing and sustaining ACFs across convention centers, hotels, tents, and other non-traditional spaces. Participants reported that effective sites integrated clinical staff into security and de-escalation rather than relying on law enforcement alone, controlled access through single monitored entrances, and managed both the internal care space and the external perimeter as part of patient care. Multidisciplinary walkthroughs were essential to identifying physical hazards before activation. Persistent challenges included the absence of smoke compartments in open and temporary structures, unverified ventilation and negative-pressure performance, unreliable power and connectivity, and environments lacking day-night differentiation that contributed to patient delirium. Recommended best practices include engineering environmental controls in advance, embedding infection prevention, wellness, and safety functions from activation, and protecting staff through dedicated respite and decompression space.

items.title: Development of the Alternate Care Facility Symposium: Understanding National Experiences in Planning and Operations.
items.abstract: Health care systems face challenges with patient surge during disasters. Alternate Care Facilities (ACFs) represent one strategy for expanding health care capacity when hospitals become overwhelmed. ACF implementation guidance remains largely informed by retrospective reports and expert opinion. Recognizing that many operational lessons reside within the experiential knowledge of responders rather than the published literature, the authors developed a national symposium to systematically learn from experts with direct ACF operational experience. Informed by prior research, the symposium employed purposive recruitment, structured facilitator guides, rotating breakout groups, dedicated facilitators and note takers, and standardized discussion prompts to capture practice-based insights across operational domains. This manuscript describes the rationale, conceptual framework, planning process, and execution of the 2025 Alternate Care Facility Symposium. The methods described provide a reproducible approach for translating distributed experiential expertise into actionable knowledge to strengthen disaster preparedness. Summaries of the findings from this symposium are published separately.

items.title: Breakout Session 3: Leadership Structures.
items.abstract: Establishing leadership and management structures for alternate care facilities (ACFs) presented governance challenges distinct from those of conventional hospital operations and were frequently shaped as much by political and inter-organizational dynamics as by clinical need. Symposium participants summarized operational lessons from leading ACFs across multiple jurisdictions and partnership models. Participants reported that effective ACFs typically mirrored hospital executive structures while operating under hybrid governance models that distributed authority, liability, and resources across multiple hospital systems and state agencies. Hospital Incident Command System (ICS) provided necessary scaffolding but was insufficient on its own; success depended on pre-existing inter-agency relationships and on credible leaders with the gravitas to mobilize resources across organizational boundaries. Persistent challenges included credentialing and electronic medical record (EMR) access delays, political directives that superseded clinical judgment, and severe interpersonal conflict that overwhelmed leadership without embedded human resources support. Recommended best practices include pre-identifying and training a cadre of ACF leaders, embedding human resources and behavioral health support within the leadership team, and clearly defining and protecting the ACF mission throughout activation and operations.

items.title: Breakout Session 10: Miscellaneous Topics.
items.abstract: This final breakout session provided subject matter experts with an opportunity to discuss additional considerations that were not previously covered during the Alternate Care Facilities (ACF) Symposium. Participants reflected on operational experiences not otherwise captured and discussed barriers, mitigation strategies, and future priorities for ACF implementation. Several recurring themes emerged. Despite significant hospital strain, many ACFs experienced underutilization due to institutional reluctance to transfer patients, financial and political considerations, limited stakeholder engagement, and patient mistrust of nontraditional care settings. Participants described successful approaches to improving operations, including staff wellness initiatives, work-rest cycles, community engagement, and communication strategies to improve patient trust. Persistent challenges included patient refusal of transfer, difficulties coordinating care and patient movement across multiple ACFs within a region, loss of institutional knowledge following staff turnover, and leadership fatigue due to limited redundancy among key operational personnel. Participants emphasized the need for regional coordination mechanisms, centralized repositories of operational lessons learned, earlier integration of non-clinical operational leaders, and deliberate communication strategies to increase trust among referring hospitals and communities. These findings suggest that successful ACF implementation depends on institutional trust, regional coordination, workforce sustainability, and preservation of operational knowledge to support future emergency response efforts.

items.title: Breakout Session 4: Clinical Operations.
items.abstract: Alternate care facilities (ACFs) established during disaster response operations are required to deliver safe clinical care under severe operational, staffing, and infrastructure constraints. This breakout session explored real-world experiences managing clinical operations within ACFs, emphasizing lessons learned from frontline leaders responsible for patient flow, escalation of care, documentation, discharge planning, and support services. Participants described highly adaptive workflows shaped by limited laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, and electronic health record capabilities. Many sites relied on simplified triage models, selective laboratory testing, courier-based diagnostics, and external vendor partnerships to sustain operations. Clinical success was associated with integration of social work, discharge planning, culturally responsive care, and management of vulnerable populations, including patients with behavioral health and substance use disorders. Participants identified significant challenges related to fragmented medical records, EHR downtime, staffing fatigue, language barriers, and inability to replicate hospital-level ancillary services. Key recommendations included embedding social support services early in operational planning, standardizing workflows, developing culturally informed liaison infrastructure, and strengthening backup documentation training. Findings highlight that effective ACF clinical operations depend not only on medical capability, but also on flexible systems supporting communication, discharge coordination, and continuity of care during disaster conditions.

items.title: Selection of Genetic Conditions for Multi-State Genomic Newborn Screening in BRIDGES-NBS.
items.abstract: Purpose BRIDGES-NBS is a feasibility study evaluating the integration of genome sequencing into newborn screening (NBS) across multiple U.S. states and territorial public health laboratory programs (PHLPs). We developed a list of conditions for screening. Methods We designed inclusion criteria and assembled an initial condition list from published resources. The list was revised by clinical experts, molecular geneticists, genetic counselors, PHLPs, rare disease advocacy organizations, the BRIDGES-NBS Community Advisory Board, and project leadership from the National Institutes of Health. For each condition, we provided a rationale for early detection, diagnostic signs or biomarkers, and treatments or surveillance strategies. Results The BRIDGES-NBS condition list includes 777 condition entries associated with 743 genes, one copy number variant, and two aneuploidies and is larger than those used in other genomic NBS research studies in the U.S. and United Kingdom. Most condition entries are inborn errors of immunity (37.2%), inherited metabolic disorders (18.7%), or endocrine conditions (18.1%). Nearly all condition entries (93.3%) can be confirmed using a non-genetic test. Conclusion BRIDGES-NBS has established a condition list for implementation across multiple state and territorial PHLPs, enabling the prospective evaluation of feasibility of population-wide genomic NBS.

items.title: Frailty Is Associated With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Adults With and Without HIV.
items.abstract: Background Frailty is a risk factor for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in older adults. People with HIV (PWH) have a heightened frailty burden, but the association of HIV and frailty with LUTS in people with and at risk for HIV is unknown. Methods Data from 1356 PWH (505 men, 851 women) and 820 without HIV (419 men, 401 women) enrolled in the MACS-WIHS Combined Cohort Study who completed the Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network 10-Item Symptom Index (LURN SI-10) from 10/2021 to 9/2022 were included. Frailty was determined using the Fried frailty phenotype (robust, pre-frail, and frail). Regression models stratified by sex evaluated the cross-sectional associations of HIV and frailty with LUTS severity, urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), and overactive bladder (OAB). Due to low prevalence in men, mixed urinary incontinence (MUI) was analyzed only in women. Effect modification by sex and HIV was tested using the interaction terms with frailty. Results Mean age was 56 years (SD 11), and 58% of participants were Black. For women, 53% were pre-frail and 23% were frail. For men, 46% were pre-frail and 13% were frail. There was no association of HIV with LUTS. Among women, 21% reported UUI, 61% reported OAB, and 14% reported MUI at least weekly. Compared to robust women, frail women had higher LURN SI-10 scores (absolute difference = 3.3 (95% CI: 2.3, 4.3)). Similarly, frail men had higher LURN SI-10 scores than robust men (absolute difference = 1.6 (95% CI: 0.4, 2.9)). Frailty was associated with greater odds of UUI and OAB in women and men, and MUI in women. There was no evidence of effect modification by sex. Conclusions LUTS are common in people with and at-risk for HIV and are more severe among those who are frail. More research is needed to investigate the sex-independent mechanisms that underlie frailty and LUTS in this population.

items.title: General nutrition knowledge and malnutrition knowledge, attitudes and practices among nurses working in Lebanese hospitals.
items.abstract: Objective The aim of the study is to assess the nurses' knowledge, attitudes and practices related to malnutrition (M-KAP), as well as their general nutrition knowledge about food groups and nutrient sources (GNKQ2), and diet and disease relationships (GNKQ4) and determine the associated factors. Design A cross-sectional study was conducted among nurses, using a multi-component questionnaire that assessed the socio-demographic characteristics, health and eating habits, M-KAP and sections Methodology and Discussion of the general nutritional knowledge questionnaire (GNKQ2 and GNKQ4). Setting Hospitals located in North Lebanon. Participants Nurses working in Lebanese hospitals ( n 404). Results A positive association was detected between malnutrition knowledge and each of malnutrition-attitudes ( P P P P = 0·035), and compared with supervisor/chief nurses, practical and head nurses had lower GNKQ2 ( P P = 0·046, respectively). Additionally, practical nurses had lower GNKQ4 compared with supervisor/chief nurses ( P = 0·011). M-KAP levels were significantly associated with occupational title and nationality ( P = 0·032 and P = 0·008, respectively). Finally, M-practices were associated with hospital district ( P = 0·043), and practical and head nurses had better adequate M-practices compared with supervisor/chief nurses ( P = 0·001 and P = 0·016, respectively). Conclusion A better knowledge is significantly associated with better attitudes and practices, therefore, in order to improve the nutritional status of these patients; it is of prime importance to increase knowledge among nurses.
