items.title: Impact of taxes in Tonga targeting foods high in fat, salt and sugar: interrupted time series analyses.
items.abstract: Objective Sugar-sweetened beverage taxes have been widely evaluated; however, less is known about the effects of taxes on unhealthy foods. This study examines the effects of Tonga's food taxes on food prices and import volumes. Design Interrupted time series analysis using segmented linear regression was used to evaluate tax impacts on both retail prices and import volumes of taxed foods. Observed post-tax trends were compared with a counterfactual. The counterfactual was the projected pre-tax trends, with adjustment for autocorrelation and changes in GDP, tourism, season, exchange rates and oil prices over time. Random effects meta-analysis was used to summarise outcomes across food types. Setting Nine Tongan food tax increases were examined, varying from US$0·17/kg to US$1·08/kg, and averaging 28 % of import value. Results In the first-year post-tax, retail prices increased for ten of eleven taxed foods, with an average increase of 13 % (95 %CI: 5 % to 21 %). Price increases for chicken pieces (46 % and 39 %), mutton flaps (20 %), corned beef (20 %), ice cream (11 %), salted beef (6 %) and mayonnaise (3 %) were statistically significant. Import volumes decreased for eight of nine taxed foods with a mean decrease of 41 % (95 %CI: 17 % to 58 %). Import decreases for sausages (68 %) and ice cream (72 %) were significant. Conclusions Consistent with economic theory, excise taxes on unhealthy foods in Tonga were associated with increases in retail prices and decreased imports of taxed foods. These findings add to the limited evidence base that excise taxes on unhealthy foods can effectively raise prices and reduce supply.

items.title: Are intervention effects on fruit and vegetable intake maintained after 48 months of follow-up? A randomised controlled community trial.
items.abstract: Objective To assess whether participants from a transtheoretical model-based intervention maintained increases in fruit and vegetables (FV) intake 48 months after baseline. Design Randomised controlled community trial. Setting A Brazilian primary health care service. Participants Primary health care service users. The control group (CG) received usual care, and the intervention group (IG) received usual care and a 7-month collective intervention to promote FV intake. We analysed individuals with positive changes 12 months after baseline (baseline intake n 2·232). Outcomes were FV intakes at 36 and 48 months after baseline compared to previous intakes to identify maintenance. We used generalised estimating equations models to assess time and intervention effects in follow-up intake. Results Participants were mostly adult women. We identified decreases of 54.4 g/d in fruit intake and 38.5 g/d in vegetable intake at 36 months and increases of 6.9 g/d in fruit intake and 23.4 g/d in vegetable intake at 48 months. According to adjusted models, at 36 months, CG and IG participants presented similar decreases in FV intakes, which means initial changes in the IG were not maintained. At 48 months, small increases in intakes were also similar between IG and CG. Conclusions Intervention participants did not maintain initial changes on FV intake in the long term, and boosters might be necessary to maintain initial increases.

items.title: UK immigration statuses and rural/urban contexts: towards a research agenda on (forced) migrant food insecurity.
items.abstract: In light of rising forced global migration and disproportionately high levels of poverty among migrants, immigration systems have come to be understood as drivers of food insecurity in higher-income countries. At present, the mechanisms through which this operates are not well understood. The complex nature of immigration systems and statuses mean that experiences of migrant food insecurity are highly situated. There is a pressing need to examine, theorise and measure how these manifest in order to inform effective intervention and policy. In this article, we focus on the UK context to identify potential directions for the evolving food insecurity research agenda around forced migration. We outline how certain immigration statuses (trafficked, asylum seeker and refugee) intersect with different physical settings (rural/urban) to produce specific forms of food insecurity that urgently warrant further attention.

items.title: Ubuntu and Structural Injustice in FASD Prevention: Relational Responsibility and the Ethical Limits of Criminalisation in South Africa.
items.abstract: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) remains a persistent public health concern in South Africa, yet prevention debates often default to individualised "maternal responsibility" framings, and at the coercive end, to criminalisation or other punitive maternal-fetal governance. This article argues that such approaches are ethically unstable in structurally constrained settings, where prenatal alcohol use is shaped by intersecting social and institutional constraints. Because FASD is a spectrum that may involve enduring neurocognitive, behavioural, and adaptive impairments, the prevention imperative is real; the question is how to institutionalise it without entrenching maternal blame or ableist framings. Ubuntu does more than supply culturally resonant vocabulary. It provides independent relational reasons to treat trust, mutual recognition, least infringement and shared stewardship as central to legitimate prevention. Where supportive alternatives remain under-implemented, coercive legal responses are difficult to justify and may undermine disclosure, care-seeking and reproductive autonomy.

items.title: School food availability and surrounding food outlet density in New Zealand primary schools.
items.abstract: Objective To provide a snapshot of the food landscape around New Zealand (NZ) primary schools and to examine the association between food outlet density and the healthiness of primary school canteen menus. Design Cross-sectional analyses of external food outlets around schools and school canteen menus. Setting NZ primary schools. Participants Seventy-one primary schools provided their school canteen menu, and all external food outlets within 1·6 km of these schools were mapped using Google's Places API. Results The average number of food outlets around primary schools was 45, with a median health score of -3·12. Unhealthy food outlets outnumbered healthy ones (23 v . 6, P P = 0·019). School canteen menus comprised 19·7 % healthy 'green', 35·1 % occasional 'amber' and 35·5 % unhealthy 'red' food items. There was a weak association between types and density of external food outlets and school canteen menus. Conclusions The food environment around NZ primary schools is highly obesogenic, with greater exposure to unhealthy outlets observed in more deprived areas, reinforcing the need for zoning regulations to promote health equity. The healthiness of school canteen menus showed little association with the external food environment. Despite widespread exposure to nearby takeaway outlets, schools demonstrated variable adherence to national nutrition guidance. Strengthening implementation support for schools may be more impactful than regulating the surrounding foodscape alone.

items.title: Rising mortality from small intestinal cancer in Spain, 1999-2023: joinpoint and age-period-cohort analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction Small intestinal cancer is a rare neoplasm whose mortality has been increasing in several high‑income countries, yet long‑term patterns in Spain remain poorly described. Objectives This study aims to analyse temporal trends and decompose the effects of age, period, and birth cohort on small intestinal cancer mortality in Spain between 1999 and 2023. Material and methods A population-based time-series study was conducted using national mortality data from the National Statistics Institute. Age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population. Joinpoint regression was used to identify significant trend changes, and age-period-cohort modelling was applied to quantify the contributions of biological aging, calendar period, and generational effects. Results Between 1999 and 2023, the ASMR rose significantly in men (0.43 to 0.81 per 100,000; average annual percentage change: 2.1%) and more modestly in women (0.30 to 0.38 per 100,000; AAPC: 1.1%). The increase was driven almost entirely by individuals aged 50 years and older, while rates in those under 50 remained low and stable. Age-period-cohort analysis revealed a significant net drift (1.07% per year) and strong birth cohort effects in men, with mortality risk increasing for successive generations born through the mid-20th century. In women, the rise was primarily attributed to the age effect. Conclusions Small intestinal cancer mortality in Spain is increasing, particularly among men and older age groups. The significant cohort effect in men suggests that shifting environmental or lifestyle exposures are contributing to the growing burden of this malignancy.

items.title: The Madrid Declaration on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Innovation, equity, and transformation of the health-system response to the metabolic disease challenge of the 21st century.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and one of the most clinically important manifestations of systemic metabolic dysfunction. Rather than a condition confined to the liver, MASLD represents an early marker of risk within the cardio-hepato-renal-metabolic continuum and an opportunity to intervene before irreversible organ damage becomes established. The Madrid Declaration on MASLD emerged from the meeting 'Innovation and Equity in the Management of MASLD', held on 4 March 2026 at the headquarters of the Spanish General Medical Council, with the endorsement of the Council and several scientific societies. In line with resolution WHA79.4, adopted by the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly in May 2026, the Declaration sets out a ten-point framework for a health-system and policy response commensurate with the scale of the challenge. It calls for MASLD to be recognised as a public health priority and explicitly integrated into national strategies for noncommunicable diseases. Key proposals include early detection and risk stratification using non-invasive tools in primary care, supported by stepwise referral pathways that ensure an effective clinical response after detection. The Declaration further advocates value-based care and risk-proportionate interventions, reserving specialist care for people at greatest risk of progression and currently authorised disease-specific pharmacotherapies for appropriately selected patients with non-cirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis. Equity is positioned as a structural principle of care, alongside stigma-free communication, integrated multidisciplinary models of care, and transparent evaluation against verifiable targets. The Declaration calls on policymakers, institutions, scientific societies, health professionals, and civil society to act in a coordinated and evidence-based manner.

items.title: Increasing Language Access for Intimate Partner Violence Support Services: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern. Survivors face numerous barriers to accessing services, particularly when services in many places are only provided in English. This scoping review aimed to identify research and practice-based articles that explore interventions to increase language accessibility to support services for IPV. Articles were identified through a systematic search of databases and selected for inclusion if they involved language accessibility for IPV support services across settings (e.g., legal services, advocacy, hotlines, social services, healthcare, law enforcement). We identified 15 research and 14 practice-based articles for inclusion. Most interventions and practices for increasing language access were in settings related to health care, advocacy and social services, or community-based organizations. Research articles described various adaptations to interventions for increasing language access, which mostly included interpretation, translation, bilingual assistance, and culturally tailored programs. All research articles had language access adaptations for their intervention, but only 60% of the research articles included specific findings related to language access and culture. Practice-based articles discussed guidance around the development, assessment, and evaluation of a language access plan, language access engagement and implementation, and different elements and settings for language access. Findings highlight the intersection between language and culture, underscoring the need to address these interconnected aspects beyond simple translation and interpretation. IPV support services should hire multilingual and multicultural staff and address fear around immigration status. Increased funding is needed to ensure higher quality language access supports are implemented. Additional implications for research, practice, and policy are discussed.

items.title: Associations between types of residential greenspace and depressive symptoms in older adults: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
items.abstract: Residential greenspace may prevent older-adult depression, but it is unclear whether this depends on type of greenspace and population subgroup. We examined associations between six greenspace measures and depressive symptoms among 6,799 U.S. older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (1-3 observations per participant in 2000-2012). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression scale. Time-varying residential address-linked exposures included street-view-based vegetation (grass, trees, other, and total), satellite-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and park access. In fully adjusted mixed-effects Poisson models, overall associations were null (symptom count ratios [CRs], 0.98-1.03 per SD increase). Associations varied by site, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status, and population density. In site-stratified analyses, fewer symptoms were associated with NDVI in New York, NY (CR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), park access in Winston-Salem, NC (CR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), and grass in Minneapolis, MN (CR=0.87, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.97). The greenspace metric most strongly associated with fewer symptoms differed across racial/ethnic groups. Greater street-level greenspace was associated with more symptoms in high-density areas. Greenspace-depression associations may therefore depend on greenspace type and context, suggesting that mental-health-oriented greenspace interventions should be tailored to local populations and environments.

items.title: Precarious employment and health: Expanding the Boundaries of Research.
items.abstract: The historical deterioration of employment and working conditions in wealthy nations is captured by the concept of precarious employment (PE), which has spurred scholarly and policy interest. A decade after identifying key research gaps, persistent and emerging challenges remain. Although a clear and standardized definition of PE as a social determinant of health already exists, many scholars still struggle to define and operationalize it effectively, obscuring its roots in power relations and social mechanisms. Evidence confirms it as a critical, unequally distributed social determinant of health, disproportionately affecting workers by class, gender, race, and migration status. Yet the structural mechanisms underlying these inequities-such as occupational segregation-remain insufficiently theorized and empirically studied, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where PE often overlaps with informal employment. Intersectional frameworks illustrate how interconnected systems of oppression shape health outcomes, particularly through the syndemic entanglement of precarious work, housing insecurity, and other forms of social precariousness. These dynamics demand broader conceptual and empirical approaches. Spain's recent PRESME Report represents an important step forward, offering a strategic transdisciplinary framework for implementing intersectoral labor and public health policies. Understanding how PE harms health is essential for advancing health equity and guiding evidence-based policy.

items.title: Use of Sparse Internal Validation Data.
items.abstract: Internal validation sub-studies compare an observed imperfect measurement of a variable with its gold standard measurement in a sample of participants. The gold standard is often expensive or difficult to collect, so the validation sample is usually small. We simulated a small cohort study with a nested, balanced validation sub-study and used the simulated cohorts to evaluate three analytic strategies with the objective of determining which of them, alone or in combination, improved the performance of quantitative bias adjustments informed by the validation sub-study. The strategies were: (1) incorporating a weak prior to the beta distributions assigned to the bias parameters, as opposed to no prior (2) restricting beta distribution assignment to the three predictive values informed by sampling, as opposed to all four predictive values, and (3) restricting imputation of gold-standard measurement to study cohort members who were not sampled for the validation sub-study, as opposed to imputing for all members of the study cohort. All twelve combinations of bias adjustment strategies returned bias-adjusted estimates with less bias and higher coverage than the simulated misclassified cohorts, although all had higher root mean squared errors and wider intervals because of the uncertainty added by incorporating the sparse validation data into the analysis. We found that assigning a prior may sometimes have utility, whereas restricting assignment of beta distributions for use only with sampling and restricting imputation to only cohort members not selected for the validation study adds computational complexity with little utility in return.

items.title: One-shot learning of paired association navigation with biologically plausible schemas
items.abstract: After learning a multiple paired-association (MPA) navigation task, rodents can rapidly learn new cue–location associations after a single exposure, a phenomenon proposed to be facilitated by cognitive schemas. However, it remains unclear what schemas support this behavior and how they could be implemented in biological neural circuits. Here, we identify a set of schemas sufficient for gradual then one-shot paired-association navigation, and implement them in a fully neural agent using biologically plausible plasticity rules. The agent gradually acquires a low-dimensional spatial metric representation using a path-integration based temporal-difference error, enabling self-localization across different environments. It also contains a memory network that forms one-shot associations between sensory cues and goal locations, implemented using reward-modulated exploratory Hebbian (EH) plasticity. A third network performs vector subtraction between the agent’s current and goal location to compute goal-directed actions. Supplementing these schemas with an actor–critic enables one-shot navigation past obstacles. Lastly, learning a working-memory gating mechanism using the temporal-difference error enables one-shot learning even with brief cue and distractor presentation. The model reproduces key behavioral features of rodent learning in the MPA task and generates testable predictions about the neural mechanisms underlying schema-based one-shot learning. Significance Statement Schema-dependent learning is exemplified by better recall of a lecture when one already has a schema for understanding. A rodent navigation task showing a shift from slow to rapid learning has been proposed to reflect such schema use, yet how schemas are neurally implemented and enable faster learning is poorly understood. We clarify this gap in this computational study by describing several schemas and implement them as neural networks with biologically plausible learning rules. Composing them into an agent reproduces schema-dependent rodent learning behavior. Because schemas also shape self beliefs, clarifying their neural basis has implications for psychopathology. At the same time, understanding how biological schemas support rapid learning may inform advances in machine learning.

items.title: When, where, and for whom do errors compound? Error sequences, contagion, and individual vulnerability in professional football
items.abstract: Attentional Control Theory: Sport (ACTS) proposes that competitive anxiety arises from appraisals of both the cost and the probability of failure, predicting that an error should be most disruptive when the stakes are already high. We report the first large-scale test of this account in association football, drawing on 1,190,821 StatsBomb open-data event records from 330 professional matches across ten competitions. Three studies examined unforced passing errors. In Study 1 (272,381 passes, 2,202 players), situational pressure and a player’s own immediately preceding error each independently raised error probability: the odds of an error were approximately 21% higher per additional pressure component, and 57% higher following an error than following a success (OR = 1.57). The interaction, however, ran opposite to the ACTS prediction, with pressure narrowing rather than widening the post-error gap (OR = 0.91). Study 2 (54,409 post-error sequences) showed that this elevation was not confined to the player who erred: teammates taking the team’s next pass erred 3.9 percentage points above their own baseline rate, an interpersonal effect roughly half the magnitude of the within-player effect. Study 3 followed chains rather than pairs of consecutive errors. Error probability escalated monotonically with each additional consecutive prior error, from 17.7% following a success to 51.6% at a chain depth of six, and mediation analysis indicated that most of this escalation (91.7%) operated through riskier pass selection rather than degraded execution. Between-player variation in susceptibility was substantially greater for error chains than for success chains, and within every playing position the players with the lowest baseline error rates showed the steepest escalation, an association only partly accounted for by pass selection. Errors in elite football are therefore sequentially dependent, partially contagious, and unevenly damaging across players, suggesting that the cost of an error lies less in the error itself than in what it becomes if allowed to compound.

items.title: Creative project teams’ adaptive responses to task alterations at different points in time
items.abstract: Abstract How does a project team’s response to the timing of task alterations affect its receptiveness to these alterations? In addition, what role do creative team processes play in determining the team’s response? The purpose of the present research is to explore answers to these questions. We start our theoretical analysis with the assumption that creative project teams facing a deadline progress through varying levels of divergent and convergent team processes, manifesting in process-specific trajectories. In Study 1a, we empirically demonstrate these trajectories for 20 creative project teams. We then examine how creative project teams respond to task alterations at two times of heightened readiness—early or at the temporal midpoint of a team project (Study 1b). In a sample of 68 creative project teams, we find that optimal information integration requires teams to recalibrate some of those processes that are disturbed when a task alteration occurs. Specifically, midpoint (relative to early) intervention teams integrated more novel information when they engaged in idea implementation right after the task alteration, whereas early (relative to midpoint) intervention teams integrated more novel information when they engaged in problem formulation. Higher levels of information integration, in turn, predicted creative outcomes. We discuss implications for team creativity and team adaptation.

items.title: ROLE OF ACCELERATORS AND INCUBATORS IN INSPIRATION LABS- A DETAILED FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIO-ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION
items.abstract: This paper examines the role of incubators and accelerators within the Inspiration Economy framework, arguing that these mechanisms are not merely institutional tools but constitute a coherent methodology for converting socio-economic problems into sustainable opportunities. Drawing extensively on the theoretical and empirical corpus developed by inspiration economy theory lab, the paper situates incubators and accelerators within the broader architecture of Inspiration Labs—field-based environments where observation, associative thinking, and iterative experimentation converge. The paper expands the theoretical foundation by engaging particularly with Mednick's associative theory of creativity, Koestler's concept of bisociation, and Edgar Morin's complexity theory, to demonstrate how the incubator-accelerator continuum operationalizes a distinctive epistemology of problem-solving. Through analysis of case studies from Mauritania, Bahrain, Bosnia, and Ghana, the paper shows that incubators build the "roots" of capacity and self-reliance, while accelerators drive the "growth" of proven models toward scale and systemic impact. The paper concludes that the integration of these two mechanisms within Inspiration Labs represents a viable pathway toward what a civilizational renaissance grounded in local assets, associative capacity, and the transformation of challenges into inspirational currencies.

items.title: AI awareness relates to university students’ boundaryless career through the parallel mediation of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity
items.abstract: The in-depth penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has reshaped career forms and the structure of the labor market, exerting a profound impact on university students’ cognition and orientation towards career development. Based on the conservation of resources theory and self-determination theory, we conducted three studies—an experimental study and two survey studies—to explore correlational linkages between AI awareness and university students’ boundaryless career. Studies 1 and 3 consistently demonstrated that AI awareness is indirectly associated with boundaryless career through the parallel mediating pathways of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. Study 2 provided experimental evidence that heightened AI awareness increases both intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. This research enriches the application scenarios of boundaryless career theory in the context of technological change, deepens the understanding of the mechanism linking technological perception to youth career psychology, and offers practical implications for career guidance in universities.

items.title: A systematic review of human- and emerging AI-generated reformulation in L2 writing
items.abstract: Reformulation has long served as a feedback approach in second language (L2) writing. With the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), particularly ChatGPT, AI-generated reformulation has recently begun to appear in L2 writing research, although this area remains nascent. Guided by the PRISMA framework, this study reviews 26 empirical studies on reformulation in L2 writing published up to January 13, 2026. Unlike previous reviews of positive evidence feedback or model texts more broadly, this review provides a reformulation-focused synthesis and maps both human-generated and emerging AI-generated practices. The review focuses on three key dimensions: (1) research contexts and trends, (2) methodological characteristics, and (3) primary focus areas and key findings. Results indicate that: (1) research has predominantly targeted university-level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners, with emerging interest in AI-generated feedback; (2) methodologies have mainly employed quasi-experimental designs situated in classroom-based, three-stage narrative tasks; and (3) while reformulation-only studies have tended to conceptualize writing as a process and emphasize learners’ attention to lexical and grammatical features, reformulation-integrated studies have produced mixed findings regarding the transition from cognitive processing to written products. These findings underscore the multifaceted role of reformulation in L2 writing development and identify critical directions for future research, particularly concerning the integration of emerging AI-assisted pedagogical practices.

items.title: Soil health management outweighs edaphic properties in explaining soil organic matter across working organic farms
items.abstract: Abstract. Rebuilding soil organic carbon (SOC) on working lands plays a pivotal role in mitigating climate change and improving soil function, yet its accumulation is constrained by both management decisions and inherent soil properties. Scientists and farm advisors recommend that farmers plant cover crops, reduce tillage, and add organic amendments to increase SOC, yet the effectiveness of practices intended to improve soil health may be limited by underlying edaphic controls such as mineralogy, texture, and pH. Given that SOC consists of two distinct fractions—particulate organic matter (POM) and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM)—which differ in their stability and response to management, a critical question emerges: How much do inherent soil properties limit the effectiveness of recommended soil health practices in increasing SOC? Despite extensive research in controlled field settings, real-world farming contexts remain less understood, limiting our ability to predict SOC gains across diverse soil conditions. Here, we evaluate how in-season and recent (<5 yr) implementation of soil health management systems on working farms affects SOC fractions and stocks across 28 organic fields growing leafy greens in the Central Coast of California. We find that continuous living cover (e.g., through cover cropping) increases three of our measured carbon pools – free POM, MAOM, and surface soil total carbon stocks – while reduced disturbance (i.e., less tillage) increases two – free POM and MAOM. Crop diversity enhances both free and occluded POM fractions. Surprisingly, organic matter amendments do not show any relationship with any of the measured carbon pools. On average, management variables explain 3.7 times more variance than edaphic variables across carbon fractions, whereas, for carbon stocks, the opposite is true: edaphic variables explain ~2.1 times the variance compared to management. Our findings highlight that soil health practices, and in particular continuous cover, can significantly increase soil carbon levels, including both particulate and mineral-associated organic matter fractions, across diverse soil conditions.

items.title: Macro constraints and local eutrophication shape sediment nitrogen removal in the Eastern China Plain lakes
items.abstract: Abstract. Eutrophication poses a profound threat to the provisioning of ecosystem services in lakes worldwide. Understanding how eutrophication, alongside other biotic and abiotic factors, drives sediment nitrogen removal is essential for maintaining the intrinsic purification capacity of ecosystems and safeguarding water security. To address this, we conducted a systematic investigation of 17 representative lakes across the Eastern China Plain using 15N stable isotope tracing, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, and metagenomics profiling. This study aims to quantify the contribution of the anammox to nitrogen removal, elucidate the impacts of eutrophication on overall nitrogen removal, and identify the critical biotic and abiotic factors driving these processes. Results revealed that while denitrification was the dominant process across all lakes, anammox made substantial contributions of up to 34.3 %, exhibiting a distinct environmental dependency. Eutrophication significantly amplified both the overall nitrogen removal capacity and the relative contribution of anammox, with local physicochemical properties and microbial communities demonstrating a pronounced joint driving effect on these processes. Notably, the observed decoupling among microbial community structure, functional gene abundance, and nitrogen removal rates highlights a significant discrepancy between genetic potential and active expression. This discrepancy is further manifested by the superior environmental adaptability of functionally redundant denitrifying bacteria compared to narrow ecological niche anammox bacteria. Furthermore, we demonstrate that macro scale factors, including spatial, climatic, and anthropogenic, indirectly drive nitrogen removal by reshaping local water-sediment physicochemical properties, rather than acting as direct determinants of process rates. Collectively, this study enriches our fundamental understanding of nitrogen removal, particularly the anammox process, and its multidimensional drivers in the Eastern China Plain lakes. We advocate that future lake management strategies must rigorously account for the overarching constraints jointly imposed by trophic status, alongside spatial and climatic gradients, to ensure the sustainability of nitrogen purification ecosystem services.

items.title: ATMOSPHERIC DISPERSION MODELING OF PM10 AND SO2 FROM OPEN BURNING OF SOLID WASTE IN IBADAN, NIGERIA
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and inadequate municipal waste management in sub-Saharan Africa have exacerbated severe environmental and public health crises, prominently characterized by the operation of uncontrolled open dumpsites. In Ibadan, Nigeria, major disposal facilities such as La Awotan dumpsite rely heavily on open dumping and unmitigated burning. This present study aimed to examine the atmospheric emissions generated from the open burning of solid waste across these four sites from 2018 to 2024 using dispersion modelling. The criteria air pollutants (CAPs) such as particulate matter (PM) and Sulfur dioxide (SO2) were determined using the emission factor approach. The ground level concentrations of each of the CAPs within a 15 km radius were predicted using the AERMOD software. The results showed that the emission inventory for PM and SO2is in the range of 2553.91–7654.10 and 66.10-198.11 tons per annum between 2018 and 2024, respectively. The maximum 1, 8, 24 h, and annual concentrations were 268475µgm−3, 45065µgm−3, 15155µgm−3 and 614µgm−3 for PM and 6049µgm−3 1166µgm−392µgm−3 and 15.9µgm−3 for SO2, respectively. Research indicates that open burning of solid waste emits hazardous gasses and has negative impacts on nearby communities. These findings will serve as a baseline for environmental protection agencies.

items.title: The fishery biology of the three-spot seahorse (Hippocampus trimaculatus) in the Con Dao Archipelago, Vietnam
items.abstract: The three-spot seahorse (Hippocampus trimaculatus Leach) is among the most heavily harvested seahorse species in Vietnam. Due to overexploitation and habitat degradation, H. trimaculatus is listed in Appendix II of CITES (2014), the IUCN Red List (IUCN, 2025), and the Vietnam Red List of Threatened Species (Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, 2024). Although H. trimaculatus is harvested throughout Vietnamese waters, its fishery biology data remain limited, particularly for the Con Dao Archipelago, a biodiversity hotspot of high conservation importance. This study investigated the fishery biology of H. trimaculatus in the Con Dao Archipelago and proposes conservation measures. A total of 499 H. trimaculatus specimens were collected from local fishers in April and October 2024 in the Con Dao Archipelago and identified on the basis of molecular analysis and morphology. Interviews were conducted with 16 fishers and seven seafood shops to gather information on exploitation and trade. The results indicated that H. trimaculatus is being exploited unsustainably, as evidenced by the fishing gear used, the male-to-female sex ratio of 1:1.1, the portion of brooding males (21.04%) in the total catch, the capture of immature individuals, and the scarcity of mega-spawners. Sexual dimorphism, allometric growth, and differences in the length-weight relationships of the H. trimaculatus population are described and compared with other seahorse populations. This study proposes management recommendations concerning fishing gear, sex ratios, and size limits of H. trimaculatus to support its conservation in the Con Dao Archipelago.

items.title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health
items.abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. This Perspective proposes sustainable nutrition as a unifying concept: maintaining nutritional status that supports growth, development, and health across the lifespan while accounting for population needs, context, and the capacity and resilience of food systems. We describe a Nutritional Ecology framework that conceptualizes nutrition as the product of dynamic, reciprocal interactions among human biology, dietary patterns, food systems, and environmental conditions. Agricultural practices affect food quantity, quality, nutrient composition, biodiversity, water resources, greenhouse gas emissions, and ecosystem resilience, while environmental change influences crop productivity, nutrient density, food safety, and nutrition security. Dietary patterns simultaneously affect chronic disease risk and the environmental footprint of food systems. These interdependencies argue against evaluating human health and environmental sustainability in isolation. We therefore call for a transformation toward integrated, systems-based nutrition research that incorporates biological variability, environmental drivers, and system-level interactions. Multidisciplinary collaborations spanning nutrition, food, agricultural, environmental, epidemiologic, computational, systems, and implementation sciences will be essential. Emerging approaches, including systems mapping, network analysis, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, and multiscale data integration, can identify trade-offs and leverage points for intervention. Integrating nutrition, food systems, and environmental science is a scientific necessity for generating evidence across diverse population contexts that supports resilient food systems, effective dietary guidance, improved clinical care, healthier people, and a healthier planet.

items.title: Functional systems integration: a framework for reconciling livestock production and wild herbivore conservation in nature-positive rangelands
items.abstract: Reconciling livestock production, wild herbivore conservation and human well-being remains a persistent challenge in rangeland management. Conventional approaches have largely pursued these objectives through separate production and conservation strategies, reinforcing a production–conservation trade-off while overlooking the ecological and institutional processes linking them. This narrative review synthesises literature identified through Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect across diverse rangeland systems globally. It examines the roles of institutional and governance arrangements, landscape management, and ecosystem functioning in livestock–wild herbivore coexistence. The synthesis identifies a recurring management disconnect between livestock production and wild herbivore conservation in rangeland systems experiencing conflict and degradation. The review therefore proposes Functional Systems Integration (FSI) as a conceptual framework for managing livestock production and wild herbivore conservation within a shared social–ecological system. FSI brings together institutions, spatial planning, and ecosystem processes to support coordinated governance and landscape connectivity while pursuing production, conservation, and livelihood goals. It shifts the focus of rangeland management towards sustaining the processes that underpin multifunctional landscapes. FSI remains a conceptual framework rather than a validated management model, and its applicability requires empirical testing across contrasting rangeland contexts. Two priorities are identified for advancing FSI from concept to practice: testing mechanisms for FSI governance, assessment, and monitoring in integrated livestock–wild herbivore systems, and developing measurable indicators across its institutional, spatial, and ecological dimensions.

items.title: Contact in context: How land use histories, sociocultural practices, and animal profiles shape human-animal contact and zoonotic pathogen exposure in a fragmented forest of the Democratic Republic of Congo
items.abstract: Pathogenic spillovers from animals into humans have catalyzed epidemics throughout history. They result from multiple factors. One such factor, human-animal contact, remains poorly understood. Current studies often neglect variability in human-animal engagements across ecological zones and the broader processes bringing people, animals, and pathogens into engagement. We investigated factors and longer-term processes shaping human-animal contacts and indirectly, potential exposures to zoonotic pathogens in a fragmentated forest. We conducted our mixed-methods investigation in three villages along an ecological gradient of forest fragmentation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), a hotspot of biodiversity and disease emergence. Twenty-four village participants recorded their daily activities and contacts with animal species over five months. We developed a cluster analysis to categorize classes of animals according to type and frequency of contact and conducted transects to estimate animal species abundance according to village proximity. We then tested the influence of species abundance, human activities, gender, and village on contact frequency. We also undertook ethnographic and ethnohistorical interviews and observations to explore changing human-animal relations. Participants had physical and environmental contact with 61 animal species, which clustered into three classes according to their contact profiles. Relative abundance of animal species was associated with contact frequency, but its effects were weak. Our ethnohistorical and anthropological analyses, however, situated these contacts within their longer-term processes and sociocultural practices that our models could not capture. The animals with which participants had most frequent contact were those whose abundance and accessibility resulted from decades of land use change and hunting intensification. Several abundant species were rarely contacted because local categorizations of animals as ngeyi (“disgusting”) suppressed contacts that proximity alone would have predicted. Human-animal contact profiles are thus historically produced and socioculturally mediated; they cannot be derived exclusively from species ecology, land cover, or demographic variables.

items.title: Community assembly in mountain grasslands: decoupled aboveground versus belowground processes driven by contrasting soil resources
items.abstract: Introduction Mountain habitats feature steep environmental gradients that shape specific vegetation diversity and soil heterogeneity. However, how plants coordinated aboveground and belowground reproductive strategies under varying resource availability remained poorly understood. Methods We quantified the belowground bud bank, functional traits, and phylogenetic structures to elucidate plant resource allocation strategies governing community assembly in mountain grasslands of northern China. Six habitat types (SubAlpine Meadow, Forest-Edge Meadow, Floodplain Meadow, Hillside Steppe, Dry Steppe and Sandy Steppe) were selected based on resource availability along the elevation. Results 1) Subalpine Meadow exhibited the highest density and diversity. Floodplain Meadow and Dry Steppe had higher ramet density but lower diversity. Bud densities and diversities in the Subalpine, Floodplain and Hillside Steppe were higher than those in other low-elevation habitats; 2) None of the bud bank density, plant height and abundance showed strongly phylogenetic signals. The NTI, NRI were positively related with B/V density, while they were negatively correlated with height and B/V diversity indices; 3) Soil resources distinctly regulated aboveground and belowground populations: Total nitrogen, porosity and soil moisture were negatively correlated with diversities but positively with densities, acting as constraints on the density-diversity trade-off. Importantly, soil organic carbon specifically promoted belowground bud diversity, while total potassium drove aboveground ramet diversity. Conclusion Our results revealed that deterministic processes (niche theory) governed community assembly in the Saihanwula mountain grassland. The aboveground and belowground populations in mountain grasslands were governed by distinct ecological processes and soil resources. Interspecific competition and environmental filtering drove aboveground community assembly, whereas resource availability constrained the belowground bud bank. Our findings provided significant insights for predicting the renewal and recovery potential of plants under global changes.

items.title: Complete chloroplast genome of Atriplex taltalensis (Amaranthaceae), an endangered endemic species from the Chilean Atacama Desert
items.abstract: Background Atriplex taltalensis is an endangered halophytic species endemic to the Chilean Atacama Desert, for which genomic resources are currently lacking. Complete chloroplast genomes provide valuable resources for comparative genomics, phylogenetics, and conservation genetics because of their conserved structure and informative evolutionary patterns. This study aimed to assemble and characterize the first complete chloroplast genome of A. taltalensis and compare it with representative Atriplex plastomes. Results The complete chloroplast genome of A. taltalensis was a circular molecule of 150, 919 bp with the typical quadripartite structure, comprising a large single-copy region, a small single-copy region, and two inverted repeats. The plastome encoded 130 genes, including 85 protein-coding genes, 37 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs, with an overall GC content of 37.29%. Comparative analyses of 15 Atriplex plastomes revealed high conservation of genome organization and gene content, together with high sequence similarity, whereas nucleotide variation was concentrated in a limited number of intergenic regions and a few coding genes. Hypervariable loci, simple sequence repeats, and long repeats were identified as potential candidates for informative molecular markers. Most protein-coding genes showed Ka/Ks ratios consistent with strong functional constraint, while a limited number of genes exhibited elevated pairwise Ka/Ks ratios in specific comparisons. Phylogenomic reconstruction based on complete plastomes recovered well-supported plastome relationships within Atriplex , supporting their utility for resolving relationships among closely related taxa. Conclusions This study provides the first complete chloroplast genome sequence of A. taltalensis and establishes a valuable genomic resource for comparative genomics, phylogenomics, and conservation genetics.

items.title: Phylogenomics reveal incomplete lineage sorting as the primary source of phylogenetic discordance in East African Zanthoxylum L. and Vepris Comm. ex A. Juss. (Rutaceae)
items.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary relationships in Zanthoxylum L. and Vepris Comm. ex A. Juss. remain poorly resolved due to limited genomic resources and conflicting signals from individual markers, hindering efforts to understand their diversification and adaptation across tropical environments. In this study, we generated Angiosperms353 target‐capture data for 187 individuals representing 51 Zanthoxylum and Vepris species from East Africa. Using concatenated and multispecies coalescent analyses combined with concordance‐factor approaches, we recovered Zanthoxylum and Vepris as monophyletic clades. However, species‐level relationships within each genus exhibited substantial phylogenetic discordance. Concordance factor analysis revealed moderate genome‐wide site concordance (mean sCF = 46.64%) but markedly lower gene concordance (mean gCF = 28.76%), indicating widespread gene‐tree heterogeneity. Both sCF and gCF exhibited strong positive correlations with branch lengths; r = 0.698 and r = 0.687, respectively. Discordance patterns showed an almost perfect balance between alternative topologies (sDF1 = 24.9%, sDF2 = 24.8%), minimal mean asymmetry (3.5%–5.1%), and a high proportion of polyphyly (gDFP = 59.7%), all consistent with incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) as the primary source of phylogenomic conflict. A small fraction of branches (1.9%–4.7%) displayed significant asymmetry, which signals only limited evidence for processes beyond ILS and should be interpreted with caution pending explicit tests of introgression. Generally, our findings offer a comprehensive phylogenomic framework for East African Zanthoxylum and Vepris and demonstrate that ILS has played a major role in shaping genomic variation and phylogenetic discordance within these genera. Further analyses are required to investigate the extent to which hybridization or other reticulate processes have contributed to their evolutionary history.

items.title: Seasonal community structure and environmental associations of putative pathogenic microorganisms in the Shelf-Margin Sea of the Northwestern South China Sea
items.abstract: Marine pathogenic microorganisms are crucial to ecological health and fishery aquaculture. However, the composition and influencing drivers for pathogenic microorganisms in the Shelf-Margin Sea of the Northwestern South China Sea (SMS-NWSCS) are still unclear. This study applied 16S rRNA and ITS gene high-throughput sequencing combined with multiple bacterial pathogen detection (MBPD) and FUNGuild database to explore putative pathogenic microorganisms in the SMS-NWSCS and to investigate the main environmental associations of the composition, diversity, complexity and stability of putative pathogenic microbial communities. Results showed that Escherichia coli (31.77%), Pseudomonas fluorescens (16.25%) and Sphingomonas paucimobilis (6.90%) were dominant putative pathogenic bacteria, while Pseudozyma sp. (48.36%) and Malassezia globosa (48.34%) dominated the putative pathogenic fungal communities. The putative pathogenic bacterial community exhibited higher alpha diversity in winter, while the fungal community showed greater alpha diversity in summer. Beta diversity analysis revealed significant seasonal dynamics in both putative pathogenic bacterial and fungal communities (bacteria: R 2 = 0.12, p = 0.001; fungi: R 2 = 0.08, p = 0.007). Spearman’s correlation analysis suggested that a suite of environmental factors, including temperature, pH, DO, Chla and nutrients, played significant roles in influencing putative pathogenic microbial community structure. PLS-PM analysis demonstrated that bacterial alpha diversity was positively associated with community complexity (R 2 = 0.10, p < 0.01) and stability (R 2 = 0.45, p < 0.001), and both alpha and beta diversity (R 2 = 0.10, p < 0.05; R 2 = 0.21, p < 0.001) showed positive correlations with the stability of the putative pathogenic fungal community. Our study reveals the seasonal patterns of putative pathogenic microorganisms in the SMS-NWSCS and enhances the understanding of their community maintenance mechanisms.

items.title: Translational plausibility of honey-derived antimicrobial biomaterials against biofilm-associated infections
items.abstract: Chronic biofilm-associated infections drive antimicrobial resistance (AMR) via prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy that is often ineffective. Honeys from Apis mellifera and stingless bees (Meliponini) exhibit antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity via complementary mechanisms: osmotic stress, low pH, hydrogen peroxide, methylglyoxal, bee defensin-1, and phenolic and organic compounds. This is most effective when concentrated at the application site. Yet honey therapeutics are often framed as systemic nutraceuticals despite biologically incoherent pharmacokinetics. We propose translational plausibility, an analytical framework built on four interdependent dimensions: spatial, temporal, dose, and compositional coherence that distinguishes microbiologically defensible interventions from speculative ones, applicable beyond honey to natural-product antimicrobials. Applied to honey, the framework identifies topical, localized application as the only translationally coherent clinical route. Reframed as ecological therapeutic biomaterials, honeys address interconnected AMR priorities: disrupting polymicrobial ESKAPE biofilms, preserving distant microbiotas, reducing systemic antibiotic use in wound care, potentiating antibiotics, and supporting stewardship. Planetary health benefits, pollinator conservation, meliponiculture, and equitable access emerge as corollaries, not primary justification.

items.title: Transdisciplinary team science: a field study in understanding and improving complex scientific problem solving
items.abstract: Introduction Transdisciplinary team science requires foundational teamwork competencies that support complex collaborative problem solving. This study examined the development of these competencies among graduate students from different disciplines. Methods We conducted a field study of a training program grounded in foundational competencies for scientific teamwork. We examined participants’ self-reported collaboration competencies and the relationship between their teamwork self-ratings and independent expert evaluations of their scientific output. Results Participants reported improved collaboration competencies following the training program. Their teamwork self-ratings also correlated with independent expert evaluations of their scientific output. Discussion These findings suggest the value of competency-based training for transdisciplinary scientific teams and connect participants’ perceptions of teamwork with independently evaluated scientific output. They inform the development and testing of team science principles and approaches to studying complex collaborative problem solving.

items.title: Variation in the Content of Proteins, Phenolic Compounds, and Flavonoids and the Antioxidant Capacity of Wild Medicinal Plants in Arid Environments, as Determined by Soil Structure
items.abstract: This chapter examines how soil physical and chemical properties drive variation in protein profiles, phenolic compounds, and flavonoids of wild medicinal plants in arid and semi-arid coastal environments, using Al Jubail (Saudi Arabia) as a model system. Integrating edaphic measurements – soil texture, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and major ion composition – with plant biochemical and molecular assays, we characterize how salt and moisture regimes shape secondary metabolism and proteomic signatures in cooccurring halophytic and xerophytic taxa (e.g., Zygophyllum, Salsola, Halopeplis, Anabasis). SDS-PAGE protein banding patterns are used to assess genetic similarity and stress-responsive protein expression, while spectrophotometric quantification of total phenolics, flavonoids, and antioxidant capacity reveals metabolite patterns linked to soil salinity and texture. Across studied sites, higher EC and Na +/Cl – dominance are associated with elevated phenolic and flavonoid concentrations and increased antioxidant activity – especially in obligate halophytes – concurrent with distinct stress-related protein bands and reduced interspecific proteomic distance among salt-adapted populations. Conversely, coarse-textured, low-moisture soils promote specific flavonoid profiles and proteins indicative of drought tolerance in xerophytes. Multivariate analyses elucidate strong correlations between ion composition and both metabolic output and proteomic similarity, suggesting soil-mediated selection on biochemical traits. We discuss implications for conservation and sustainable utilization, highlighting how edaphic profiling can guide targeted collection of high-value accessions for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical development, and inform breeding strategies for climate resilience. The chapter underscores the value of linking soil ecology with plant biochemistry and proteomics to harness arid-land medicinal biodiversity.

items.title: Body-Territory and Sociobiodiversity: Traditional Ancestral Knowledge in Ecological Conservation
items.abstract: Objective: To investigate how the knowledge and expressions of traditional communities and the concept of body-territory function as socio-ecological strategies and technologies for biodiversity conservation. Theoretical Framework: This study is grounded in the dialogue between sociobiodiversity, political ecology, and the analytical categories of “body-territory” and “territory-body,” understanding the body as a living extension of biodiversity. Method: A qualitative, descriptive-exploratory study using an integrative literature review approach. Data were collected from the SciELO, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases using combined search terms via Boolean operators. The selected bibliographic material was subjected to thematic content analysis (Bardin, 2016). Results and Discussion: The synthesis shows that the management of fauna and flora and territorial governance depend on the integrity of bodily memories and traditional epistemologies. It demonstrates that environmental degradation compromises socio-ecological health and that ecological preservation is inseparable from the guarantee of territorial rights. Research Implications: Strengthening political ecology and recognizing traditional knowledge as socio-ecological technologies indispensable to the planning of public environmental policies. Originality/Value: Valuing ancestral epistemology in the scientific debate on sustainable management, deconstructing the myth of untouched nature, and promoting territorial justice.

items.title: A systematic review of the impacts of El Niño-driven drought, fire and smoke on non-human primates in Southeast Asia
items.abstract: Abstract During the El Niño phase of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, much of Southeast Asia experiences intense droughts and surging temperatures, exacerbating wildfires and creating a blanket of hazardous haze across much of the region. These patterns are predicted to worsen with climate change, further increasing the vulnerability of the region’s primate species, 94% of which are threatened with extinction. Here, we report findings from a systematic search of the literature and synthesize the current state of knowledge regarding the impacts of El Niño-driven heat, drought, fire and smoke on non-human primates in Southeast Asia. Our review shows that habitat loss and degradation driven by El Niño-induced drought and fire cause changes to diet, activity patterns, social interactions and physical condition, and lead to population crowding, reduced group sizes, increased infant mortality, displacement of individuals and local extirpation. Furthermore, prolonged exposure to smoke alters behaviour and worsens the health of primates. Two studies presented evidence for the recovery of primate populations in habitats damaged by fire if forest is allowed to regenerate. We highlight significant gaps in our understanding of the impacts of El Niño on non-human primates, particularly the need for research that considers the interconnected effects of rainfall, temperature, fire and smoke, as well as long-term effects on reproduction and mortality. Because of the unpredictable nature of El Niño, we acknowledge the difficulties of planning research in this area and emphasize the potential of long-term research sites to add to our understanding of this key conservation issue.

items.title: Illegal Fishing and its Impacts on Local Communities in Ghana
items.abstract: Illegal fishing remains a significant challenge in Ghana, reflecting a broader problem faced by many coastal countries worldwide. It encompasses fishing activities that violate national laws and fisheries regulations, including fishing in prohibited areas, using unauthorized fishing gear, and exceeding established catch limits. Such practices undermine fisheries governance, weaken regulatory enforcement, and threaten the long-term sustainability of marine resources. In Ghana, illegal fishing poses a serious threat to coastal communities whose livelihoods depend heavily on fisheries. The continued exploitation of fish stocks through unauthorized and unsustainable fishing practices contributes to declining fish populations and reduced catches for local fishers. These developments can undermine household incomes, disrupt local economic activities, and exacerbate food insecurity, particularly among communities that rely on fish as an important source of protein and income. Beyond its socioeconomic consequences, illegal fishing can also contribute to marine environmental degradation. Destructive fishing practices, including the use of explosives and toxic substances where they occur, can damage aquatic habitats, disrupt ecological processes, and threaten marine biodiversity. The resulting deterioration of marine ecosystems may affect fish reproduction, reduce the resilience of fish populations, and undermine the ecological conditions necessary to sustain fisheries over the long term. Recognizing these challenges, the Ghanaian government has undertaken measures to strengthen fisheries management, improve law enforcement, and enhance the monitoring of fishing activities. Nevertheless, addressing illegal fishing requires a comprehensive approach that extends beyond enforcement alone. Strengthening public awareness, promoting compliance with fisheries regulations, supporting alternative livelihood opportunities for fishing-dependent communities, and improving cooperation among government institutions, local stakeholders, and regional and international partners are essential strategies.

items.title: Nonlinear coupling between motional modes in trapped-ion quantum processors
items.abstract: Trapped-ion crystals are a leading platform for quantum information science, but achieving the high-fidelity entangling gates required for fault-tolerant quantum computing becomes harder as system size increases. As systems scale, spectral crowding makes low-order nonlinear resonances between collective motional modes increasingly common and can limit gate performance, especially in monolithic or global-mode architectures. We develop a general model to identify and simulate nonlinear motional-mode coupling (NoMoCou) arising from third-order Coulomb terms and quantify its impact on the Molmer-Sorensen gate across linear chains and 2D crystals in rf and Penning traps. We delineate the regimes where NoMoCou dominates the error budget and provide design rules: detune operating points from low-order resonances, tune trap anisotropy to reshape spectra, and shape gate waveforms.

items.title: The KPF SLOPE Survey: Small, Compact Multiplanet Systems Appear Spin–Orbit Aligned
items.abstract: Abstract The angle between stellar spin axes and planetary orbits—stellar obliquity—probes the dynamics of planetary migration and evolution. The obliquities of giant planets have been extensively studied because they are the most easily measured. Smaller planets, while more difficult to measure, have the advantage of better reflecting the dynamics of planetary systems because they trigger negligible backreactions onto the host star. This paper introduces a new observational campaign called the Small, Low-mass Oblique Planets Experiment (SLOPE) survey with the Keck Planet Finder (KPF) spectrograph and presents four new obliquity measurements. The SLOPE survey focuses on planets smaller than Saturn across a variety of system architectures. The sky-projected obliquities of the four planets measured—TOI-1386 b, TOI-480 b, TOI-4596 b, and TOI-1823 b—are all consistent with spin–orbit alignment. We validate the planetary nature of TOI-4596 b with a significant detection of the Rossiter–McLaughlin effect. Including these measurements, we conducted a statistical analysis of the obliquities of sub-Saturn-mass planets in different planetary system architectures. Compared to other architectures, those in compact multiplanet systems reside in orbits that appear preferentially aligned with the stellar equator with 6 σ confidence.

items.title: A Cosmological Framework for Stellar Collisions at High Redshift in Proto-globular Clusters, Nuclear Star Clusters, and Little Red Dots
items.abstract: Abstract Observations and cosmological simulations indicate that the early Universe hosted numerous compact, high-density stellar systems, where close encounters and physical collisions between stars were likely common. We develop a bottom-up framework for stellar dynamics in such environments, spanning systems with and without intermediate-mass and supermassive black holes, and covering regimes where stellar collisions may or may not dominate the evolution. This radially resolved analytic model connects dense star clusters in their cosmological context to observable outcomes mediated by stellar collisions. Initial conditions and environmental properties are drawn from high-resolution cosmological simulations, enabling exploration across a broad region of parameter space. The analytic predictions are validated against Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrating good agreement across key regimes. We find that stellar collisions are ubiquitous in many high-redshift environments, with runaway sequences naturally leading to the formation of very massive stars at early times. Finally, we show that high rates of destructive collisions can rapidly build up extremely dense gaseous environments around massive black holes, potentially providing an analog to the observed population of Little Red Dots.

items.title: Quantum protocols for time synchronisation and distribution: a critical assessment
items.abstract: Precise time synchronisation underpins critical infrastructure from telecommunications and financial markets to power grids and scientific metrology. Several families of quantum protocols have been proposed and demonstrated for clock synchronisation and time distribution, exploiting entangled photon pairs, quantum key distribution (QKD) correlations, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and entangled clock networks. We critically assess these approaches, reviewing the main quantum time synchronisation (QTS) protocol families, quantifying the gap between theory and experiment, and identifying practical bottlenecks in sources, detectors, and channels. We survey the classical timing landscape from Network Time Protocol (NTP) and GPS to laboratory-grade optical frequency transfer, and compare quantum and classical methods at equivalent maturity. We examine use cases including financial trading, power grids, telecommunications, scientific metrology, and military applications, evaluating whether quantum timing offers a realistic advantage. We show that time transfer, not clock performance, is now the bottleneck for distributed optical timekeeping: the best demonstrated quantum synchronisation uncertainty (2.46 ps, over 20 km of fibre) falls two to three orders of magnitude short of what optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainties of 10 −18 –10 −19 require. The best deployed link, ELSTAB, calibrates to a few tens of picoseconds in the laboratory and to about 0.2 ns on its 421 km field installation, a further factor of twenty to a hundred behind, while research-grade classical links using optical frequency combs already reach the regime the clocks require, though none is in operational service. Our assessment is that quantum time synchronisation will not replace classical methods for most applications in the near-to-medium future, yet it can complement them. Its near-term value lies in physical-layer security against timing manipulation and integration with quantum communication networks, while closing the synchronisation gap for scientific metrology remains the most critical open challenge.

items.title: Ringdown and echoes from compact objects: Debye series and Debye quasinormal modes
items.abstract: We introduce a new series decomposition of the waveform constructed in the spirit of Debye expansions in scattering theory, and we use this to analyse the time-domain response of compact, horizonless bodies to scalar-field perturbations on curved spacetimes. The Debye decomposition separates out direct exterior propagation, surface reflection, and successive transmissions through the interior of a compact body, and it provides an intuitive interpretation of the waveform in terms of geodesic trajectories. By analysing the quasinormal-mode (QNM) content of individual Debye terms, we set out a Debye-QNM description that is complementary to the standard QNM description. With this framework, we examine a scalar field propagating on two illustrative `Schwarzschild star' compact-body spacetimes: a neutron-star-like model \(R>3M\) and an ultracompact object \(R<3M\). We show that the Debye reconstruction matches well with the exact waveform, and that (unlike the standard QNM reconstruction) it converges even at early times, giving an accurate description of all waveform features including the prompt response. In the neutron-star case, the low-order Debye terms mainly describe the ringdown and a non-modal component associated with the sub-threshold branch cut. In the ultracompact case, the Debye series organizes the waveform into a prompt/ringdown contribution followed by a succession of individually resolved echo-like wavepackets. The new Debye-QNM expansion and the standard QNM expansion have complementary spectral interpretations: the former identifies modes in individual propagation channels, whereas the latter describes collective resonances that are resummations of the former. This distinction clarifies how echo-like structures emerge from repeated interior propagation, and how pole and branch-cut contributions enter the time-domain signal.

items.title: The impact of stellar binaries and star cluster dynamics on pair-instability supernovae
items.abstract: Pair-instability supernovae (PISNe) are among the most luminous transients in the Universe. However, they have never been confidently observed. Solving this puzzle would have key implications for several astrophysical topics, including galaxy chemical enrichment, the interpretation of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers, and the nature of red dropout sources seen by JWST. With this aim, we present the first in-depth study of PISN occurrence in binary stars, both in isolation and in dense star clusters. We employed the stellar tracks, to evolve a suite of 35 synthetic binary populations, including variations on formation channels, cluster properties, and upper limits of the stellar initial mass function. Combining this with an up-to-date, semi-empirical determination of the metallicity-dependent star formation rate density, we provide new results on the cosmic rate of PISNe. code, with state-of-the-art parsec We find that binary interactions can boost the PISN rate by as much as threefold relative to single stars, whereas binary hardening can either enhance or suppress PISN production, depending on whether the progenitors are primordial or dynamically formed. Moreover, we showcase how our comprehensive framework for the cosmic PISN rate can be used to constrain uncertain aspects of stellar and galaxy evolution models via comparison with observations, including the recipes for stellar-wind mass loss in very massive stars and the galaxy metallicity distribution throughout the Universe.

items.title: Monopoles, strings, walls, and gravitational waves
items.abstract: The gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2) \to U(1) \to Z_2 \to 1$ successively produces monopoles, strings and domain walls bounded by strings (WBS), with the elementary monopole carrying a $U(1)$ magnetic flux twice as large as the elementary string. The elementary strings and subsequently WBS emit gravitational waves, and during their decay, the WBS yield a network of composite strings that carry the same $U(1)$ flux as the monopoles. Depending on the cosmological evolution, we provide the gravitational wave spectra generated by the elementary strings and WBS, in combination with the composite strings which are either effectively stable, quasistable, or metastable. These three scenarios are also realized in the symmetry breaking chain $SU(3) \to SO(3) \to Z_2 \to 1$. Both $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have appeared in the literature as flavor gauge symmetries.

items.title: Parameter estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a binary merger triggers with subsolar mass components
items.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

items.title: Pulse-Controlled Topologically Protected Quantum Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Remote charging in the field of quantum batteries is particularly appealing because it minimizes interference between the charger and the battery, making it a subject of considerable interest. Here, we propose a robust remote charging protocol for quantum batteries based on a pulse-controlled superconducting qubit chain. By dynamically modulating the pulse-mediated couplings, we realize chiral-symmetry-protected energy transfer from the charger to the battery. We show that the charging process suppresses energy backflow due to the pulse control, and remains robust against pulse imperfections due to the chiral symmetry of the system. Moreover, the energy stored in the battery at the target time is almost fully extractable, and the protocol remains effective over a moderate range of chain lengths. To further accelerate charging, we optimize the pulse shape and elucidate the underlying physical mechanism. Our pulse-controlled topological quantum battery protocol provides a versatile framework for implementing remote topological charging and establishes a theoretical foundation for designing optimal-control strategies to enhance quantum battery performance.

items.title: Semiclassical initial value representation in curvilinear coordinates
items.abstract: A semiclassical propagator originally defined on Euclidean space is systematically extended to general curvilinear coordinate systems. This method time-evolves nuclear wave packets on the fly in curvilinear coordinates, without prior construction of global potential energy surfaces or complicated kinetic energy operators, and enables dimensionality reduction by isolating the physically essential degrees of freedom through coordinate constraints. By propagating the dynamics in a redundant coordinate space, the coordinate singularities inherent to curvilinear systems are circumvented in a numerically robust manner. In addition, the topology of each coordinate-such as its periodicity and boundary conditions-is properly taken into account by modifying the coherent state basis of the propagator. We applied this approach to molecular motions that are difficult to describe in conventional normal coordinates-pure rotation of hydrogen and methane, rovibrational dynamics of hydrogen, and large-amplitude torsional motion of butane-and reproduced reference eigenenergies and the characteristic features of the corresponding spectra.

items.title: Discovery of an isolated RELHIC candidate: J1351+0039
items.abstract: We report the discovery of J1351+0039, a new isolated dark galaxy candidate identified through a blind ̋I survey with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) combined with deep optical imaging from the DESI Legacy Survey. The object displays a compact ̋I structure with a systemic velocity of ( LSR = 429.0 ± 1.4 , -1 ) and an inferred ̋I mass of ( (4.5 ± 1.7) 10^ 5 , ̊m M_⊙ ) at a distance of 3.6 ± 0.7 Mpc. No optical counterpart was detected in the DESI images, with a g-band surface brightness limit of 28.1 mag arcsec -2 , corresponding to a stellar mass limit of ( M_⋆ łesssim 1.2 10^ 5 , ̊m M_⊙ ). The dynamical mass is estimated to be ( M_ dyn ≈ 1.3 , M_⊙ ), yielding a dark-to-baryonic mass ratio of ( ∼ 200 ), implying that J1351+0039 is overwhelmingly dominated by dark matter. While weak rotation was detected in J1351+0039, the kinematics are dominated by internal velocity dispersion, confirming pressure support and reminiscent of reionization-limited ̋I clouds (RELHICs). J1351+0039 stands out as one of the most promising isolated RELHIC candidates, offering a unique laboratory for studying baryonic physics and dark matter in the absence of star formation. 10^ 8
