items.title: Measuring masses of transiting Earth-like planets: first insights from the PLATO RV data challenge
items.abstract: The PLATO Stellar Variability Mitigation Working Group designed a radial-velocity (RV) data challenge to assess the precision and accuracy achievable on RV semi-amplitudes in the context of the future PLATO follow-up. Using Sun-as-a-star observations obtained with HARPS-N, we generated three multi-planet systems with realistic sampling, an effective signal-to-noise ratio of S/N ~ 450, an exposure time of 15 minutes, and a total of approximately 1000 observations. The resulting data set is publicly available and can serve as a benchmark for the community to test and compare RV analysis methods. Eight independent teams participated in the challenge, aiming to recover the semi-amplitudes of both transiting and non-transiting planets. A meta-analysis of the submitted results shows that, with current data analysis methods, HARPS-N-like stability and the observing strategy studied in this paper, achieving a precision on semi-amplitudes better than 10% for habitable-zone signals around a solar-type star is challenging, and is typically limited to planets with masses of approximately 8-10 Earth masses. This performance is expected to improve for K dwarfs, where planets down to approximately 2-5 Earth masses may be characterized at a similar level of precision. Finally, based on the results of this challenge and the occurrence of false positives, we derive an empirical detection threshold for RV surveys, which can be used to distinguish robust planetary detections from candidates.

items.title: Propulsion Systems for a Starshade Rendezvous Mission with the Habitable World Observatory
items.abstract: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints affect exo-Earth characterization with a starshade rendezvous mission for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)-like telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with EXOSIMS, we model a 60 m starshade for visible-band spectroscopy (500-1000 nm) and a 35 m starshade for near-ultraviolet characterization (250-550 nm). For the 60 m design, we compare AEPS Hall, NEXT ion, and Starlink-class Hall thrusters and examine sensitivity to propellant capacity, the fraction of each retargeting slew spent accelerating and decelerating, and on-orbit refueling. With 1000-3000 kg of initial propellant and no refueling, NEXT provides the highest characterization yield: 9-13% more characterizations than AEPS and 13-16% more than the Starlink-class option. Its higher specific impulse enables more retargeting slews per kilogram of propellant. With refueling, yields converge across thruster choices to about 120 cumulative characterizations over 10 years, while propulsion choice mainly affects the number of refueling events. For the 35 m starshade with AEPS, yields are less sensitive to fuel and are dominated by mission duration and geometric accessibility. Increasing the minimum solar keepout angle from 40 to 50 degrees has little effect on yield; increases from 50 to 65 degrees have a modest effect, while angles above 65 degrees rapidly reduce yield, with severe degradation near 80 degrees. These results distinguish fuel-limited and time- or keepout-limited regimes and guide propulsion selection, tank sizing, refueling policy, and keepout constraints for HWO starshade missions.

items.title: A Model to Map Brown Dwarf Companions to White Dwarfs in Partial Secondary Eclipse
items.abstract: Eclipse mapping is a well-established technique for constraining the spatial emission of hot Jupiter exoplanets. Brown dwarfs in ultra-short orbits around white dwarfs are an analog to hot Jupiters that can only ever be eclipsed within a limited range of latitudes. We adapt the eigenmapping method to disentangle the signals from the ever- and never-occulted regions. The result of this signal separation is a super-position of map structures, yielding sharp boundaries at the occultation region. We introduce a model that penalizes the harmonic complexity of the model map with Tikhonov regularization, whose parameters are tuned to reproduce the fit quality of the eigenmapping model. We use JWST NIRSpec/PRISM full-orbit observations of the eclipsing WD 1202-024 system as a template to construct and run injection-recovery tests on simulated light curves, isolating both latitudinal structures as well as emission from a physically-realistic general circulation model (GCM). In the latter, the narrow equatorial jet driven by the BD's rapid rotation manifests as an eclipse depth asymmetry, which our model reproduces as a latitude-dependent phase offset. Such a model, however, is only statistically preferred at approximately $3 \times$ the signal-to-noise ratio of the JWST data. When fitting to the actual JWST data of WD 1202, the full-phase eigenbasis model is statistically preferred. However, the resulting model map of WD 1202 B does not resemble the GCM predictions, with a concentrated day-side hotspot at the sub-stellar point with an angular size $\approx 15^\circ$. Interpreting this result more carefully requires follow-up work to disentangle systematics from true emission signals. This model framework provides a means to detect emission features from these rare types of eclipses, and ultimately to test predictions of models of atmospheric circulation across hot Jupiters and their BD analogs.

items.title: Mineralocorticoid receptor signaling reduces somatostatin expression in developing sensory neurons and drives neonatal pain after early-life stress.
items.abstract: Abstract Early-life stress (ELS) causes pain hypersensitivity in neonatal mice and alters the transcriptional profile of the immature dorsal root ganglia (DRG), highlighted by a marked reduction in the expression of a neuropeptide, somatostatin (Sst), which is known to constitutively suppress peripheral nociceptive transmission during adulthood. However, the mechanisms that drive plasticity in gene expression within the developing DRG and neonatal pain after ELS remain unclear. Here, we investigated the degree to which ELS-induced neonatal pain was mediated by corticosterone signaling onto sensory neurons and potential changes in peripheral Sst transmission. The conditional knockout of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), but not the glucocorticoid receptor, from immature DRG neurons prevented ELS-evoked neonatal pain. In contrast, the systemic administration of the selective MR antagonist eplerenone failed to acutely influence pain after ELS, thus suggesting that MR activation enhances pain during the neonatal period via canonical effects on gene transcription. Meanwhile, hind paw injection of the Sst receptor antagonist cyclo-somatostatin increased spontaneous nocifensive behaviors in control pups, but not in pups previously subjected to ELS, raising the possibility that a disruption in tonic antinociception mediated by peripheral Sst contributes to neonatal pain after ELS. Furthermore, administration of the peripherally restricted Sst analog octreotide reversed noxious cold and pressure hypersensitivity in neonatal mice after ELS. Finally, the selective deletion of MR from sensory neurons prevented the ELS-induced decrease in Sst expression. Collectively, these results provide novel mechanistic insight into the effects of chronic early-life adversity on nociceptive processing in the developing nervous system.

items.title: From structure to experience: a Spinozist framework for consciousness rooted in critical brain dynamics.
items.abstract: The study of consciousness is divided between mechanistic accounts that overlook subjective experience and phenomenological approaches limited to neural correlates. We propose a unified framework by grounding our ConCrit model of consciousness and critical brain dynamics within Spinoza's ontological monism. Spinoza's principle of psycho-physical parallelism-mind and body as attributes of one substance-provides a metaphysical basis to dissolve the explanatory gap between neural processes and lived experience. Within this framework, three properties which are maximized near criticality correspond, under Spinoza's parallelism, to mental dimensions: entropy corresponds to experiential richness-the diversity of idea under the attribute of Thought, internal susceptibility to reflexive capacity or degrees of autonomy, and scale-free dynamics to the structural alignment with the common order of nature that, under the attribute of Thought, is expressed in adequate ideas. Thus, we propose that brain activity near criticality under the attribute of Extension is the very same phenomenon that, under the attribute of Thought, is conscious experience. This synthesis reinterprets leading theories-including Integrated Information Theory, Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, and the Entropic Brain Hypothesis-as complementary views of a shared underlying reality. By situating ConCrit within Spinoza's monism, we argue that consciousness is not emergent or epiphenomenal but the parallel manifestation of universal organizational principles, offering a conceptually unified and interpretively transparent framework for neuroscience.

items.title: Is it possible to make unconscious inferences? The limits of the influence of unconsciously perceived stimuli on conscious decisions.
items.abstract: Stimuli presented outside conscious awareness can influence behavior, yet the extent to which such information supports complex decision-making remains unclear. The present study examined the limits of unconscious influence across three levels of decision complexity. Participants made decisions based on stimuli presented using sandwich masking. Stimulus presentation parameters were held constant across conditions, while decision requirements varied. Simple decisions required no contextual integration, intermediate decisions required the integration of masked information with consciously presented context, and complex decisions additionally required logical inference. The results showed that decision accuracy decreased with increasing complexity: it was highest in the simple condition (58%, with strong Bayesian evidence for above-chance performance), lower but still above chance in the medium condition (54%), and not reliably above chance in the complex condition. This suggests that unconscious influence can extend beyond simple decisions but becomes increasingly unreliable when decisions require more demanding integration or inferential processing. Our findings indicate that one of the functional roles of consciousness may be to support the flexible use of information in higher-order cognitive processes and are broadly consistent with theoretical approaches such as the Global Neuronal Workspace Theory.

items.title: Is It Possible to Establish Thresholds for Depressive Symptom Severity Associated With Cognitive Impairments in Bipolar Disorders? Findings From the FACE-BD Cohort.
items.abstract: Individuals with bipolar disorders (BDs) with depressive symptoms exhibit poorer cognitive performance and are often excluded from procognitive interventions and cognitive research. Threshold values on depression severity scales, based on cutoffs defining depressive episodes, have traditionally been used to exclude patients suspected of having depression-associated cognitive impairment. Identifying a threshold value for depression-associated cognitive impairment on these scales could help guide patient selection and treatment. We assessed neuropsychological performance in outpatients with BD with varying levels of depressive symptom severity measured by the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS). The sample was divided based on the total MADRS score or subscores in MADRS theoretical domains. We then compared average cognitive performance between groups while adjusting for relevant covariates to determine a MADRS score above which cognition is significantly impaired. We included 2532 individuals with BD. The composite cognitive score was significantly lower in individuals with a MADRS score ≥ 12 than in those with a score ≤ 1 but did not differ from that of individuals with scores between 2 and 11. Symptoms of detachment and sadness were more strongly associated with cognitive impairment than other symptoms. Individuals with type I BD with MADRS detachment subscores higher than 4 and individuals with type II BD with nonzero sadness subscores had significant cognitive impairment compared to individuals with lower subscores. Excluding individuals with BD whose cognition may be affected by depressive symptoms would require omitting those with MADRS detachment subscores higher than 4 or nonzero sadness subscores. Our findings question the existence of a total depression severity threshold for cognitive impairment, as specific depressive symptoms seem more strongly associated with cognitive impairment than total symptom severity.

items.title: Gut consciousness: a perspective on visceral phenomenal awareness.
items.abstract: The proposition that the enteric nervous system sustains a form of consciousness is seldom entertained in mainstream neuroscience, yet it follows from a disciplined reading of contemporary theories of mind. We argue that the 400-600 million neurons embedded in the mammalian gastrointestinal wall, taken together with the vast interoceptive surface they supervise, the enteroendocrine-immune interface, and the microbial community they co-regulate, constitute a substrate that satisfies, on several of the leading theories of consciousness, the criteria those theories use to attribute experience elsewhere. We synthesize evidence on enteric autonomy, chemo- and mechanosensory resolution, vagal and humoral signalling, self/non-self-discrimination at the epithelial-immune boundary, comparative data from invertebrates whose nervous systems are dominated by gut-like plexuses, and convergent clinical signatures (irritable bowel syndrome, food intolerances, psychedelic nausea, glucagon-like peptide-1 signalling) that are difficult to accommodate under a purely sensorimotor account. Throughout we distinguish two claims that are easily conflated: that the gut makes a large and underappreciated contribution to the single consciousness of the whole animal, and that enteric processing constitutes a second, much simpler locus of experience of its own. Most of the available evidence bears on the first, and we set out five lines of investigation that would discriminate between them. We conclude that gut consciousness is a testable hypothesis, likely corresponding to an 'animal' mode of consciousness dominated by interoceptive feel, drive and affect, and we propose empirical directions for its further investigation.

items.title: Next-Generation Brain Health Monitoring Enabled by Integrated Wearable AI Infrastructure.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are difficult to detect during their pre-symptomatic stages, when intervention is most effective. Advances in wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuroscience now enable continuous monitoring of brain-related physiological signals in real-world settings. However, progress in sensing technologies, signal analytics, and machine learning remains fragmented, limiting the biological specificity, robustness, and clinical translation of many digital biomarkers. This review presents an integrated framework that links molecular pathology and neural circuit dysfunction to sensor-detectable digital phenotypes across sleep, autonomic regulation, gait, speech, and ocular dynamics. We evaluate emerging wearable platforms, including bioelectric, optical, and neuromotor sensors, and discuss critical design considerations such as signal quality, user-centered form factors, and ultra-low-power edge AI systems. We further examine how self-supervised learning, federated AI, mechanistic modeling, and fairness-aware validation can improve biomarker reliability, interpretability, and generalizability. To facilitate clinical deployment, we introduce the Personalized Brain-Health Operating System (pBH-OS), a privacy-preserving reference architecture for scalable digital phenotyping. The framework maps conceptual layers to existing technologies while identifying key validation gaps. We also address practical challenges, including adherence, device dropout, informative missingness, regulatory compliance, and accountability. Together, these advances provide a pathway toward biologically grounded and regulation-ready systems capable of identifying neurodegenerative risk years before clinical symptom onset.

items.title: Extracellular vesicle packaging of a supercluster-encoded antimicrobial combination with enhanced potency against fungal biofilms
items.abstract: Bacterial specialized metabolites are bioactive compounds that have been mined extensively as antibacterials, antifungals, and other drugs. They are widely used as experimental probes of complex biological systems. Since their discovery, their functional characteristics have typically been investigated as single, soluble compounds. The discoveries in this work expand this model. First, we report the co-packaging in extracellular vesicles (EVs) of two specialized metabolite complexes, candicidin and antimycin A, the products of a supercluster of biosynthetic genes, by a Streptomyces soil isolate. Secondly, we report that the products of this supercluster have synergistic antimicrobial activity against fungal biofilms, whereas biofilms are tolerant to the individual compounds. Finally, we show that co-packaging these compounds in EVs ensures simultaneous delivery with enhanced potency. This research advances understanding of the elegant complexity that shapes the evolution and function of bacterial specialized metabolites. In particular, the enhanced antibiofilm activity of co-packaged metabolites compared to individual soluble compounds is notable given the relevance of biofilms to microbial ecology and to pathogenesis. Our work supports the evolution of coordinated activity of specialized metabolites to counter conditional environmental challenges, and highlights co-packaging in EVs as one mechanism for secretion and co-delivery of combinations of bioactive molecules.

items.title: Ecological and metabolic signatures of biofilm viromes across a national river surveillance network
items.abstract: Benthic biofilms are biogeochemical hotspots in rivers, yet their endogenous viral communities remain poorly resolved at national scales. We analysed 447 biofilm metagenomes from 146 sites within England's River Surveillance Network (RSN), sampled in spring and autumn from 2021 to 2023, integrating viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), water-quality gradients, predicted host associations and auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs). We recovered 38,534 vOTUs, revealing extensive viral novelty, where 93% of the vOTUs could not be assigned to a known family. Viromes were dominated by Caudoviricetes and unclassified lineages and were extremely heterogeneous: no vOTU occurred in more than 8.3% of samples. Season, but not sampling year, structured virome composition (family-level PERMANOVA R2 = 0.050, p = 0.001; year p = 0.08), and within-site turnover between spring and autumn exceeded turnover between years. Bray-Curtis ordination linked virome structure weakly to pH, dissolved organic carbon, conductivity, nitrate-N and dissolved oxygen (envfit R2 ≤ 0.066), while threshold indicator taxa analysis (TITAN) identified vOTUs with abrupt change points along alkalinity, dissolved oxygen, nitrate-N and temperature gradients. Predicted host associations were concentrated in Pseudomonodota, Cyanobacteriota and Bacteroidota, with Microcoleus, Chamaesiphon and Flavobacterium among the dominant host genera. Virus-host networks were modular, and module abundances correlated with water quality variables (dissolved oxygen, pH, nitrate etc.), suggesting that environmental filtering acts partly through host ecology. Predicted virus-host associations formed a sparse network organised around a few highly connected viral lineages. Functional profiling showed that the biofilm virome was dominated by nucleotide metabolism, DNA methylation, phosphate-stress, glycan-modification and photosynthesis-related AMGs, with nrdA/nrdB ribonucleotide reductase as the dominant AMG signal. Few vOTUs (1.2%) were detected as proviruses, although provirus fractions were higher in selected host-linked lineages. Collectively, these results show that river biofilm viromes are seasonally structured ecological communities whose composition, host associations and metabolic potential reflect the physicochemical and biological state of rivers. We propose that biofilm viromes provide a complementary layer of information for understanding river health, microbial ecology and the propagation of anthropogenic pressures in freshwater systems.

items.title: V-RAD (Vaginal Radar Assessment Diagram): A Conceptual Framework for the Standardized Multidimensional Representation of the Vaginal Ecosystem
items.abstract: Molecular diagnostics and next-generation sequencing have greatly expanded our ability to identify and characterize microorganisms within the vaginal environment. However, identifying which microorganisms are present does not fully describe the ecological state in which they interact with the host. Routine vaginal microscopy provides complementary information by simultaneously revealing microbial morphology and abundance, epithelial status, microbial organization, cytolytic changes, and the host inflammatory response. Yet, while disease-specific diagnostic systems standardize selected microscopic findings, no common framework exists to represent this broader ecological information as a whole. To address this gap, we developed the Vaginal Radar Assessment Diagram (V-RAD), a conceptual framework that translates routine microscopic observations into a standardized graphical representation of the vaginal ecosystem. V-RAD integrates six independently assessed dimensions covering microbial composition and abundance, epithelial status, microbial spatial organization, host–microbiota interaction, and inflammatory response, preserving their individual contribution without reducing them to a composite score. Representative profiles illustrate how the framework can describe physiological conditions, classical dysbiotic syndromes, mixed presentations, and transitional states within the same graphical language. By making the multidimensional information generated during microscopy explicit and comparable, V-RAD may provide a common framework for documenting vaginal ecology, following its changes over time, and integrating microscopic findings with current and emerging diagnostic technologies.

items.title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California.
items.abstract: The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). We observed an average of 5.9 ± 5.6 (Std Dev) microplastics per fish, with significantly higher overall contamination in striped bass but higher concentrations (microplastics/gram of tissue) in shiner surfperch. For each, we considered contamination relevant to their consumption by recreational anglers. For striped bass, where only the fillet is typically ingested, we found that contamination among tissues differed significantly (on average 3.8 ± 3.1 microplastics/fish fillets). Shiner surfperch, which are typically consumed whole, had an average body burden of 9.1 ± 1.2 microplastics/fish. Contamination varied significantly (p-value < 0.0001) among sampling locations for shiner surfperch, with the highest amounts observed near urban centers (no significant spatial pattern was observed for striped bass). Our findings show microplastics in tissues beyond the gastrointestinal tract, posing concerns for fish health and suggesting that fish caught from San Francisco Bay are a pathway for human consumption of microplastics.

items.title: Prevalence of Decisional Regret and Associated Risk Factors in Patients With Hepatitis B Undergoing Pegylated Interferon Alpha Therapy.
items.abstract: Background Pegylated interferon alpha has been shown to enhance the likelihood of achieving a functional cure in patients with hepatitis B. However, it was associated with a greater number of contraindications and adverse reactions compared with nucleotide analogs. Current research has placed comparatively less emphasis on the potential for this treatment to induce decision regret among patients. Aim The aim of this study was to investigate the current status of decision regret in hepatitis B patients undergoing interferon therapy and to explore its influencing factors. Method A cross-sectional study was conducted in a comprehensive hospital in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China, from February 20 to June 13, 2024. The study recruited hepatitis B patients undergoing treatment with pegylated interferon alpha. The survey encompassed general information, the All Aspects of Health Literacy Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, the Control Preferences Scale, the Decisional Conflict Scale, and the Decision Regret Scale. Results A total of 130 questionnaires were analyzed. Only 13.85% of patients had no regrets at all about the decision, 34.60% experienced mild regret, and the proportion of patients with moderate to severe regrets reached 51.50%. Mild impact on life, active decision-making roles, passive decision-making roles, and decision conflict were the influencing factors of decisional regret in hepatitis B patients on pegylated interferon alpha therapy, which together explained 29.6% of the total variation. Conclusion Hepatitis B patients undergoing pegylated interferon alpha therapy had a high percentage of decisional regret. Healthcare professionals should pay close attention to this phenomenon. In the future, they can investigate additional potential influencing factors and promptly develop intervention strategies to effectively reduce decision regret.

items.title: Geographic Variation in Peromyscus leucopus Population Size and Small Mammal Community Richness in Northern Pennsylvania.
items.abstract: The white-footed mouse, Peromyscus leucopus , is a generalist species found throughout the eastern and central United States that serves as an important reservoir for many tick-borne pathogens relevant to human health. Patterns of P. leucopus relative abundance within small mammal communities have been shown to correlate with the prevalence of Borrelia burgdorferi , the main causative agent of Lyme disease, in vector species. However, efforts to investigate patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community structure often lack geographic variation. In this study, we characterized patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community species richness across a broad geographic range in Pennsylvania. Population sizes and small mammal community richness values in northeastern Pennsylvania (mean N^ = 28.6; mean richness = 5.3) were greater than those in northwestern Pennsylvania (mean N^ = 19.7; mean richness = 2.8). Projected changes in climate and the expansion of human-caused disturbance have the potential to greatly influence the prevalence of P. leucopus in small mammal communities, so regular characterizations of P. leucopus community dynamics will likely be helpful to inform projections and assessments of human exposure to tick-borne pathogen risk.

items.title: Fertility knowledge in Portuguese adolescents: Findings from the serious game "MyFActs!"
items.abstract: Objective Fertility awareness has become crucial for informed reproductive decision-making in the context of rising infertility rates, delayed parenthood, and evolving social norms. Research shows that adolescents have limited fertility knowledge, which may lead to poorly informed future reproductive decisions, making adolescence a particularly important period for fertility education. This study assessed fertility knowledge among Portuguese adolescents using an innovative digital assessment tool, the 12-question serious game "MyFActs!". Patterns of fertility knowledge and demographic predictors across multiple fertility dimensions were examined. Methods A total of 970 adolescents aged 15-18 years participated in this study. Data were analysed using analysis of variance (ANOVA), chi-square tests, and stepwise binary logistic regression models to examine demographic differences and relationships among fertility knowledge dimensions. Results Participants answered a mean of 8.77 qutions correctly (SD=1.88). Significant gender differences were observed, with girls demonstrating greater knowedge than boys in some dimensions. Age-related diffeenes were also found, with older adolescents (17 and 18 years) demonstrating greater knowledge than youner paicipants (15 and 16 years). Binary logistic regrsion analses revealed strong associations among fertility knowledge dmensions. Conclusion These findings suggest that fertilty knowedge among Portuguese adolescents remains moeate, with persistent demographic disparities that rquire tareed educational interventions. The interconnected nature of fertility knowledge dimensions supports comprehensive rather than fragmented educational approaches. The sucessful use of the serious-game format demostrates the potential of digital platforms to engage adlecents with sensitive health topics and overcome tradtioal educational barriers.

items.title: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life After Corticobasal Implant-Supported Rehabilitation: A Single-Center Observational Study.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate changes in oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) following Corticobasal implant-supported prostheses, using the Geriatric Oral Health Assessment Index (GOHAI). Materials and methods This prospective, single-arm pre-/postobservational study included patients undergoing Corticobasal implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation at Narsinhbhai Patel Dental College and Hospital; no control or comparison group was included. Participants were recruited from January 2023 to August 2024. OHRQoL was assessed using the GOHAI at baseline and at the predefined 6-month follow-up visit. The final 6-month assessment included in the analysis was completed in March 2025. Data were analyzed using SPSS Version 17.0. Paired t -tests were used for within-participant pre-/postcomparisons, and repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to evaluate changes over time and exploratory differences in change across participant and treatment subgroups. Results Of 116 enrolled participants, one was lost to follow-up; 115 completed the 6-month assessment and were included in the analysis (completion rate: 99.14%). Among them, 70.4% were female, 57.4% were aged ≥ 60 years, 78.3% were nonsmokers, and 57.4% had no reported medical history. The mean overall GOHAI score increased from 33.58 ± 7.36 at baseline to 50.84 ± 4.40 at 6 months, with a mean improvement of 17.26 points (95% CI: 15.77-18.75; p dz = 2.14). Significant improvements were observed in the functional, pain/discomfort, and psychological domains (all p Conclusion Within the limitations of this prospective, single-center observational study, OHRQoL, as assessed by the GOHAI, improved significantly from baseline to 6 months following Corticobasal implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation in the investigated cohort. These findings indicate favorable patient-reported outcomes following Corticobasal implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation and should be interpreted in the context of the uncontrolled study design and the absence of a comparison group for evaluating implant-system-specific effects. Further controlled longitudinal studies with larger and more diverse populations are warranted to confirm these findings and evaluate their longer-term clinical relevance.

items.title: Prefrontal Planning Latency Associated With Age and Serological Evidence of Microbial Exposure.
items.abstract: Background It has been hypothesized that certain cognitive disorders characterized by frontal executive dysfunction, such as Alzheimer's disease (a neurodegenerative conformational proteinopathy involving amyloid-β and tau), may be associated with prior exposure to infectious agents. This study aimed to test the hypothesis that serological markers of microbial exposure are associated with frontal lobe activity in humans. Methods Executive planning latency was measured in 53 adult participants in this cross-sectional study. A venous blood sample was collected from each participant. Assays for the serological markers of bacterial and viral exposure were performed in a blinded manner. Results Generalized linear modeling (likelihood ratio χ 2 = 27.76, df = 5, p = 0.0001) included five statistically significant independent variables. Among these, age (| t | = 4.360, p = 0.0001), Borrelia burgdorferi lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (| t | = 3.260, p = 0.002), and Ehrlichia chaffeensis and Anaplasma phagocytophilum assays (| t | = 3.138, p = 0.003) were highly significant. Conclusion This study supports the hypothesis that frontal lobe executive function, as indexed by prefrontal cortical planning latency, is associated with serological evidence of exposure to several bacterial genera, particularly Borrelia and Ehrlichia / Anaplasma , as well as with age.

items.title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
items.abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

items.title: Biotechnological Approaches to Biodiversity Conservation and Environmental Management
items.abstract: Biodiversity refers to the structural, functional and evolutionary variability among living organisms across genetic, species and ecosystem hierarchical tiers. Accelerating industrialization, habitat fragmentation, deforestation, agrochemical saturation and anthropogenic climate change have initiated a modern mass extinction event that compromises ecological stability and human survival. Traditional conservation frameworks, while foundational, are increasingly constrained by environmental stressors and spatial limitations. Modern biotechnology provides powerful interventions that mitigate biodiversity loss through integrated ex-situ and in-situ conservation strategies. Techniques such as somatic embryogenesis, apical meristem micro propagation, cryopreservation at ultra-low temperatures, synthetic seed technology and high-density DNA banking facilitate the long-term preservation and recovery of endangered, endemic and economically vital germplasm. Recombinant DNA technology, high-throughput molecular marker profiling and next-generation sequencing further allow precise monitoring of population genetics, overcoming bottlenecks such as inbreeding depression. In environmental management, microbial bioremediation, phytoremediation and bio-fermentation processes offer scalable solutions for soil and aquatic detoxification. This review analyses the biotechnological tools applied to biodiversity conservation through a structured literature synthesis and four comparative assessments. Peer-reviewed global assessments show that between 13.6 % (birds) and 40.7 % (amphibians) of assessed species in six major lineages are threatened, with a distinct dominant driver in each lineage, so interventions must be matched to the lineage. An ordinal field-suitability index ranks SSR and SNP platforms highest (4.00 of 5) for conservation genetics, while comparisons of ex-situ and remediation technologies show that they are complementary rather than interchangeable. The review also examines regulatory and bio safety considerations and emerging techniques including genome editing and environmental DNA. The synthesis concludes that biotechnological intervention functions most effectively as a complement to habitat protection rather than as a substitute for it.

items.title: Epidemiology of Animal Viruses with Emphasis on Prevention: The Growing Importance of Arboviruses
items.abstract: Viral diseases remain a major threat to animal health, livestock production, biodiversity, and, in some cases, public health. Their epidemiological dynamics are determined by complex interactions among the virus, susceptible hosts, vectors, environmental conditions, animal movements, and management practices. Among these diseases, arboviruses are of particular importance because their transmission depends on arthropod vectors and is therefore strongly influenced by vector ecology, climate, host availability, and environmental change. Important veterinary arboviruses include bluetongue virus, African horse sickness virus, West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever virus etc. Changes in temperature, rainfall patterns, land use, vector distribution, and animal movement may modify the geographical and seasonal patterns of arboviral transmission, increasing the risk of emergence and spread into previously unaffected areas. Wildlife and migratory birds may further contribute to the maintenance and dissemination of several arboviruses, creating complex interactions between wildlife, vectors, domestic animals, and humans. A coordinated One Health approach is therefore essential for anticipating emerging viral threats and implementing timely, evidence-based prevention and control strategies. items.title: Balancing Management and Risk in a New European Pyrogeography
items.abstract: Wildfires are an increasingly important challenge across Europe. Climate change is altering the conditions under which fires can ignite and spread, but wildfire risk is also shaped by how landscapes are used, managed, and planned. These choices influence vegetation and fuel availability, landscape structure, and the resilience of ecosystems and communities. Understanding these interactions is therefore important for developing landscapes that are better prepared for a changing climate. Wildfire research draws on multiple disciplines, including ecology, climate science, land-use research, and fire modelling. This broader perspective is referred to as pyrogeography—the study of how fire interacts with climate, vegetation, landscapes, and human activities across space and time. Although wildfire research in Europe is growing, fewer studies combine land-use change, fuel management, ecosystem function, and wildfire modelling to examine how future landscapes can balance multiple objectives. This dissertation addresses this challenge by investigating how land management, future land-use change, and fuel management influence wildfire risk across Europe. The research combines continental-scale assessments with a regional case study. Chapter 2 maps the suitability of three fuel-relevant management strategies—herbivory, mechanical fuel removal, and prescribed burning—across Europe. The results show that opportunities for these strategies vary considerably between regions, highlighting the importance of adapting management to local ecological and social conditions. Chapter 3 examines how wildfire management interacts with biodiversity and carbon storage. It identifies areas where reducing wildfire risk may also help protect important ecosystem functions, as well as areas where fuel management requires careful consideration of potential trade-offs. Chapter 4 focuses on central Portugal and explores how different land-use trajectories influence wildfire susceptibility. The results indicate that continued agricultural abandonment generally increases wildfire susceptibility, whereas renewed agricultural activity can reduce susceptibility by altering vegetation patterns and fuel continuity. Chapter 5 returns to the European scale and simulates how different fuel management strategies perform under alternative land-use and climate futures. Management targeting fine fuels, either alone or combined with other fuel classes, generally produces greater reductions in wildfire behaviour than strategies focused only on coarse fuels. However, responses vary considerably between regions, reinforcing the importance of adapting management to local conditions. Taken together, the findings demonstrate that wildfire in Europe is shaped not only by climate, but also by decisions about how landscapes are managed. Land-use planning, fuel management, and ecological conservation are closely connected, and effective wildfire management requires balancing multiple objectives, including reducing fire risk, conserving biodiversity, storing carbon, and supporting agriculture and forestry. Because these priorities and landscape conditions vary across Europe, management strategies cannot be applied uniformly. The modelling approaches presented in this dissertation do not predict exactly where or how future wildfires will occur. Rather, they provide ways to explore alternative futures, identify potential management opportunities and trade-offs, and examine how different land-use and fuel management pathways may influence wildfire outcomes. By bringing together wildfire science, land-use planning, ecology, and modelling across spatial scales, this dissertation contributes to a more integrated understanding of wildfire management and provides evidence to support the development of landscapes that are better prepared for a changing climate.

items.title: Classical Mechanics
items.abstract: This textbook provides a thorough coverage of classical mechanics. Meant for undergraduate and graduate physics students, it contains discussions on topics beneficial for researchers also. Along with standard graduate-level topics, it highlights and demonstrates the applications of classical mechanics in various areas of physics, astronomy, and astrophysics, thus emphasizing the subject's relevance to current research. Detailed explanations are provided throughout to support self-study and ensure clear understanding of concepts. The text begins with preliminary topics and then proceeds to Lagrange's equation of motion, Hamilton's principle of stationary action, and conservation principles in classical mechanics. It then extends to topics like Hamiltonian formulation of laws of mechanics, two-body central force problem, and restricted three-body problem, among others. Lagrange and Poisson brackets are discussed in exclusive chapters. The book concludes with expositions on Hamilton–Jacobi formulation of dynamics, perturbation theory in Hamiltonian mechanics, dynamics of rigid bodies, and nonlinear dynamics and chaos.

items.title: Scalable high-density tactile arenas for measuring ground-contact forces in freely moving animals
items.abstract: Understanding how animals physically interact with their environment is fundamental to studying movement, sensorimotor control, and neurological function. Yet most behavioral measurement systems primarily capture movement and posture, while direct measurements of contact forces often require specialized instrumentation or involve trade-offs among spatial coverage, resolution, and acquisition speed. Here, we introduce a scalable tactile sensing platform that transforms the surface beneath freely moving animals into a high-resolution contact-imaging instrument. By combining modular sensor arrays with adaptive compressive tactile sampling, the platform provides 16,384 tactile sensing elements at 2-mm pitch across a 512 x 128-mm runway, with nominal 1 kHz acquisition. Rather than exhaustively scanning the entire array, the system concentrates measurements around active contacts, enabling high-speed sensing across an extended behavioral surface. Synchronized overhead video and a camera-assisted analysis pipeline enable paw-resolved measurements of contact loading, stance dynamics, footprint morphology, interlimb weight redistribution, and center-of-pressure trajectories. In a longitudinal rat model of sciatic nerve injury, the platform detected reduced loading of the injured hindlimb and increased loading of the contralateral limb, including changes that conventional gait timing measures underestimated. The modular architecture, together with openly available hardware designs, software and data, provides an accessible framework for studying the mechanical interactions underlying freely moving behavior, with potential applications across neuroscience, injury, and motor recovery research.

items.title: Neuroscience-informed Psychoeducation for Eating Disorders
items.abstract: Eating disorders are serious psychological concerns associated with high levels of physical and psychological comorbidity and elevated premature mortality rates. Despite the severity of these disorders, gaps in clinical care exist and most individuals with eating disorders either do not receive or do not benefit from existing evidence-based treatments. There has been a growing movement to incorporate neuroscience-informed targets into eating disorder treatment; however, to date psychoeducation for eating disorders remains narrowly focused on eating- and weight-related behaviors and less directed towards their underlying mechanisms. Yet, neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) can provide vital insights into diagnostic distinctions, patterns of psychiatric comorbidity, risk and maintenance mechanisms, brain-body relations, prognostic course, and therapeutic targets for eating disorders. Further, knowledge of neuroscience can assist in designing the delivery of psychoeducation with the neurobiology of eating disorders in mind by tailoring content to consider the impact of personality and illness stage on the learning process. In this chapter, we highlight the promise of NIPE for eating disorders, provide a case example of NIPE for eating disorders delivered in a clinical setting, and discuss future directions for research in this area. Ultimately, NIPE can be used to bridge the gap between research knowledge and clinical care in eating disorders, thereby enhancing patient self-efficacy, dispelling misconceptions about eating disorders, and enhancing the accessibility of the science for individuals with these serious, yet undertreated disorders.

items.title: Brain synchrony between interacting sibling pairs during real-time cooperation: an fMRI hyperscanning study
items.abstract: Siblings typically represent the longest-lasting social relationships. Second-person neuroscience provides a framework for studying the neural mechanisms of real-time, reciprocal social interactions. Yet, most studies have focused on simplified coordination tasks, limited brain regions, and did not investigate neural dynamics between siblings. In the first study investigating brain synchrony between siblings to date, we used fMRI hyperscanning to simultaneously record brain activity in 50 same-sex healthy young adult sibling pairs while they played a complex collaborative problem-solving Tetris game requiring continuous non-verbal complementary coordination. Brain synchrony was quantified using inter-subject correlation across 36 regions of interest (ROIs) of the social brain atlas. The interacting sibling pairs showed significantly higher brain synchrony than randomly permuted non-sibling pairs in 19 ROIs (FDR-corrected p < .05). These regions were primarily located within the higher-level theory of mind subnetwork (including bilateral temporo-parietal junction, precuneus and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex), and intermediate-level subnetwork (including anterior insula, inferior frontal gyrus). Greater synchrony in the left temporo-parietal junction significantly predicted better cooperative performance, suggesting that shared neural modelling of a partner's intentions supports effective collaboration. Synchrony in frontal and temporal regions was weakly modulated by cooperative and competitive sibling relationship characteristics; however, these effects did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously (uncorr. p < .05). This study provides first evidence that real-time cooperation between siblings is supported by inter-brain synchrony in core social brain networks. We highlight the value of ecologically valid hyperscanning approaches for investigating neural mechanisms of cooperation in long-term relationships, advancing the field of relational neuroscience.

items.title: Remote sensing applications in solid waste monitoring and management.
items.abstract: The rapid growth of solid waste generation carries significant environmental and public health challenges globally. Traditional waste monitoring methods are not cost-effective and are limited in spatial and temporal scope. Remote sensing, encompassing satellite, aerial, and unmanned platforms, has emerged as a transformative approach to identify, monitor, and manage solid waste sites. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the state-of-the-art in remote sensing applications for solid waste monitoring and management, covering technological developments in the past 2 decades. We examine sensor platforms (optical, hyperspectral, thermal, synthetic aperture radar, light detection and ranging), data processing and machine learning workflows, major application domains (landfill mapping, illegal dumping detection, volumetric assessment, thermal anomaly detection, greenhouse gas monitoring, marine plastic tracking), and integration with geographic information system and IoT (Internet of Things) systems. The present study also evaluates operational successes, methodological challenges, policy implications, and outlines a research roadmap for enhancing the accuracy, scalability, and real-world adoption of remote sensing in waste management.

items.title: National memory path study: Formation of register-based cohorts of persons diagnosed with dementia in Finland in 2019 and 2021.
items.abstract: Aims This study describes the study design and methodology for the formation of novel National Memory Path cohorts, outlined to investigate dementia incidence and health and social service use preceding dementia diagnosis in Finland before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, and to enable further national-level analyses. Methods A register-based study was conducted, consisting of all Finnish home-dwelling adults who received a dementia diagnosis in 2019 or 2021. Dementia was defined based on the diagnosis in the Finnish Health Care Registers, or on the prescription of an anti-dementia drug in the Finnish Prescription Centre. Health and social service use within 12 months before the diagnosis included visits to outpatient and inpatient care in primary and secondary healthcare, emergency departments and home care recorded in the Finnish Health Care Registers. Results Altogether, 23,121 and 22,419 persons were diagnosed with dementia in 2019 and 2021, respectively, corresponding to an incidence of 520 and 501 per 100,000 in mean population. The highest number of diagnoses occurred in the 75-84 age group. Within 12 months before the diagnosis, 98% had used health and social services. Outpatient care in primary healthcare was the most often used service, followed by outpatient care in secondary healthcare and emergency department use. Conclusions National health registers enable comprehensive analysis of dementia incidence and service use. Frequent service use prior to the dementia diagnosis creates opportunities for dementia symptom detection across various parts of the health and social care system.

items.title: Grief, adjustment, and acceptance: A qualitative study of mental health, coping, and identity in people with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH).
items.abstract: Receiving a diagnosis of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH) presents unique challenges. Little is known about MRKH-related mental health, coping, and identity across the lifespan or the role of positive adaptation in individuals' experiences of MRKH. Participants completed interviews on mental health, family planning, sexual well-being, relationships, and healthcare experiences. A reflexive thematic analysis approach was used to analyze the data. Three themes represented experiences of living with MRKH: grief, adjustment, and acceptance. Our analysis reconstructed a common pattern across participants' retrospective accounts, in which experiences of grief were often described in relation to the period following diagnosis, while adjustment and acceptance were frequently reflected in participants' narratives of living with MRKH. Participants' experiences of mental health, coping, and identity differed across the three themes. The results suggest that many people with MRKH demonstrate psychological resilience and describe enhanced well-being alongside experiences of grieving, adjustment, and acceptance.

items.title: Characterizing genetic determinism about body weight: An exploratory study.
items.abstract: Genetic determinism, the belief that genetic factors are the major determinant of a trait, shapes attitudes about body weight. This study explores deterministic beliefs, evaluates potential predictors, and examines associations with weight-related psychosocial outcomes. Data were collected through an online survey of 678 U.S. adults. Items assessed genetic determinism about body weight, demographics, causal attributions for weight, and weight stigma-associated attitudes. Endorsement of genetic determinism was relatively uncommon, with 21% of participants agreeing to some extent with deterministic statements on average. Deterministic attitudes were positively correlated with genetic and environmental attributions for weight and negatively correlated with dietary and physical activity attributions. Predictors included political orientation and an interaction where parents of more children had more deterministic attitudes at higher body weights. Findings highlight nuanced ways genetic determinism beliefs associate with body weight attitudes, suggesting the need for further research into mechanisms and implications for stigma reduction and health behavior.

items.title: The association between pension and mental health of older adults: Evidence from China.
items.abstract: In the context of high coverage of social pension insurance in China, there is a lack of comprehensive empirical research on how different pension levels affect the mental health of older individuals. Drawing on nationally representative data from the 2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, this study empirically examines the link between pension and the mental health of older adults in China. Furthermore, a three-step approach and Karlson-Holm-Breen decomposition method were employed to estimate the mediating effect of social activities. The results indicate that pension level is related to older adults' mental health. Further analysis demonstrates that pensions mitigate depressive symptoms among older Chinese adults through increased participation in social activities. The positive association between pension and mental health is more pronounced among older adults without wage income. Our study provides evidence for China's efforts to refine the social pension insurance system and gradually enhance pension benefits.

items.title: Internalized weight stigma as a mediator between past weight stigma and current healthcare avoidance/comfort in seeking medical care.
items.abstract: Youth may experience weight stigma from medical providers, which can be internalized and reduce quality of life. However, little is known about how early provider-based weight stigma relates to later healthcare behaviors. This study examined whether internalized weight stigma statistically mediated associations between provider-based weight stigma during childhood and adolescence and (1) healthcare avoidance and (2) comfort in seeking care in adulthood. Participants were 488 university students who reported past and current weight stigma in healthcare, internalized weight stigma, healthcare avoidance, and comfort in seeking medical care. Over half experienced provider-based weight stigma during youth and one-third within the past year. Early provider-based weight stigma was associated with greater avoidance and lower comfort, with significant indirect effects through internalized stigma. Findings underscore the lasting associations between early weight-stigmatizing healthcare experiences and adult healthcare engagement, with internalized weight stigma statistically accounting for these associations.

items.title: The Quantitative Psychologist Is Dead, Long Live the Quantitative Psychologist
items.abstract: Much of what quantitative psychologists publish consists of developing statistical methods, implementing them in software, and evaluating them in simulation studies. I argue that artificial intelligence (AI) can already do much of this work, and that its share will only grow. The quantitative psychologist has always been a jack of all trades, combining programming, statistics, and psychological knowledge without being a master of any one of them. AI is now the better jack of all trades. When methods become cheap, value moves to what AI cannot supply and to what it newly makes possible. I describe three directions: collecting trustworthy data from real people, formalizing psychological theory now that computational modeling is within reach of any researcher, and rethinking methodological educationso that students learn to judge the analyses that AI will run for them. Thespecialist role built around producing methods for others will fade, whilequantitative thinking spreads through all of psychology.

items.title: The Map Is Not the Territory: Construct Names, Items, and Responses in Measures of Mentalizing, Epistemic Trust, and Emotion Regulation
items.abstract: Psychology has a measurement problem: different constructs often share the same name, and the same construct is measured under different names. This matters most for constructs theorized as interdependent. In theory, these constructs are defined by name, and their interdependence is posited at that level; in practice, each is measured by a pool of items, often from separate questionnaires, which may overlap or diverge in ways the names do not anticipate. We asked whether construct names correspond to the items that operationalize them, whether items reflect the structure of responses, and whether responses follow the boundaries posited by names or drawn by items. Using reflective functioning, epistemic trust, and difficulties in emotion regulation as a case study, we compared semantic similarities of construct names and items with response correlations in 1,167 emerging adults (aged 18–29, 72% female; item-level analyses preregistered) and 1,068 secondary school students (aged 14–20, 67% female). Construct names best matched their own items in 4 of 11 subscales. Items reflected the structure of responses (r = .62 and .58), also, less closely, across questionnaires (.42 and .37). Responses followed boundaries drawn by items more than those posited by names. A correlation between such measures, usually read as evidence of interdependence, may also arise from items that describe the same experience or from shared method variance. What theory says about a construct thus applies only in part to what its items measure.

items.title: Accidental overdose admissions and premature death: A large population-based data-linkage cohort study in New South Wales, Australia (PAVLOVA 4).
items.abstract: Background and aims People with substance use disorders have reduced life-expectancy; however, risks of premature death from injuries and natural causes following an accidental overdose are not well characterised. This study aimed to estimate risk of premature death (by cause and over time), and disease burden following hospitalised accidental overdose. Design An observational study using the Poisoning And enVenomation Linkage to evaluate Outcomes and clinical Variation in Australia (PAVLOVA) cohort. Setting A population-based data-linkage including admissions from all public and private hospitals in New South Wales, Australia (population ~8 million), 2011-2020. Participants 14 036 individuals [median age 43.5 years, interquartile range (IQR) = 29.4-61.8 years, 46.7% female, n = 6557] with an index non-fatal accidental poisoning, as defined by hospital coding, followed for a median of 3.9 years (IQR = 1.7-6.3). We restricted our analysis to people with accidental poisonings with prescription and illicit drugs that are associated with non-medical use and dependence, including opioids and benzodiazepines. Measurements Standardised mortality ratio (SMR) by cause (natural causes stratified by body system, and external causes stratified by intent and mechanism), SMR over time (post-index poisoning), years of life lost (YLL) by cause, age and sex. SMR and YLL were calculated based on expected values generated using official statistics. Results Of the 14 036 people included, there were 2588 deaths. Death was more likely in individuals with accidental poisoning compared with the general population [SMR = 3.5, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 3.4-3.7]. SMRs were highest for external causes (SMR = 12.8, 95% CI = 11.5-14.1), including accidental poisoning (SMR = 59.5, 95% CI = 51.7-67.3) and suicide (SMR = 10.5, 95% CI = 8.2-12.9). Death was also more likely across all natural causes, particularly infectious (SMR = 7.0, 95% CI = 5.1-8.9) and respiratory diseases (SMR = 6.2, 95% CI = 5.4-6.9). Median YLL per death was 21.2 (IQR = 10.0-35.6) and 15.2 (IQR = 7.2-30.2) for males and females, respectively. The main contributors to YLL were natural causes (64.0%): neoplasms (19.5%), circulatory (12.2%) and respiratory disease (11.1%). The remainder of YLL was from external causes (36.0%): mainly accidental poisoning (22.4%). Summary People in New South Wales, Australia, who experience an accidental overdose appear to have an increased risk of death over subsequent years, but particularly in the first month, compared with the general population; however, accidental poisoning accounts for only 22% of years of life lost, with death from natural causes being much more common.

items.title: Trends in Opioid Prescribing for Nonspecific Low Back Pain After CDC Guidelines and California Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs, 2012-2024.
items.abstract: Objective Nonspecific low back pain (ns-LBP) is a widespread health challenge, and opioids were frequently prescribed upon first LBP presentation in the United States during the opioid epidemic. We assessed temporal changes in quarterly (Q) opioid prescriptions for new-onset ns-LBP from 2012 through 2024 at a California medical center amid evolving voluntary federal recommendations and mandatory state regulations. Methods We analyzed opioid prescription rates (prescription within 6 months of diagnosis) for ns-LBP patients diagnosed in all departments and stratified by emergency department (ED), and we compared high- versus low-dose prescription (≥50 morphine mg equivalents/day). Change point detection identified transitions without policy priors, and interrupted time series regression quantified level changes and trend modifications. Results Of 31 940 ns-LBP patients, 2077 (6.5%) received opioids (mean [SD] age, 51.0 [17.6] y; 45.3% male; 53.7% White). Change points occurred at 2015 Q2 and 2018 Q4. Prescribing odds declined 2.7% per quarter from 2012 Q1 through 2024 Q4 (95% CI, 0.4%-5.0%; P = .02). ED patients (16.5% prescribed opioids vs 5.8% non-ED) showed a 54.2% immediate reduction at 2015 Q2 (95% CI, 18.8%-74.2%; P = .008), declining from 27.4% to 12.2% before plateauing; non-ED patients showed a 42.8% reduction at 2018 Q4 (95% CI, 27.5%-54.9%; P Conclusion Change points coincided with anticipatory adoption of the 2016 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommendations and 2018 California mandatory drug monitoring implementation. ED settings showed disproportionate reductions at 2015 Q2, consistent with knowledge diffusion of voluntary guidelines in settings with frequent opioid prescribing, while non-ED reductions coincided with immediate regulatory compliance at 2018 Q4. This distinction can guide future policy selection to address environment-specific adoption barriers.

items.title: An Integrated Housing Intervention for People Involved in the Criminal-Legal System: Contributors to Successfully Moving Along the Housing Continuum.
items.abstract: Objectives People impacted by the criminal-legal system face challenges to securing and sustaining permanent housing. This study was designed to deliver an integrated housing, medical, and behavioral health services intervention to individuals with criminal-legal involvement. Methods After a baseline needs assessment, participants were linked to services and completed quarterly study visits for up to 12 months. We used descriptive statistics to assess frequency and multivariate logistic regression to assess correlates of housing status at last follow-up. Results Between June 2019 and November 2023, 187 participants were enrolled in Project CHANGE (Comprehensive Housing and Addiction Treatment Network of Greater New Haven). At baseline, 43% of participants were unstably housed, 37% were homeless, and the remaining resided in a shelter or institution. At the time of last follow-up, 49 participants (26.2%) reported improved housing outcomes, and an additional 121 participants' (64.7%) housing situation did not worsen. In multivariate models, individuals who were older (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.1; 95% CI, 1.0-1.1), unstably housed at baseline (AOR = 7.6; 95% CI, 3.8-15.9), and enrolled in the study for longer (AOR = 1.2; 95% CI, 1.1-1.3) had higher odds of being housed at last follow-up, whereas those with high-severity substance use had lower odds of being housed (AOR = 0.3; 95% CI, 0.1-0.6). Conclusions In this comprehensive program, integrated housing and health services were time and cost intensive but were associated with positive housing outcomes. People involved in the criminal-legal system face unique barriers to housing, particularly when compounded by substance use.

items.title: Exploring the role of COVID-19 pandemic preparedness in Norway's Ukrainian refugee crisis response.
items.abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to explore how and in what ways COVID-19 preparedness in Norway shaped the organization and delivery of the country's response to the Ukrainian refugee crisis and identify lessons learned from the overlap of the pandemic and the refugee crisis to strengthen Norway's preparedness for future crises, as perceived by the participants. Methods A qualitative study with in-depth, semi-structured, individual interviews was conducted among 10 individual, civil society, and government actors who worked in relation to both the COVID-19 pandemic and the Ukrainian refugee crisis. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results The following four themes emerged, including both positive and negative consequences of the end of the pandemic overlapping with the beginning of the Ukrainian refugee crisis: (1) pandemic-shaped mindsets and momentum in crisis response, (2) adapting pandemic resources for refugee crisis response, (3) participation and power in crisis decision-making, and (4) lessons learned: continuity is key. Conclusions This study provides an enhanced understanding of how selected Norwegian actors perceived the role of COVID-19 preparedness in the Ukrainian refugee crisis response. Participants identified both strengths, such as the reuse of resources and coordination structures, and challenges related to communication and participation in decision-making. Understanding these experiences may help inform future preparedness planning across overlapping crises.

items.title: Sunscreen use at Danish beaches in 2025 and long-term changes in sun protection related to public advice.
items.abstract: Background National health authorities advise against excessive sun exposure and recently advised the public to increase sun protection factor (SPF) to ⩾30 to reduce sunburns and lower the risk of developing skin cancer. Aim To examine the prevalence of sunscreen use and level of SPF used at Danish beaches on sunny days in 2025, and the development in sunscreen use over time related to recommendations by the European Union and the Danish Health Authorities. Methods : We investigated the prevalence of sunscreen use at beaches in the Copenhagen area during summer 2025 and related the data to sex, age, SPF, time of sunscreen purchase and frequency of sunscreen application. We compared our data to similar investigations performed during the last 35 years. Results The study population was 389 persons, of which 10% were children. Participating men and women had an identical mean age of 34 years. About 70% of men and 90% of women used sunscreen. Mean body SPF was 30 for women and 28 for men. Mean face SPF was 46 for women and 38 for men. Sunscreen use and SPF were independent of age. Newly acquired sunscreens had a higher SPF than sunscreens bought before 2025. We found an exponential rise in SPF related to recommendations by the EU and Danish Health Authorities. Conclusions In the last 35 years, the level of SPF used at the beach has increased exponentially from a median of SPF 4 to SPF 30, with a clear relation to public health recommendations.

items.title: Frequent Social Media Use Associated With Tobacco, Alcohol, and Drug Use Among US High School Students.
items.abstract: Objectives The purpose of this study was to examine the associations between frequent social media use and tobacco, alcohol, and drug use among US high school students in grades 9 through 12. Methods Data from the 2023 national Youth Risk Behavior Survey (N = 20 103) were analyzed to assess the associations between frequent social media use and current tobacco or nicotine use, current alcohol use, current binge drinking, ever marijuana use, ever prescription opioid misuse, and ever select illicit drug use. Frequent social media use was defined as using social media several times a day, about once an hour, or more than once an hour. Quasi-Poisson regression models estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (APRs) comparing substance use behaviors among students with frequent social media use versus infrequent or no social media use, overall and by sex. Models were adjusted for race and ethnicity and grade. Results Compared with students reporting infrequent or no social media use, students with frequent social media use were more likely to report current tobacco or nicotine use (APR = 1.88; 95% CI, 1.25-2.83), current alcohol use (APR = 2.07; 95% CI, 1.54-2.78), current binge drinking (APR = 2.55; 95% CI, 1.45-4.48), and ever marijuana use (APR = 2.09; 95% CI, 1.68-2.60). Associations were observed among female and male students. Conclusions Frequent social media use was associated with several substance use behaviors among US high school students. Future research should examine mechanisms, including type of social media platform used, exposure to substance use-related content, and peer influences, to inform prevention strategies.

items.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Positive and Adverse Childhood Experiences with Adulthood Awareness of and Participation in Children's Cafeterias (Kodomo Shokudo) in Japan.
items.abstract: Childhood experiences shape social participation in adulthood. However, evidence remains limited regarding how positive childhood experiences (PCEs) and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate to participation in low-threshold, community-based initiatives. This study examined the associations between PCEs and ACEs and adulthood awareness of and engagement in children's cafeterias ( kodomo shokudo ) in Japan. Using nationwide online survey data, PCE and ACE scores were categorized as 0, 1-2, 3-5, and 6-7, and 0, 1, 2, and ≥3, respectively. Outcomes were awareness and past-year engagement. In fully adjusted models, higher PCE and ACE categories were associated with greater awareness (ORs [95% CIs]: 2.11 [1.95-2.29] for PCE 6-7; 2.13 [1.96-2.33] for ACE ≥3). Higher PCE categories were also associated with engagement (1.32 [1.08-1.63] for PCE 6-7), whereas ACE categories were not. Supportive childhood environments may facilitate engagement in flexible community initiatives.

items.title: Respiratory pathogens across rural populations: general practice patients with community-acquired pneumonia, residents, and goat farmers.
items.abstract: Background Residents living near goat farms ( Methods This cross-sectional study included general practitioner (GP)-diagnosed pneumonia patients (PP; n = 108), non-farming rural residents without pneumonia (NFR; n = 200), and goat farm workers (GFW; n = 91). Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and analyzed by a multiplex and two additional PCR test targeting in total 12 bacteria, 20 viruses and 1 fungus. Between-group differences in detection were assessed by Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations between pathogen detection and residential proximity to goat farming and other covariates. Results Presence of any of the examined pathogens was highest in the PP group (94.5%), followed by GFW (88.8%), and NFR (70%). The most frequently detected pathogens overall were Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and rhinovirus. Of these, M. catarrhalis and S. pneumoniae were significantly more often detected in PP, whereas Salmonella spp. and S. aureus were more frequently detected in GFW. Eight pathogens, including Coxiella burnetii, were not detected. Age, season of sampling, smoking and other covariates were significantly associated with certain bacteria and viruses. However, no associations were identified between residential proximity to goat farming and detection of specific pathogens in NFR and PP. Conclusions Respiratory pathogens were detected in nearly all PP, while substantial proportions of positives were also observed in GFW and NFR, likely reflecting (transient) colonization rather than active infection. Detection of the examined pathogens was not associated with residential proximity to goat farms, suggesting that these pathogens do not explain the observed increased pneumonia risk among nearby non-farming residents. As a substantial proportion of the Dutch population (~ 7%) lives within 2,000 m of a commercial goat farm, and goat farming is expanding globally, further research efforts, including microbiologic diagnostics and surveillance, are needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the increased pneumonia risk among nearby residents.

items.title: Cariprazine Augmentation and Sustained Remission of Physical Aggression in Clozapine-Treated Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Persistent aggression may occur in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) despite long-term clozapine treatment and multiple augmentation strategies. We describe a male patient in his sixties with a decades-long history of schizophrenia who required prolonged psychiatric inpatient care because of recurrent, unpredictable physical assaults toward other patients, staff, relatives, and police. This included treatment at a state forensic psychiatric hospital because of treatment complexity and safety concerns, not forensic legal status. Aggression persisted during adequately monitored high-dose clozapine treatment and several augmentation strategies. The last documented physical assault occurred in October 2021. Cariprazine 1.5 mg/day was initiated in November 2021, primarily for longstanding negative symptoms. Within approximately seven weeks, mood and participation in communal ward activities improved. No further physical assaults were documented during more than 4 years of follow-up. The patient subsequently transitioned to voluntary treatment and supported housing. Later somatic illnesses, temporary interruptions of oral medication, and substantial fluctuations in clozapine serum concentrations were not followed by renewed physical aggression. This case describes a prolonged temporal association between cariprazine augmentation and the absence of recurrent physical assaults, but the single-case design, episodic pretreatment course, concomitant treatment changes, and absence of standardized ratings preclude causal inference.

items.title: A Gamified Mobile Application for Orthodontic Education: Usability Assessment and Impact on Knowledge and Attitude of Dental Students.
items.abstract: Purpose The use of gamification-based educational interventions in dentistry has been proposed as a novel approach to increase cognitive engagement and improve learning; however, evidence regarding the simultaneous effect of these tools on students' knowledge and attitude in the field of orthodontics is limited. This study evaluated the usability of a gamified orthodontic application and compared its knowledge and attitude outcomes with traditional reference-book study. Methods In an experimental study, 80 sixth-year dental students were assigned to the intervention and control groups. The intervention group used a gamified scenario-based application for 1 month. Usability was assessed with the Mobile Health App Usability Questionnaire (MAUQ). Knowledge and attitude scores were measured before and after the intervention, and data were analysed using a mixed linear model. Results The mean usability scores were assessed as satisfactory. Although both groups improved, significant time × group interactions favoured the intervention group for knowledge (p = 0.013) and attitude (p = 0.001). However, the observed effect sizes were small to moderate, suggesting a limited but potentially meaningful educational benefit. Orthodontic course grade showed a positive and significant association with both outcomes (p 0.05). Conclusion Compared with traditional reference-book study, the gamified application was associated with modest improvements in knowledge and attitudes. However, the design did not allow the specific contribution of gamification to be distinguished from other digital-learning effects.
