items.title: Motor control of song and song-like vocalizations in the white-crowned sparrow.
items.abstract: Oscine songbirds show remarkable diversity in song organization spanning from long songs composed of many different syllables to short single songs. All of these likely arose through sexual selective forces and therefore are thought to reflect a singer's skill, often described as vocal performance. It is therefore important to gain insight into the song production mechanisms in species that sing a single, short song. Here we investigated the physiological control underlying learned song and other song-like vocalizations in the white-crowned sparrow (Zonotrichia leucophrys) by recording air sac pressure, tracheal and bronchial airflow and sound during spontaneously generated vocal behavior in 19 males (11 tutored, 8 untutored). The left side of the syrinx tends to produce more contributions to most song syllables than the right side, while both sides generate similar and overlapping frequency ranges and interact in the production of buzzy syllables. Two other song-like vocalizations, trills and twitter song also require sophisticated respiratory and syringeal movements. Trills display the most rapid temporal pattern with mini-breath rates of > 20 Hz. This illustrates that vocalizations other than typical song can also inform us about vocal performance. The basic production mechanism and syringeal lateralization was consistent between tutored and untutored birds, as well as across the different vocalizations studied here, suggesting innate development of the respective contributions of the two sound sources.

items.title: Beyond single risk factors: defeat and genetic variations linking cumulative interpersonal risk to suicidal ideation in Chinese adolescents.
items.abstract: Suicide among adolescents is a major global health concern. While poor interpersonal relationships are well-established risk factors for adolescent suicide, most research has focused on isolated interpersonal domains, limiting our understanding of how cumulative interpersonal risks shape the developmental trajectories of suicidal ideation, particularly within a gene × environment framework. A total of 760 adolescents (Mage = 13.01, 54.6% girls) were assessed at baseline and followed up across three additional six-month intervals over one and a half years. Adolescents' saliva was collected at T2 for genetic extraction, and the multilocus genetic composite (MGC) was created based on the gene-by-environment interaction between SNPs and cumulative interpersonal risk for defeat via the leave-one-out machine learning approach. Findings of latent growth modeling revealed that adolescents' suicidal ideation increased over time. Cumulative interpersonal risk was indirectly associated with higher initial levels and a faster increase in suicidal ideation through defeat, particularly among adolescents with a higher MGC compared to those with a lower MGC. These findings suggest that intervention strategies should aim to reduce adolescents' exposure to interpersonal risk, alleviate feelings of defeat, and consider the genetic susceptibility.

items.title: Heart rate variability and cortisol responses to acute low- and moderate-intensity exercise in stress-related exhaustion.
items.abstract: Purpose Exercise is commonly recommended to support stress regulation and mental health, yet it remains unclear whether these benefits translate to conditions characterized by prolonged stress and fatigue. The aims were to examine whether autonomic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis responses to a single exercise bout differ between individuals with stress-related exhaustion and healthy controls, and whether responses vary by exercise intensity. Methods In a randomized, counterbalanced crossover design, 30 individuals with stress-related exhaustion (93.3% women; age 46.3 ± 5.89) and 29 healthy controls with a comparable age and sex distribution (93.1% women; age 45.5 ± 5.47) completed two 22-min cycling sessions at workloads corresponding to 40% (low intensity) and 55% (moderate intensity) of estimated maximal oxygen uptake (V̇O₂max) on separate occasions. Heart rate variability (HRV; RMSSD, SD2/SD1, LF/HF) and salivary cortisol were assessed pre-exercise, post-exercise, and 30 min post-exercise, with HRV also assessed during exercise. Results Compared with controls, individuals with stress-related exhaustion showed lower RMSSD overall, with the most apparent between-group differences observed during the post-exercise period. Within the exhaustion group, moderate- compared with low-intensity exercise was associated with lower RMSSD and higher SD2/SD1 and LF/HF, whereas no intensity effects were observed in controls. No between-group differences were observed in HRV during exercise. Cortisol analyses suggested overall group-related differences, without clear differences across time points. Conclusions These findings suggest altered physiological stress-system regulation in stress-related exhaustion and highlight the post-exercise period and exercise intensity as important considerations when tailoring exercise recommendations for this population. The study was retrospectively registered on 05/30/2024 at Clinical Trials.gov, with trial registration number NCT06429423.

items.title: Unit-Level Burnout Dimensions and Patient Experience: A Multilevel Study of Aggregated Contextual Strain in a Southeast European Health System.
items.abstract: To examine whether aggregated unit-level nurse burnout is associated with patient-reported experience across hospital units using a multilevel framework, conceptualizing burnout as aggregated contextual strain rather than homogeneous unit climate. A cross-sectional multilevel study was conducted across 11 regional public hospitals in Albania (October 2024-July 2025). Nurse burnout was assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory among 2000 nurses, and patient experience was measured with HCAHPS among 679 patients. Burnout scores were aggregated at the clinical-unit level. Multilevel linear modeling with patients nested within units examined associations between emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, personal accomplishment, and patient experience. Cluster-robust standard errors and leave-one-unit-out sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess estimate stability. Patient experience varied significantly between units (ICC = 0.229). In the multilevel model, higher unit-level emotional exhaustion and depersonalization were both associated with lower patient experience. Under cluster-robust estimation (t-distribution, df = 9), depersonalization remained statistically significant (robust p < 0.001), and emotional exhaustion remained significant (robust p = 0.028), whereas personal accomplishment was not significant (robust p = 0.187). Leave-one-cluster-out and exact wild-cluster-bootstrap sensitivity analyses confirmed depersonalization as the most robust association across all specifications (bootstrap p = 0.003), whereas emotional exhaustion, while directionally consistent, was only borderline under the most conservative correction (exact wild-bootstrap p = 0.052), underscoring the statistical fragility inherent to a 10-cluster design. Aggregated unit-level depersonalization, and to a lesser and more fragile extent emotional exhaustion, may be relevant to patient-centered care, but the strength and consistency of these unit-level estimates are constrained by the small number of analytical clusters and by heterogeneity in how those clusters were formed across hospitals. Given the modest number of clinical units, findings should be interpreted as exploratory contextual associations. These findings support further investigation of workload support and team-level resources as potential targets for improving nurse well-being and patient-centered care.

items.title: The Epidemiology and Associated Factors of Ectopic Pregnancy in Saudi Arabia: A Literature Review.
items.abstract: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is a serious maternal complication with a worldwide prevalence of about 2%. It is defined as the implantation of the product of conception outside the uterine cavity. Patients with EP may present with a wide range of clinical symptoms, including abdominal/pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, missed menstrual cycle, and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound. After diagnosing EPs, medical and/or surgical treatment options are available based on the patient's hemodynamic status, ectopic location, fetal cardiac activity, size of the gestational sac, level of β-HCG, and patient profile. This narrative literature review aims to summarize published primary studies on the epidemiology and reported associated factors of EP in Saudi Arabia between 2000 and 2024. A total of 1342 EP cases were reported across the included studies. Reported prevalence estimates ranged from 0.23% to 1.20%. The reviewed studies were from different regions of the Kingdom, including Abha, Khamis Mushait, Yanbu, Makkah, Madina, Jeddah, Khobar, and Majmaah. The prevalence of EPs fluctuated between 2000 and 2019 and had three peaks: 1.13% (2012), 1.14% (2013), and 1.2% (2019). Multiple associated factors linked to EP were reported in this review, including a history of pelvic surgery, C-sections, previous EP, abortions, intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) use, and pelvic inflammatory diseases (PIDs). EP is a serious complication that causes significant maternal morbidity and mortality and has a substantial burden on the healthcare system. In this review, eleven studies were reviewed regarding the epidemiology of EPs in the Kingdom. No clear pattern or trend in prevalence was identified, although the majority of studies reported lower EP rates than the worldwide prevalence. Several associated factors were reported across the included studies; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because most studies were retrospective and descriptive in nature.

items.title: Effectiveness of a School-Centered Intervention for Myopia and Obesity Comorbidity in Children: A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
items.abstract: The rising comorbidity of myopia and overweight/obesity (OWOB) in children shares modifiable behavioral pathways, yet evidence for integrated prevention remains limited. We conducted a cluster-randomized, hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation trial in 36 pair-matched Beijing schools. Of 4991 enrolled students in Grades 1-4 and 7, 3426 (68.6%) completed the 12-month follow-up. The school-centered "22510SS" intervention targeted outdoor activity, screen time, diet, sleep, and health monitoring. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in spherical equivalent or BMI change, or in the prevalence of myopia, OWOB, or their comorbidity. The intervention improved the overall behavior-improvement rate (39.7% vs. 33.7%; OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.00-1.80). In a prespecified analysis, students in Grades 1-4 showed slower myopia progression (OR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.25-0.86); an exploratory analysis suggested benefits among children from less supportive family environments. Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) evaluation showed 100% fidelity for school-based activities, approximately 60% completion of family-facing health-tip dissemination, an incremental cost of ¥215.43 per participant, and a Program Sustainability Assessment Tool (PSAT) score of 6.10/7. The intervention was feasible and improved targeted behaviors but did not produce significant population-level clinical effects within 12 months. Stronger family engagement and longer follow-up may be needed. Trial Registration: NCT05275959.

items.title: Development of an HPV Self-Collection Brochure for Unhoused Individuals Using Learner Verification and Revision.
items.abstract: Individuals who are unhoused face disproportionately high rates of cervical cancer incidence and multiple barriers to screening, yet tailored educational materials to support human papillomavirus (HPV) self-collection in this population remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a sequential, two-phased qualitative study using Learner Verification and Revision methodology to iteratively develop and refine an instructional brochure on HPV self-collection designed for, and with, individuals who are unhoused. We first conducted focus groups with community health educators (n = 6) and street medicine team members (n = 12), followed by semi-structured interviews with individuals who were unhoused (n = 19) and had participated in an HPV self-collection pilot study. Data collection assessed comprehension, attraction, cultural-linguistic acceptability, and persuasion of the brochure, with trauma-informed care as an additional domain, and transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis. Participants broadly found the brochure clear, visually appealing, and easy to follow, while identifying key areas for refinement, including greater brevity, more inclusive visuals, regional Spanish vocabulary adaptation, and language modifications to strengthen trustworthiness and empowerment. Street medicine team members emphasized that the brochure best complements verbal counseling rather than serving as a standalone resource. This community-engaged, iterative process yielded a tailored, trauma-informed educational tool which is publicly available and editable. As HPV self-collection expands across the United States, such materials will be valuable to support equitable access to cervical cancer screening.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of COP and CHOP Chemotherapy Protocols in Feline Intermediate- to Large-Cell Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Feline intermediate- to large-cell lymphoma is commonly treated with COP or CHOP chemotherapy, but the clinical benefit of adding doxorubicin (CHOP) remains controversial given its associated toxicity profile and cost. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis summarized response and survival outcomes reported for COP- and CHOP-based protocols in feline intermediate- to large-cell lymphoma. Searching PubMed, Scopus, and CAB Abstracts (2000-2024), we included 21 studies comprising 1054 cats. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis utilizing Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) estimation was conducted to evaluate overall (ORR), complete (CR), and partial response (PR) rates. The overall pooled ORR was 81.0%. Subgroup meta-regression revealed no statistically significant differences between COP and CHOP for ORR (83.0% vs. 77.0%, p = 0.360), CR (57.0% vs. 49.0%, p = 0.350), or PR (28.0% vs. 22.0%, p = 0.468). Profound heterogeneity (overall I2 = 85.4%-89.6%) persisted across all analyses, driven primarily by the pooling of diverse anatomical subtypes and uncontrolled confounding by Feline Leukaemia Virus (FeLV) status. Furthermore, inadequate variance reporting and a widespread lack of standardized response criteria (e.g., VCOG-RECIST) precluded a formal meta-analysis of survival outcomes. Descriptively, reported median survival times ranged broadly (COP: 108-610 days; CHOP: 62-973 days) without a clear advantage for CHOP. A custom weighted risk-of-bias assessment highlighted significant methodological deficiencies across the literature. In conclusion, current aggregate evidence does not demonstrate a statistically detectable difference in response rates between CHOP- and COP-based protocols. Severe methodological heterogeneity and retrospective selection bias prevent definitive conclusions regarding long-term survival, emphasizing the critical need for homogeneous, prospective randomized trials utilizing standardized reporting guidelines.

items.title: Can Generative Artificial Intelligence Interpret Culture? Assessing ChatGPT's Role in Qualitative Health Research.
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into research has raised urgent questions about whether generative models can contribute meaningfully to qualitative inquiry, particularly in health contexts where cultural nuance and contextual interpretation are essential. This study evaluates ChatGPT's capacity to support ethnographic analysis by comparing AI-assisted outputs with a previously conducted human-led analysis of 20 interviews with college students managing Type 1 diabetes. Guided by Spradley's four-phase ethnographic interview method, it examines ChatGPT-4o's ability to identify cultural domains, construct taxonomies, articulate contrastive dimensions, and synthesize higher-order themes. While ChatGPT efficiently generated surface-level summaries and facilitated early data organization, its analytic contributions remained largely descriptive. The model struggled to identify symbolic tensions, contextual meanings, and culturally embedded interpretations that human analysts derived through iterative reading, reflexivity, and familiarity with the lived experience of chronic illness. AI-generated taxonomies lacked internal structure, and thematic interpretations failed to account for the institutional, relational, and identity-based dynamics shaping students' experiences. These findings suggest that although generative AI can serve as a useful assistive tool for preliminary coding and pattern recognition, it cannot replicate the interpretive depth central to qualitative health research. The study highlights the methodological implications of incorporating AI into qualitative inquiry, underscoring the need for critical oversight and researcher reflexivity when integrating AI-assisted approaches. As the use of AI expands in health education and behavior research, understanding its limitations is essential for ensuring that culturally grounded, meaning-rich insights remain at the center of qualitative analysis.

items.title: Advancing clinician-patient communication in academic hospitals: Insights from a multisite rapid qualitative analysis.
items.abstract: High-quality clinician-patient communication is associated with improved patient understanding, trust, and healthcare outcomes. However, the hospital environment poses unique challenges to effective communication, and research documents that many hospitalized patients report poor communication with clinicians. Characterize current efforts and barriers to improving clinician-patient communication across hospital medicine. We conducted a multi-methods study using virtual focus groups with an online survey. Focus groups were held with hospital medicine clinicians and members of the Hospital Medicine ReEngineering Network (HOMERuN) Patient and Family Advisory Council (PFAC). We analyzed focus groups using rapid qualitative analysis. Across 8 total focus groups, 37 clinicians and 4 PFAC members participated. We received 26 survey responses (63% response rate); the majority (19, 73%) reported their institution had initiatives in place to improve clinician-patient communication. Our qualitative analysis revealed four primary themes: (1) hospital medicine communication initiatives vary widely in approaches and objectives; (2) trainees are taught foundational communication skills through formal and informal mechanisms, but these efforts may be siloed from other initiatives; (3) hospital medicine clinicians perceive multiple barriers to improving individual communication behaviors; and (4) systems-level factors make it challenging to effectively develop, evaluate, and sustain communication initiatives. Hospital medicine groups are actively engaged in diverse communication initiatives, but these efforts are undermined by fragmentation, inadequate feedback mechanisms, and competing priorities. Our findings highlight a need for coordinated strategies that align communication projects with real-world clinical workflows, provide clinicians with actionable feedback, and incorporate genuine partnership with patients and caregivers.

items.title: Educational Interventions for Perinatal Depression Management Among Non-Specialist Providers in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Descriptive Systematic Review of Limited Evidence.
items.abstract: This descriptive systematic review synthesizes evidence from resource-constrained primary and non-specialist care settings on the structural components of educational interventions for frontline health care workers regarding perinatal depression (PND). A comprehensive search was conducted across CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Scopus for experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between January 1, 2019, and August 31, 2025, in Resource-Constrained Settings. Three quasi-experimental, non-randomized studies met the pre-specified inclusion criteria, representing a total of 351 participants across Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Thailand. Quality appraisal conducted via the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions, Version 2 (ROBINS-I V2) tool judged all 3 studies to be at an overall critical risk of bias. A descriptive narrative synthesis was conducted in accordance with the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines, as high clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded a statistical meta-analysis. Preliminary patterns across the included studies suggest that educational models in these settings commonly feature standardized reference frameworks such as the World Health Organization (WHO) Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) and structured active learning approaches. Multi-session delivery formats, cascade (train-the-trainer) models, and practical clinical phases accompanied by remote mobile supervision were reported alongside improvements in immediate provider-level metrics. The extremely narrow evidence base, high attrition rates, lack of comparative control groups, and complete absence of patient outcomes severely constrain the ability to draw definitive conclusions regarding intervention effectiveness or causal mechanisms. The findings are presented as hypothesis-generating, emphasizing the critical need for methodologically rigorous trials in global maternal mental health.

items.title: Oral Antihyperglycemic Agents Versus Insulin for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Societal Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of the SUGAR-DIP Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: To assess the cost-effectiveness of treatment with sequential oral antihyperglycemic agents (OHA; metformin and glibenclamide) versus insulin for gestational diabetes (GDM). Cost-effectiveness analysis from a societal and healthcare perspective alongside a randomized controlled trial (SUGAR-DIP). Twenty-five hospitals in the Netherlands. Women with GDM and a singleton pregnancy, randomized to OHA (n = 409) or insulin (n = 411) between 16 to 34 weeks' gestation. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Differences in costs and effects were estimated using bivariate regression with bootstrapping to derive incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves were constructed across a range of willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds. Large for gestational age (LGA), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), costs and cost-effectiveness. OHA slightly increased QALYs (0.009; 95% CI 0.004 to 0.014), corresponding to approximately 3 days in perfect health. There were no statistically significant differences in LGA avoided (-0.039; 95% CI-0.097 to 0.018) or societal costs (mean difference-€1004; 95% CI-€3503 to €1495). OHA were less costly and less effective than insulin for LGA, whereas for QALYs they were less costly and more effective. The probability of OHA being cost-effective at a WTP threshold of €0 was 79% for both outcomes. OHA have a high probability of being cost-effective compared with insulin for QALYs, although the QALY gain is small and of limited clinical relevance. For LGA, OHA were less costly but less effective, and cost-effectiveness depends on acceptable trade-offs between costs and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: Univariate Health-Related Inequality Aversion in Sweden: Evidence of Nonconstant Aversion and Support for Prioritizing the Worse Off.
items.abstract: To test whether the assumption of constant health-related inequality aversion holds for Atkinson and Kolm-Pollak social welfare functions (SWFs) and to assess whether there is public support in Sweden for prioritizing the worse off when allocating health care resources. In an online survey experiment, respondents (n = 1,654) completed two task sets in which they chose between interventions benefiting better-off and worse-off groups to different extents. To test for constant inequality aversion, we checked whether the inequality-aversion parameter from the second task set was one of the parameters closest to that elicited from the first set. A majority displayed nonconstant inequality aversion (71.4% for Atkinson, 72.3% for Kolm-Pollak). However, the design may not fully isolate inequality aversion from age preferences and cannot rule out learning effects. Among the valid responses (n = 1,029), 50.4% valued health gains to worse off higher, but only up to a point; 19.4% were unwilling to help the better off before nothing more could be done for the worse off; 14.4% preferred a more egalitarian system; 10.8% were unwilling to sacrifice total health gains to benefit one group more than the other; and 4.8% were willing to sacrifice total health to benefit the better off more than the worse off. If our findings were not confounded by age preferences or learning effects, the Atkinson and Kolm-Pollak SWFs would not seem to reflect the sample's preferences for prioritizing the worse off. Most respondents traded efficiency for equity in ways largely consistent with Swedish health care priority setting.

items.title: Bioengineered Stroma-Camouflaged Nanovesicles Disrupt the IDO1/CD276 Immunosuppressive Circuit to Reinvigorate Antitumor Immunity.
items.abstract: The cooperative upregulation of IDO1 and the immune checkpoint CD276 in solid tumors establishes a dual immunosuppressive circuit that depletes tryptophan, accumulates kynurenines, and silences T-cells. We engineered fibroblast-mimetic nanovesicles (AM@UIO-BMS/DOX) that uniquely integrate stromal-camouflaged tumor accumulation, CD276 checkpoint blockade, and co-delivery of doxorubicin with the clinical IDO1 inhibitor BMS-986205. The fibroblast-derived membrane coating promotes accumulation in fibroblast-rich tumor regions, while surface-anchored anti-CD276 scFv enables precision tumor specific targeting and concurrent checkpoint neutralization. Within the tumor microenvironment, doxorubicin elicits immunogenic cell death, and BMS-986205 metabolically recalibrates the tryptophan-kynurenine equilibrium, relieving the metabolic suppression that otherwise blunts T-cell priming. In syngeneic tumor models, this bioengineered platform profoundly remodeled the immune microenvironment, as evidenced by a tripartite shift: enhanced dendritic cell maturation and cross-presentation, expansion of Granzyme B+ cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes, and selective depletion of CD25+FoxP3+ regulatory T cells. This concerted action effectively converted immunologically "cold" tumors into an inflamed phenotype, overcoming intrinsic chemoresistance and adaptive immune evasion. Collectively, our findings establish that bioengineered stroma-camouflaged nanovesicles disrupt the dual IDO1/CD276 immunosuppressive circuit, enhancing antitumor immunity and offering a promising strategy to surmount chemo-immunotherapy resistance in advanced solid tumors.

items.title: Genome-wide analysis identifies pleiotropic genes shared between severe mental disorders and biomarkers of cellular aging.
items.abstract: Severe mental disorders such as bipolar disorder (BD), major depressive disorder (MDD) and schizophrenia (SZ) are characterized by reduced life expectancy, premature mortality and alterations of aging biomarkers, leading to hypothesize that they might be associated with accelerated cellular aging. We quantified the genetic overlap between severe mental disorders and a comprehensive set of aging biomarkers including multivariate longevity and healthy aging (mvAge), brain age gap (BAG), leucocyte telomere length (gLTL), mitochondrial DNA copy number and epigenetic age acceleration (gEAA) using cutting-edge methods, and evaluated their functional enrichment and suitability as drug targets. All disorders were negatively correlated with mvAge. Further, MDD correlated negatively with gLTL and positively with gEAA. We identified several pleiotropic variants, with nine genes (AC068490.2, ASIC2, CNNM2, FURIN, GPM6A, HS6ST3, RP5-1043L13.1, SORCS3 and SP4) containing variants shared between aging biomarkers and all disorders. Functional analyses with summary-data-based Mendelian randomization showed that increased expression of the druggable gene CRHR1 in the prefrontal cortex was associated with increased risk of MDD and BAG measures. Our findings suggest that shared heritability might contribute to reduced longevity and healthy aging in severe mental disorders and identify pleiotropic genes involved in synaptic function and metabolic processes related to micronutrients such as folate and magnesium.

items.title: Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir Failure in Hepatitis C Subtype 6f: A Paired Virological Analysis Before and After Therapy.
items.abstract: Pangenotypic direct-acting antivirals are presumed globally effective, but subtypes endemic to low- and middle-income countries are underrepresented in the trials and replicon systems that define resistance. In a Thai elimination program, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) failures were concentrated in HCV subtype 6f. We investigated whether this reflects acquired resistance. Within a province-wide SOF/VEL test-to-treat program, 124 treatment failures were referred for genotyping with the genotype unknown at referral. NS5A and NS5B were deep sequenced in paired pre-treatment and failure specimens from 29 patients infected with subtype 6f, giving codon-level amino acid composition at both time points. Subtype-specific failure burden was compared with the province's viremic subtype prevalence. Subtype 6f comprised 81.4% of genotyped failures but 34.4% of provincial viremic infections (odds ratio 8.4; 95% CI 5.0-14.1). Across the 29 patients, six of the seven NS5A drug-target positions were immobile, and six carried the reference residue; 27/29 patients carried NS5A-58 proline. Movement was confined almost entirely to NS5A-93, was bidirectional, and left the summed per-patient resistance burden unchanged (p = 0.47). Acquired NS5B S282T was excluded at a median detection limit of 0.06%, low enough to detect a 1% subpopulation in every specimen. The cohort differed from the reference genome at 12 of 1042 codons, and nucleotide diversity contracted under purifying selection without convergent substitutions. Subtype 6f fails SOF/VEL against a drug-target landscape of ordinary lineage sequence, present before treatment and unchanged after it. Sofosbuvir-based retreatment therefore remains appropriate, and a post-failure resistance report cannot distinguish virological from non-virological failure.

items.title: A Malaysian Expert Consensus on The Identification, Evaluation, and Pharmacological Management of Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy.
items.abstract: Diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy (DSPN), the most common form of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), is a chronic complication of diabetes associated with sensory loss, foot ulceration, lower-limb amputation, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality. Despite its substantial clinical burden, DSPN remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in Malaysia. This consensus aimed to develop practical, evidence-informed recommendations for screening, diagnosis, and management of painful and non-painful presentations of DSPN tailored to the Malaysian healthcare setting. An expert panel comprising 11 endocrinologists from public and private healthcare institutions in Malaysia was convened. Draft recommendations were adapted from international and local guidelines for Malaysian clinical practice. Consensus development involved pre-meeting review and anonymous voting, followed by structured face-to-face discussion. Consensus was defined as ≥80% agreement. The panel finalized 61 consensus statements covering screening, diagnosis, sensory examination, and treatment. Recommendations emphasize annual screening for all individuals with diabetes and clinical examination to detect sensory deficits, including in individuals without painful symptoms. Assessment should include multiple bedside tests to evaluate small- and large-fiber function and loss of protective sensation. Recommended tests include the 10-g monofilament, vibration and pin-prick testing, and the Ipswich Touch Test, particularly in resource-limited settings. Assessment of painful and non-painful symptoms should complement rather than replace objective examination. Validated screening questionnaires, including the Malay-language PainDETECT may support assessment. Management includes optimization of glycemic control, lifestyle interventions, adjunctive pathogenetically oriented therapies such as alpha-lipoic acid, and evidence-based pharmacological treatments including pregabalin, gabapentin, duloxetine, and tricyclic antidepressants. Routine opioid use is discouraged. This Malaysian expert consensus provides practical, context-specific recommendations for early detection, diagnosis, and management of DSPN. By adapting international guidance to local healthcare realities, these recommendations aim to improve care consistency, reduce DSPN-related complications, and enhance patient outcomes in Malaysia.

items.title: Impact of Semaglutide Introduction on the Use of Concomitant Medications: An Interrupted Time Series.
items.abstract: To evaluate the impact of semaglutide initiation for weight management on the use of concomitant medications commonly prescribed for obesity-related comorbidities. We conducted a nationwide interrupted time series study using data from Danish registers, including adults initiating semaglutide for weight management between 12/2022 and 12/2024. Monthly prescriptions for 10 medication classes were analysed in the 24 months before and 12 months after initiation. Effects at 12 months were expressed as rate ratios (RRs) comparing observed values with expected values based on pre-initiation trends. Among 189 392 semaglutide initiators (68% women; median age 50 years), prescription volumes at 12 months declined and were lower than projected from pre-initiation trends for antiasthmatics (RR: 0.82, 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.86), topical corticosteroids (0.91, 0.87-0.96), antipsoriatics (0.91, 0.83-1.00), analgesics (0.93, 0.90-0.96), antidepressants (0.93, 0.89-0.98) and topical antifungal formulations (0.92, 0.86-0.99). Antihypertensive prescriptions continued to rise after semaglutide initiation, but more slowly than projected (0.92, 0.89-0.95). Glucose-lowering medications declined (0.87, 0.82-0.92), mainly non-insulin agents, but a similar reduction was observed in the negative control cohort. Anxiolytic use increased (1.16, 1.08-1.24) and remained elevated at 2 years. Changes in lipid-modifying agents and medications for gastric acid disorders were small or transient. Semaglutide initiation for weight management was associated with reduced use of several concomitant medications for obesity-related comorbidities, while anxiolytic use increased. Changes in other therapeutic classes were limited. These findings suggest that semaglutide treatment may influence overall medication use and support continued monitoring of prescribing patterns during therapy.

items.title: Association of CT-Derived Skeletal Muscle Radiodensity and Index With Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: A Community-Based Study.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle composition is linked to metabolic health, but its association with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) remains unclear. We examined associations of CT-derived skeletal muscle radiodensity (SMD) and skeletal muscle index (SMI) with CSVD. This cross-sectional analysis included 2395 adults from the PRECISE study. SMD and SMI were measured on abdominal CT at L3. CSVD was assessed using Wardlaw and Rothwell scores. Individual MRI markers included lacunes, white matter hyperintensities, basal ganglia enlarged perivascular spaces (BG-EPVS) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs). Logistic and ordinal logistic regression models were used, with additional covariate adjustment examined in sensitivity analyses. False discovery rate correction was applied to marker-specific analyses. The mean age was 60.9 ± 6.6 years (56.8% women). In primary multivariable analyses, each 1-SD decrement in SMD was associated with CSVD presence (Wardlaw: OR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.03-1.31; Rothwell: OR: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.00-1.25) and burden (total: cOR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.33; modified total: cOR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.03-1.27). With broader covariate adjustment, most of these associations were attenuated, with only Wardlaw total burden remaining statistically significant. The SMD-BG-EPVS association was similarly attenuated. Lower SMI was associated with CMB presence and burden, whereas no consistent association with overall CSVD was observed across models. Lower SMD was associated with overall CSVD in primary analyses, but most associations were attenuated after broader adjustment. Lower SMI was consistently associated with CMBs, whereas its association with overall CSVD was less consistent across models.

items.title: Preventive Effect of Smoking Cessation on Diabetes Onset: A Target Trial Emulation Approach.
items.abstract: Smoking cessation may transiently increase diabetes risk through weight gain, but its temporal trajectory remains unclear. We evaluated the long-term effect of smoking cessation on incident diabetes. We conducted a target trial emulation using a sequential-cohort design with repeated annual enrollment. Using annual health checkup data of Japanese employees from 2008 to 2022, we newly enrolled, at each annual assessment, and started follow-up individuals aged 40 years or older who were currently smoking and free of diabetes. Inverse probability weighting was used to adjust for baseline confounding in every sequential cohort. We estimated cumulative risks for quit-smoking and persistent-smoking groups, and their differences and ratios. From 52 880 unique participants, a total of 331 701 participants were followed-up in the sequential cohorts, with a mean (standard deviation) age of 49.1 (5.7) years, and 25 749 developed diabetes. The risk ratio (95% confidence interval) for diabetes in the quit-smoking group relative to the persistent-smoking group was 1.15 (1.07-1.24) at 3 years and 0.95 (0.85-1.06) at 15 years. Per-protocol analyses showed a similar pattern. Smoking cessation was associated with a short-term increase in diabetes risk, but this excess risk diminished over time, and no long-term increase in risk was observed. These findings support sustained smoking cessation as metabolically beneficial in the long term.

items.title: Diagnosed Dental Diseases, Tooth Loss and the Risk of Primary Liver Cancer in a Nationwide Swedish Cohort.
items.abstract: Poor dental health has been shown to increase the risk of several types of cancer, but its association with primary liver cancer (PLC) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between dental diseases, tooth loss and the risk of PLC. We conducted a large population-based retrospective cohort study including 5,893,325 adults registered in the Swedish Dental Health Register between 2009 and 2016. Participants were linked to multiple Swedish national registers to ascertain incident PLC cases. Cox regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association between dental diseases, tooth loss and the risk of PLC, using attained age as the timescale and adjusting for potential confounders. Additionally, in a sibling comparison analysis we controlled for shared genetic and early-life environmental factors. During a mean follow-up of 6.36 years, 2374 PLC cases were identified through linkage with the Cancer Register: 1856 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and 518 non-HCC PLC cases. Both caries (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.02-1.30) and periodontitis (HR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.12-1.39) were associated with an increased risk of PLC. Further, a clear dose-response relationship was observed between fewer remaining teeth and PLC risk, with HRs ranging from 1.15 to 1.84 (p 27 remaining teeth. Subtype-specific analyses showed that caries was associated with non-HCC PLC, whereas periodontitis was associated with HCC. Tooth loss was more strongly associated with HCC than with non-HCC PLC. The overall findings were generally consistent across sibling-controlled, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. Our large population-based cohort study suggests that caries, periodontitis and tooth loss are associated with an elevated risk of PLC, with distinct patterns of association observed for HCC and non-HCC PLC.

items.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of HIV-1 subtype B transmission networks in Uruguay.
items.abstract: To reconstruct the evolutionary and demographic history of HIV-1 subtype B in Uruguay and characterize the establishment, persistence, and regional connectivity of its major transmission lineages. Nationwide molecular epidemiological and phylodynamic study of 491 HIV-1 subtype B pol sequences derived from routine resistance genotyping in Uruguay between 2007 and 2021. Maximum-likelihood and Bayesian phylogenetic approaches were used to classify pandemic and Caribbean subtype B lineages, identify viral introductions and local transmission clusters, estimate their times of emergence, reconstruct the demographic dynamics of major Uruguayan lineages, and assess their regional origins and transmission tempo. Pandemic subtype B accounted for 96.3% of sequences. We identified 229 independent introductions, of which only 52 (22.7%) generated detectable local transmission clusters, revealing marked heterogeneity in lineage establishment. The two largest country-specific lineages, BPAN-UY-I (n = 37) and BPAN-UY-II (n = 30), emerged independently in the mid-to-late 1980s and underwent sustained expansion until approximately 2010, followed by stabilization and recent declines in effective reproductive number. The median estimated maximum interval between successive infections was 25.4 months, with 49.3% of intervals 5 years. Among South American lineages with inferred regional ancestry, Brazil was the predominant source of both clustered and sporadic introductions. HIV-1 subtype B in Uruguay represents a mature, highly compartmentalized epidemic shaped by recurrent viral introductions but sustained predominantly by a small number of early-established founder lineages. These findings highlight the enduring effects of historical contingency, transmission-network structure, and regional connectivity on contemporary HIV epidemic dynamics.

items.title: miR-138-5p: From Multidimensional Tumor-Suppressive Regulatory Networks to Nanocarrier-Based Delivery for Solid Tumor Therapy.
items.abstract: MicroRNA-138-5p (miR-138-5p) has been reported to exert tumor-suppressive effects in several solid tumors, and its downregulation has been associated with malignant progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. This review summarizes research trends and current evidence on the molecular functions, regulatory networks, and therapeutic potential of miR-138-5p in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulation and nanocarrier-based delivery strategies. Bibliometric analysis and CiteSpace visualization were conducted using English-language original articles and reviews retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2014 to October 2025. Relevant literature was reviewed to examine miR-138-5p expression, biological functions, target genes, signaling pathways, ceRNA networks, and therapeutic strategies. Studies focused exclusively on hematological malignancies were excluded. Bibliometric mapping identified research clusters spanning multiple solid tumor types, cell-cycle regulation, and proliferation, while metabolic reprogramming and therapeutic resistance emerged as relevant research themes. Mechanistic studies suggest that miR-138-5p regulates proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, autophagy, immune-related signaling, and chemosensitivity through diverse targets and pathways. Long non-coding RNA- and circular RNA-mediated ceRNA networks have been proposed as an additional regulatory layer, although their physiological relevance requires further quantitative validation. Preclinical findings, including exosome-mediated delivery of miR-138-5p, suggest potential for replacement therapy; however, challenges involving delivery efficiency, tumor specificity, biosafety, pharmacokinetics, and manufacturing standardization remain. miR-138-5p is a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in solid tumors. Further validation of its context-dependent mechanisms and optimization of targeted delivery strategies are needed to support clinical translation.

items.title: Exploratory donor-aware analysis of developmental transcriptomic trajectories in 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids.
items.abstract: This descriptive, hypothesis-generating study examined whether 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids show developmental transcriptomic differences overlapping retinoic acid (RA)-related gene-expression programs. Signatures derived from early RA exposure and prolonged, 7-day all-trans RA (ATRA) treatment were evaluated in public cortical organoid data from three deletion and 17 control donors. Donors, rather than individual samples, were the units of inference; 16 controls and all three deletion donors had sufficient time points for slope testing. Early human, early mouse, and conserved early RA signatures were not significant. A broad ATRA-derived differentiation score showed a negative deletion-control slope difference (exact P = 0.0083; false-discovery rate = 0.0206), but a non-RA maturation score was also significant. The prolonged score correlated strongly with maturity. Sensitivity analyses adjusting for measured maturation and composition did not identify an RA-specific component; neither the targeted RA program nor the covariate-adjusted joint trajectory test was significant. External and single-cell analyses provided biological context, not independent validation. The findings suggest a developmental/maturation-associated trajectory difference overlapping a broad prolonged ATRA-associated program. The three-donor case group and heterogeneous source models limit stability and generalizability; the results do not establish altered RA signaling, vitamin A deficiency, or retinoid-treatment relevance.

items.title: Disulfiram attenuates paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis accompanied by changes in Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression.
items.abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is a highly toxic herbicide that induces renal injury through oxidative stress and progressive fibrosis, contributing to chronic kidney disease. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy for accelerating therapeutic development. This study evaluated the nephroprotective potential of disulfiram (DSF), a clinically approved drug with emerging antioxidant and antifibrotic properties, against PQ-induced renal injury, including its association with changes in the expression of the Smad3 and Smad7 genes. Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to seven groups: Control, Vehicle, DSF20, PQ (1.5 mg/kg), and PQ co-treated with DSF (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg). Renal injury was evaluated using histopathology (H&E, PAS, and Masson's trichrome staining), α-SMA, serum biomarkers (BUN, creatinine, and uric acid), oxidative stress parameters (malondialdehyde [MDA], catalase [CAT], and glutathione peroxidase [GPx]), and Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression determined by qRT-PCR. PQ exposure caused marked renal histopathological injury, increased α-SMA, increased oxidative stress, impaired renal function, and elevated fibrosis, accompanied by increased Smad3 and decreased Smad7 gene expression. DSF co-treatment, particularly at 10 mg/kg, significantly ameliorated these changes by reducing tissue injury, decreasing α-SMA-positive area% and collagen deposition, restoring antioxidant enzyme activity, lowering lipid peroxidation, improving renal function, and altering Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression toward PQ levels. Disulfiram at an optimal dose of 10 mg/kg significantly attenuated PQ-induced renal injury and fibrosis, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and altered Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression. These findings support the potential of DSF as a repurposed therapeutic candidate for mitigating paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis. Further studies evaluating protein-level changes and activation of the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway are warranted to clarify the underlying molecular mechanisms.

items.title: Service preservation from matching non-matching socks under stochastic loss
items.abstract: Abstract Socks are produced and replaced at a massive scale, yet their paired use makes them unusually vulnerable to service loss, as the disappearance of a single sock can leave usable wear-capacity stranded and create sockless days even when functional socks remain available. In this study, we examine whether pairing non-matching “orphan” socks can preserve daily sock service under stochastic loss, and how this benefit trades off against perceived social discomfort. We formalize sock ownership as a sequential decision problem under uncertainty in which socks wear out and disappear stochastically during laundering, while public exposure induces a person-specific mismatch penalty. We conducted an in-person study to estimate mismatch sensitivity and diversity preference, linking behavioral heterogeneity to interpretable mixing policies. Using these results, an exact benchmark on small tractable instances, and a simulation-based evaluation of pairing policies, we show that strict matching can appear resource-frugal largely because it generates many sockless days. In contrast, controlled tolerance for mismatch sustains service and reduces stranded wear-capacity across loss regimes. The ecological-cost term is treated as a proportional embodied-cost proxy rather than an independent life-cycle assessment measure, so the environmental interpretation is suggestive and mechanism-based rather than a direct estimate of environmental savings. This study establishes the feasibility and limitations of matching non-matching socks as a simple strategy for preserving service from already-owned garments.

items.title: “We just don’t know why”: students’ epistemic risk taking in the social construction of an explanation of plate tectonics
items.abstract: Abstract Epistemic risk is inherent in the practice of science and can be intimidating for students in classrooms building their science skills. We argue here that science learning must be designed to scaffold epistemic risk that supports students in social knowledge construction. Through the case study of a group of four middle school students and their class working to explain the relationship between earthquakes and volcanoes in relation to the larger theory of plate tectonics, we illustrate students’ engagement in epistemic practices and the scaffolds that enabled them to fully participate in these practices. Our analysis suggests that scaffolding in participant structures, more knowledgeable others, and organizational tools supported students in fully engaging in the epistemic practices of science. Though epistemic risk taking is critical to students’ engagement in epistemic practices, there is a need to attend to the interpersonal and socioemotional influences on students’ epistemic agency, attending to students’ sense of belonging, connectedness, and safety. We advocate for the intentional design of epistemic tools that purposefully include supports for students to navigate epistemic risk.

items.title: Affordance-based designed stools invite dynamic sitting for children: a classroom study
items.abstract: Abstract Children spend much of their day sitting in classrooms, often in prolonged static postures. Sedentary behavior is associated with health risks. This study investigates whether stools designed to afford more dynamic sitting, promote greater postural variety and more frequent posture transitions compared to regular school chairs. We observed the sitting behaviors of 34 children aged 6 to 8 years at the beginning and end of a two-week classroom intervention. Results showed that the stools significantly increased posture diversity and the frequency of posture transitions. The initial effects sustained over time, underlining that the stools facilitated more than a novelty effect as children continued to engage with the affordances provided. Additionally, we observed that the stools encouraged sitting in unconventional postures rarely seen with regular chairs, further supporting their role in promoting posture diversity. These findings highlight the potential of affordance-based designs in classroom environments to foster healthier sitting behaviors.

items.title: 心灵的分岔:从无意识到可观察——心理学流派的六次划线 / The Forking Mind: Six Ways Psychology Drew Its Lines
items.abstract: 中文. 本著作是同一作者"六个核心"系列的第一本科普专著:用六个提问,重读心理学一百五十年的流派史。 核心主张:心理学流派史不是一部"谁取代谁"的进步史,也不是一部"谁都被冤枉"的平反史,而是一部"谁在哪里划线、又把什么划到外面、最后由谁付账"的账本史。每个流派都是一次尝试:先划一条线,再决定记住什么、用什么钟、保哪两项、请谁定价、在哪里设门槛;六核问的是"它在哪一步让出了什么",不是"它对不对"。 结构与证据:6 部分、25 章、附录 A—Q、309 页、25 幅矢量插图、68 个表、约 26 万字。第一部分(1—4)划线的诞生:柏拉图—康德、冯特、布伦塔诺、詹姆斯、构造/机能、格式塔;第二部分(5—11)深度的代价:弗洛伊德、荣格、阿德勒、客体关系、自体/依恋、拉康、神经精神分析、心理测量;第三部分(12—15)可观察的约束:华生、巴甫洛夫、斯金纳、行为疗法、行为主义的遗产;第四部分(16—19)内部的回归:认知革命、皮亚杰/乔姆斯基、认知神经科学、社会认知;第五部分(20—22)意义与时间:人本主义、存在主义、发展心理学;第六部分(23—25)系统与定价:系统/后现代、CBT/正念/积极/文化/进化、六核回望。每章以一个人物或争议开场,以一个核心主提问展开,以一句"它让出了什么"收束。 诚实的纪律:所有结论标注 A/B/C 证据等级(A 可查证/可复算,B 稳定但有争议,C 思辨/开放),结论强度不超过证据强度;有争议的实验(小艾伯特、斯坦福监狱、米尔格拉姆)同时给出原始报告与后来的方法学批评;对人物的临床推测一律标 C。附录 F 是可证伪登记簿(20 条主张,逐条给出"什么会推翻它""怎么查""当前状态");附录 G 是数据缺口与四条边界。 边界:本书不提供临床建议,不裁判疗效;"讲述"这一核心不做"揭穿",只做"定价审计";六核不能替代领域知识,也处理不了权力与制度的全部。它明确让出了临床细节、非西方传统、定量证据与制度史,并在附录 G 逐条列出。 版本:2026-10-25,309 页,25 章,25 图,68 表,附录 A—Q;源码与可复现脚本开源,内容 CC BY 4.0,代码 MIT。 本版说明(2026-10-25)。初版。正文采用四层装置(正文/多想一层/再想一层/给专家的注/动手试试);目录为部分—章—节—子节四级;每章附"案例"与"反例"两个子节,用来防止"让出"变成事后编造。附录 A—Q 依次为:流派×六核对照表、一百五十年时间线、术语表、一百个人名、被埋没与重新发现清单、可证伪登记簿、数据缺口、延伸阅读与主题索引、分支地图、精神病理学的另一条线、被主流漏掉的传统、中国心理学一百年、二十种疗法对照、心理学与 AI、十二个常见误解与练习册、十个实验/十次复现/方法手册、二十对易混概念。 系列 / Series. 同一作者的独立研究系列:九本书(六本学术专著 + 两本通俗读本 + 本书)与九篇论文。入口与外部登记库:https://github.com/lyp0746/knowledge-tradeoffs;源码与可复现脚本:https://github.com/lyp0746/mind-forks。首选预览文件:mind-forks-print.pdf(印刷版)。 English. Abstract (English). This is the first popular-science monograph in the author's six-core series: six questions reread 150 years of psychology. Core thesis: the history of psychological schools is neither a chronicle of replacement nor a rehabilitation of the wronged, but a ledger of who drew which line, what was left outside it, and who paid. Every school is an attempt that first draws a line and then decides what to remember, which clock to use, which two of completeness, composability and transfer to keep, who may set the price, and where to put the threshold; the six cores ask what it gave up, not whether it was right. Structure and evidence: 6 parts, 25 chapters, appendices A–Q, 309 pages, 25 vector figures, 68 tables, about 260,000 Chinese characters. Part I (1–4) the birth of the line: Plato to Kant, Wundt, Brentano, James, structuralism/functionalism, Gestalt; Part II (5–11) the price of depth: Freud, Jung, Adler, object relations, self/attachment, Lacan, neuropsychoanalysis, psychometrics; Part III (12–15) the observable constraint: Watson, Pavlov, Skinner, behaviour therapy, the behaviourist legacy; Part IV (16–19) the return of the interior: cognitive revolution, Piaget/Chomsky, cognitive neuroscience, social cognition; Part V (20–22) meaning and time: humanistic, existential, developmental; Part VI (23–25) systems and pricing: systemic/postmodern, CBT/mindfulness/positive/cultural/evolutionary, and a six-core retrospect. Each chapter opens with a person or a controversy, develops one core question, and closes with one sentence on what the school gave up. Discipline: every claim carries an A/B/C grade (A verifiable/recomputable, B stable but contested, C speculative/open) and no conclusion is stronger than its evidence; contested experiments (Little Albert, Stanford Prison, Milgram) are presented with both the original report and later methodological criticism; clinical conjectures about persons are graded C. Appendix F is a falsifiability ledger (20 claims, each with what would refute it, how to check, and current status); Appendix G lists data gaps and four boundaries. Boundaries: the book offers no clinical advice and does not adjudicate efficacy; the "telling" core audits pricing rather than debunking; the six cores do not replace domain knowledge and cannot handle all questions of power and institutions. It explicitly gives up clinical detail, non-Western traditions, systematic quantitative evidence and institutional history, as listed in Appendix G. Edition: 2026-10-25, 309 pages, 25 chapters, 25 figures, 68 tables, appendices A–Q; source and reproducible scripts open, content CC BY 4.0, code MIT. What this edition is (2026-10-25). First edition. The text uses four reader levels (main text / one layer deeper / one more / expert note / hands-on) and a four-level table of contents (part–chapter–section–subsection). Each chapter adds a "case" and a "counterexample" subsection so that "what it gave up" cannot become a post-hoc story. Appendices A–Q are, in order: a school-by-core table, a 150-year timeline, a glossary, one hundred names, a register of buried-and-recovered ideas, a falsifiability ledger, data gaps, further reading with a thematic index, a map of subfields, a second line in psychopathology, marginalized traditions, a century of Chinese psychology, twenty therapies compared, psychology and AI, twelve misconceptions and a workbook, ten experiments / ten replications / a methods handbook, and twenty confusable concept pairs.

items.title: In What Contexts Do Supporters Provide Positive and Negative Responses to Victims of Nonconsensual Intimate Image Abuse?
items.abstract: Nonconsensual intimate image distribution (NCII) occurs when a person's intimate images or videos are shared or shown to others without their consent. Although NCII victimization is common among young adults and many victims disclose their experiences to others, there is a dearth of research examining the reactions victims receive when they disclose or the factors that might contribute to these reactions. Informed by the broader intimate partner and sexual violence literature, the present study examines supporter, victim, and relational factors that might contribute to social reactions to NCII disclosure. Based on attribution theory and victimization perspective theory, we also hypothesize that these supporter, victim, and relational factors may have primarily indirect effects on social reactions through victim empathy, victim blame, and perceptions of confusion and ineffectiveness in helping. Among a sample of 726 undergraduate students who reported receiving disclosures of NCII, positive and negative social reactions were bivariately associated with several supporter, victim/victimization, and relational factors. Consistent with attribution theory and victimization perspective theories, empathy, victim blame, and feelings of confusion/ineffectiveness about helping mediated associations between a range of victim, supporter, and relational characteristics and social reactions to disclosure. Efforts to modify these perceptions of victims and reduce confusion and ineffectiveness in how to respond to survivors could improve disclosure experiences for NCII survivors.

items.title: Why consumers favour or resist foreign brands: A systematic review of antecedents, mechanisms and moderators
items.abstract: Consumers’ orientations towards foreign brands have been studied through separate constructs, including ethnocentrism, xenocentrism, cosmopolitanism, affinity, animosity and country of origin image, yet no review integrates them around purchase intention as a common outcome. This study presents a systematic literature review of 52 peer reviewed studies published between 2012 and 2026, following PRISMA 2020 and supplemented by umbrella review guidance for the meta analyses and reviews included. Predisposition towards foreign brands (PTFB) is used as an organising label and not as an established construct, and the evidence is structured into an Antecedents Mechanisms Moderators (AMM) framework. Antecedents form three clusters: outgroup oriented dispositions (xenocentrism, cosmopolitanism, affinity), ingroup protective dispositions (ethnocentrism and animosity, with patriotism and nationalism acting as distal drivers through ethnocentrism) and image based perceptions (cognitive and affective country image). Brand attitude, perceived quality and value, and consumer disidentification emerge as the main mediating mechanisms. Product category and involvement, national culture, economic development gaps and demographics are the most consistent moderators. The evidence base is largely cross-sectional, and important gaps remain in digital purchasing contexts, longitudinal and experimental designs, xenocentrism in African and Middle Eastern markets, and links with sustainable consumption. The framework offers researchers a basis for theory testing and gives global brand managers guidance on segmentation, localisation and country image positioning.

items.title: Building environmental engagement: Can bridging social-ecological and learning systems theories be a lever for change?
items.abstract: Abstract Pressing sustainability issues are rooted in human and earth systems interactions that are difficult to address because of their complex, dynamic, and unpredictable nature. Addressing these social-ecological challenges requires systems-level change, which relies on both direct improvements to natural systems and indirect drivers of change, such as educational levers. We aim to provoke more transdisciplinary work between environmental scientists and educators by bringing together key constructs from social-ecological and learning systems theories. Writing from the perspective of educators and social scientists, our objectives are to encourage ecologists and other environmental scientists to (1) recognize that learning systems are essential elements of social-ecological ecosystems and (2) embrace their role as keystones within these learning systems, uniquely positioned to drive interest in the environment and support transformative learning. We suggest potential areas of intersection between social-ecological and learning systems, seeking leverage points for transformative change toward more sustainable communities.

items.title: 自由意志的本体论重构:基于相继耦合原理的二阶自返调控解释
items.abstract: 传统哲学中自由意志与决定论的长期对立,根植于心物二元的实体本体论预设:要么将自由意志设定为独立于因果链的精神实体,要么将其消解为物理因果的副现象,二者始终无法在一元本体论框架内实现自洽统一。后世相容论多停留在语义层面的概念调和,始终未能从本体论层面说明自主选择的存在形态与相对独立性来源。 本文以“认知的本质是前后相继”这一不可证伪的第一原理为逻辑起点,依托存在几何化体系的相继耦合本体论框架,从一阶客观耦合、二阶自返耦合的层级生成规则出发,线性推导出自由意志的本体论本质、运作机制与存在边界。本文证明:自由意志并非独立的精神实体,也非对因果律的突破,而是高阶闭合射线簇演化出的二阶自返调控功能;它以模拟预判、定向选择、偏差修正为核心运作方式,天然具备可错性,其核心价值在于通过纠正认知偏差、实现逻辑序列与本真因果序列的1:1对齐,服务于个体稳态的存续与优化。自由意志具备相对的自主调控空间,但不具备脱离相继因果的绝对自由,其本质是高阶稳态对自身因果链条的自觉校准权。这一界定从根源消解了传统自由意志争论的二元困境,为认知科学、心理学、伦理学等领域提供了统一的本体论基础。 The long-standing opposition between free will and determinism in traditional philosophy is rooted in the substance-ontological presupposition of mind-body dualism: either free will is posited as a spiritual entity independent of the causal chain, or it is reduced to an epiphenomenon of physical causation. Neither approach can achieve self-consistent unity within a monistic ontological framework. Later compatibilist theories mostly remain at the level of semantic conceptual reconciliation, failing to account for the existential form and relative independence of autonomous choice at the ontological level. Taking the unfalsifiable first principle that "the nature of cognition is sequential succession" as its logical starting point, this paper draws on the successive coupling ontological framework of the geometrization of existence system, and linearly deduces the ontological essence, operating mechanism and existential boundary of free will based on the hierarchical generation rules of first-order objective coupling and second-order self-reflexive coupling. This paper proves that free will is neither an independent spiritual entity nor a break from the law of causality, but a second-order self-reflexive regulatory function evolved from high-order closed ray clusters. With simulation and prediction, directional selection, and deviation correction as its core operations, it is inherently fallible. Its core value lies in correcting cognitive biases and realizing 1:1 alignment between logical sequences and real causal sequences, so as to serve the persistence and optimization of individual steady states. Free will has a relative space of autonomous regulation but no absolute freedom independent of successive causality; its essence is the conscious calibration right of high-order steady states over their own causal chains. This definition fundamentally resolves the dualistic dilemma in the traditional debate on free will, and provides a unified ontological foundation for cognitive science, psychology, ethics and other fields.

items.title: Effects of Embodied Cognition Through Arts-Based Strategies in Developing Mathematical Competencies of Grade 7 Learners of Leonarda D. Vera Cruz National High School
items.abstract: This study examined the effects of embodied cognition through arts-based strategies on the mathematical competencies of Grade 7 learners at Leonarda D. Vera Cruz National High School, Unisan, Quezon, Philippines. Grounded in Embodied Cognition Theory and an Input–Process–Output–Outcome framework, the study employed a descriptive quasi-experimental, single-group pretest–posttest design involving 26 Grade 7 learners during School Year 2025–2026. Data were collected using a researcher-developed, validated 20-item competency test and analyzed through mean scores, mean percentage scores (MPS), standard deviations, learning gains, and paired-samples t-tests. The intervention incorporated movement, gestures, artistic expression, and kinesthetic activities to develop three mathematical competencies. Results revealed improvements in using positive and negative numbers to describe directions or opposites (38.46% to 73.63%), locating integers on a number line (41.67% to 91.03%), and performing addition and subtraction of integers (19.78% to 58.24%). The respective learning gains were 35.17, 49.36, and 38.46 percentage points, with a reported overall mean gain of 41.00 percentage points. Statistically significant pretest–posttest differences were observed across all competencies (p < .001). Locating integers demonstrated the greatest improvement, while integer operations remained the most challenging competency. The findings supported the development of a Mathematics 7 lesson exemplar integrating arts-based activities, movement, and formative assessments. Although the absence of a comparison group limits causal interpretation, the results suggest that embodied arts-based instruction is a promising approach to strengthening mathematical understanding. The study aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) by supporting learner-centered approaches to foundational numeracy. Its educational sustainability contribution lies in providing a structured instructional resource that may support continued teaching improvement and meaningful Mathematics learning.

items.title: EKSPLORASI DAMPAK PERILAKU BULLYING TERHADAP PERKEMBANGAN SOSIAL-EMOSIONAL SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR DI KOTA TERNATE
items.abstract: Masa sekolah dasar merupakan periode penting dalam perkembangan sosial dan emosional anak karena pada tahap ini siswa mulai membangun hubungan pertemanan, belajar bekerja sama, serta mengembangkan konsep diri melalui interaksi dengan teman sebaya. Apabila pada masa tersebut anak mengalami perlakuan bullying secara berulang, maka pengalaman tersebut berpotensi menghambat perkembangan sosial maupun emosionalnya. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi bentuk-bentuk perilaku bullying yang terjadi di SD Negeri 25 Kota Ternate serta menganalisis dampaknya terhadap perkembangan sosial dan emosional siswa. Metode penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain deskriptif eksploratif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis dengan teknik reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa bentuk perilaku bullying yang paling dominan di SDN 25 Kota Ternate adalah bullying verbal, diikuti oleh bullying relasional (social bullying) dan bullying fisik. Temuan lain menunjukkan bahwa dari bentuk perilaku bullying tersebut ternyata memberikan dampak yang signifikan terhadap perkembangan sosial dan emosional siswa sekolah dasar di Kota Ternate. Rekomendasi penelitian ini ialah diperlukan upaya pencegahan dan penanganan secara kolaboratif melalui penguatan budaya sekolah yang aman, pendidikan karakter berbasis kearifan lokal, keterlibatan orang tua, serta dukungan kebijakan pemerintah daerah untuk menciptakan lingkungan belajar yang bebas dari bullying.

items.title: Between Frustration and Dedication: The Influence of Organizational Constraints and Job Satisfaction on Turnover Intention in a Sample of Indonesian Lecturers
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the influence of organizational constraints and job satisfaction on the turnover intention of university lecturers in Indonesia. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected via survey from a sample of 77 Indonesian lecturers selected through convenience sampling. Organizational constraints were measured using the Organizational Constraints Scale (OCS), while job satisfaction was assessed using the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), and turnover intention was measured using the Turnover Intention Scale (TIS). Hypothesis testing via multiple linear regression analysis revealed a significant simultaneous effect (R² = 0.35; p ≤ 0.05). Individually, organizational constraints were found to have a significant positive influence on turnover intention, while job satisfaction showed a negative though not statistically significant influence. This study is limited by its sample size and sampling technique; therefore, future research should utilize a larger sample collected through randomized sampling. Furthermore, future studies are encouraged to examine the mediating role of organizational constraints in the relationship between job satisfaction and the turnover intention of lecturers.

items.title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
items.abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

items.title: Critical Thinking and Related Cognitive Processes in Career Decision-Making: A Narrative Literature Review
items.abstract: Career decision-making is a complex process involving the selection of educational and career pathways based on an individual’s values, interests, preferences, and available information. Critical thinking has been proposed as a potentially relevant cognitive competence in this process; however, direct empirical evidence of its role in career decision-making remains limited. This study aimed to synthesize empirical evidence on the relationship between critical thinking, related cognitive processes, and career decision-making. A narrative literature review was conducted using systematic search strategies across major bibliographic databases. Seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Only a small proportion of these studies directly examined critical thinking, whereas most investigated related cognitive constructs, including thinking styles, dysfunctional career thoughts, and other cognitive variables. Overall, the findings suggest that critical thinking and related cognitive constructs may be associated with career decision-making outcomes; however, the available evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly indirect. These findings highlight the need for further research directly examining critical thinking using validated measures and suggest that fostering critical thinking may represent a promising direction for educational and career guidance.

items.title: Energetic feasibility in ecological systems
items.abstract: Ecological communities can persist for long periods despite strong competition and environmental variability, yet they can also reorganize or collapse abruptly after seemingly modest change. Explaining persistence, diversity, and collapse has produced several major traditions in ecology, including species-interaction models, consumer--resource theory, coexistence theory, feasibility analysis, and stability theory. These approaches are often developed separately, even though they all describe systems that capture energy from the environment, redistribute it through ecological interactions, and lose it through metabolism. Here I propose an energetic framework that helps place these traditions in a common language. The central idea is that ecological communities persist only when external energy supply can support both the maintenance of biomass and the losses associated with internal redistribution, while remaining within finite supply and throughput limits. For flux-based ecological models, this perspective yields an exact aggregate balance identity; for other model classes, the mapping is partial or reduced-form and depends on how the system boundary is defined. This framework clarifies why persistence is conditional on energetic compatibility, why enrichment need not always promote persistence, and how feasibility, coexistence, stability, and early warning signals can be interpreted as related aspects of the same underlying constraint. It also shows how finite supply and throughput can bound energetically compatible community states, while superlinear scaling of internal throughput provides one simple special case that yields transparent reduced-form limits on community size and, with additional assumptions, on ecological complexity. More broadly, the framework offers a physically grounded way to connect historically separate areas of ecological theory.

items.title: Contextualizing Islamic Ecotheology through Sasak, Samawa, and Mbojo Cultural Practices for Nature Conservation in West Nusa Tenggara
items.abstract: How Islamic ecotheological principles acquire culturally specific meanings and expressions in environmental conservation remains insufficiently understood, particularly across ethnocultural communities sharing a broader religious and regional context. This study examines the contextualization of Islamic ecotheology through Sasak, Samawa, and Mbojo cultural values and practices in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. A qualitative interpretive multi-site design was employed, involving 30 informants equally distributed across the three communities. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, three focus-group discussions involving previously interviewed participants, direct observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed through thematic interpretation, hermeneutic analysis, and cross-cultural comparison. The findings indicate that khalifah, amanah, mizan, and the prohibition of fasad provide shared ethical orientations emphasizing environmental responsibility and ecological balance. Among the Sasak, awiq-awiq reflects customary arrangements associated with natural-resource protection, while Samawa values, including Larap, Saling Sadu, and Saling Puji, and the Mbojo philosophy of Mori ro Mada provide culturally situated interpretations of collective responsibility. However, empirical evidence supporting specific Samawa and Mbojo conservation functions remains less direct than that supporting Sasak customary arrangements. The study proposes a religious–cultural translation framework comprising normative orientation, cultural interpretation, institutional mediation, and ecological enactment. This framework explains culturally embedded environmental responsibilities without establishing causal relationships or independently measured conservation outcomes.
