items.title: The evolving role of diamond materials in neuroscience and neuroengineering.
items.abstract: Diamond-based materials are increasingly investigated in neuroscience and neuroengineering because of their tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, electrochemical stability and photostability. This review compares particulate nanodiamonds (NDs), fluorescent NDs, conductive and nanocrystalline diamond electrodes, and NV-containing diamond sensors across neural sensing, imaging, neurochemical monitoring, neural interfacing, regenerative engineering and experimental therapeutic applications. We examine how synthesis, particle size, purity, aggregation, surface chemistry and defect structure influence application-specific performance, biological interactions, biodistribution and safety. Translational potential is assessed according to the available evidence, systemic exposure, technical maturity, manufacturing requirements and regulatory complexity. Localized diagnostic and neurochemical-sensing applications may offer comparatively plausible near-term pathways because they can reduce dependence on systemic delivery. Implantable neural electrodes and retinal interfaces also avoid some systemic barriers but remain predominantly supported by preclinical evidence. ND-based central nervous system (CNS) drug delivery, glioblastoma treatment, neurodegenerative scaffolds and mammalian quantum-neuronal sensing remain at earlier experimental stages. Key barriers include formulation-dependent biocompatibility, sensitivity in complex tissues, blood-brain barrier delivery, long-term biodistribution and clearance, manufacturing reproducibility, GMP-compatible scale-up and regulatory qualification. Although some of these limitations may be reduced through material and process optimization, comparative validation and stronger long-term safety evidence are still required for clinical translation. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Diamond-based materials are increasingly finding their way into neuroscience and neuroengineering by bridging the gap between advanced nanotechnology and living neural systems. This review highlights the versatility of distinct diamond structures-ranging from detonation nanodiamonds and fluorescent defect centers to conductive boron-doped electrodes-across applications like biosensing, neurochemical monitoring, neural interfacing, and targeted therapy.

items.title: A novel and adaptable method to prepare samples for postmortem imaging with artifact reduction.
items.abstract: Background Postmortem MRI enables ultra-high-resolution image acquisition and subsequent biomarker validation. This approach requires that postmortem specimens be suspended in solution, which is not required for in vivo MRI. Susceptibility artifacts occur at surface-air interfaces and around air bubbles that remain in and around the sample, leading to image distortions. New method We set forth our protocol, the Seven Seals Method, whereby we prepare brain specimens for MRI scanning, with special attention to removing artifact-causing air bubbles. This protocol evolved over twenty years of ex vivo imaging experience. The method uses freezer bags to create a custom-shaped container for brain samples with a temporary reservoir pocket that collects air for removal. The protocol provides step by step instructions with diagrams and videos, a history of experimentation, and a troubleshooting guide. Results We have successfully applied this method to whole brains, brain hemispheres and blocked brain specimens, and have prepared samples in a variety of solutions. Comparison with existing methods The strengths of the Seven Seals Method include its high adaptability for shape and size fit, proven air bubble removal techniques, and inexpensive packing materials that do not require the use of a 3D printer. The tailored container minimizes motion and allows for closer proximity of the specimen to the coil elements than when using hard sided plastic containers, which yields better signal-to-noise ratio for structure visualization. Conclusions We anticipate this rigorous protocol will enable other groups to optimize their ex vivo scans for validation studies.

items.title: PPT1-mediated GABA<sub>A</sub>Rα1 depalmitoylation maintains inhibitory synaptic homeostasis and cognition.
items.abstract: GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs), essential for inhibitory neurotransmission, are palmitoylated proteins and their depalmitoylation is catalyzed by palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1). By generating Gabra1 em1 knock-in mice carrying mutations that disrupt the interaction between GABA A Rα1 and PPT1, we found that the mutant mice exhibited impaired learning and memory, whereas the underlying cellular mechanisms remained largely unclear. Molecular analyses showed that heterozygous (HET) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HET) displayed normal GABA A Rα1 protein expression but persistent hyperpalmitoylation of GABA A Rα1. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated the decreased neuronal excitability, enhanced inhibitory synaptic transmission and impaired hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP). Behavioral analyses further revealed deficits in learning, memory and social behavior. The homozygous (HOMO) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HOMO) exhibited a marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, accompanied by enhanced neuronal excitability and excitatory synaptic transmission, but impaired LTP and learning and memory along with a shorten life span. Collectively, these findings indicate that Gabra1 em1 HET mice represent a valuable model for investigating the physiological and pathological roles of protein palmitoylation, as aberrant GABA A Rα1 palmitoylation disrupts neuronal excitability, synaptic plasticity, and cognitive function without altering receptor expression. In contrast, the phenotypes observed in Gabra1 em1 HOMO mice are primarily attributable to the marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, which consequently impairs synaptic plasticity and learning and memory. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of protein palmitoylation in neurological disorders and offer a theoretical foundation for the development of precision therapeutic strategies targeting palmitoylation homeostasis.

items.title: Common Phenomenal and Neural Substrate Geometry in Visual Motion Perception.
items.abstract: What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive. To overcome the challenge of expressing subjective experience, recent structural and relational approaches have been proposed from mathematics. Yet, as far as we know, no attempts have been made to evaluate the relationship between a certain structure of qualia and the structure of a candidate underlying physical substrate. Towards this ambitious goal of linking the structures of qualia and physical, we set out to make an empirical first step by focusing on experienced dissimilarity of visual motion in human participants and stimulus-evoked neural population response geometry recorded from mouse primary visual cortex. From human participants (N=171), we obtained dissimilarity ratings of visual motion experiences induced by 48 stimuli, spanning across 8 directions and 6 spatial frequencies. Analysis revealed a human dissimilarity structure that was not well captured by a simple monotonic function of physical motion-direction difference alone nor by a pure orientation-symmetry account. From nine individual mice, we recorded single-neuron activity (n=751) with optical imaging in both awake and lightly anaesthetised conditions (isoflurane 0.6-0.8%). From neuron population responses to a similar set of motion stimuli, we computed a distance matrix that is comparable to our human dissimilarity matrix. Quantitative analyses show structural commonalities between a human dissimilarity structure and mouse neural structure, where a categorical organisation of stimulus direction best explained both. These commonalities were similar in awake and anaesthetised recordings, suggesting that this coarse V1 geometry is relatively insensitive to this type of anaesthesia; future work combining behaviour with causal intervention is required to relate such neural structures to conscious experience. Finally, we list several empirical factors that can be improved to promote our qualia structure approach in the future.

items.title: Pain mechanisms in trigeminal neuralgia: From peripheral pathology to brain network reorganization and neurosurgical implications.
items.abstract: Objectives Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) involves peripheral neurovascular pathology and may also be associated with maladaptive neuroplastic changes in central nervous system networks. This review synthesizes evidence on peripheral and central pain mechanisms, neuroimaging biomarkers, molecular and transcriptomic correlates, and neurosurgical implications, including emerging neuromodulation strategies. Materials and methods This narrative review drew on topic-oriented searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science conducted between June 27 and July 5, 2026, covering literature published through June 2026. Supplementary targeted searches and reference-list screening were used to identify relevant publications. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively. Results Evidence supports a multilevel model of TN involving peripheral pathology and central neuroplastic changes. Neuroimaging studies report structural and functional alterations in sensorimotor, salience, limbic, and default mode networks, alongside disrupted structure-function coupling. Partial restoration of functional connectivity after neurosurgical treatment has been reported, although outcomes vary. Transcriptomic findings link imaging abnormalities to genes involved in ion channel function, synaptic signaling, neuroinflammation, and energy metabolism but remain hypothesis-generating. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) may provide short-term analgesic benefit; however, evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions TN may be understood as a disorder involving interactions between peripheral pathology and central nervous system reorganization. Integrating neuroimaging and molecular evidence may inform future patient stratification and neurosurgical decision-making. Individualized neuromodulation remains investigational and requires further clinical validation.

items.title: Is It a "Hybrid Swarm"? Opportunities for More Informative Terminology in Conservation Genomics.
items.abstract: Hybridization is common in wild taxa, which may cause conservation concerns if hybridization occurs following disturbance or species introductions. High throughput DNA sequencing makes genomic analysis of many individuals feasible, vastly improving and promoting more studies on hybridization. However, more precise genomic identification of hybrids has not always extended to more precise use of terminology to describe hybrid ancestry. For hybridizing species of conservation concern, it is critical to understand hybridization dynamics precisely in order to effectively manage imperiled taxa. We conducted a review of 67 representative journal articles that use the term "hybrid swarm" in reference to hybridization, as variation in the usage of the term makes it difficult to understand which biological processes are being described. We found that "hybrid swarm" is used in several contexts across studies using various methods and numbers of genetic markers, reflecting vastly different statistical power and degrees of evidence for extensive hybridization. We encourage researchers working with genomic datasets to use clearer terminology when describing hybridization outcomes. We elaborate on scenario-specific terminology to strengthen uniformity in hybridization language, which we hope will promote more precise descriptions of hybridization and improve the clarity of future research on hybridization.

items.title: Turtle Herbivory Suppresses Seagrass Function but Reveals Recovery Potential in a Remote Coral Reef Atoll.
items.abstract: Seagrasses are recognised as ecologically and culturally significant habitats across the globe supporting human livelihoods, biodiversity, and carbon storage. In the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, a remote coral reef atoll in the eastern Indian Ocean, seagrasses provide ecosystem services and support culturally, ecologically, and economically important species. However, these meadows have suffered devastating declines, with ongoing green turtle herbivory identified as a key pressure restricting Thalassia hemprichii persistence.To examine how herbivory shapes seagrass traits and function, we compared plots protected from grazing for over two years using exclusion cages against continuously grazed plots across two sites.Seagrass traits at the meadow-scale (shoot density, leaf area and biomass), as well as some functionality (primary production and nutrient storage capacity), were improved with protection from herbivory pressure. Substantial reductions in the belowground biomass in the grazed plots indicate that these seagrasses are operating under severe metabolic constraints. In contrast, some plant-scale traits (photosynthetic rate and growth rate) were not altered despite ongoing herbivory pressure, indicating some capacity for recovery at the individual plant scale.Representing one of the longest turtle exclusion studies in seagrass ecosystems, these results demonstrate that herbivory is driving systemic degradation across multiple biological scales, but these seagrasses currently retain the capacity to recover once grazing pressure is reduced. Synthesis . Tropical seagrass meadows subjected to continuous herbivory pressure can persist in a chronically depleted state. Herbivore exclusion experiments demonstrate that reducing herbivory can unlock the recovery potential of seagrass. These findings highlight the need for nuanced management strategies to safeguard these meadows in a time where seagrasses continue to decline at both localised and global scales, and the global turtle populations are simultaneously on the rise.

items.title: Concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional changes in HepG2 cells following long-term nominal nanomolar PFOA exposure.
items.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent environmental contaminant whose transcriptional effects under prolonged low-dose exposure remain insufficiently characterized. We investigated transcriptomic responses in HepG2 cells exposed to nominal PFOA concentrations of 1, 10, or 100nM for 6- or 12-weeks using RNA-seq, differential expression analysis, Gene Ontology enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). No differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were detected at 1nM PFOA at either time point. At 10nM and 100nM PFOA, respectively, 149 and 183 DEGs were identified after 6 weeks, predominantly downregulated, compared with 10 and 56 DEGs after 12 weeks. The 6-week response included induction of immediate-early genes (FOS, EGR1) and repression of transcriptional and developmental regulators. At 12 weeks, six downregulated genes, including FOS, FOSB, and PLA2G2A, were shared between concentrations, with no shared upregulated genes. GSEA showed negative enrichment of transcriptional and developmental gene sets at both time points, whereas protein folding and stress response gene sets were enriched only at 6 weeks. WGCNA identified one dominant concentration-associated module at 6 weeks and several smaller modules at 12 weeks, most showing preservation across exposure durations. Together, these findings demonstrate concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional differences following prolonged nanomolar PFOA exposure, while the underlying biological mechanisms and potential contributions of culture-associated changes require further investigation.

items.title: Targeted flavour development in chocolate: omics-driven insights into cocoa fermentation.
items.abstract: Cocoa fermentation is the critical microbially driven process that transforms the genetic potential of cocoa beans into the complex flavour precursors essential for high-quality chocolate. Despite its importance, fermentation remains highly variable and poorly controlled, representing a major bottleneck in the production of premium chocolate. This review explores how advanced multi-omics approaches are improving our understanding of cocoa fermentation and flavour formation by linking microbial ecology, metabolite production and sensory outcomes. It highlights the transition of cocoa fermentation from a traditional practice towards a predictive, controllable biotechnological process. Such advances pave the way for the development of tailored starter cultures, optimised fermentation processes, and ultimately, consistent production of targeted flavour development in chocolates with enhanced quality and market value.

items.title: Novel ecological observations of Gobiodon assemblages and an extended species distribution on Nyinggulu Reef, Western Australia
items.abstract: Coral-dwelling gobies (Gobiodon Bleeker 1856) are among the most specialised cryptobenthic reef fishes, living almost exclusively within branching and corymbose corals throughout the Indo-Pacific. Despite extensive research on the ecology of the genus, comparatively little is known about Gobiodon assemblages from Western Australia. Here, we document the diversity, habitat use, host associations, social organisation, and notable behavioural observations of Gobiodon inhabiting shallow Acropora corals at Manimanira (Five Fingers Reef), Nyinggulu Marine Park, during two field seasons in 2025 and 2026. Seven species were recorded: Gobiodon axillaris, G. citrinus, G. histrio, G. oculolineatus, G. okinawae, G. rivulatus, and G. quinquestrigatus. Repeated observations suggested habitat partitioning among dominant species, with G. axillaris occurring primarily on shallow reef flats, while G. oculolineatus and G. quinquestrigatus occupy deeper corals. Host associations differed in several respects from previous reports, including frequent occupancy of Acropora protoeiformis and use of a plating coral by G. citrinus, and mixed-species occupancy of A. acervata. Species also differed markedly in social organisation, from pair-forming species to those forming large social groups. In addition, the confirmed occurrence of G. oculolineatus represents the first documented record from coastal Western Australia, offering a new locality and substantial extension (~3,500 km) to its known distribution. These observations provide the first detailed account of the Gobiodon assemblage from Nyinggulu and establish an important baseline for future studies of coral-associated gobies in this region.

items.title: Ecophysiological assessment of aquatic plants in a Southern Türkiye Lake: heavy metal bioconcentration, phytochemicals, and biological activities.
items.abstract: In the present study, the aquatic macrophytes of Golbasi Lake, located in Hatay Province, the southern part of Türkiye, were investigated for heavy metal pollution. The investigation focused on commonly found macrophytes, such as Ceratophyllum demersum , Lemna minor , and Salvinia natans , to assess cadmium, cobalt, copper, chromium, iron, lead, manganese, nickel, and zinc using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry. Nickel and lead concentrations exceeded the prescribed threshold values. Cadmium, lead, nickel, and zinc concentrations were higher, with copper and iron exceeding the critical values. Among the three species, L. minor showed the greatest accumulation of Cd, Cu, Pb, and Zn, with Cd concentrations approximately 2911% and 300% higher than those in C. demersum and S. natans , respectively. L. minor exhibited the highest total phenolic and flavonoid contents, which were approximately 24.9% and 34.2% higher, respectively, than those of C. demersum . In contrast, S. natans showed the highest DPPH radical-scavenging activity, approximately 14.4% higher than C. demersum . All the extracts showed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus ; the highest antibacterial activity was observed for L. minor . The present study thus shows the impact of agricultural, industrial, mining, and drainage activities on the Golbasi Lake ecosystem, highlighting the role of aquatic plants as bioindicators for heavy metal detection. The results emphasize the need to remove heavy metals before discharging them into Golbasi Lake and to implement effective environmental management strategies to maintain the balance of nature and the eco-sustainability of the Golbasi Lake ecosystem.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Trends in Suicide: Sociodemographic, Economic, and Environmental Factors.
items.abstract: Suicide is one of the world's leading public health problems, with more than 720,000 deaths annually. Suicide has traditionally been studied from an individual perspective. However, research has increasingly highlighted the influence of community-level factors on suicide risk. This study aimed to (1) analyze the spatial distribution of suicide mortality at the provincial level in Spain (2018-2022); (2) perform stratified analyses by sex and age group; and (3) compare suicide risk across different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. We used data from the Spanish National Institute of Statistics on 17,809 suicide deaths in 47 peninsular provinces between 2018 and 2022. Covariates included sociodemographic (e.g., aging rate, population density), economic (e.g., unemployment, GDP), and environmental (e.g., temperature) indicators. Bayesian hierarchical spatial Poisson regression models were fitted to estimate suicide risk and identify relevant contextual variables. The general spatial model revealed a higher risk of suicide in provinces with lower population density, higher aging rates, and lower health expenditure. Other covariates such as gross domestic product, unemployment, or temperature were associated with specific sex or age groups. Suicide risk was highest in the northwestern provinces and lowest in the central regions. Stratified analyses showed similar patterns across gender and age groups, and between time periods, with some variations in spatial distribution. This study reveals significant spatial heterogeneity in suicide risk across Spanish regions, influenced by sociodemographic, economic, and environmental factors. These findings underline the importance of regionally tailored suicide prevention policies, especially in aging and low-density areas with low health investment.

items.title: Parenting stress spirals and a gendered labour division over the Christmas holidays.
items.abstract: The Christmas period heightens parental demands and invisible labour, yet little is known about how these processes unfold in daily life. This study used experience sampling data from 293 UK parents over 35 days to examine temporal associations between cognitive labour, emotion suppression, and subjective stress across the holiday season. Dynamic Structural Equation Modelling revealed strong autoregressive stability for all constructs and reciprocal moment-to-moment links between cognitive labour and stress, indicating a self-reinforcing cycle. Cognitive labour and stress also predicted subsequent emotion suppression, suggesting that emotion suppression operates as a situational coping response to mental and stress overload. At the between-person level, social support reduced emotion suppression but did not buffer stress or cognitive labour. Gender differences emerged only for cognitive labour, with mothers reporting higher levels than fathers. Findings highlight the dynamic interplay between invisible labour and stress and underscore the psychological strains parents face during the holidays.

items.title: Influence of Sex and Fatigue on Velocity Loss as a Set Termination Criterion in the Bench Press.
items.abstract: Purpose To analyze the relationship between the percentage of velocity loss (VL) and the percentage of completed repetitions relative to the maximum possible (%Rep) during a single set to failure, preceded by previous efforts (PE), in the bench press exercise in men and women. Methods Thirty participants (15 men and 15 women) performed 4 protocols (1 week apart) consisting of a set to failure with 60% of one-repetition maximum preceded by a previous effort, consisting of 3 sets at 60% one-repetition maximum. Each protocol differed in the VL attained during the preceding effort: 0% (PEVL0), 20% (PEVL20), 40% (PEVL40), and 60% (PEVL60). The VL-%Rep relationship was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2) and the standard error of estimate. Results The R2 in the VL-%Rep relationship remained stable for different fatigue levels and sexes (men: R2 = .94-.93; women: R2 = .92-.90, with standard error of estimate values of 7%-9%). Men performed a higher %Rep than women for the same VL, particularly at low-to-moderate VL thresholds. However, prior high fatigue reduced these sex differences. Conclusions The strong and consistent relationship between VL and %Rep observed across all conditions confirms that VL is a robust indicator of the level of effort in bench press, regardless of sex or previous fatigue. However, men completed a greater proportion of repetitions for the same VL, especially under low-to-moderate fatigue. This suggests that, to improve precision when using VL to prescribe or monitor the level of effort, women may require higher VL thresholds to achieve an equivalent relative effort.

items.title: A behavioral and electrophysiological study on the influence of menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone on the social approach-avoidance behavior tendencies of women.
items.abstract: It remains unclear whether women's social approach-avoidance behaviors toward different facial expressions are influenced by their menstrual cycles, estradiol and progesterone levels, or what the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms might be. This study collected data on the levels of estradiol and progesterone, social approach-avoidance behavior and electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings from 27 women with natural menstrual cycles during three phases- early follicular phase, late follicular phase, and mid-luteal phase. The results showed that women in the late follicular phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to happy faces compared to the early follicular phase; women in the mid-luteal phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to fearful faces compared to the late follicular phase. Estradiol levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward happy faces, while progesterone levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward fearful faces. The results show that women's social approach-avoidance behaviors are specifically regulated by the menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone, and exhibit higher cognitive processing efficiency in the late positive potential (LPP) of the brain. These findings are manifestations in social interactions of the characteristics of women's interest pursuit and self-restraint under the influence of different sex hormones formed during evolution, updating established hormone-behavior links in social emotional contexts.

items.title: Delivering psychotherapy when there is no "post": The Healing for Gaza Global Clinic's model for care in conditions of ongoing violence.
items.abstract: Humanitarian responses to war-related trauma frequently prioritize scalable psychosocial activities or medication-adjacent services, while clinically governed psychotherapy remains uncommon in settings shaped by ongoing state violence. When psychotherapy is introduced, it is often without the conditions that make care safe and clinically coherent: stable privacy, continuity, supervised decision-making, culturally grounded formulation, and enforceable boundary governance. Further, in crises, cultural adaptation may be reduced to literal, decontextualized translation rather than interpretation as part of clinical work. This manuscript provides a program description of Healing for Gaza, a hybrid remote and field-based care model developed to extend access to clinically governed psychotherapy and psychiatric care for Palestinians from Gaza amid protracted violence and displacement. The model integrates trauma-informed psychotherapy, psychiatric services, periodic field missions for in-person and community interventions, and a structured training curriculum emphasizing both learning about care for trauma in this setting and countering clinical assumptions anchored in stable settings. In addition, this paper offers an operational account of how Healing for Gaza delivers psychotherapy as a governed clinical process: centralizing triage and coordination; providing clinic-managed communication channels to protect confidentiality in a system reliant on telehealth care; ensuring interpreters and clinicians are trained, consistently assigned, and integrated into supervision; applying workforce safeguards, including structured supervision and debriefing, reflective practices, caseload caps, and access to psychotherapy; and using a mixed-methods monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning framework oriented toward clinical quality and emerging risks. The manuscript concludes with principles that may guide adaptation of this architecture in other humanitarian contexts.

items.title: Moving towards evidence-based screening and investigations in first episode psychosis: A commentary on the ANZJP GRADE Schizophrenia Guidelines.
items.abstract: Physical health assessment and investigations are important considerations during the first episode of psychosis. These activities support diagnostic clarification, monitoring for iatrogenic harms and opportunistic screening to limit the multimorbidity that is often associated with psychotic disorders in the longer term. The recent 'Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE) guidelines for the management of schizophrenia' and the associated systematic review by Warren et al. fill a critical gap by providing evidence-based guidance on which investigations should be routine and when more targeted investigations are warranted. However, the guidance provided has a limited focus on affective psychosis, and its focus on targeted screening for sexually transmitted infections may underestimate the extent to which people experiencing the first episode of psychosis reflect an at-risk group. This commentary explores the relevance of further consideration of sexual health issues and affective psychosis in developing evidence-based guidance for physical health assessment and investigations at the first episode of psychosis.

items.title: Noise, Inequality, and Mental Health. Urban Challenges in the State of Mexico.
items.abstract: Environmental noise is an increasing public health concern, with effects that extend beyond hearing loss to include anxiety and depression. In the Global South, however, evidence remains limited, and most studies focus primarily on objective exposure measures, while subjective dimensions of noise experience remain less explored. This study examines the relationship between sociodemographic characteristics, perceived noise, and mental health in households of the State of Mexico, considering urban-rural differences. Data were collected from a probabilistic, stratified household survey (n = 400). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied using the diagonally weighted least squares estimator adjusted with expansion factors, and an exploratory spatial analysis was conducted through IDW interpolation to explore territorial patterns in predicted outcomes. The findings indicate that household size was a significant predictor of perceived noise, with larger households reporting higher levels. Perceived noise was significantly associated with depressive symptoms but not with anxiety, and living in urban municipalities was directly associated with higher levels of depression, independent of perceived noise. Spatial analysis further revealed that patterns of high perceived noise and depression are concentrated in metropolitan areas. Overall, the results suggest that environmental noise is a relevant, though modest, environmental factor associated with mental health in the State of Mexico, particularly in urban contexts, indicating that it merits consideration alongside other urban stressors in planning and public health efforts addressing territorial disparities.

items.title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
items.abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

items.title: Dioscin attenuates aniline-induced liver injury by targeting the ACOT2-mediated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis and restoring mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and lysosomal lipophagy.
items.abstract: Chronic aniline exposure causes prominent hepatotoxicity accompanied by hepatic lipid metabolic disorders and cellular senescence, yet the molecular cascade underlying aniline-triggered liver injury remains unclear. Here, a 90-day chronic aniline intoxication mouse model and an AML12 murine hepatocyte model were established to systematically dissect toxic mechanisms and identify candidate hepatoprotective agents. Adverse outcome pathway analysis revealed lipid metabolic disturbance and cellular senescence as core toxic events, with lipid metabolic disturbance acting as an upstream driver of aniline-induced hepatocyte senescence and injury. Integrated multi-omics analysis showed that acyl-CoA thioesterase 2 (ACOT2), a key rate-limiting enzyme in fatty acid β-oxidation, was markedly downregulated in aniline-damaged livers. Hepatic ACOT2 overexpression restored mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation capacity, alleviated lipid overload, excessive ROS accumulation and hepatic dysfunction, and reduced bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP) accumulation by suppressing neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis protein 5 (CLN5) expression. Mechanistically, ACOT2 deficiency caused ROS overproduction and activated JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Phosphorylated STAT3 translocated into the nucleus and directly bound the Cln5 promoter, enhancing its transcription. Elevated CLN5 disrupted lysosomal structural integrity and acidification, thereby blocking lipid degradation during lipophagy. Conversely, Cln5 silencing restored lysosomal homeostasis and autophagic flux and reduced hepatic lipid deposition. Virtual screening identified dioscin as a natural small molecule that directly interacts with ACOT2, as confirmed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance assays. PPARα-dependent transcriptional regulation contributed to ACOT2 suppression across multiple liver injury models, whereas dioscin restored ACOT2-dependent fatty acid oxidation and conferred broad hepatoprotection against aniline-, CCl 4 -, and APAP-induced liver injury. Collectively, this study reveals, in male mice and murine hepatocyte models, a previously unreported ACOT2-regulated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis linking impaired mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, lysosomal dysfunction and defective lipid clearance during aniline hepatotoxicity. These findings further support dioscin as a promising hepatoprotective candidate drug that directly targets ACOT2.

items.title: Time-resolved profiling reveals nonlinear dose-time trajectories of gut microbiota in PM<sub>2.5</sub> and PFOS exposure models.
items.abstract: The gut microbiota is a dynamic ecological system, yet environmental microbiome studies often provide only limited temporal resolution. We characterized gut microbial responses across multiple exposure levels and sampling stages in two independent but complementary mouse models of PM 2.5 inhalation and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) drinking-water exposure. Time-resolved 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ecological analyses, PICRUSt2-based functional inference, and generalized additive models (GAMs) were integrated to examine temporal succession and nonlinear dose-time relationships. Under unexposed conditions, temporal microbial succession was evident in both models, highlighting the importance of accounting for background community dynamics. Within the PM 2.5 model, community restructuring was most apparent during early-to-intermediate exposure stages, with prominent nonlinear trajectories in Lactobacillus, Prevotella, and the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio. In the PFOS model, microbial restructuring extended across a longer observation period and involved taxa including Akkermansia, Allobaculum, and UBA7173. PICRUSt2 suggested temporal and dose-associated variation in predicted pathways related to nitrogen metabolism, carbohydrate utilization, and fermentation, although these functions were not directly measured. GAMs identified stage-specific nonlinear response windows in both models. These findings highlight the importance of jointly considering dose and time in environmental microbiome studies and demonstrate the value of time-resolved modeling for detecting microbial response patterns that may be missed by endpoint analyses.

items.title: The environmental pollutant benzo[k]fluoranthene alters CD4<sup>+</sup> T-cell subset distribution via AhR signaling.
items.abstract: We examined associations of 16 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with aryl hydrocarbon receptor expression in circulating CD4 + T cells. In healthy human controls, BkF showed the strongest association with AhR + CD4 + T cells (r = 0.342, 95% CI 0.130-0.523, P = 0.0021; BH-adjusted q = 0.033); in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, it did not survive multiplicity correction. In PBMCs from three healthy donors cultured for five days with BkF (3 or 10µg/L) with or without the AhR antagonist CH223191, BkF increased Th2, Th17, cTfh, and Treg populations, decreased naïve CD4 + T cells, and raised the Th1/Th2 ratio, shifts attenuated by CH223191. These findings identify BkF as an immunomodulatory AhR ligand that reshapes CD4 + T-cell subset distribution.

items.title: Erianin Targets Glutathione Reductase to Trigger Immunogenic Cell Death and Sensitize Pancreatic Cancer to PD-1 Blockade.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), largely because of its immunosuppressive and T-cell-excluded tumor microenvironment. While inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) offers a promising strategy to enhance tumor immunogenicity, redox-targeted ICD inducers with defined molecular targets remain limited in PDAC. Here, a functional screen of natural compounds identified erianin as a potent ICD inducer in PDAC. Erianin triggered canonical ICD hallmarks, including cell-surface calreticulin exposure, extracellular release of HMGB1 and ATP, thereby promoting dendritic-cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation and CD8 + T-cell activation. Target-engagement assays together with genetic perturbation supported glutathione reductase (GSR) as a functionally important erianin target. Erianin decreased the GSH/GSSG ratio, accompanied by increased oxidative stress and preferential activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP branch of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response. Mutational and rescue experiments identified residue ARG-233 as an important residue required for GSR-dependent protection against erianin-induced redox stress and ICD. In syngeneic PDAC models, erianin-treated tumor cells elicited protective antitumor immunity in a tumor-challenge setting, while a therapeutic regimen combining erianin with anti-PD-1 antibody suppressed tumor growth and was associated with increased dendritic-cell activation and enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration. These findings define a GSR-associated redox-immune axis that links glutathione metabolism to immunogenic ER stress and provide a rationale for combining erianin with PD-1 blockade in immunologically cold PDAC.

items.title: AIM2 as a therapeutic target in autoimmunity: balancing inflammasome inhibition with immune homeostasis.
items.abstract: Absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) is a cytosolic pattern recognition receptor that functions as a critical sensor of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) of microbial or host origin. Upon DNA recognition, AIM2 assembles into a multiprotein inflammasome complex that drives pyroptotic cell death and maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18. Beyond its canonical role in host defense, aberrant AIM2 activation by self-DNA has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of various inflammatory autoimmune diseases. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of AIM2 biology. We examine the role of AIM2 in different immune cell populations, its effects on multiple downstream signaling pathways, and its complex association with autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and multiple sclerosis. Finally, we discussed therapeutic prospects and remaining challenges in targeting AIM2 for the treatment of autoimmunity.

items.title: Serum metabolic characteristics and potential biomarkers of first-episode schizophrenia: An exploratory machine learning-based metabolomics study.
items.abstract: Metabolomics studies in first-episode schizophrenia (FES) remain limited and heterogeneous. This study aimed to characterize the serum metabolomic profile of FES, identify metabolic biomarkers, and develop machine learning-based predictive models. In this exploratory study, serum metabolomic profiles were compared among healthy controls (HCs; n = 10), untreated FES patients (n = 10), and the same patients after second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) treatment. Candidate biomarkers were evaluated using six machine learning algorithms. Bayesian network analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were further applied to explore the network relationships. Cross-dataset integrative analysis was additionally performed using an external public dataset comprising patients with schizophrenia (n = 30) and HCs (n = 30). Disease-associated candidate biomarkers included PG(16:0/18:1), PC(20:4/15:0), PC(22:5/15:0), PG(18:1/18:1), and PE(16:0/16:0), whereas treatment-associated biomarkers included PG(16:0/18:1), PC(20:4/15:0), PC(22:5/15:0), cholesterol sulfate, DG(20:4/22:4), and Phe-Thr-Asn-Lys. All selected candidate biomarkers achieved Area Under the Curve (AUC) values above 0.9, with performance varying across algorithms. In the Bayesian networks, disease served as a direct parent node of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score and all biomarkers, whereas treatment shared direct edges with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) score and all biomarkers except cholesterol sulfate, which was indirectly connected via Phe-Thr-Asn-Lys. WGCNA identified metabolite modules significantly associated with disease status (r = -0.88, p < 0.01) and treatment (r = 0.75, p < 0.01). Cross-dataset analysis identified phenylpyruvic acid, SM(d18:1/22:1(13Z)), and 2-octenoylcarnitine as shared differential metabolites with modest-to-moderate discrimination. These exploratory findings reveal potential serum metabolic signatures of FES and provide a basis for the development of objective biomarkers for diagnosis and SGAs treatment monitoring, warranting validation in larger independent cohorts.

items.title: Developmental toxicity of curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles in the freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata.
items.abstract: Curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles (Curc-AgNPs) are promising biogenic nanomaterials in medical and environmental applications. However, their ecotoxicological impact to non-target aquatic species remains understood. This study assessed the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs in the neotropical freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata, considering multiple developmental and post-hatching endpoints, including embryonic mortality, hatching success, developmental progression, heart rate, embryonic cell viability, and mortality of newly hatched snails. Curc-AgNPs (14 ± 4 nm) were synthesized by reducing AgNO 3 with curcumin and characterized by multiples techniques. Curc-AgNPs induced mortality, hatching inhibition, developmental delay, decreased heart rate and cell viability in a time- and concentration-dependent pattern. The cumulative developmental toxicity was confirmed by declining 50% effective concentration (LC50) to embryos (20.96 mg L -1 at 24 h to 1.47 mg L -1 at 168 h) and newly hatched snails (53.7 mg L -1 at 24 h to 37.5 mg L -1 at 120 h). Curc-AgNPs almost completely inhibited snail hatching at concentrations ≥ 1.88 mg L -1 and delayed embryonic development, mainly at gastrula and trochophore stages. Sub-lethal effects were observed in terms of cardiac activity (heart rate reduced by ∼41% at 1.88 mg L -1 ) and reduced cell viability in embryos exposed to Curc-AgNPs at concentration ranging 0.18 to 0.75 mg L -1 . Also, Curc-AgNPs induced higher toxicity in embryos than in newly hatched B. glabrata, indicating that the early developmental stages of gastropod are more susceptible to the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs. Overall, Curc-AgNPs exhibited pronounced embryotoxicity and stage-dependent molluscicidal effects. Although toxic, these concentrations exceed predicted environmental levels, representing hazard, not environmental risk.

items.title: Climate-induced extreme heat associated with suicide risk mediated by poor sleep and emotional dysregulation: A nationally representative panel study from Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Climate change-induced heat exposure is an emerging public health concern with potential mental health consequences, including suicide risk. Yet, in climate-vulnerable low- and middle-income countries the association between heat exposure and suicide risk, and the mediating mechanisms underlying this connection, remain underexplored. Using a nationally representative two-round panel survey from Bangladesh (n=7,492), we empirically examined whether poor sleep quality and emotional dysregulation mediate the relationship between exposure to extreme heat and suicide risk. Risk was assessed using a validated suicide cognitions scale across two seasonal rounds surveying the same individuals. Exposure to days ≥28°C over a two-week period was the lowest temperature threshold significantly associated with elevated suicide risk, with the highest risk detected at ≥35°C. At this 35°C threshold, 29.5% of the total association was mediated through poor sleep quality and 1.8% through emotional dysregulation. Risk was notably higher during the summer, and among less educated and poorer populations. This study provides novel evidence from a climate-vulnerable country on psychosocial mechanisms connecting heat and suicidality. As heat extremes intensify across the Global South, targeted mental health interventions, both infrastructural and psychological, may need consideration in climate adaptation strategies to protect the well-being of at-risk populations.

items.title: Beyond treatment selection: Interim hypothesis addition and deletion in confirmatory seamless designs.
items.abstract: Inferentially seamless Phase 2/3 designs can accelerate drug development by combining learning and confirmatory objectives within a single protocol while preserving strict Type I control. Standard multiplicity frameworks for such trials typically assume that the complete set of efficacy hypotheses is fixed at trial initiation. In practice, however, emerging internal or external evidence can motivate the introduction of new confirmatory hypotheses at an interim analysis (IA), for example by adding a new dose that was not initially planned for confirmatory testing. This creates a tension between operational flexibility and rigorous Type I error control, a statistical and regulatory requirement. We extend the conditional error rate (CER) framework to permit hypothesis addition and deletion at an IA while maintaining strong familywise error rate (FWER) control under a closed testing principle. We also derive the conditional covariance structures and reference distributions needed when intersection hypotheses involve a newly introduced component. We compare our CER procedure to (i) an inverse-normal stagewise p-value combination approach and (ii) a straightforward split-α comparator that allocates separate one-sided error to "old" versus newly introduced hypotheses. We evaluate operating characteristics in a two-stage seamless setting with interim best-dose selection and an added dose at the IA. Simulations under the global null and under partial-null configurations support the strong FWER control of the implementation, while sensitivity analyses examine misspecification of the working reference distribution. Across alternative scenarios, the CER procedure can provide meaningful power gains, especially when the newly introduced dose is promising.

items.title: Social Determinants of Health Screening Tools Used with Immigrant Populations: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Social determinants of health (SDOH) are increasingly recognized as major contributors to health outcomes. Beyond general social challenges, immigrants face additional barriers related to language, immigration status, legal concerns, discrimination, and exclusionary policies. Despite growing interest in SDOH screening, little is known about how existing screening instruments address immigrant-specific factors. Searches of Web of Science, PubMed, CINAHL, and PsychINFO identified peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible studies included original research articles focused on immigrant populations and the use of an SDOH screening tool. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts. Data were extracted on screening tool characteristics, SDOH domains assessed, immigrant-specific indicators, language availability, study setting, and tool validation status. The final search yielded 1,155 articles. Eight studies met full inclusion criteria, describing nine screening tools or variants, including adaptations of the Health Leads Social Needs Screening Toolkit, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Accountable Health Communities screening tool, and the Protocol for Responding to and Assessing Patients' Assets, Risks, and Experiences. Most studies occurred in urban primary care settings and primarily served Hispanic/Latinx immigrant populations. Core SDOH domains were well-represented across all tools. While all studies included at least one immigrant-specific measure, these were generally limited to language preference, nativity, legal concerns, and migrant worker status. No adapted or newly developed tool demonstrated formal psychometric validation. Current SDOH screening tools may fail to capture the broader structural factors that shape immigrant health, including immigration-related policies, legal precarity, discrimination, and fear. Significant gaps remain in culturally responsive, psychometrically validated instruments developed with and for immigrant communities.

items.title: Large-scale semantic indexing of Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning.
items.abstract: Motivation The exponential growth of biomedical literature has made automatic indexing essential for advancing biomedical research. While automatic indexing has made strides in English biomedical literature, there has been limited research on non-English biomedical texts due to insufficient high-quality training data. Results We propose BERTDeCS, a novel deep learning framework for automatically indexing Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning. BERTDeCS utilizes a multilingual BERT (M-BERT) to generate multi-language representations and adapts M-BERT for Spanish biomedical literature domain through contrastive learning. Additionally, BERTDeCS enhances its semantic indexing capabilities on Spanish biomedical literature by leveraging enriched English annotated literature in MEDLINE through transfer learning. Experimental results on Spanish datasets demonstrate that BERTDeCS outperforms state-of-the-art indexing methods, achieving top performance in the MESINESP and MESINESP2 Tasks on medical semantic indexing in Spanish within the BioASQ challenge. Additional experiments on Portuguese provide preliminary evidence that BERTDeCS can transfer to a closely related language sharing substantial lexical and biomedical terminology with Spanish. Availability The source code is available at https://github.com/yourh/BERTDeCS and at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23212468.

items.title: Remote sensing and the EU nature restoration Regulation: monitoring biodiversity indicators for integrated forest management
items.abstract: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear. This review synthesises current evidence on the use of RS for monitoring forest biodiversity indicators defined in the NRR and identifies methodological gaps and operational priorities. Following a systematic review of 222 studies, we evaluate the suitability of different platforms, sensors, and scales of observation. Our results show that RS capabilities are strongly indicator and scale dependent, with no single approach suitable across all indicators. Airborne laser scanning is most effective for capturing forest structural attributes, including uneven-aged forest structure, while satellite multispectral imagery provides consistent, large-scale monitoring of forest connectivity. Tree species composition and diversity can be assessed using multi-sensor approaches, though accuracy declines in mixed and structurally complex forests. In contrast, the common forest bird index cannot currently be monitored using remote sensing, and deadwood indicators are limited by the resolution required for national monitoring. Key challenges include limited availability of repeated high-resolution data, difficulties in detecting high-resolution features, and reduced classification accuracy in complex forest systems. Overall, RS has strong potential to support monitoring when integrated with National Forest Inventories and multi-sensor data streams. Advancing towards operational implementation of RS within the NRR will require harmonised products, improved methods for complex forest conditions, and greater emphasis on temporal monitoring.

items.title: Human–wildlife conflict and farmland transfer under informal land institutions: Evidence from rural China
items.abstract: Abstract Human–wildlife conflict (HWC) affects not only agricultural production but also how farming households adjust access to and use of land. Existing research has focused largely on welfare losses and land‐use responses, while little is known about whether ecological risk is associated with the governance arrangements through which farmland is transferred Drawing on risk and uncertainty theory, we examine the relationship between HWC and informal farmland transfer (IFT) using survey data from 921 land‐transferring households drawn from 3213 surveyed households in Asian elephant range areas of Yunnan Province, China (2022–2024). We employ Probit, Heckman two‐step and IV‐Probit models for analysis. HWC is significantly associated with greater participation in IFT among land‐transferring households. Specifically, HWC increases both the probability and area of informal transfer‐out, but has no significant effect on informal transfer‐in. The effect is context‐dependent: Informal transfer‐out increases among households both near and far from nature reserves and is concentrated among small‐scale farmers, whereas reductions in informal transfer‐in are observed only in specific subgroups, namely households near reserves and households whose head is employed in the public sector. These findings suggest that ecological risk is associated with asymmetric land adjustment, primarily through informal transfer‐out, and that informal arrangements remain an important channel through which households reorganize land commitments under uncertainty. The study extends relational perspectives on HWC by showing that wildlife‐related risk is associated not only with individual land‐use responses but also with socially embedded forms of land reallocation. Policies in ecologically vulnerable regions should improve the flexibility and accessibility of formal land‐transfer institutions and strengthen coordination with wildlife damage compensation and agricultural insurance to support more secure and adaptive land adjustment. items.title: Comparing Population Census Methods for Howler Monkeys ( Alouatta palliata ) in a Fragmented Rainforest
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Accurate population density estimates are important for guiding conservation management practices for threatened animal species. Aims This study tests the efficacy of population census methods at a long‐term study site for the mantled howler monkey ( Alouatta palliatta ), La Suerte Biological Research Station (LSBRS) in Costa Rica. This monkey is a group‐living Neotropical primate with long distance vocalizations that is declining throughout its range. Methods We compared the visual count and long calling acoustic triangulation census methods to determine population count and number of social groups. Results We found 14 monkey groups according to both population census methods, indicating the accuracy of the acoustic triangulation method at determining group number. Visual count data showed that the 1.36‐km 2 study area within a 3‐km 2 forest fragment had a population density of 125.7 individuals/km 2 , one of the highest population densities ever recorded for this species, although mean group size of 11.6 (±4.7 SD) monkeys/group at LSBRS remained within the 10–15 monkeys/group range found at other sites. Discussion The observed mean group size at LSBRS fell within the commonly reported range for the species, suggesting that the acoustic triangulation method alone may provide a reasonably accurate estimate of population density for sites with average monkey group sizes and/or where mean group sizes have previously been quantified using visual count surveys. Recommendations We recommend collecting both types of census data where possible, while suggesting that acoustic triangulation censuses can be used on their own when financial resources are limited. Visual counts are necessary to confirm group number and size, and to enable detailed demographic studies.

items.title: Coastal Climate Change Adaptation: A Review of Engineering, Nature-Based, Governance, and Socio-Economic Adaptation Strategies
items.abstract: Adaptation is becoming a key part of climate policies, including the Paris Agreement, for coastal areas, which host a large proportion of the world's population. Coastal areas are prone to intensive urbanization and tourism, which can exacerbate the threats of sea-level rise, storm intensification, erosion, and saltwater intrusion. Existing reviews have examined engineering, ecological, governance, and socio-economic aspects of coastal system adaptation to climate change, but these studies have generally been limited to a single discipline and offer limited cross-domain information. Such fragmentation can limit their applicability to planners who are interested in context-specific, integrated solutions. This review offers a critical synthesis of engineering, nature based, governance, and socio-economic adaptation approaches used in coastal areas worldwide. The synthesis suggests that no single adaptation pathway performs uniformly well across settings. Rather, the effectiveness of the strategies depends on asset density, ecological and sediment conditions, governance capacity, and the urgency of the hazard. Hard engineering solutions provide a stable short-term solution in urban environments, but they externalize erosion costs and interfere with natural sediment transport. Nature-based solutions provide greater ecosystem and long-term co-benefits but require specific physical conditions to be achieved, which diminishes their transferability. While governance instruments and socio-economic measures help ensure effective, equitable, and sustainable outcomes, they do not directly provide measurable reductions in risk. The review compares the domains to identify points of overlap, interdependencies between strategies, and implementation challenges unique to each domain, and highlights the lack of standardized evidence across domains as an area for future research. This study focuses on integrated, context-adapted solutions that account for physical, ecological, and institutional dimensions to support sustainable and climate-resilient coastal development amid rapid environmental change.

items.title: The promises and perils of satellite Earth observation for just transformations in sustainability
items.abstract: Satellite Earth observation (EO) is considered an essential tool for the ‘Decade of Action’ towards the Sustainable Development Goals. While advocates claim that innovation in satellite EO will bring widespread environmental and societal benefits, satellite EO also raises significant epistemological and ethical challenges. This review examines the use of satellite EO for sustainable development, focusing on use cases related to renewable energy projects, smallholder agriculture programmes, disaster recovery, carbon accounting, water and ocean governance, and environmental activism. We explore the politics behind data capture, access, and use, recognising that satellite EO has ‘world-making’ effects. We find that satellite EO applications can generate unequal material impacts for people and the planet, while consolidating state or private control over natural resources. Yet, we also discuss how EO data can be collected and applied in locally led participatory ways to advocate for sustainability. Critical and reflexive dialogue is therefore needed to support policymakers, practitioners, and communities to realise the potential of satellite EO for just transformations in sustainability.

items.title: Diversität von Blütenbesuchern in Anbaufeldern einheimischer Wildpflanzen in Luxemburg
items.abstract: This study investigated the importance of wild plant propagation fields for flower-visiting insect communities within agricultural landscapes in Luxembourg. To assess their ecological value, we compiled faunistic inventories across 15 sites using coloured pan traps. We investigated how cultivated plant species and surrounding landscape structures drive community composition of three major insect groups: the orders Coleoptera and Thysanoptera, as well as the clade Anthophila within the order Hymenoptera. Patterns of species richness and the effective number of species were compared between fields. Overall, generalist species dominated the insect communities, although several rare and specialised species were also registered. Nineteen species of Thysanoptera and one species of Coleoptera were documented as new records for Luxembourg. In addition, several patterns regarding species richness and the effective number of species became apparent, particularly suggesting an influence of surrounding landscape structure on flower visitor communities. Wild plant fields embedded in suitable and structurally diverse habitats generally appeared to support higher flower visitor diversity, particularly bees, than fields located in intensively managed agricultural landscapes. In some cases, relationships between cultivated plant species and the specialisation of associated insect species could also be observed. However, these relationships remained inconsistent, likely because the observed diversity patterns resulted from a complex interplay of environmental and plant-related factors. We recommend establishing wild plant propagation fields in areas with a richly varied landscape whenever possible, as these conditions help attract a greater number of pollinators.

items.title: Trophic Connectivity of Pelagic Ecosystems in the Western Pacific Ocean and Its Marginal Seas Inferred From Stable Isotope Analysis
items.abstract: We used carbon and nitrogen stable isotope ratios to quantitatively assess predator–prey relationships among predatory fishes and their prey in the pelagic and mesopelagic layers of the East China Sea, the Sea of Japan, and the Pacific Ocean around southern Japan. Predatory fishes and their potential prey were collected from each region to evaluate spatial and species‐level differences in trophic structure. Isotopic niche widths were evaluated for prey taxa by region using standard ellipse areas corrected for small sample sizes. Overall, niche widths of predatory fishes in the Sea of Japan were larger than those in the Pacific Ocean. Niche overlap between the Pacific Ocean and the other regions was limited. Collectively, niche widths and niche‐overlap results were consistent with greater isotopic similarity between the East China Sea and the Sea of Japan, whereas the trophic structure of the Pacific Ocean was more distinct. Bayesian mixing model analysis suggested that Evermann's lanternfish ( Symbolophorus evermanni ) and prickly lanternfish ( Myctophum asperum ) were important inferred prey sources for several predators in the Pacific Ocean, whereas pearlside ( Maurolicus japonicus ) contributed substantially to several predator groups in the East China Sea. These findings suggest that micronekton may represent an important energy pathway supporting predatory fish communities in the Pacific Ocean and the East China Sea.

items.title: Development of biomaterials for bioremediation in agriculture: the importance of correct classification of the biocompatibility of immobilized microorganisms
items.abstract: The development of biomaterials for environmental bioremediation has emerged as a sustainable and promising strategy, becoming a consolidated research area within the field of contaminated soil treatment. In this context, advances in material science and biotechnology have enabled the development of innovative immobilization supports that improve microbial stability, protection, and biodegradation performance. Among these materials, polymeric matrices combined with natural biodegradable components have demonstrated significant potential for enhancing pesticide degradation efficiency while reducing environmental impacts. However, the accurate, standardized, and robust characterization of biocompatibility remains a critical challenge, which limits the large-scale application and commercialization of these biomaterials. To address this knowledge gap, this review discusses the importance of biocompatibility classification, microbial immobilization strategies, and viability assessment methods for microorganisms entrapped in different matrices. Additionally, it underscores the imperative for the development of more dependable quality control methodologies to guarantee the efficacy, safety, and scalability of biomaterial-based bioremediation technologies.

items.title: The interplay of landscape connectivity, composition and configuration in alien plant invasions across an ecological network
items.abstract: Abstract Context Biological invasions are deemed to be the second most important global driver of biodiversity loss showing strong interactions with the aftermaths of land use change and landscape fragmentation. The role of landscape composition and configuration in biological invasions is widely considered while its interplay with landscape connectivity is less understood. However, ecological connectivity can be equally crucial for both native and alien species, constituting the backbone of ecological network initiatives. Objectives We aim to assess how landscape composition, configuration and connectivity (in the ecological network) influence α- and β-diversity (floristic uniqueness) of both alien and native plant species, and to determine whether these effects differ according to habitat type. Methods The study was conducted in a 298 km 2 ecological network in the lowlands of Friuli Venezia Giulia, northeastern Italy, encompassing a mosaic of agricultural, natural, and semi-natural habitats. A hierarchical sampling design was applied to 87 terrestrial habitat nodes, where plant species composition and abundance were recorded in 219 plots. Landscape composition, configuration and connectivity were quantified to examine their influence on native and alien plant α- and β-diversity across different habitat types. Results We found contrasting effects of landscape connectivity, composition and configuration for native and alien species. Peripheral, less connected sites favored native species richness (α-diversity) and contributed to maintaining native floristic uniqueness (high β-diversity). In contrast, alien species richness was mainly associated with landscape composition and configuration, particularly the proportion of natural land use and edge-related effects in wooded habitats, while plots with higher alien richness showed lower compositional uniqueness within the alien species pool. Landscape composition and configuration also influenced invasion dynamics, as nodes surrounded by a high proportion of natural land uses with simple shapes helped contain plant invasions while preserving native richness and uniqueness. These patterns were often habitat-dependent, with stronger effects observed in wooded areas, where alien α-diversity increased with fragmentation, whereas native species richness declined. Conclusions Our findings suggest that managing landscape connectivity and reducing fragmentation can enhance resistance to invasions and support native species richness. Peripheral nodes may act as native refugia, supporting high native richness and floristic uniqueness, while more accessible central nodes may function as alien hubs associated with greater alien compositional uniqueness and potential propagule exchange. Shifting from intensive to extensive land uses through green infrastructures provides a win–win strategy, promoting native species and limit alien establishment.

items.title: QUIJOTE scientific results – XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
items.abstract: Abstract We present an analysis of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power-spectrum level in the multipole range 30 ≤ ℓ 20○, hinting toward a steepening of the BB spectrum relative to EE at the ∼1.6σ level. The synchrotron frequency spectral indices are found to be $\beta _{\rm s}^{\rm EE} = -3.26 \pm 0.05$ and $\beta _{\rm s}^{\rm BB} = -3.25 \pm 0.10$ for the same cut, in agreement with earlier real-space analyses. We find no evidence for spatial variations of βs across different Galactic latitude cuts, within current uncertainties. The synchrotron BB/EE power ratio is approximately 0.2 over the considered multipole range, lower than typical values for thermal dust, and consistent with previous measurements. We also measure a dust-synchrotron spatial correlation in the range 0.1–0.25 over 30 ≤ ℓ < 130. Using these results, we estimate the level of synchrotron contamination in future CMB B-mode measurements, finding an average power in the considered sky masks equivalent to r ≃ 0.003 at 90 GHz and r ≃ 0.0002 at 150 GHz for the relevant angular scales.

items.title: The Ghost of the Native Speaker and the Dark Energy Shadowing the Learner: A Posthumanist Inquiry into Human– AI Relationships in Second Language Writing
items.abstract: Abstract While existing research indicates the utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assisting language learners, how human–AI relationships may condition learners' being and becoming remains underexplored. In this article, we draw on Barad's agential realism to discuss findings of a posthumanist phenomenological study on 110 Chinese students' experiences with GenAI in a L2 writing workshop. Five forms of human–AI relationships are identified from the metaphors that the student participants employed to describe their experiences: user–tool, king–minister, friend–partner, student–teacher, and slave–tyrant. Across these entangled relationships, human and GenAI agents are differentiated in ways that foreground the figure of a ghostly GenAI native speaker, experienced as competent, efficient, and self(‐)less. By contrast, learners' weaknesses are brought forth as deficient, slow, and unreliable. As our analysis reveals, the ghostly GenAI native speaker is rendered possible and intelligible through a range of existing apparatuses, whose enactment has summoned a dark energy, reconfiguring the way in which native‐speakerism exerts influence upon language learners—it reinforces a technical view of L2 writing and excludes learners not from native‐speaker communities but potentially from the sociality of L2 writing as a whole, with foreclosed possibilities for imagining diverse ways of relating to the target language.

items.title: A morpho-kinematic view of the Necklace nebula
items.abstract: Abstract We present a morpho-kinematic study of the Necklace Nebula based on spatially resolved spectroscopic observations and 3D modeling performed with the shape software. The nebula is characterized by an equatorial disrupted ring accompanied by bipolar outflows. The geometry and velocity field of these different components are derived from the comparison between observed and synthetic images and position-velocity diagrams. The best model successfully reproduces the main morphological and kinematic features of the nebula, allowing us to constrain its 3D structure. We confirm that the disrupted ring is tilted about 60○ from the plane of the sky, but the bipolar outflows are inclined by 46○ with respect to the line of sight. This situation might indicate that the bipolar structures are not simple extensions of the equatorial ring, but instead correspond to a distinct mass-ejection event. The slight misalignment between these two components suggests either precession of the ejection axis, a temporal change in the dominant mass-loss geometry, or a misalignment in the magnetic field. Given that the Necklace Nebula hosts a close binary central star and is a well-established post-common envelope planetary nebula, our results support a scenario in which binary interaction plays a central role in shaping its morphology, even before the common envelope phase.

items.title: yippy : Standardized Yield Input Package Processing and Fourier-Domain PSF Interpolation for HWO Coronagraphs
items.abstract: Abstract Coronagraphs are a fundamental component of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), and nearly every aspect of mission design depends on accurate coronagraph performance data. Coronagraph designers generate yield input packages (YIPs), a standardized FITS-based format consumed by HWO yield calculators like ayo and exosims. However, no standard tool exists to process and use them: each research group independently recreates the same steps to extract throughput curves, compute contrast, and interpolate PSFs, and small method differences produce significant errors. We present yippy (Yield Input Package Python), an open-source library that standardizes YIP usage. yippy reproduces all coronagraph performance metrics used by ayo and exosims, so HWO researchers can use coronagraph data consistently with the community’s yield and exposure time calculators. Beyond scalar metrics, yippy implements Fourier-based PSF interpolation that generates spatially continuous off-axis images from the discrete PSF set in a YIP at yield-pipeline speeds, providing a reusable interface for coronagraph image simulation from yield input data. A jax-compatible interface supports batch processing on accelerators: on an H100 GPU yippy calculates nearly 15,000 PSFs per second, while the underlying physical optics propagation sustains roughly 4–5 PSFs per second on an Apple M2 Pro CPU. We validate the interpolation accuracy across three coronagraph architectures, demonstrating median relative RMS errors of ∼10−4 at typical grid spacings, and cross-validate performance metrics against both ayo (to 3% error) and exosims (to 6% error), two yield calculators whose ETCs have known disagreements.
