items.title: Ecological impact of steeplebush (Spiraea tomentosa L.) invasion on mite communities (Acari, Mesostigmata) in wet meadow ecosystems.
items.abstract: Invasive plants are species introduced outside their natural range and often cause ecological or economic harm. By modifying litter quality, root architecture, and soil chemistry, invasive plants can alter many soil processes, including nutrient cycling and edaphic activity. The main aim of our study was to provide the first assessment in Poland of the ecological impact of Spiraea tomentosa L. invasion on the abundance, diversity, and species richness of soil Mesotigmata (Gamasida; Gamasina and Uropodnia) mite communities in wet meadow ecosystems, thereby offering novel insights into the belowground ecological consequences of this invasive species. The research was carried out in a wet meadow complex located in the Lower Silesian Forests in south-western Poland. A total of 104 soil samples were collected from 26 experimental plots (13 invaded by Spiraea tomentosa and 13 uninvaded) in May and October 2024. In total, we identified 2,502 mesostigmatid mites belonging to 71 taxa. The three most abundant mite species across the entire study were Paragamasus vagabundus (Karg) (409 ind.), Zercon gurensis Mihelčič (228), and Trachytes aegrota (C. L. Koch) (216). Mite abundance was negatively associated with soil Fe, while litter pH and litter Pb showed positive but non-significant trends. Species richness was positively associated with soil Mn and litter Pb, and negatively associated with soil Fe and litter Cu. Mite diversity showed a significant overall effect of collection time and site type, although Tukey HSD post hoc tests did not detect significant pairwise differences among treatment combinations. Moreover, Mesostigmata diversity increased with soil Mn and K and decreased with soil Fe, Na, and soil moisture. However, diversity was lower at uninvaded sites than at invaded sites. Overall, our findings show that microhabitat alteration associated with the biological invasion of Spiraea tomentosa has a complex impact on the diversity and composition of mite communities.

items.title: Context-dependent sublethal hazard of glyphosate to non-target predators revealed by functional response analysis.
items.abstract: Glyphosate, one of the most widely used herbicides globally, is a significant environmental contaminant that may affect non-target organisms crucial to ecosystem services, including biological pest control. While glyphosate targets the shikimate pathway in plants, which is absent in animals, there is increasing evidence that glyphosate induces sublethal effects on arthropod predators. However, the factors modulating these effects remain unclear. Here, we investigated how physiological context, specifically pre-treatment with the broad-spectrum antibiotic tetracycline, commonly used to experimentally alter host associated microbial communities, modulates the sublethal hazard of glyphosate-based herbicide (GBH) on the predatory behavior of adult female Pardosa wolf spiders. Predation efficiency was measured using functional response assays across varying prey densities. Our results showed that GBH significantly reduced the spiders' predation rates, confirming its sublethal toxicity. However, spiders pre-treated with antibiotics exhibited higher capture rates following GBH exposure compared to the GBH only group. These findings demonstrate that the sublethal hazard of GBH on predators is context-dependent and can be altered by antibiotic-sensitive processes (such as host-symbiont interactions). This study highlights the complexity of pesticide effects on ecosystem services and suggests that the functional response of non-target predators depends strongly on their physiological background.

items.title: Low variability in the capsid gene of a generalist densovirus across lepidopteran hosts and geographic regions.
items.abstract: Viruses are ubiquitous in all ecosystems, and insects can serve as model host systems for understanding their geographic range and host specificity. Lepidoptera are relatively easy to collect and rear and are known to harbor diverse groups of viral pathogens. Much of the research on viruses in Lepidoptera has focused on baculoviruses, but this is beginning to change with better sequencing techniques. In this study, we use genetic tools to characterize the host and geographical range of the Junonia coenia densovirus (JcDV) (Family Parvoviridae, subfamily Densovirinae, genus Protoambidensovirus, specific epithet lepidopteran1). Using host tissue and larval frass, we screened 25 lepidopteran families from 11 locations across North and Central and South America for JcDV. We detected JcDV in the frass from 11 families of Lepidoptera, originating from both Neotropical and Nearctic biogeographic realms. To characterize genetic variation in the viruses detected, we conducted Sanger sequencing of a segment of the viral capsid gene in ten frass samples and from an additional 56 individual lepidopteran cadavers from three families in the Papilionoidea superfamily. Across all sequences obtained, the average sequence identity to the Oxford reference genome sequence was 99.85% and within our samples 99.77%. Compared to the reference, we found 18 nucleotide changes which were characterized into ten JcDV haplotype variants. These differences conferred seven amino acid substitutions and were not predicted by sample type (frass or cadaver tissue), geographic location, or lepidopteran host family. Ultimately, we conclude that JcDV is a widespread virus to which many lepidopteran families are exposed in their natural environment, and the capsid gene of JcDV is genetically well-conserved across geographic space and lepidopteran host species.

items.title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision.
items.abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

items.title: The effects of affect: Working memory, rumination and emotion reactivity - Insights from an affective n-back task.
items.abstract: Objective Internalizing disorders are associated with emotion regulation characterized by repetitive negative thinking. There is a proposed relationship between rumination and working memory and there are gaps in understanding how emotions impact this association. In the present study, we investigated differences in negative (hot) and neutral (cold) working memory processing in relation to measures of rumination and emotion reactivity. Our aim was to address hot working memory as a potential clinically relevant mechanism in challenges with emotion regulation. Emotion reactivity was hypothesized to mediate the relationship between rumination and working memory. Method Participants were undergraduate students (N = 120). Working memory was assessed using the Memory Affective Flexibility Task (MAFT), an affective experimental paradigm based on the n-back task that incorporates neutral and valenced visual stimuli. Facets of maladaptive emotion regulation were measured through self-report questionnaires for rumination and emotion reactivity. Associations were examined using multiple linear regression with rumination as the outcome variable. Results There were small relationships between working memory performance in both neutral and negative conditions of the MAFT with measures of rumination and emotion reactivity. There was a significant moderate correlation between emotion reactivity and rumination. Conclusion Despite correlations among self-report measures of emotion reactivity and rumination, we observed limited support for the links of task-based hot or cold working memory performance with self-rated emotion measures. This aligns with previous reports of modest correlations between task-based and self-report measures. The findings add to a growing literature on the challenges of capturing the interplay between emotion processes, affect and cognition in neuroscientific research.

items.title: Anthropocentric Thinking about Antibiotic Resistance and Ecosystems: Relations between Explanations and Misconceptions in American Undergraduates from Urban and Rural Backgrounds.
items.abstract: Intuitive conceptual frameworks can shape students' reasoning for biology concepts, sometimes forming misconceptions. Anthropocentric thinking-reasoning that centers humans-often relates to misconceptions about antibiotic resistance and ecosystem change. Cultural influences, such as lifestyles with greater exposure to nature, have been associated with reduced anthropocentric reasoning. The backgrounds of rural and urban children vary in opportunities for experiences with nature-rural children have greater exposure and urban children less exposure to outdoor settings. The relationship between students with rural and urban backgrounds and anthropogenic thinking highlights potential differences in students' biology misconceptions. Here, we compare students' rural and urban backgrounds and institutions to their use of anthropocentric reasoning and its relatedness with misconceptions in biology. Students from rural and urban backgrounds were recruited to complete a survey with written and categorical agreement ratings for misconceptions in biology. All students-regardless of hometown population and institution densities-showed similar rates of anthropocentric reasoning. However, the use of anthropocentric language was highly correlated with biological misconceptions. Our research suggests that anthropocentric thinking is pervasive in undergraduate students and influences biological misconceptions.

items.title: Emotional inertia in daily life: a dynamic structural equation modelling analysis of the role of emotion regulation strategy use.
items.abstract: High negative affect inertia refers to negative emotional states that show strong carryover from moment to moment and has been linked to maladjustment and poor mental health. Recent ecological momentary assessment (EMA) research has suggested that emotion regulation strategy use in daily life may contribute to emotional inertia. We build on this by examining the roles of rumination, suppression, reappraisal and acceptance in negative affect inertia for seven affective states in a sample of n = 451 emerging adults (mean age 27) who completed a 2-week EMA protocol. Using two-level dynamic structural modelling with within-person cross-lagged effects, rumination showed significant mediating effects with four negative affective states, implying a role in perpetuating negative affect; however, no other significant mediation effects were identified. Results point to rumination as the most promising intervention target among the emotion regulation strategies examined for reducing negative affect inertia, though the effects were modest.

items.title: Not everything can be counted: how awe enhances perceptions of immeasurability.
items.abstract: Awe arises in reaction to events or objects that exceed our expectancies, such as vast landscapes, breathtaking sunsets, or mind-blowing ideas (Gocłowska, M. A., Elliot, A. J., van Elk, M., Bulska, D., Thorstenson, C. A., & Baas, M. (2023). Awe arises in reaction to exceeded rather than disconfirmed expectancies. Emotion , 23 (1), 15-29.; Keltner, D., & Haidt, J. (2003). Approaching awe, a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion. Cognition and Emotion, 17(2), 297-314.Keltner, D., & Haidt, J. (2003). Approaching awe, a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion. Cognition and Emotion , 17 (2), 297-314.). Little psychological research has investigated how experiencing awe influences people's epistemic beliefs (e.g. beliefs about the nature of knowledge and the process of knowing). To achieve this, we tested how awe affects people's subjective sense of immeasurability , defined as a perception that conventional measures, such as words or numbers, are inadequate to describe aspects of the world around us (e.g. the beauty of nature). Across one correlational study and three experiments ( N = 596, collected between 2024 and 2025), we investigated the relationship between awe and immeasurability. We found that manipulated awe increased people's sense of immeasurability of the beauty of nature. In the final experiment, this effect was explained by the extent to which the awe experience was seen as exceeding (but not disconfirming) expectancies. These findings provide new insights into how awe affects people's epistemic beliefs.

items.title: School-based prevention of anabolic-androgenic steroid use: mapping the evidence from adolescent prevention programs.
items.abstract: Adolescents are vulnerable to sociocultural influences related to body image and appearance, which may increase the risk of anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) and other image- and performance-enhancing drug (IPED) use and subsequent adverse health outcomes. School-based prevention initiatives targeting AAS use and its associated health risks may prevent the initiation and use of these substances among adolescents by educating them about the dangers, adverse effects, and risks of AAS use while promoting healthier choices. This scoping review aimed to map the characteristics, intervention components, and reported outcomes of school-based prevention programs targeting AAS and other IPED use among adolescents. Peer-reviewed English-language studies evaluating school-based prevention programs addressing AAS and IPEDs among adolescents were included. Searches were conducted through Scopus, Embase (Elsevier), CINAHL (EBSCOhost), Web of Science, ProQuest, MEDLINE (Ovid), and PsycINFO, covering all eligible records published up to September 2025. Data were charted to map study characteristics, intervention types and delivery features, populations, and outcome domains assessed, with findings synthesised descriptively in line with scoping review methodology. Seventeen studies were included. Interventions mostly involved classroom-based education (70.6%) and sport- or exercise-integrated components (52.9%). Outcomes were predominantly evaluated by study-specific questionnaires (58.8%). Most studies examined knowledge, attitudes, intentions, and psychosocial outcomes, whereas fewer studies assessed behavioural outcomes, particularly actual AAS use (≤ 20%). Considerable variation was identified in intervention content, outcome measures, and follow-up periods. The available literature is heterogeneous and primarily focuses on knowledge, attitudinal, intentional, and psychosocial outcomes rather than behavioural outcomes. Future research should include more consistent outcome measures, longer follow-up periods, and greater attention to behavioural outcomes and psychosocial determinants of AAS and IPED use.

items.title: Performance psychology workshops for surgical trainees: A prospective pilot study on anxiety and mental toughness.
items.abstract: Background Performance anxiety and resilience are critical determinants of surgical trainee performance. Aims To evaluate the feasibility and preliminary impact of a brief performance psychology intervention, combining individual self-regulation with team-based performance strategies, on performance anxiety and mental toughness in surgical trainees. Methods In a prospective single-arm pilot and feasibility study in a university teaching hospital, nine surgical trainees from various subspecialities enrolled, with eight completing follow-up assessments. The intervention comprised two immersive workshops over two weeks, integrating individual and team-based psychological skills grounded in the biopsychosocial model of stress, challenge-threat appraisal, and high performance principles. Participants completed the Sport Anxiety Scale-2 and the Mental Toughness Evaluation Questionnaire-2 (MTE-2) at baseline (T0), three weeks (T1), and three months (T2). Results Eight of nine trainees (89%) completed all follow-up assessments, and the programme was delivered as planned. Mental toughness (MTE-2) improved over time (p = 0.002), and a median improvement of 580 points (95% CI 200 to 880) was sustained at three months. Most marked improvement seen in pre-performance distraction control. Anxiety (SAS-2) showed a short-term reduction, clearest for the worry subscale, though returned to baseline at three months. Frequency of technique use did not correlate with outcomes. Conclusions This brief high-performance psychology intervention was feasible and acceptable and was associated with short-term reductions in performance anxiety and sustained improvements in mental toughness in surgical trainees. These findings support the feasibility of integrating time-efficient psychological training in surgical education. Larger, controlled studies are required to confirm efficacy and mechanisms.

items.title: Boundaries and Bridges: The Complex Alliance Between Counselling and Learning Theories.
items.abstract: Counselling theories have traditionally been conceptualised within psychological, therapeutic, and developmental frameworks while learning theories have largely evolved as a separate field of inquiry. Although both domains are concerned with personal change, adaptation, and the development of new understandings, explicit theoretical integration between counselling and learning remains relatively limited. This article explores whether counselling may be usefully understood through the lens of learning theory and examines the extent to which key learning concepts can illuminate processes commonly associated with counselling. Drawing on major traditions in learning theory, including behaviourist, cognitive, constructivist, social, experiential, transformative, and humanistic perspectives, the paper develops a conceptual framework for analysing counselling as a context in which intensive personal learning frequently occurs. Rather than proposing an equivalence between counselling and learning, the analysis identifies significant areas of conceptual overlap and highlights how counselling may facilitate changes in knowledge, self-understanding, behaviour, meaning making, and identity. Attention is given to the roles of reflection, experience, dialogue, agency, and relational processes in supporting learning-oriented forms of personal development. The article concludes that a learning perspective offers a valuable complementary lens for understanding counselling processes and provides a basis for strengthening interdisciplinary dialogue between counselling theory and learning theory. Implications for theory development, research, and professional practice are discussed, alongside the limitations of the present conceptual analysis.

items.title: Emotion regulation difficulties are selectively associated with executive and behavioural apathy in Huntington's disease.
items.abstract: Objective Apathy occurs frequently in psychiatric and neurological disorders and is associated with functional impairment, reduced quality of life, and caregiver burden. Its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood, but recent studies indicate that apathy is multidimensional and has heterogeneous manifestations across disorders. Self-regulatory processes, such as emotion regulation, may contribute to these manifestations, but this relationship has received little attention. Huntington's disease (HD) provides a clinical model for examining whether emotion regulation difficulties are associated with global and multidimensional apathy. Methods Eighty-nine HD gene expansion carriers (HDGECs) completed the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale, Lille Apathy Rating Scale, and Dimensional Apathy Scale. Cognitive screening included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Hierarchical regressions examined associations between emotion regulation difficulties and apathy, adjusting for depressive symptoms. Results Greater emotion regulation difficulties were associated with global, Executive, and Behaviour/Initiation apathy, but not Emotional apathy. After accounting for depressive symptoms, Executive and Behaviour/Initiation apathy explained an additional 24.2% of variance in emotion regulation difficulties, whereas global apathy explained an additional 5.8%. Exploratory subgroup analyses found an independent association between Executive apathy and emotion regulation difficulties in premanifest but not manifest HDGECs. Conclusions Emotion regulation difficulties were associated with global apathy and showed the strongest associations with Executive and Behaviour/Initiation apathy, independent of depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that self-regulatory processes may be relevant to the heterogeneous manifestations of apathy and highlight the importance of examining specific apathy dimensions when investigating its underlying mechanisms and informing potential treatment approaches.

items.title: Developing a Measure of the Double-Edged Health-Related Consequences of Lottery Participation (DEHC-LP) Among Chinese Lottery Participants and Examining Their Psychological Correlates: The Roles of Lottery Beliefs and Passion.
items.abstract: Lottery participation may be associated with both beneficial and detrimental consequences relevant to individuals' health, well-being, and daily functioning, reflecting a double-edged phenomenon. Understanding the psychological factors associated with these divergent consequences is important for promoting responsible lottery participation. This study developed the Double-Edged Health-Related Consequences of Lottery Participation scale (DEHC-LP) and examined how lottery beliefs and passion were associated with these consequences among legal lottery participants in mainland China. Two independent samples comprising 588 lottery players were used for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, followed by a third sample of 918 lottery players who completed measures of luck beliefs, strategy beliefs, lottery passion, and the DEHC-LP. Results supported a two-factor second-order structure comprising lottery-related benefits and harms, with satisfactory reliability and validity. Structural equation modeling indicated that luck beliefs were indirectly associated with lottery-related benefits through harmonious passion. Strategy beliefs showed a more complex pattern: they were indirectly associated with lottery-related benefits through harmonious passion and were associated with both lottery-related harms and benefits through obsessive passion. These findings suggest that lottery participation should not be evaluated solely from a risk perspective, as psychological factors such as lottery beliefs and passion may be associated with divergent health-related consequences. The DEHC-LP provides a multidimensional measure of participants' perceived lottery-related consequences across domains relevant to health, well-being, and daily functioning. The findings underscore the importance of considering individuals' beliefs and passion when developing responsible lottery participation initiatives aimed at enhancing potential benefits while reducing harms.

items.title: An updated conceptual framework on physical performance and training in soccer: a narrative review.
items.abstract: Soccer practitioners routinely use external load (EL), internal load (IL) and fitness measures to monitor players; however, the same monitoring variable may be interpreted as training load (TL), performance, or athlete capacity depending on its purpose and reference. The conceptual problem addressed in this review is therefore not the absence of definitions for EL, IL, or fitness status, but rather the lack of an integrated interpretative structure explaining how these established constructs should be differentiated when evaluating soccer physical performance. This conceptually focused narrative review therefore aims to clarify the distinction between TL, physical performance output, physiological response, and athlete fitness capacity, and to integrate these established concepts within an interpretative framework for soccer training and monitoring. The framework does not propose match demands, physiological responses, or fitness status as replacements for the established concepts of EL, IL, and fitness. Rather, it organizes their interpretation according to three related questions: what external output did the athlete produce, what physiological response accompanied that output, and what does the relationship between output and response indicate about the athlete's capacity to perform?. By separating the purpose for which monitoring variables are interpreted, the framework aims to support practitioners in selecting appropriate measures and aligning training prescription with either physiological adaptation targets or the external performance demands that players are required to reproduce in competition.

items.title: Episodic memory in immersive virtual reality environments: the role of affective context and navigation control.
items.abstract: Memory in immersive virtual reality (VR) may depend on the encoding context and on users' control over virtual exploration. We examined memory for a single immersive episode in 234 young adults using a 2 × 3 between-subjects design crossing navigation control (self-directed vs. automated movement) with affective audiovisual context (pleasant, unpleasant, neutral). Memory was assessed through free recall, visual-feature memory, spatial-location memory, and complementary error indices. One effect held up under Holm correction across the three non-derived memory-performance outcomes. Free recall differed across affective contexts, F(2, 228) = 4.75, p = .010, ω² = 0.031, Holm-adjusted p = .030, with lower recall in the unpleasant than in the neutral condition, and the difference remained evident after adjustment for age, gender, and prior VR experience. Navigation control showed no robust general association with the principal memory-performance outcomes. A localized navigation-control × affective-context pattern emerged for spatial false object reports (raw p = .032), but the interaction did not survive correction across the corresponding family of memory-error tests (Holm-adjusted p = .192) and is treated as exploratory. The unpleasant-neutral contrast cannot be attributed uniquely to emotional valence, because the neutral condition lacked the concurrent audiovisual stream present in the affective conditions and may therefore differ in attentional or other stimulus properties. The results yield one multiplicity-robust performance effect and a set of exploratory error patterns; together they argue for tighter control of audiovisual and attentional features in immersive-memory research.

items.title: Ketamine Beyond Anaesthesia: Analgesic, Psychiatric, Antitumour, and Immunomodulatory Actions and Their Signalling Mechanisms.
items.abstract: To synthesize current evidence on ketamine for cancer-related pain and its intersecting psychiatric, anti-tumor, and immunomodulatory actions, emphasizing mechanisms, clinical relevance, and uncertainties relevant to oncology. Ketamine provides analgesia primarily through non-competitive antagonism of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and additional effects on excitatory, inhibitory, and opioid-related signaling. In patients with refractory cancer pain, it may be a useful adjunct to opioid-based multimodal analgesia and may reduce opioid requirements; however, clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Its rapid antidepressant effects may be relevant to the reciprocal burden of pain and depressive symptoms in cancer. Preclinical studies report antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, and ferroptosis-associated effects across several tumor models, involving phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin, extracellular signal-regulated kinase, and non-coding RNA-associated pathways. These findings are not uniform: breast cancer models have suggested potentially pro-metastatic effects. Immune effects are likewise dose-, context-, and perioperative-setting dependent, with reports of anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, and neutral effects. Ketamine is a potentially valuable opioid-sparing adjunct for selected patients with cancer-related pain and may also address comorbid depressive symptoms. Its putative direct anti-tumor and immunomodulatory actions remain predominantly preclinical and context dependent and should not currently guide oncologic treatment decisions. Appropriately powered clinical studies should define patient selection, dose and route, duration, safety, immune consequences, and long-term oncologic outcomes.

items.title: Open Surgery in the Robotic Era: National Trends and Training Implications from Two Decades of American Board of Urology Case Logs.
items.abstract: Purpose Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) has rapidly transformed the surgical management of urologic diseases, with robotic-assisted techniques increasingly replacing open approaches (OA). We aimed to characterize trends in OA versus MIS across major urologic oncologic procedures and evaluate surgeon-specific factors associated with surgical approach. Material and methods Operative logs from American Board of Urology examinees from 2000-2023 were examined for radical nephrectomy (RN), partial nephrectomy (PN), radical nephroureterectomy (RNU), radical prostatectomy (RP), and radical adrenalectomy (RA) and categorized by surgical approach. Approach proportions were assessed over time and stratified by individual procedure, surgeon gender, geographic region, certification status, and fellowship training. Results A total of 54,972 procedures were analyzed, of which 23% were OA and 77% were MIS. While surgical volume increased more than tenfold from 2003-2005 to 2021-2023, the proportion of OA declined from 75% to 9.9%. Declines in OA were observed across all procedures. Surgeon factors including age, sex, and fellowship training were associated with OA. Regional variation in the United States was identified, with the Southeast demonstrating the highest proportion of OA. Conclusions Open surgery in urologic oncology has declined dramatically over the past two decades and now represents a minority of cases. While this transition reflects advances in surgical technology and patient care, it raises important concerns regarding declining exposure to OA during training. As robotic surgery continues to dominate contemporary practice, targeted efforts may be necessary to ensure adequate training and competency in open surgical techniques.

items.title: Digital Archiving of Direct-to-Consumer Marketing Claims Made by Businesses Selling Unproven Stem Cell Interventions.
items.abstract: Over the last 2 decades, a large global marketplace has emerged in which businesses use direct-to-consumer advertising to sell putative stem cell treatments that are unsupported by convincing scientific evidence of safety and efficacy. It is common for such purported stem cell therapies not to have been reviewed and approved by national regulatory authorities, even though they are supposed to undergo rigorous premarketing review by regulatory bodies responsible for evaluating such medical products and determining whether they are backed by sufficient evidence to warrant approval. The marketing claims, commercial activities, and clinical practices of such businesses have resulted in patients experiencing serious harms, including loss of life, physical injuries, financial losses, and avoidable delays in accessing evidence-based treatments. Such businesses are also responsible for collective harms, including diverting patients from participating in legitimate stem cell clinical studies, damaging the field of credible stem cell research, and contributing to public confusion and misunderstandings about how to distinguish evidence-based stem cell therapies from stem cell interventions that are not backed by robust data. Researchers in bioethics, health law, the social sciences, and other academic fields have made important contributions to the critical analysis of direct-to-consumer digital marketing claims made by businesses selling unproven and unapproved stem cell interventions. Scholars studying such marketing representations have documented the use of persuasive "tokens of legitimacy" to make advertised stem cell interventions seem credible, trustworthy, and backed by current scientific evidence. Acknowledging the value of such scholarship, there is a growing need for the development of best practices in research methods and data-archiving practices. In particular, there is a need for increased digital archiving of online marketing claims made by businesses selling supposed stem cell treatments. Numerous parties can benefit from increased digital archiving of such problematic marketing representations. However, analyzing, archiving, and critiquing the marketing claims, business operations, and clinical practices of such businesses must be done in a careful, rigorous, and evidence-based manner that is attentive to the intimidating tactics some of these businesses use when responding to public criticism. Researchers need to document the marketing representations made by businesses selling unapproved and unproven stem cell interventions in ways that minimize exposure to legal threats and other efforts to suppress critical analysis. Using the Wayback Machine or other comparable archiving tools to create digital repositories of such marketing representations is one way to mitigate such threats, by capturing the exact claims such businesses make when promoting putative stem cell therapies. Archiving such digital marketing representations is important for academic research and can play a valuable role in other contexts, such as in legal actions taken against businesses using purportedly deceptive marketing claims to sell unproven and unapproved stem cell-based interventions.

items.title: Word Retrieval in the Wild: The Feasibility of an Audio-Based Ecological Momentary Naming Protocol Completed by Adults With and Without Poststroke Aphasia.
items.abstract: Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) involves collecting data regarding behaviors or states of interest repeatedly in individuals' natural environments, typically from a smart device. The feasibility of EMA protocols with people with aphasia (PWA) remains relatively unexplored, particularly for objective assessments of language ability. We assessed the feasibility of a novel, smartwatch-delivered, audio-based ecological momentary naming protocol. Fourteen PWA and 13 healthy controls completed a 3-week EMA protocol in which they attempted to name pictured objects delivered via smartwatch prompts while going about daily routines. Participants were pseudorandomly assigned to either a single-item (36 prompts per day, one image each) or nine-item (four prompts per day, nine images each) condition. Feasibility metrics were compliance (number of naming attempts/number of scheduled prompts), completion (number of naming attempts/number of delivered prompts), and perceived ease and burden of completing EMAs (captured via weekly surveys). Average compliance for both PWA and controls was 77%, with completion at 83% and 84% for controls and PWA, respectively. Participants in the one-item condition trended toward higher compliance (at 83.3%) than individuals in the nine-item condition (at 71.9%). Perceptions of EMA ease and burden did not change over time or vary by group or EMA condition. Higher compliance was associated with temporal variables (day of protocol, time of day, day of week), older age, and better inhibitory control. Higher completion was associated with being unemployed and higher perceived burden. Qualitative analysis of exit interviews indicated that 89% of participants had a generally positive impression of the protocol. This novel EMA was feasible for adults with and without aphasia. Although EMA research with PWA is still in its infancy, mobile health methodologies provide several promising avenues for improving the accuracy of long-term, in situ surveillance of aphasia symptoms.

items.title: Common mental health problems experienced by adolescents living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
items.abstract: Adolescents living with HIV (ALWH) carry a substantial burden of mental health problems, yet summary data remain limited. Previous reviews, particularly systematic reviews, have focused mainly on diagnosed disorders among adults or broader populations of young people living with HIV, while substance use and emotional and behavioural symptoms remain understudied and often underreported. This scoping review synthesized existing evidence on common mental health problems among ALWH aged 10-19 years in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). We searched five electronic databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Embase, and Open Access for Africa) and Google Scholar, and screened the bibliographic references of selected articles for additional studies. Search terms were combined using Boolean operators and organized into four concept categories: HIV, age, mental health, and region. Eligible studies were original, peer-reviewed research published in English between 2020 and 2026, conducted in SSA, and reporting on mental health among ALWH aged 10-19 years. The search yielded 427 records, of which 29 duplicates were removed. Of the 398 articles screened, 317 were excluded at the abstract stage and a further 57 after full-text review, leaving 24 articles for inclusion. The review identified six common mental health problems among ALWH in SSA: depressive disorders and symptoms, generalized anxiety, suicidality, emotional and behavioural problems, posttraumatic stress, and substance use problems. Depression and suicidality were the most frequently reported, whereas substance use, generalized anxiety, posttraumatic stress, and emotional and behavioural problems were less frequently reported. ALWH in SSA experience a range of mental health problems that may affect their well-being and engagement in HIV care. Routine mental health screening, prevention, and psychosocial support should be integrated into HIV care for this population. Strengthening integrated mental health and HIV services may help address unmet needs and improve health outcomes among ALWH in SSA.

items.title: Gut virome remodeling after fecal microbiota transplantation is associated with virus-bacteria co-variation and metabolic response in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
items.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modifies gut bacterial composition and improves metabolic outcomes in subjects with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObT2), but bacterial changes alone do not fully explain the heterogeneity in clinical response. We performed virus-like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing coupled with bulk-DNA metagenomic sequencing on longitudinal fecal samples from a randomized controlled FMT trial in ObT2. Using random forest classification, post-FMT virome changes showed accuracy comparable to bacteriome changes (84.8% vs 81.4%) in distinguishing LDL responders from non-responders. Donor-derived viral contig engraftment was detected in 64.7% (11/17) of recipients receiving FMT alone and 58.8% (10/17) receiving FMT with lifestyle intervention (LSI), versus 5.6% (1/18) in the sham with LSI group. FMT was associated with increased virome diversity, compositional shifts toward the donor virome, and coordinated virus-bacteria associations, with most responsive viral contigs classified as Caudoviricetes. FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

items.title: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk.
items.abstract: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.

items.title: The science of child and adolescent mental health in Mozambique: A systematic review of prevalence estimates, measurement tools, and interventions.
items.abstract: Mozambique is home to 18 million children and adolescents largely underrepresented in mental health research. We conducted a systematic review of evidence-based resources (prevalence estimates, assessment instruments, and interventions) on mental health-related outcomes addressing individuals aged 0-19 years in Mozambique. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Google Scholar, African Index Medicus, and local catalogues. Extraction followed COSMIN and Cochrane manuals (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251016208). The search yielded 81 unique publications, including 61 reports presenting prevalence estimates from 25 studies, 29 reports providing data on 42 assessment instruments, and 9 intervention reports describing 8 intervention trials. The clinical prevalence of mental disorders were estimated in two surveys, conducted in Nampula (ADHD: 13·4%; N = 748, 6-18 years) and Maputo (any mental diagnosis: 23%, anxiety disorders: 17·5%; major depression episode: 8·5%; disruptive behavior disorder: 6·6%; substance use disorders: 4·5%; ADHD: 3·3%; PTSD: 1·2%; N = 486, 12-19 years). Most research focused on psychosocial adversities, with nationally representative adolescent surveys reporting significant exposure to violence (physical/emotional violence annually: 24·86%; girls suffering intimate partner violence: 21·11%; lifetime sexual abuse: 16·55%). National suicide rates were highest among 15-19-year-olds (1·53 per 100,000). Only four instruments were cross-culturally adapted and showed reliable psychometrics (MINI-KID, GAD-7, PHQ-A, and SDQ), whilst unadapted tools performed poorly. There was a single randomized clinical trial which reported a cost-effective intervention for neurodevelopment among high-poverty preschoolers. Children and adolescents in Mozambique face significant psychosocial adversity, and available evidence suggests a substantial burden of mental disorders according to limited clinical data. There are few available instruments assessing mental conditions, and culturally sensitive approaches are warranted for strengthening local research.

items.title: "Carrying the burden silently": A mixed-methods analysis of common mental health disorders among women caregivers living with HIV in Enugu, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Women caregivers living with HIV (WCLHIV) face a dual burden of managing their own health while caring for their families, increasing their vulnerability to mental health disorders. This study aimed to ascertain the prevalence and factors associated with common mental health disorders among WCLHIV in Enugu, Nigeria. A cross-sectional study employing a mixed method approach was conducted among 1,011 WCLHIV accessing anti-retroviral therapy in four tertiary health facilities in Enugu State, Nigeria. Quantitative data were obtained face-to-face using pre-tested, validated tools to assess the prevalence of depression, anxiety, stigma, and other psychological characteristics. Multivariate logistic regression identified significant risk factors of mental health disorders at a 95% confidence interval and p < 0.05. Four focus group discussions involving 35 WCLHIV explored factors impacting their mental well-being. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically using an inductive approach. Participants had a mean age of 44.3 (SD ± 8.44) years. The prevalence of depression and anxiety was 25.7% and 19.2%, respectively, while 79.0% reported high perceived stigma. Having primary education (AOR = 1.53; 95% CI: 1.06 -2.22), and low social support (AOR = 2.32; 95% CI: 1.11-5.07) were risk factors while low income (AOR = 0.42; 95% CI: 0.21-0.85), and low perceived stress (AOR = 0.05; 95% CI: 0.02-0.15) were protective of depression. Low perceived stress was protective of anxiety (AOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.02-0.22). Qualitative findings converged with quantitative data, highlighting the impact of stigma, poor social support, pill burden, fear of status disclosure, and financial strain on the mental health of WCLHIV.The prevalence of common mental health disorders was high among WCLHIV with a substantial proportion experiencing depression and anxiety, reflecting the significant impact of stigma, low social support, and stress. Targeted multi-level psychosocial interventions and community empowerment programs are needed to strengthen social support and reduce stigma among WCLHIV.

items.title: Changes in the acceptance of artificial intelligence in medicine among physicians and the general public in Japan: A repeated cross-sectional comparison of 2018 and 2025.
items.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced rapidly, yet whether growing societal familiarity with AI is accompanied by greater willingness to receive relatively autonomous AI-led care remains unclear. We conducted repeated cross-sectional online surveys in Japan in 2018 and 2025 using the same questionnaire and compared self-identified physicians and members of the general public (2018: 399 physicians and 600 members of the public; 2025: 300 physicians and 300 members of the public). Mean responses to the item assessing intention to use medical AI did not differ significantly between survey years in either group, despite consistently favorable evaluations of its usefulness and future necessity. Among physicians, the unadjusted mean response regarding the potential of medical AI to improve clinical efficiency was higher in 2025, but this difference was not significant after adjustment for age and sex. Among members of the public, self-rated knowledge of medical AI was higher in 2025, while expectations that medical AI would increase healthcare costs were also greater. These findings suggest that increased self-rated knowledge may not necessarily be accompanied by greater intention to use relatively autonomous medical AI. Implementation strategies should therefore address concerns regarding responsibility, safety, data protection, and healthcare costs alongside efforts to improve public understanding.

items.title: Smart Paper Technology for maternal and newborn health data in The Gambia: A qualitative study of early implementation.
items.abstract: Many low- and middle-income countries rely on paper-based maternal and child health records that are often incomplete, fragmented, and difficult to use for continuity of care and decision-making. Smart Paper Technology (SPT), a hybrid paper-digital documentation system, has been proposed as a practical alternative to fully electronic medical records in resource-constrained settings. This study explored the early implementation of SPT in maternal and infant health services in The Gambia, focusing on feasibility and acceptability. We conducted a qualitative descriptive implementation evaluation guided by Rapid Assessment Procedures (RAP) in two pilot facilities in the Western Region of The Gambia between September and December 2024. Data were collected through 30 semi-structured interviews; four focus group discussions with 30 participants spanning facility-level clinical, management, and administrative staff, Ministry of Health staff, and technical and implementing partners; and non-participant observations across key service delivery areas. Data were analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Participants described SPT as feasible and broadly acceptable because it built on familiar paper-based workflows, was introduced through a participatory process, and offered advantages in reporting, information retrieval, and maternal-infant record linkage. However, these benefits were contingent on the implementation context. Key challenges included uneven training coverage, dual documentation, limited internet connectivity, scanning and data capture errors, storage constraints, and concerns about data governance. Staff adapted through peer mentoring, remote troubleshooting, and local workarounds. Participants emphasised that successful scale-up would require sustained training, clear governance arrangements, adequate human and technical resources, and a phased transition to government ownership. SPT offers a practical pathway towards digitisation in maternal and infant health services in LMICs, but its success depends on strong organisational systems, workforce support, and implementation processes that are responsive to routine service realities.

items.title: The intention to use Kangaroo Mother Care among first-time mothers 15-24 years in Kinshasa, DRC: An application of the integrated behavioral model.
items.abstract: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) is a low-cost, safe, and simple method that has proven efficacious at improving neonatal health outcomes, including mortality, in low-income countries. While beneficial for all newborns, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends KMC specifically for low birthweight (LBW) and premature infants. This study examined the applicability of a modified Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) framework for predicting KMC intentions among first-time mothers (FTMs) 15-24 years old in Kinshasa, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This study used secondary cross-sectional data from the 2020 Momentum Project endline survey, a quasi-experimental study in three intervention and three comparison health zones in Kinshasa, DRC. The association between IBM components and KMC intentions was tested using multivariate logistic regression. The total sample consisted of 1,918 adolescent and young first-time mothers (FTMs). About half of the respondents stated that they were "very likely" to practice KMC if they had a LBW or preterm baby. Approval of KMC, normative expectations, descriptive norms, self-efficacy, and autonomy were all positively associated with the intent to practice KMC. Age was also found to be a significant predictor; the odds of KMC intentions were 90% higher (95% CI= (1.11-3.24)) for FTMs 20-24 years compared to FTMs 15-19 years. The association between autonomy and KMC intentions was moderated by age. Marginal effects of the interaction found that the probability of intending to practice KMC for respondents 20-24 years was constant regardless of autonomy level, while autonomy significantly increased the probability of KMC intentions for younger women aged 15-19 years. Results suggest that KMC intentions among first-time mothers 15-24 years are associated with multiple factors simultaneously. Programs seeking to improve KMC intentions among this population should consider implementing age-specific empowering and norms-based strategies.

items.title: Risky sexual behaviors and associated factors among adolescent girls and young women in the context of HIV prevention pre-exposure prophylaxis in Tanzania: Analysis of the Tanzania HIV Impact Survey 2022-2023.
items.abstract: Risky sexual behavior contributes to HIV acquisition among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), including Tanzania. However, nationally representative evidence on its prevalence and associated factors remains limited. This study examines the prevalence and associated factors of risky sexual behavior among AGYW aged 15-24 years in Tanzania, in the context of the expanding Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) provision. A secondary analysis of nationally representative data from the 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) was conducted among 3,669 sexually active AGYW aged 15-24 who answered PrEP-related questions. Survey-weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were carried out. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.The survey-weighted prevalence of risky sexual behaviors was 38.29%, higher among those aged 15-17 years than 18-24 years (61.57% versus 35.63%). Not being in a union was associated with increased odds of risky sexual behaviors among participants aged 15-17 years (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI: 4.33-17.55; p < 0.001) and 18-24 years (AOR = 15.13, 95% CI: 11.40-20.08; p < 0.001). Alcohol use was also associated with increased odds in both age groups (15-17 years: AOR = 13.38, 95% CI: 1.53-116.64; p = 0.019; 18-24 years: AOR = 2.47, 95% CI: 1.57-3.89; p < 0.001). Among young women aged 18-24 years, health facility attendance, family planning use and willingness to use PrEP were associated with higher odds, whereas secondary or higher education, parent or guardian communication about sex or HIV, and prior HIV testing were associated with lower odds. Risky sexual behavior remains common among Tanzanian AGYW, particularly those aged 15-17 years. Age-responsive prevention programmes need to integrate behavioral and biomedical interventions, prioritizing AGYW who are not in a union and who use alcohol or have limited access to PrEP.

items.title: Readability and Citation Sources of ChatGPT-Generated Responses to Lymphoma-Related Health Questions: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Lymphoma is one of the most prevalent groups of cancers among people aged 15 to 29 years. Increasingly, patients with lymphoma and their caregivers use generative AI systems, supported by large language models (LLMs), to seek cancer-related online health information. Despite the need for plain and clear health information for clinical decision-making, there is a dearth of research on the readability and citation source classification of LLM-supported online health information. The objective of this study was to assess the reading level and reading ease of lymphoma-related health information using OpenAI's GPT-5.2 model, as well as the citation sourcing of LLM-generated results. Questions were submitted to the LLM through an automated pipeline. The application code was written with Claude and run and hosted on Vercel. Standardized instructions were submitted to the LLM, asking for evidence-based sources with URLs to enable citation analysis. The final dataset included 392 citations garnered from 96 standardized lymphoma-related questions. Readability was assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Flesch Reading Ease scores. Citation sources were classified into 9 predefined organization types, and topics included Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma and clinical trials. Differences in readability were tested using linear models fitted to all 392 citations, with standard errors clustered by question. Estimated marginal means (EMMs) were used to summarize model-adjusted readability scores by citation source and topic. When the omnibus test was statistically significant, pairwise comparisons were performed using the Tukey-Kramer adjustment for multiple comparisons. The Flesch-Kincaid reading levels of the ChatGPT responses by citation source and topic type were determined to be at the college or university level, well above the recommended sixth-grade level. Grade level did not differ by citation source (P=.58). The reading grade level of responses for Hodgkin lymphoma responses was statistically higher than that of clinical trial responses (mean 16.2, SD 3.4 vs 13.6, SD 2.5; P=.005). Flesch Reading Ease scores across source and topic were found to be very difficult at the university graduate academic level and did not differ by source (P=.27) or topic (P=.17). Although LLMs frequently produce responses that include cited information, the readability of these outputs may limit accessibility for many patients and caregivers. These findings highlight the need for improved readability standards in AI-generated health information and reinforce that LLM outputs should complement, not replace, professional medical guidance.

items.title: Characterization of the complete mitochondrial genome of Haemaphysalis hystricis and its phylogenetic implications.
items.abstract: Haemaphysalis hystricis is a medically important tick vector, and three complete mitochondrial genomes derived from specimens collected from different geographic regions and hosts have previously been reported. In this study, we sequenced and analyzed the complete mitochondrial genome derived from H. hystricis specimens collected from a human host in Shaoguan, Guangdong Province, China, and systematically compared it with previously published H. hystricis mitogenomes. The complete mitogenome is 14,714 bp in length and contains 13 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, 2 ribosomal RNA genes, and two non-coding control regions. The overall gene order and composition are highly conserved and consistent with those reported for other Haemaphysalis species. The genome exhibits a strong A + T nucleotide bias, which is a typical feature of hard tick mitogenomes. Most tRNAs fold into typical cloverleaf secondary structures, whereas several exhibit truncated structures, reflecting a common pattern of mitochondrial tRNA structural simplification in arthropods. Selective pressure analysis indicated that all 13 PCGs are under purifying selection. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis showed that H. hystricis was most closely related to H. longicornis, consistent with previous studies. This study provides an additional H. hystricis mitogenome and compares it with the three previously published conspecific mitogenomes. The comparison revealed differences in genome length, the structure of non-coding regions, and tRNA secondary structures and provided estimates of gene-specific selective pressures. These findings provide valuable data for comparative mitogenomics and studies of intraspecific genetic variation in ticks.

items.title: Anti-Bacterial and Anti-Biofilm Activities of Cell-Free Supernatant of Lactobacillus johnsonii Against Salmonella Typhimurium.
items.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a predominant foodborne pathogen whose robust biofilm-forming capacity poses a persistent challenge to food safety and public health. This study investigated the inhibitory effects of cell-free supernatant (CFS) derived from Lactobacillus johnsonii on biofilms and characterized the transcriptional responses associated with CFS exposure using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). L.johnsonii CFS retarded bacterial growth at high concentrations. Moreover, CFS at various concentrations significantly inhibited biofilm formation in both S. Typhimurium strains, SL1344 and 14028, with maximum inhibition rates of 88.22% and 79.32%, respectively. CFS treatment markedly reduced metabolic activity, surface hydrophobicity, and auto-aggregation, meanwhile impaired bacterial motility and disrupted the architectural integrity of the biofilms. Furthermore, the CFS effectively prevented biofilm formation on various food and food-contact surfaces. RNA-seq analysis revealed that CFS treatment significantly altered the transcriptional profiles of Salmonella, with differentially expressed genes mainly enriched in ribosome, carbon metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, and microbial metabolism in diverse environments. These findings demonstrate the antibiofilm potential of L. johnsonii CFS under laboratory conditions and indicate its potential in controlling Salmonella contamination in food industry.

items.title: Mapping the debate on the role of national ethics councils in democratic reasoning. A narrative literature review.
items.abstract: Developments in science and society are moving fast. Emerging technologies give rise to ethical questions about manipulability of life and the ethical limits of biomedical science. To foster legitimate and justified policymaking on bio-ethical issues, governments seek expert guidance from bioethics advisory bodies such as national ethics councils. This raises questions about how they fulfil their advisory role within the democratic context. In what way can national ethics councils best contribute to democratic reasoning and decision-making regarding complex bioethics issues? We performed a narrative review of academic literature that concerns the role and legitimacy of national ethics councils. We searched literature databases PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar. The goal was to identify key themes that emerge as common threads across the literature. We identified five themes. We examined the discussions on the conceptualization of advice and the forms deemed appropriate for a national ethics council in relation to democratic decision-making, on the role of consensus, on the dimensions of expertise and council composition, on the dual tasks of formulating policy advice and stimulating public debate, and on the normative frameworks underpinning the work of national ethics councils. Our results indicate that in the context of complex policy issues, national ethics councils can make important contributions to democratic reasoning, though this involvement is shaped by several underlying dynamics. This narrative review urges national ethics councils to increase (self-) awareness as well as transparency about how they interpret their role within the democratic system.

items.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
items.abstract: Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation. The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report. On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions. This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

items.title: Perceived Discrimination, Preparation for Bias, and Associations with Physical and Mental Health of Racially/Ethnically Marginalized Children.
items.abstract: Prior studies suggest that perceived discrimination and preparation for bias are associated with children's mental health, yet few studies have examined relationships with children's physical health. The current study expands on prior literature by examining associations between perceived discrimination and preparation for bias parenting practices on the physical and mental health of racially/ethnically marginalized children. Children (n = 227, ages 7-13 years, 58% female; 28% Non-Hispanic Black, 26% Hispanic, 15% Hmong, 15% Native American, 10% multiracial/ethnic with White and 6% multiracial/ethnic without White) completed an in-clinic assessment of cardiometabolic health and self-reported perceived discrimination. Parents completed survey measures of their child's mental health (self-efficacy, inhibitory control, depression) and their use of preparation for bias parenting practices. Physical health measures (BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, pulse rate, hair cortisol) were taken at a lab visit. In adjusted regression analyses, children who self-reported any experiences of perceived discrimination had significantly lower levels of self-efficacy (p < 0.05) and inhibitory control (p < 0.05) than those who did not report experiences of discrimination. Preparation for bias parenting practices differed significantly by race/ethnicity and higher levels were associated with higher hair cortisol concentrations in children, reflecting elevated activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary adrenal (HPA) axis (p < 0.05). There were otherwise no statistically significant differences in children's mental or physical health outcomes as a function of perceived discrimination or preparation for bias parenting practices. Our findings highlight the potential importance of interventions that reduce interpersonal discrimination and the need for further research on parenting practices that may influence children's health.

items.title: Brief Report: User Participation in the Iterative Co-Design of Public Child Mental Health Services.
items.abstract: Service planning should necessarily involve the community. This brief report presents parental feedback collected after a psychoeducational group for parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and places these observations within recent literature on participatory co-design. At the end of the psychoeducational group, parents completed the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8) and were invited to provide optional free-text comments. The results show a high level of satisfaction with the intervention, and subjective observations of interest were collected. Collected feedback illustrates how parental input can guide iterative, user-centered improvements in public ASD services. More research is needed on what are the most appropriate means to integrate the experience of patients and their families into a process of continuous improvement that a public child and adolescent mental health resource should undergo.

items.title: Methodological challenges and uncertainties in human health risk assessment of nitrate exposure.
items.abstract: Safe and clean water is a fundamental requirement for human health and well-being. Both the quantity and quality of drinking water directly affect population health, which makes the investigation of contaminants and their associated health risks a matter of growing scientific and public concern. Among the many waterborne contaminants, nitrate is of particular importance. It is a recalcitrant compound found in most water bodies, originating from both natural sources and anthropogenic activities such as agriculture and wastewater discharge. Numerous studies have attempted to evaluate the health risks of nitrate exposure across different age groups, including infants, children, and adults. However, in reviewing the literature, we have identified recurring methodological inconsistencies that may compromise the reliability of risk estimates. In this discussion paper, we examine key methodological issues in nitrate-related human health risk assessment, including the misapplication of nitrate reference dose (RfD) values across different population groups, inconsistencies in chemical units and nomenclature, and uncertainties arising from the conversion of nitrate to nitrite during exposure and risk assessment. Examples from published research will be used to illustrate and critically analyse these common methodological pitfalls.

items.title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China.
items.abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. In this study, we report the co-circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and H5N6 HPAIVs associated with mortality events in Anseriformes and Charadriiformes at a coastal wintering site in Fujian Province, China. H5N1 and H5N6 viruses were identified in four species of waterfowl (Bean Goose, Eastern Spot-billed Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, and Eurasian Curlew). Phylogenetic analysis indicated that these H5N1 and H5N6 isolates were clade 2.3.4.4b strains circulating within Eurasia and lacked known mammalian adaptation markers in key proteins. The infected birds exhibited severe systemic multi-organ pathology, with the most pronounced damage observed in the lungs. H5N6 and H5N1 viruses caused lethal injury in BALB/c mice, with H5N1 leading to systemic infection. Environmental sampling also revealed the presence of H5N1 HPAIVs alongside low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) such as H3N1 and H6N1. Our findings highlight the complex and dynamic transmission patterns of H5 HPAIV in wild bird populations and the substantial threat they pose to mammals, underscoring the critical importance of sustained surveillance for high pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds.

items.title: Altered GABA<sub>B</sub> receptor sensitivity in heavy drinkers indexed using a TMS-based biomarker: a randomized controlled experimental medicine trial.
items.abstract: Metabotropic γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptors (GABA B Rs) are implicated in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and represent a promising therapeutic target. However, robust biomarkers of GABA B Rs target engagement and sensitivity in humans are lacking. We examined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-derived cortical inhibition and growth hormone (GH) release as measures of GABA B R function, and whether heavy alcohol use is associated with altered responses to pharmacological GABA B R activation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 31 healthy volunteers (16 heavy drinkers, 15 light drinkers) received baclofen 30 mg, baclofen 60 mg, or placebo across three sessions. Long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), short-interval intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation were assessed with paired-pulse TMS at baseline and ~60 min post-dose. Baclofen blood concentrations and plasma GH levels were measured. Baclofen produced dose-dependent increases in GH release, confirming neuroendocrine GABA B R engagement. The LICI response to baclofen differed between groups: In light drinkers, baclofen at 30 mg potentiated LICI, and a similar potentiation was seen at 60 mg, indicating that a plateau may have been reached. In contrast, in heavy drinkers, a potentiation of LICI similar to that in light drinkers was seen at 30 mg baclofen, but was absent at the 60 mg dose despite comparable pharmacokinetics, suggesting altered GABA B R function. Effects were selective for GABA B R-mediated inhibition, with no consistent modulation of short-interval intracortical inhibition or corticospinal excitability. Acute baclofen administration reveals altered GABA B R sensitivity in heavy drinkers, with preserved responses at lower doses but reduced response under stronger agonist stimulation. LICI and GH release provide complementary biomarkers of central and peripheral GABA B Rs engagement and may support translational development of mechanism-based treatments for AUD.

items.title: Circuit architecture and regulation of the Drosophila brain neuroendocrine system.
items.abstract: Insect neurosecretory cells (NSCs), located in distinct regions of the brain and the ventral nerve cord (VNC), are a major source of neuropeptides and peptide hormones (NPHs) that facilitate communication between the nervous system and peripheral tissues. NPHs, in turn, regulate growth and development, and modulate diverse behaviors and physiological processes including feeding, locomotion, social behaviors, metabolism, and reproduction. Given their central role in regulating systemic homeostasis, NSCs are tightly regulated. Recent advances in connectomics and single-cell transcriptomics have enabled comprehensive identification of NSCs in the Drosophila melanogaster brain and identified factors that modulate their activity. Here, we review the current state-of-the-art on insect NSCs and the inputs regulating them, predominantly focusing on adult Drosophila. We highlight: 1) major synaptic inputs, 2) neuromodulatory inputs, 3) gut-derived NPHs, and 4) cell-autonomous internal sensors that influence NSC activity. Finally, we discuss open questions in the field and how advances in omics approaches can bridge the gap in our understanding of NSC regulation between Drosophila and other insects.

items.title: Mechanisms of Seizure Generation and SUDEP in Cortical Dysplasia: A Role for Cortical Up and Down States.
items.abstract: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) remains the primary cause of epilepsy-related mortality, yet the preictal brain dynamics that distinguish fatal from nonfatal seizures are not well understood. Identifying the network mechanisms determining these outcomes is critical for developing SUDEP risk biomarkers. Using a neuron-specific PTEN knockout mouse model of cortical dysplasia-which exhibits spontaneous seizures and SUDEP-like events-we employed long-term video-EEG monitoring to analyze cortical state transitions and network signatures. We found that nonfatal seizures are preceded by a progressive "ramp-up" of cortical up and down states, characterized by alternating neuronal depolarization and hyperpolarization, which appears to facilitate seizure initiation. In sharp contrast, sudden death is preceded by a marked suppression of these state transitions and the emergence of infraslow EEG activity, suggestive of spreading depolarizations. This pattern differed from the sustained spike-wave complexes and preserved state transitions observed during status epilepticus. These physiological differences are mirrored behaviorally: nonfatal events typically feature forelimb clonus and spike-wave discharges, whereas fatal seizures are characterized by kicking, tonic hindlimb extension, and diffuse EEG attenuation. Together, these findings suggest that cortical up and down states support seizure initiation, while their disruption and failure to recover postictally predisposes neocortical networks to spreading depression episodes that very likely propagate to brainstem circuits, ultimately triggering SUDEP. By delineating these divergent peri-ictal signatures, this study identifies candidate neurophysiological markers for SUDEP risk stratification.

items.title: Cross-species evaluation of commercial primary antibodies by Western blotting for immunohistochemical protein detection in mouse, rat, and human brain tissue.
items.abstract: Background Commercial antibodies show variable specificity and performance, limiting reproducibility of immunohistochemical studies. We systematically evaluated antibodies used to detect brain proteins across species. New method Established Western blotting (WB) and immunofluorescence (IF) validation approaches were applied systematically and in parallel to mouse, rat, and human brain tissue. The distinctive scope of the study was the comparative evaluation of 23 antibodies targeting 17 proteins, with WB results interpreted in the context of expected molecular weights, isoforms, post-translational modifications, and published evidence concerning each target. Antibody performance was further compared with publicly available validation information, and logistic regression was used to assess whether antibody citation count and manufacturer-provided validation information predicted successful experimental validation. Results Ten antibodies (43%) showed supportive WB results, and eight (35%) were validated by both WB and IF. Several antibodies produced unexplained or non-specific bands, while others showed speciesdependent performance. Validated antibodies displayed appropriate neuroanatomical and subcellular staining patterns. Antibody citation count was moderately associated with successful validation, whereas manufacturer-provided validation information did not improve predictive performance. Comparison with existing methods The overall validation rate was comparable to previously published antibody validation studies and Human Protein Atlas results. The present study extends existing work through its broader antibody panel, parallel cross-species evaluation, detailed target-protein assessment, and quantitative analysis of antibody metadata. Conclusions Commercial antibodies require independent validation before use in cross-species immunohistochemical studies. Our results provide a practical resource for antibody selection and highlight limitations of manufacturer claims and citation counts as indicators of antibody performance.
